title: Cargo audiograph C build omits Linux feature-test macro
description: The standalone audiograph Makefile defines _GNU_SOURCE on Linux, but crates/sequencer/build.rs compiles the same C sources under strict -std=c11 without that definition. A clean or refingerprinted cargo build then fails because glibc hides posix_memalign, pthread_rwlock_t, strdup, and usleep declarations. Make the Cargo C build use the same Linux feature-test contract and verify a release compile from a shell without CFLAGS.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux with CFLAGS unset, Cargo's sequencer build compiles the audiograph C sources in release mode without implicit-declaration or unknown pthread_rwlock_t errors; non-Linux build settings remain unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed crates/sequencer/build.rs so Cargo defines _GNU_SOURCE for the Linux audiograph C build, matching the standalone Makefile. User confirmed the release build compiles correctly with CFLAGS unset.

title: Clean-HEAD recipe puts the dedicated target dir on tmpfs; workspace runs exhaust /tmp
description:
eseq-linux.39 fixed the clean-HEAD recipe's shared-target-dir bug by giving the
worktree a dedicated target directory at /tmp/eseq-head-test-target. That fix is
correct, but the location is not: /tmp on this machine is a 3.9 GB tmpfs, and a
Cargo target directory does not fit in it alongside everything else already there.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-24 following the CLAUDE.md recipe verbatim:
  cargo check --workspace          -> succeeded, target dir grew to ~2.2 GB
  cargo nextest run --workspace    -> died partway through:
      rustc-LLVM ERROR: IO failure on output stream: Disk quota exceeded
      error: failed to write to .../rmeta.../full.rmeta: Disk quota exceeded (os error 122)
      /usr/bin/bash: line 1: pwd: write error: Disk quota exceeded
The failure is not confined to Cargo -- once tmpfs is full, unrelated commands in
the same shell start failing on write, which makes it look like something much
stranger than "out of space". That is the real hazard: the symptom does not name
the cause.

Note /tmp also already holds several hundred MB of eseq-related scratch from
earlier work (eseq-aubio-sys-target 159M, dgenlisp-v0.1.1 147M,
eseq-linux.33-release 66M, eseq-head-test 97M), so the headroom is smaller than a
fresh 3.9 GB suggests.

FIX: move the dedicated target directory off tmpfs. Somewhere under $HOME or a
gitignored path inside the repo (e.g. target-head/) is fine -- the requirement
from .39 is only that it is SEPARATE from the working checkout's target dir, not
that it lives in /tmp. Update the recipe in BOTH CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (they are
independent files, not symlinked).

While editing, add the caveat that a --workspace run in a cold dedicated target
directory costs multiple GB and several minutes; the recipe is intended for the
narrowest exact test, and that intent should be explicit rather than implied.

Consider also documenting a cleanup line, since these directories are easy to
forget and each one is 1-2 GB.
acceptance_criteria: The clean-HEAD recipe in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md uses a dedicated target directory that is not on tmpfs; both files carry the same corrected recipe; the recipe states that it is for narrow single-test runs and that a cold workspace run costs multiple GB; a cleanup command is documented
notes: Close-reason clarification (shell ate a backticked fragment): the only difference between the CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md sections is the code-fence language tag -- CLAUDE.md uses bash, AGENTS.md uses sh. That is pre-existing file style, not a content divergence; the recipe text is byte-identical otherwise.
close_reason:
Verified. a5d254bd moved the dedicated target dir from /tmp (3.9 GB tmpfs) to $HOME/.cache/eseq-head-test-target on btrfs; 37cd7bc8 corrected the cost caveat and the stale-worktree bug found while reviewing (eseq-linux.46).

Acceptance checked:
- Not on tmpfs: df confirms /tmp is tmpfs 3.9G, $HOME is btrfs with 178G free. Recipe run verbatim left 8.1 GB in the new location -- more than 2x the entire tmpfs, so the move is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
- Both files identical: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md sections diff clean modulo the sh fence tag (pre-existing file style).
- Narrow-test intent + cost stated: original text implied only --workspace runs were expensive. Measured otherwise -- -E filters execution, not compilation, so one -p sequencer test cold-built in 5m51s and left 8.1 GB. Replaced the estimate with the measurement and named the tmpfs size concretely.
- Cleanup documented: both commands executed successfully; worktree and 8.1 GB target dir removed, git worktree list clean.

End-to-end: recipe run verbatim twice (cold and warm), green both times.

title: 39 patcher tests fail at HEAD: harness exports DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE pointing at a nonexistent stage
description:
39 patcher tests fail at HEAD (6de7a320). Regression introduced by eseq-linux.36's
eseq-side change; the upstream artifact work in .36 is correct and verified.

REPRODUCE (no env, clean shell):
  cargo test -q -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests::
  -> 450 passed; 39 failed

  fatal error: 'dgen_runtime.h' file not found

CAUSE. 6de7a320 added to compile_patch_source_with_dgenlisp (patcher/tests.rs:1868):
    let runtime_include = patcher_test_dgen_toolchain_root(repo_root).join("include");
    ... .env("DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE", runtime_include)
        .arg("--skip-inline-audit")
and patcher_test_dgen_toolchain_root (:1850) resolves:
    ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, else repo_root/crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain

crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain DOES NOT EXIST in this tree -- it is the
gitignored ~147 MB stage that has never been produced for Linux (eseq-linux.30),
and ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT is unset in a normal shell. So the harness now
exports DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE pointing at a nonexistent directory.

WHY THIS IS PARTICULARLY UNFORTUNATE: setting that variable to a bad path
OVERRIDES the executable-relative resolution that eseq-linux.36 just added
upstream. Verified independently -- the published v0.1.1 tar.gz
(sha256 717b5cb6..., matches content/dgenlisp.lock) extracts to a self-contained
tree carrying toolchain/include, toolchain/abi and scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh,
and compiles a patch to .c/.json/.so with NO env vars set, from an unrelated
working directory, glibc floor 2.35. The binary no longer needs the hint; the
hint is what breaks it.

Note the tests currently exec crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-linux-x86_64 (the
old in-place Arch build, sha 53c4cd54...), which is NOT self-sufficient -- which
is presumably why the env var was added. But the path it points at is wrong.
Note also that CLAUDE.md's cheap clean-HEAD recipe exports the SAME nonexistent
path, so it will not rescue this either.

FIX OPTIONS -- prefer the one that removes the special case:
 A. Have the harness use the fetched, self-contained v0.1.1 distribution and set
    NO DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE at all. Cleanest, and it is what eseq-linux.35 is
    building anyway. Coordinate rather than duplicating.
 B. If an override is kept, only export it when the directory actually EXISTS,
    and fail with a clear message naming the missing stage otherwise. Silently
    exporting a bad path is what turned a resolvable situation into 39 red tests.
 C. Do not simply set ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT in developer shells and call it
    fixed -- that reproduces the works-on-my-machine pattern this chain has
    already removed twice.

Keep --skip-inline-audit; that part is right (eseq audits dylibs itself via
lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs).
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests:: passes with NO environment variables set in a clean shell; the harness never exports DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE pointing at a path that does not exist; if a stage override is retained it is applied only when present and produces an actionable error when absent; --skip-inline-audit is retained; the fix is coordinated with eseq-linux.35 rather than duplicating its fetch logic
notes:
FIXED with option A (lock-driven, self-contained distribution; NO DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE).

WHY A, not B: acceptance requires a green suite in a clean shell. Option B (export
the override only when the stage exists) would leave the tests running the vendored
crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-linux-x86_64, sha 53c4cd54..., which is the old
in-place Arch build. It only resolves its headers because /home/alec/code/dgen-audio
was baked into it at build time, so B would be green on this machine and red
everywhere else -- the works-on-my-machine pattern option C warns about. Nothing in
the tree provides a real include dir to point an override at.

CHANGE (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/tests.rs only, +269/-35):
- Removed patcher_test_dgen_toolchain_root and the DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE export.
  The published distribution resolves headers/abi/audit scripts relative to its own
  executable; the hint is what defeated that.
- Removed DGENLISP_TOOL_FILENAME; added DGENLISP_LOCK_TARGET (macos-arm64 /
  linux-x86_64 / None) and a small content/dgenlisp.lock stanza parser.
- patcher_test_install_dgenlisp: resolve the pinned artifact into
  $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/dgenlisp/<version>/ (else <repo>/target/dgenlisp/<version>/),
  guarded by a .dgenlisp-sha256 stamp. Cold cache -> curl the pinned url, verify
  sha256 against the lock as a hard error, extract (tar.gz) or install (executable)
  into a staging dir, chmod +x, then rename into place atomically.
  A tracked format=executable artifact whose sha256 already matches the pin is used
  in place, so macOS keeps using crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-macos-arm64
  (f58b2abc..., which does match the lock) with no network.
- patcher_test_dgenlisp_tool keeps the ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL escape hatch and wraps the
  installer in a OnceLock so the 38 parallel dgen tests install exactly once.
- --skip-inline-audit retained, with a comment pointing at
  crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs.

OVERLAP WITH eseq-linux.35: this installer is deliberately minimal and lives only in
the test harness; a doc comment says so and names .35. .35 should delete it and route
the harness through the product-wide fetcher. No .gitignore change was needed
(target/ is already ignored) and no vendored binary or lock file was touched.

VERIFIED, clean shell (env -i, only HOME/PATH/TERM; no ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT,
DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE or ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL):

  $ cargo test -q -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests::
  test result: FAILED. 488 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 1206 filtered out

All 38 dgen_runtime.h failures are gone. The single remaining failure,
patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x, is pre-existing and
unrelated -- confirmed failing at HEAD 6de7a320 in a detached worktree -- and is
filed as eseq-linux.38.

Also verified: the fetch really runs (target/dgenlisp/dgenlisp-v0.1.1/ holds the
extracted 62 MB tree with DGenLisp, toolchain/include, toolchain/abi and
scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh, stamped 717b5cb6...), and deleting the stamp triggers a
correct re-download and rename over the existing install. rustfmt- and clippy-clean
over the new lines.

NOT COMMITTED, NOT PUSHED (branch carries the 62 MB blob in ed326340, eseq-linux.34).
Also filed eseq-linux.39 for the unsound CLAUDE.md clean-HEAD recipe.
close_reason: Closed

title: Excise the 62 MB DGenLisp blob from unpushed history before the branch is pushed
description:
TIME-SENSITIVE. Verified 2026-08-23: the 62 MB binary blob exists ONLY in local
unpushed commits. Once it is pushed it is permanent for every clone, forever.

  git rev-list --objects origin/eseq-linux | grep -c DGenLisp-linux-x86_64
  -> 0        (not yet on the remote)

  unpushed:  bd97de3d  Resolve DGenLisp compiler per target
             ed326340  build(dgen): vendor per-target compiler binaries   <-- the blob
             995491f7  feat(eseqlisp): add deterministic text capture harness

CONTEXT: the user reversed the tracked-binary decision on 2026-08-23 after seeing
the numbers -- 62 MB compressed per re-vendor (binaries barely compress: 64 MB on
disk -> 62 MB in git), against a .git that is currently 191 MB total, with an
expected update cadence of WEEKLY OR MORE. At that cadence a tracked blob adds
roughly 3 GB per year. Vendoring moves to publish-and-fetch-by-lock; see the
sibling beads.

CONFLICT TO RESOLVE BEFORE ACTING -- READ THIS:
The eseq-linux branch must be pushed for eseq-linux.24 (the macOS glyph capture)
to happen at all; that handoff is 'worker pushes, user pulls on the Mac'. If the
branch is pushed before this bead lands, the 62 MB becomes permanent and this bead
becomes a much uglier shared-history rewrite. So either this lands first, or the
Mac handoff is done from a branch that does not carry ed326340. Do not push
eseq-linux with ed326340 intact.

WORK:
 1. Rewrite the unpushed commits so no DGenLisp binary blob is ever introduced.
    ed326340 is the only commit that adds one. Simplest correct shape: rewrite
    ed326340 to keep its non-binary content (the rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh changes
    and the path/layout intent) and drop both binary files, leaving bd97de3d's
    consumer resolution pointing at fetched, gitignored paths.
 2. This MUST be sequenced with the fetch mechanism. Removing the binaries without
    a way to obtain them leaves the tree broken exactly as it was between .15 and
    .14 -- AppPaths resolving to files that do not exist. Land the fetch bead
    first, or land both together.
 3. Confirm afterwards with:
      git rev-list --objects --all | grep DGenLisp-  # no binary paths
      du -sh .git                                    # should drop well below 191 MB
 4. Keep the macOS binary out too. It is only 4.1 MB, but a split scheme where one
    target is tracked and the other fetched is the asymmetry the user already
    rejected once.

NOTE: git gc / repack may be needed for .git to actually shrink after the rewrite;
the blob lingers in reflog and packs until pruned.
acceptance_criteria: git rev-list --objects --all shows no DGenLisp binary paths; .git size is materially below 191 MB after gc/prune; the working tree still resolves both DGenLisp targets via the fetch mechanism and the previously-failing patcher tests still pass on Linux; ed326340's non-binary content (rebuild script changes) is preserved; nothing was force-pushed over shared history -- the rewrite happened while the commits were still local, or the user explicitly approved a shared rewrite
close_reason: Rewrote the 8 unpushed commits: ed326340 amended to keep only rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh changes + old DGenLisp deletion (now 443a779f); both 62MB linux and 4.2MB macos-arm64 blobs never enter history. Final tree byte-identical to old tip. Reflog expired + gc: .git 181M->150M, zero DGenLisp-<target> objects under --all. Branch fast-forwards from origin/eseq-linux; no shared history touched. Fetch script resolves lock; 489/489 patcher tests pass. Note: pre-existing 4.2MB tools/DGenLisp blobs in already-pushed shared history remain (removing them would require the forbidden shared rewrite).

title: Resolve DGenLisp per target across all consumers of the tool path
description:
Consumer half of the per-target DGenLisp split. eseq-linux.15 produces DGenLisp-macos-arm64 and DGenLisp-linux-x86_64; this bead makes every caller pick the right one. Land them together -- between the two, the old single path crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp is gone.

COMPLETE CONSUMER LIST (grepped 2026-08-23, all of it):

  crates/sequencer/src/app_paths/mod.rs:120  fn dgenlisp_tool() -- the real resolver
    :122  Dev     -> sequencer_dir.join("tools/DGenLisp")
    :123  Release -> contents_macos.join("DGenLisp")   <-- note the macOS-only bundle
                                                             assumption baked into the
                                                             variant name; decide what
                                                             Release means on Linux
    :586  test expects "/ws/crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp"
    :854  test expects sequencer_dir.join("tools/DGenLisp")

  crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/tests.rs:1829
    Hardcodes repo_root.join("crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp") and execs it.
    THIS IS THE AWKWARD ONE. eseqlisp has no sequencer dependency (verified: nothing
    in crates/eseqlisp/Cargo.toml references it) and cannot, since sequencer depends on
    eseqlisp -- so this test CANNOT call AppPaths::dgenlisp_tool(). Pick a shape and
    justify it in the notes: a cfg-selected filename constant duplicated in the test, or
    an env override (e.g. ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL) that the resolver also honours. Prefer the
    env override if anything else will ever need to point at a custom build.
    These 38 tests are the payoff -- they are red on Linux today purely because of this.

  crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dylib_cache.rs:1548, :1592, :1699
    String literal "/tools/DGenLisp" in cache-key fixtures. Check whether the tool path
    feeds a cache key -- if it does, per-target paths change keys and that is fine, but
    confirm it does not silently invalidate or collide across platforms.

RIDER (small, do it while you are here): crates/sequencer/tools/generate_dgenlisp_api.py:10
  hardcodes DEFAULT_DGENLISP_ROOT = /Users/alecresende/code/swift/dgen/Sources/DGenLisp --
  someone else's absolute home directory, and the wrong repo besides (it is dgen-audio now).

WAS: 'Provide a Linux DGenLisp compiler tool'. That framing is obsolete -- the Linux port
already exists and works (see eseq-linux.15 for the measured evidence); nothing needs
porting, only selecting.
acceptance_criteria: No source file references a bare 'tools/DGenLisp' path; AppPaths::dgenlisp_tool() returns the correct per-target binary and its tests at mod.rs:586 and :854 assert the target-specific path; the Release variant's behaviour on Linux is defined rather than inheriting contents_macos; patcher/tests.rs no longer hardcodes the single path and the 38 previously-exec-failing patcher tests pass on Linux; generate_dgenlisp_api.py no longer contains an absolute /Users/ path; 'cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib' on Linux shows 0 'Exec format error' failures
notes: Implemented target-selected DGenLisp filenames for macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 across AppPaths and eseqlisp patcher tests. Chose ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL as the shared custom-build override: AppPaths captures it once in dev mode, while eseqlisp's dependency-independent test helper honors the same variable and otherwise duplicates only the cfg-selected filename. Renamed the Release executable root so Linux release behavior is explicit and resolves its Linux-target binary there. Cache-key coverage confirms differing target tool paths cannot collide. Removed the API generator's machine-specific default; --dgenlisp-root is now required. Validation: cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib ran all 38 DGenLisp-consuming patcher tests without execution failures (suite result 1690 passed, 3 unrelated shared-state/UI failures, 3 ignored). Targeted sequencer tests were blocked before Rust compilation by aubio-sys C99 strncasecmp build failure. Python py_compile/help and git diff --check passed.
close_reason: Implemented per-target DGenLisp resolution across all consumers

title: dgen dylib pipeline: ELF audit, -shared/-fPIC flags, .dylib -> .so
description:
The dgen compile-and-load pipeline assumes Mach-O, arm64, and .dylib.

1) crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs validates every
generated dylib before load:
  :18  use object::read::macho::{LoadCommandVariant, MachHeader}
  :91  MachHeader64::<Endianness>::parse
  :109 checks cputype == CPU_TYPE_ARM64
  :119 checks filetype == MH_DYLIB
  :243 MachOFile64 symbol walk
  :37  hardcodes "/usr/bin/clang"
  :364 test fixtures shell out to /usr/bin/cc with -dynamiclib, -arch arm64,
       -install_name @rpath/{name}.dylib
Needs an ELF sibling. crates/sequencer/Cargo.toml currently enables only the
`macho` feature on the `object` crate - add `elf`. Decide what the Linux
audit actually asserts (ET_DYN, EM_X86_64/EM_AARCH64, DT_NEEDED limited to
libc/libm, no unexpected undefined symbols).

2) Compile flags and naming across lisp_host/dgen/:
  -dynamiclib     -> -shared
  -install_name   -> -soname (or omit)
  -arch arm64     -> drop or map to the host arch
  add -fPIC
  .dylib          -> .so throughout the cache paths
See instrument_compile.rs:373 (dylib_name format), effect_compile.rs:470
(the compile Command), and the dylib_cache module
(lisp_host/dgen/dylib_cache, re-exported at lisp_host/mod.rs:58).

3) There are ~30 dylib_cache.acquire() call sites in app/edit.rs,
app/effects.rs, app/fx_chain.rs - they should not need changes if the naming
is centralized, but verify.

dlopen/dlclose semantics themselves are fine on Linux. Watch for
RTLD_LOCAL/RTLD_GLOBAL differences on hot-swap and for symbol interposition
behaving differently than on macOS two-level namespaces.

Related: the eseq-toolchain epic.
acceptance_criteria: A lisp DSP source compiles to a .so, passes an ELF audit, dlopens, and produces audio on Linux; hot-swap works across reloads; macOS path unchanged
notes:
SCOPE REDUCED 2026-08-23 by the upstream Linux port (dgen-audio linux-c-backend @ 68c6fba).

Item 2 of the description -- the compile flags and .dylib -> .so rename -- is largely handled INSIDE DGenLisp upstream, not in eseq. Verified by running the Linux binary directly:
  DGenLisp compile t.lisp -o out --name X --sample-rate 44100 --voices 12
  -> out/X.c, out/X.json, out/X.SO  (already ELF, already .so, no eseq change involved)
So do not start by rewriting -dynamiclib/-install_name/-arch flags; first check which of those paths eseq still drives itself versus which DGenLisp now owns. The manifest still reports processAbi 'dgen-host-abi-v1', so the ABI constraint in eseq-linux.9 is intact.

Item 1 -- the ELF audit -- is UNCHANGED and is now the bulk of this bead. dgen_audit.rs is still Mach-O-only (MachHeader64::parse at :91, CPU_TYPE_ARM64 at :109, MH_DYLIB at :119, MachOFile64 symbol walk at :243) and crates/sequencer/Cargo.toml still enables only the 'macho' feature on the object crate.

Item 3 -- the ~30 dylib_cache.acquire() call sites -- unchanged, still needs verifying.

Also note this bead cannot be started until the sequencer crate compiles on Linux at all: eseq-linux.16 then eseq-linux.9.
close_reason: Reviewed commit 1149c891; Linux ELF audit, .so cache pipeline, dlopen/audio reload, and targeted cache checks pass.

title: Ungate the primitive IR: MetalPrimitive -> GpuPrimitive, drop macOS cfg
description:
Make the retained-mode display list backend-neutral. This is the single
highest-leverage step in the port and it unblocks nearly everything else.

The types are ALREADY platform-free data - they are just cfg-gated and
named "Metal". In crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/mod.rs:
  :538  WidgetInstance          (#[repr(C)], f32 arrays only)
  :558  WidgetViewport
  :585  MetalRectPrimitive
  :600  MetalQuadPrimitive

  :788  MetalPrimitiveRun

title: Space Echo aborts on Play: clamp(min>max) from zeroed sample-rate state slot
description:
## Crash

Stop transport → Play → hard abort:

```
panicked at core/src/num/f32.rs:1432: min > max, or either was NaN. min = 20.0, max = 0.49
  sequencer::effects::space_echo::space_echo_process (src/effects/space_echo.rs:439)
  bind_and_run_live (audiograph/graph_engine.c:973) → worker_main
panic in a function that cannot unwind → SIGABRT
```

Preceded (same instant) by repeated:
`command failed: ReplayFailed("device scalar descriptor changed while replaying history"); restoring device values also failed: ...`

## Direct cause

`space_echo.rs:318 lowpass_coeffs`:
```rust
let omega = TAU * freq.clamp(20.0, sr * 0.49) / sr.max(1.0);
```
`max = 0.49` ⇒ `sr == 1.0` ⇒ `STATE_SAMPLE_RATE` (state slot 16) held 0 (or ≤1) and the
`.max(1.0)` guard converted it to 1.0. `f32::clamp` panics when `min > max`, and the
process fn is `extern "C"` (nounwind), so the panic aborts the whole app from a worker thread.

## Why slot 16 held a non-sample-rate value (root cause candidate)

Space Echo's descriptor param order stops matching node state slots at index ~15:
slots 0..14 are ENABLED..AGE, slot 15 = BPM, **slot 16 = SAMPLE_RATE (not a param)**, 17..32 =
mod depths, and the descriptor then appends voice-modulator params, mod depths, tension,
spring type, width (effects/mod.rs:3400-3760). So the descriptor index → node param index
mapping lives entirely in `param_node_indices`.

Every param push site falls back **positionally** when that vector is short/empty:
```rust
slot.param_node_indices.get(param_idx).copied().unwrap_or(param_idx as u32)
```
~20 sites: app/effect_params.rs:223,619; app/mod.rs:2247; app/projects.rs:62,4254;
scheduler/params.rs:182,200,252,295,340,468,520; scheduler/process.rs:191,207;
audio/params.rs:222,360,418,522,667; audio/render.rs:179. (synth.rs:749 uses `unwrap_or(0)`.)

A stale/legacy pattern-pool copy of the effect slot has a shorter param list and can carry an
empty `param_node_indices` (project.rs writes `param_node_indices: Vec::new()` for legacy/empty
slots) — the exact condition that also produces the `ReplayFailed("device scalar descriptor
changed while replaying history")` seen in the same log (effects/mod.rs:9145, apply_authoring_values).
With the positional fallback, descriptor param #16 then writes into node param 16 =
`STATE_SAMPLE_RATE` with a knob-scale value (0.0/0.5) → sample rate 0.5 → panic on the next block.

Note the existing instrument-side precedent test:
`app/edit.rs::sampler_range_edit_survives_stale_pattern_pool_descriptor` — same class of stale
pool descriptor, fixed for the instrument slot; effect slots still hit it.

## Fix plan

1. **Stop the abort (RT crash-proofing).** Add one shared helper in `effects/mod.rs`, e.g.
   `fn nyquist_clamp(freq: f32, sr: f32) -> f32` that clamps to `[lo.min(hi), hi]` and treats a
   non-finite / ≤0 sr as 48k, and use it at every `clamp(20.0, sr * 0.4x)` site:
   space_echo.rs:318; spring.rs:237; dimension.rs:148,163; filterbank.rs:496,590,1172,1177,1180;
   phaser_flanger.rs:347,354,369,379; str8_delay.rs:162,181,202; roar.rs:791; tape.rs:225,248.
   Same bug is latent in all of them.
2. **Defensive bypass**: in `space_echo_process` (and siblings that stash sample rate in state),
   if `STATE_SAMPLE_RATE` is not finite or < 1000, treat the node as uninitialised → copy dry
   in/out and return, instead of computing coefficients from garbage.
3. **Kill the positional fallback (real fix).** `param_node_indices` missing/short means the slot
   layout is unknown — falling back to `param_idx` silently writes into unrelated state slots.
   Either skip the push (and log once), or repair the slot from the live descriptor
   (`apply_descriptor`) before any push. Audit all ~20 sites above.
4. **Heal stale pool effect slots on transport start**, mirroring the instrument-slot fix, so
   Play stops emitting `ReplayFailed(...device scalar descriptor changed...)` and skipping the
   device-value restore.
5. **Tests**: (a) `space_echo_process` with `STATE_SAMPLE_RATE = 0` must not panic;
   (b) a pool effect slot with empty `param_node_indices` must not push to node param 16;
   (c) transport start with a stale pool effect-slot descriptor succeeds.

Steps 1+2 are the small, immediately shippable crash fix; 3+4 are the correctness fix.
close_reason: Fixed in 8caccf1b: nyquist_clamp/safe_sample_rate helpers across all effect coefficient sites, Space Echo dry-passthrough on an unusable stored sample rate, positional param_node_indices fallback removed (EffectSlotSnapshot::node_param_idx), restore() no longer zeroes the live layout, and stale pool effect slots heal from the live slot on device-value restore. 3 tests added.

title: S4 alias retirement orphaned late-bound handler strings: C-x p sound palette, seq-grid-mode keymap, cross-module widget names
description: Commit 493f96ed (S4 retire module compatibility aliases) deleted the compat alias rungs, but late-bound strings that resolved through them were not requalified: bind-key 'C-x p' -> 'seq-toggle-sound-palette' (seq-panels.lisp:300) now dispatches to nothing (sound palette no longer opens); mode-bind-key handlers in seq-grid-mode.lisp:81-87 (cursor-left/right, select-all-steps, delete-selected-steps, cursor-toggle, seqv-collapse-all-tracks) resolve through the deleted qualified->flat fallback; plus assorted cross-module manual strings (base-note, step-index, panel widget names) flagged by eseqlisp_migrate_module_aliases --dry-run. Fix: apply the migrate tool to the flagged files and pin the C-x p dispatch with a test.

title: Sound palette modal clobbers current sound when auditioning/choosing sounds
description: Choosing sounds in the sound palette modal is destructive: clicking another sound in the grid to try it soon causes all glyphs to change and look identical — every slot has become the same sound; the original distinct sound is lost. Choosing a sound must never be destructive: it should only change the mapping of which pool sound is bound to the track's pattern/track sound slot. Reproduces nearly every time the palette is used.

title: Patch editor burns CPU every frame: macro-action query re-reads and re-lays-out entire macro library
description:
With an instrument/effect edit session open, reactive_tick.rs:1354 calls active_instrument_editor_macro_action (edit_sessions.rs:529) on EVERY reactive tick, even when nothing changed — the != prev_editor_macro_action check only gates publishing the reactive values, not the computation. Profile shows 6.77s / 59% of a trace spent here while merely playing notes with the patch editor open.

Each call to active_macro_library_action_for_path (eseqlisp patcher/mod.rs:2488):
1. default_defmacro_library_for_write() -> DefmacroLibrary::load_available re-reads every library package from DISK per tick.
2. parse_patch_source_with_library fully tokenizes/parses/projects the patch source.
3. lisp.rs:37-48: for every library package not used in the patch, project_library_macro_patch parses + projects + assign_layout (minimize_crossings, barycenter, coordinates) — i.e. the whole macro library gets graph-laid-out per frame.

All of this only to produce two strings: macro_library_action_for_macro (mod.rs:2772) just checks whether the active macro's origin is Local (save-to-library) or Library (fork).
design:
Fixes, in order of leverage:
1. Gate computation, not publish: fingerprint (session last_valid_source hash, active macro name) and skip the query when unchanged — same pattern as prev_editor_macro_sidebar_fingerprint at reactive_tick.rs:1394.
2. Replace projection-based query with a lightweight one: local defmacro of that name in source -> SaveToLibrary; else library package index has name -> Fork. No Projector, no assign_layout.
3. Cache DefmacroLibrary loads (mtime/event invalidated) so nothing re-reads the library dir per frame.
4. Skip assign_layout when projecting library macros needed only for signature/origin resolution, not display.
acceptance_criteria: Playing notes with the patch editor open shows no per-frame parse/projection/layout or library disk reads in a profile; save-to-library/fork button state still updates correctly when switching active macro or editing source.
close_reason: Closed

title: E7: factory-wide probe validation sweep
description: Compile every curated factory DGen instrument/effect through the embedded path and probe-validate audio. Findings report, not a diff — good workflow fan-out. Completes the initial embedded version. Impl spec slice E7. Precondition: PR #40 (E6) merged.

title: Match Linux engine rate to the active PipeWire graph
description: The running Linux app opens its CPAL/ALSA PipeWire client at 44.1 kHz while the active PipeWire graph and physical sink run at 48 kHz. CPAL default_output_config reports the virtual ALSA client default (44.1 kHz), not PipeWire metadata clock.rate, so the existing “prefer device default” policy still forces realtime resampling. Preserve the internal fixed 512-frame audiograph contract; this issue concerns output sample-rate selection, not graph block size.
design: On Linux, obtain the active PipeWire graph rate through a native PipeWire API when the default ALSA route is PipeWire, validate it against CPAL f32 supported ranges, and fall back cleanly to CPAL device selection for direct ALSA/non-PipeWire systems. Keep platform-neutral config selection pure and unit-testable. Do not shell out to pw-metadata or hardcode 48 kHz as a fake system probe.
acceptance_criteria: 1. On this Linux PipeWire host, a rebuilt app appears in pw-top at the graph clock rate (currently 48,000 Hz) with no sample-rate conversion. 2. The graph still renders exact 512-frame internal blocks even when ALSA callbacks use a different quantum. 3. Unit tests cover a valid PipeWire rate hint, an unsupported hint, and no-PipeWire fallback. 4. A targeted sequencer compile/test passes on Linux.

title: Add modifier-scroll zoom fallback
description: Wayland pinch gestures do not reach the application through winit 0.29. Add an explicit application-level Ctrl+two-finger-scroll fallback that feeds the existing cursor-anchored magnify path while preserving ordinary unmodified scrolling and native TouchpadMagnify support. This is a complementary fallback and does not supersede eseq-gc7.
design: Recognize the modifier at the backend input boundary, where current modifier state and raw MouseWheel delta are both available. Centralize wheel-to-magnify conversion in backend-neutral pointer input code and use it from both wgpu and Metal backends. Do not represent Ctrl+scroll as native pinch and do not close eseq-gc7.
acceptance_criteria: Holding Ctrl while vertically scrolling over a magnifiable widget routes a stable zoom delta through the existing magnify path at the cursor. Unmodified scrolling remains unchanged. Native TouchpadMagnify remains unchanged. Focused Linux-runnable tests cover modifier recognition, delta conversion, and ordinary-scroll preservation.
notes: Implemented centralized Ctrl+vertical-scroll classification and pixel-to-magnify conversion in ui/pointer_input.rs, routed by both wgpu and Metal input backends into the existing cursor-positioned pending_magnify path. Added focused unit coverage. cargo check -p eseqlisp --lib passes. Targeted nextest and cargo-test runs reached compilation/linking but were stopped at the repository's three-minute no-completion budget; no test failure was reported.
close_reason: Implemented Ctrl+trackpad-scroll zoom fallback with shared conversion logic and focused tests; compile check passes.

title: XWayland file-drop workaround breaks Linux fractional scaling
description: Commit 3260d893 / eseq-linux.74 forces the entire winit event loop to X11 to obtain XDND file-drop events. On the native Wayland Hyprland session the monitor scale is 1.6 but the environment has GDK_SCALE=2; forcing XWayland bypasses the previously validated Wayland ScaleFactorChanged path and makes the app render materially larger. Restore native Wayland scaling without sacrificing file import; do not compensate with a hardcoded scale. Determine whether a supported native Wayland DnD path exists (dependency upgrade or proper data-device integration), and keep X11 behavior correct when actually running an X11 session.
acceptance_criteria: On the Hyprland Wayland session, eseq uses the native Wayland backend and receives the compositor's 1.6 scale; the UI returns to its pre-3260d893 physical size. File import remains available through a production-quality native Wayland drop path, or the unsupported capability is reported honestly rather than changing the whole window backend. Native X11 sessions still initialize via X11. Focused tests cover backend selection without pinning cosmetic layout.
notes: Root cause confirmed in 3260d893: forcing X11/XWayland for XDND replaced Hyprland's native 1.6 Wayland scale with the X11-side 2.0 scale. Restored winit native-session backend selection: Wayland sessions use Wayland and actual X11 sessions use X11; tests explicitly select the available backend only to permit off-main-thread event-loop construction. Winit 0.29 has no native Wayland file-drop support, so that capability remains unavailable there rather than compromising the entire window backend. Validation: exact nextest backend-selection test passed; CFLAGS=-D_GNU_SOURCE cargo check -p sequencer --bin metal_seq passed; git diff --check passed. User accepted the native Wayland/X11 behavior and tradeoff.
close_reason: Restored native Wayland/X11 backend selection and validated the scaling regression fix; user accepted the Wayland file-drop limitation.

title: Expanded slider drag: per-write step-history replay + scheduler republish owns the Linux residual
description:
## Why

eseq-z85k.2 measured the post-fix expanded-editor sweep on the x86_64 Linux
workstation (Intel i5-8250U, release, 220x110, seven production panes). With H1
fixed, the drag is 41.5 ms/event at one expanded track and 43.0 ms at three, and
the input dispatch is only ~5 ms of that. The remaining 32.6-34.2 ms is
host-command application: each coalesced drag event dispatches seven
`set-step-param-history` commands, one per crossed slider.

A Linux CPU profile of the post-fix sweep attributes ~60% of UI-thread CPU to
`dispatch_custom_host_command` -> `app::edit::apply_recorded_step_mutation`,
split between `replay_step_patch` / `replay_step_patch_cells` (42-46%) and
`SequencerState::publish_scheduler_track` ->
`SequencerSnapshot::capture_live_track` (33-34%). Every interpolated write
therefore captures the before-cells, mutates, replays the patch, and recaptures
and republishes a complete scheduler track snapshot. On the M1 Max this phase
was ~9 ms and hid inside an already fast frame, which is why it only shows up
in the Linux evidence.

## Scope

Make one coalesced pointer event cost one recorded mutation and one scheduler
republish instead of seven. The likely shape is a batched step-param edit that
records the whole crossed range as a single history entry and publishes the
track once, with the existing per-step UI invalidations unchanged. Gesture
behavior must not change: every crossed step still updates, the cursor still
lands on the last crossed step, the header still reflects it, and undo must
still restore the pre-gesture state.

Do not revive the dead HitGrid, do not add an expanded-view-specific input fast
path, and do not change hit-test semantics. Hit-testing is 7-10% of a ~5 ms
input phase and is not the owner.

## Validation

`tests::project_92_full_layout_expanded_step_slider_drag_end_to_end_perf` in
release, both configurations, before and after, on x86_64 Linux. Record the
host-command median per event alongside the total, and record the resulting
per-event count of `set-step-param-history` dispatches and scheduler
republishes. See the "Linux traces and CPU attribution" section of
UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md for the baseline this must beat.

title: Re-test Filter Table + synth on the Linux workstation for underruns after the rustfft host FFT
description:
Fix-plan step 3 of eseq-linux.78, which needs the device and a listener rather than a test run.

eseq-linux.78 replaced the portable scalar FFT behind the DGen ABI v1 host-services table with rustfft on non-Apple targets and moved the complex multiply-accumulate to Rust with an AVX2+FMA path. Hot-cache micro-benchmarks on the i5-8250U (Surface, x86_64 Linux), 2026-08-26:

  2048-pt forward, shipped table (rustfft + split<->interleaved):  4.99 us
  2048-pt forward, portable C kernel:                             34.1 us
  128x513-bin multiply-accumulate sweep, shipped table:           16.8 us  (was 467 us at the shipping -O2)

What is left: run Filter Table on a synth on the workstation and listen for / log ALSA snd_pcm_recover underruns.

If underruns persist, DSP throughput is no longer the suspect. The remaining ones named in eseq-linux.78 are the eseq-linux.73 adapter's deadline bunching (a spectral hop still lands its whole transform batch in one ~235-frame device callback) and the eseq-sj01 RT violations on the scheduler-snapshot seam (Arc<SequencerSnapshot> dropped on the audio thread, non-priority-inheriting mutex in latest_scheduler_snapshot).

Triage aid shipped with .78: ESEQ_DGEN_PORTABLE_FFT=1 forces every transform back through the portable C kernel, so the two backends can be A/B'd on the same build.
close_reason: tested it on linux and filter table works well now

title: Linux system clipboard backend: replace macOS-only pbcopy/pbpaste shell-outs
description:
The system-clipboard backend shells out to pbcopy/pbpaste, which exist only on macOS, so text-mode and text-input copy/paste can never reach the system clipboard on Linux even once the shortcut layer fires. The implementation is duplicated verbatim in two places:
- crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:9433 (write_system_clipboard / read_system_clipboard on Editor, used by copy-selection-to-clipboard and paste-from-system-clipboard)
- crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/text_input.rs:340 (free functions used by text-input widgets)

Unify these behind one shared clipboard module in eseqlisp, then make it platform-aware. Recommended approach: keep the zero-dependency shell-out style — macOS: pbcopy/pbpaste (unchanged); Linux: wl-copy/wl-paste when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set, falling back to xclip -selection clipboard (write: -in, read: -out) under X11. The primary Linux target is Wayland (Hyprland). Alternative if the shell-out matrix proves messy: the arboard crate (wraps wl-clipboard-rs/x11rb) — acceptable, but it adds a dependency tree and an event-loop-lifetime caveat on Wayland (clipboard contents can vanish when the writing process exits without a paste target holding the offer; wl-copy forks a serving process and avoids this), so justify the switch in the bead notes if taken.

Failure behavior: when no backend tool is available, surface the existing status-line error path with a message naming the missing command (the current code already reports "failed to start pbcopy: ..." — keep that shape, e.g. "failed to start wl-copy: ..."). Do not silently no-op.

Read side must tolerate an empty/absent clipboard without error spam (wl-paste exits nonzero on empty clipboard; treat that as empty string, matching current pbpaste semantics).

Testing: unit-test backend selection (env-driven) with the command names injected/mocked rather than spawning real tools; keep an ignored-by-default integration test that round-trips through the real wl-copy/wl-paste for manual Linux verification. Both call sites (editor buffer and text-input widget) must go through the shared module — grep for remaining pbcopy/pbpaste literals outside it as part of acceptance.

Related but separate: eseq-linux.79 fixes the shortcut layer; together they make text-mode copy/paste work end-to-end on Linux. No hard dependency in either direction.
acceptance_criteria: A single shared clipboard module serves both the editor (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs) and text-input widgets (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/text_input.rs); no pbcopy/pbpaste literals remain outside it. On Linux/Wayland, copying a text selection lands in the system clipboard (verifiable with wl-paste) and pasting text copied from another app inserts it; X11 fallback exists via xclip. Empty clipboard reads return empty without an error report; a missing backend tool produces a status-line error naming the command. macOS behavior is unchanged. Focused nextest tests cover backend selection and empty-read semantics without spawning real clipboard tools.
notes: Implemented shared eseqlisp clipboard module using pbcopy/pbpaste on macOS, wl-copy/wl-paste when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is nonempty, and xclip otherwise on Linux. Command execution is runner-injected for unit tests; Linux empty-selection reads return empty. Verified focused unit/editor tests and a real Wayland round trip with wl-clipboard.
close_reason: Implemented and validated shared cross-platform clipboard backend

title: Linux copy/paste shortcuts: accept Ctrl(+Shift)+C/V where macOS uses Cmd
description:
On Linux, copy/paste shortcuts for steps, arrangement regions, and text-mode selections do not work at all: the handlers gate on the Cmd/Super modifier, which the Wayland compositor typically grabs before the app sees it. Undo/redo already solved this with a per-platform primary modifier (crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:152: SUPER on macOS, CONTROL elsewhere); extend that pattern to the copy/paste family.

Decision (from the user): on Linux, accept BOTH plain Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V AND Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V for copy/paste (and Ctrl[+Shift]+D for arrangement duplicate). Both chords are currently unbound so there is no conflict; plain Ctrl matches the Linux GUI convention and the existing Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Shift matches terminal muscle memory. macOS behavior must not change (Cmd only).

Sites that hardcode SUPER and must move to the shared platform-primary helper:
- Step-grid step copy/paste: crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:1491 (the `key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::SUPER)` block handling Char('c')/Char('v') with step_clipboard).
- Arrangement region copy/paste/duplicate: handle_arrangement_region_shortcut, crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:1129-1149 (Cmd+C/V/D arms).
- Text-mode (editor buffer) clipboard keymap: crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/commands.rs bind_defaults, the (Char('c'), SUPER, "copy-selection-to-clipboard") and (Char('v'), SUPER, "paste-from-clipboard") entries.

Already tolerant, verify only (they use intersects(SUPER | CONTROL) or equivalent): timeline widget copy/paste (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/timeline.rs:3813+), text_input widget clipboard_modifier (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/text_input.rs:336), patcher command-chord passthrough (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/mod.rs:1181+).

Trap to trace first: normalize_command_shortcuts (crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:529) rewrites SUPER+a/c/v to CONTROL+a/c/v at three event_loop call sites (crates/sequencer/src/ui/event_loop.rs:498,514,771). Determine which handlers see the raw key vs the normalized key before touching the matchers — the step/arrangement SUPER checks evidently see raw keys on macOS today, and a careless change could double-handle or dead-code one path. Also ensure accepting Ctrl+Shift does not collide with SHIFT-as-coarse-modifier patterns in the same matchers (e.g. timeline uses SHIFT for coarse steps — copy/paste arms must match before those interpretations).

Note the emacs-style editor bindings (Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V are currently unbound in bind_defaults; Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B are page motion) — plain Ctrl+C/V in text mode is free, but confirm no minibuffer/prompt path binds them.

Text-mode paste will still fail on Linux until the pbcopy/pbpaste backend is replaced (separate bead); this bead is only about the shortcut layer reaching the copy/paste code paths. Step and arrangement clipboards are process-local and will work end-to-end from this bead alone.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux: Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V and Ctrl+Shift+C/Ctrl+Shift+V copy and paste selected steps in the step grid, copy/paste an arrangement region in the Arr tab (and Ctrl[+Shift]+D duplicates it), and dispatch copy-selection-to-clipboard/paste-from-clipboard in text mode. On macOS these remain Cmd-only and existing Cmd behavior is unchanged. A shared platform-primary-modifier helper replaces the hardcoded SUPER checks at the three listed sites (no per-site cfg duplication). Focused Linux-runnable nextest tests cover step copy/paste, arrangement copy/paste/duplicate, and the editor keymap under both Ctrl and Ctrl+Shift, plus a macOS-shaped test proving plain Ctrl does not trigger step copy on macOS.
notes: Implemented shared platform-primary shortcut helpers; Linux Ctrl and Ctrl+Shift copy/paste now reach step-grid, arrangement, and editor handlers, while macOS remains Cmd-based. Removed C/V command normalization so raw platform modifiers reach editor routing. Validated focused eseqlisp editor tests (2 passed), metal_seq input tests (4 passed), and cargo check -p sequencer --lib.
close_reason: Implemented and validated Linux Ctrl(+Shift) copy/paste shortcuts with unchanged Cmd-only macOS routing.

title: Portable dgen FFT is ~16x slower than rustfft; underruns with spectral effects on Linux
description:
Follow-up to eseq-linux.73: with block delivery fixed, Filter Table on a synth
underruns on the Linux workstation (ALSA snd_pcm_recover underrun spam).

Measured 2026-08-26 on the i5-8250U (Surface), benchmarking
audiograph/dgen_fft.c compiled exactly as build.rs ships it (-std=c11 -O2,
no -march, no -ffast-math):

  single 2048-pt transform:  ~125 us   (shipping flags)
  rustfft 6.2, same machine:  ~7.9 us  (release, runtime AVX dispatch)
  -> our FFT is ~16x slower; vDSP on macOS is in rustfft's class.

CMAC (conv-reverb partition sweep, 128x513 bins):
  -O2 (shipping):              467 us
  -O3 -ffast-math (shippable): 115 us   (auto-vectorizes SSE2)
  -O3 -ffast-math -march=native: 63 us  (AVX2)

Workload math: Filter Table spectral does ~8 x 2048-pt transforms per 512-frame
hop => ~1.0 ms of FFT landing in the single block where the hop fires, ~9% of
an 11.6 ms hop budget concentrated in one block. With the eseq-linux.73 adapter
that block must render inside a ~235-frame (~5.3 ms) device callback, on top of
the synth. rustfft-backed callbacks cut it to ~70-80 us incl. split<->interleaved
conversion.

The kernel itself is a scalar radix-2 with strided twiddle reads
(table[j*twiddle_step]) - the stride defeats auto-vectorization entirely:
-O3 -ffast-math does not move the FFT numbers at all (129 us), only the CMAC.

FIX PLAN (in order of value):
1. Back the host-services table's fft_forward/fft_inverse on Linux with rustfft
   wrappers (rustfft 6.2 already a sequencer dependency; eseq-linux.73's
   diagnostic plan step 3 sketched exactly this). Must preserve the vDSP
   conventions documented in dgen_fft.h: unscaled both directions, natural bin
   order, split-complex in-place (wrappers interleave/deinterleave; plan both
   directions per log2_size up front - setup creation may allocate, transforms
   may not; process_with_scratch with preallocated scratch is allocation-free).
   Keep eseq_dgen_portable_* as the reference implementation for tests; the
   existing eseq-linux.9 f64-reference-DFT tests should pass unchanged against
   the rustfft-backed table.
2. Vectorize/refile the CMAC: cheapest is compiling dgen_fft.c at
   -O3 -ffast-math (4x, shippable); better is a runtime-dispatched AVX2 path
   or moving CMAC to Rust with std::simd/manual intrinsics (7x).
3. Re-test Filter Table + synth on the workstation for underruns; if they
   persist, the remaining suspects are the adapter's deadline bunching and the
   eseq-sj01 RT violations (snapshot Arc drop + non-PI mutex on the audio
   thread), not DSP throughput.

Bench source preserved in the session scratchpad (fftbench/bench.c); numbers
above are the durable record.
close_reason:
Fix-plan steps 1 and 2 landed in 2e28291c.

Step 1: off Apple the ABI v1 host-services table is now built in Rust (crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_fft.rs) on rustfft, replacing the scalar radix-2 kernel. All the dgen_fft.h conventions are preserved (unscaled both directions, natural bin order, split-complex in place, true complex product in the MAC). Both directions are planned per log2_size at setup creation together with process_with_scratch scratch, so transforms allocate nothing. Because generated code caches one setup per call site in a static and the audiograph engine runs graph nodes on a worker pool, each setup owns a small CAS-claimed workspace pool and falls back to the portable C kernel when contended rather than blocking the audio thread. Apple keeps vDSP byte-for-byte.

Step 2: the complex multiply-accumulate moved to Rust with an AVX2+FMA specialisation behind is_x86_feature_detected!, rather than changing the C build flags.

Measured on the i5-8250U (Surface, x86_64 Linux) 2026-08-26, hot-cache, release, via the #[ignore]d benchmark test throughput_of_the_shipped_table_against_the_portable_kernel:

  2048-pt forward, shipped table (incl. split<->interleaved conversion):  4.99 us
  2048-pt forward, portable C kernel:                                    34.1 us
  128x513-bin multiply-accumulate sweep, shipped table:                  16.8 us  (467 us at the shipping -O2)

dgen_fft.c stays the reference implementation the numeric tests pin against and is still linked as the fallback; ESEQ_DGEN_PORTABLE_FFT=1 forces every transform through it for A/B triage.

Tests: the eseq-linux.9 f64-reference-DFT suite gained a rustfft_* set driving the new table directly on every platform (so a macOS run still compares both backends against one reference), plus a 32-thread concurrency test covering both the pooled and pool-exhausted paths. cargo nextest run -p sequencer -E 'test(/lisp_host::dgen/)' -> 43 passed, including the real-compiled-effect audit/load/render test.

Step 3 (re-test Filter Table + synth on the workstation for underruns) needs the device and a listener, so it is split out as eseq-linux.82.

title: Spec the bounce path: offline render vs captured realtime pass, tails, determinism
description: Write docs/export-bounce-spec.md. Decide: (a) offline render — drive the existing render path faster than realtime with a virtual clock — vs a first cut that automates the existing session-record path (play from arrangement start, stop at end + tail); (b) how the PDC/latency plan and effect tails (reverb/delay ringout) define the true end of the bounce; (c) determinism — seeded/generative sequencers (graph/neural, processes) must produce the same result in bounce as in playback, or the spec must say they do not; (d) UI entry point and file format defaults. The Wav live-record button stays as-is either way.

title: Export songs: bounce an arrangement to audio
description: Table stakes for a release: a proper 'bounce your arrangement' export. Today the only way to get audio out is the Wav button, which live-records the session in real time — fine as a capture tool, not an export story. Needs: render an arrangement (or a selected range) to a file, ideally offline/faster-than-real-time, with sane defaults (WAV, sample rate/bit depth, output naming). Open architecture questions to settle in a spec first: whether the audio graph can render decoupled from the realtime callback clock, how PDC/latency plans and tail-ringout (reverbs/delays) are honored at the end of the range, and determinism of seeded/generative sequencers between realtime and bounce. First child is that spec.

title: Sample import flow revamp: replace the TUI-like tag/categorize screen with real GUI elements
description: Drag-and-drop is the right gesture and stays. What follows it — the TUI-like categorize/tag interface before import — gets replaced with a flow built from the app's GUI elements/layout. First-session critical: importing your own samples is one of the first things a new user does. Related: file drag-and-drop does not work at all on Linux (separate bug under eseq-linux).

title: v0.1 blocker triage: sort first-session P1s into blocker vs known-issues
description: Decide explicitly, rather than letting the release date decide: eseq-sj01 (audio-thread RT violations — intermittent glitches a musician notices in minutes), eseq-0ij (scheduler load grows monotonically — degrades long sessions), eseq-jo7.21 (project switch leaves stale sequencers — hit immediately by anyone flipping between demo project and their own), eseq-4tl.1 (compiler stack overflow on deeply nested user source). Output: each marked blocker (scheduled before release) or known-issue (listed in release notes).

title: Onboarding surface: user-facing quickstart, keybinding reference, visible version string, feedback channel
description: README is dev-oriented. Ship: a short first-10-minutes quickstart, a keybinding reference, a version string visible in the app (so tester reports are attributable to a build), and a stated place to report bugs (likely GitHub issues). Testers without a feedback channel are wasted testers.

title: First-run demo project: sound within 60 seconds
description: A demo project that loads on first launch, built from the curated instruments and builtin samples. Triple duty: onboarding, showcase, and an implicit smoke test that bundled content resolves under AppPaths::Release (exercises eseq-4tr.1). Depends on the curation and samples beads for its material.

title: Curate 5-10 showcase instruments; define the shipped-content manifest
description: content/instruments has 37 entries; many are dev scratch (testfm1, fakemctest, trynaflutebotfailing, wips, badsubass2). Pick 5-10 efficient, good-sounding synths as the shipped set, and decide what the release bundle includes as an explicit manifest rather than a copy of the dev tree — that manifest decision feeds eseq-4tr.2 (dist/macos/build.sh). Non-shipping content stays in the repo, just not in the artifact.

title: Builtin sample library: source drum-machine samples, settle licensing, wire into shipped kits
description: Ship out-of-the-box samples (drum machine recordings via Alec's friend). Before they bake into a distributed artifact: settle rights explicitly — recordings of a machine's synthesized sounds are generally fine; sample-playback ROM content is murkier, so one clear sentence of agreement up front. Then wire into 1-2 shipped kits (content/kits currently holds conga-kit, Drum-Rack-1, test-drum-rack — the test kit goes). Mind DMG size.

title: v0.1 pre-release prep: curated content, first-run experience, onboarding
description: The non-packaging half of v0.1: what a stranger meets in their first session. Packaging mechanics stay in eseq-4tr; demo-script curation is eseq-mods.17. This epic covers content curation (what ships), first-run experience (sound within 60 seconds), onboarding docs, feedback channel, and the explicit blocker-vs-known-issue triage. Discussed 2026-08-25.

title: Retire the Scripts tab: curate content/scripts into importable modules, delete the seven-name contract
description: Spec: docs/attachable-packages-spec.md rev 2 §4. Curate the 27 dev-era demos in content/scripts/** (part of the v0.1 content pass): keepers gain module headers and move under the factory root at module-shaped paths (already an unprefixed load root — no loader work); the rest are deleted. Add a migrate_factory_content_paths rewrite (project.rs:357) mapping known kept-demo load lines to their (import …) form; plain load keeps working for unknown paths. Then delete the Scripts tab, the script-picker load flow, and the seven eseq.vanilla/script-* contract defs; the contract emitters at ui/edit_sessions.rs:848 and ui/host_commands/scripts.rs:178 migrate with the new-script template (eseq-mods.16).

title: New-script affordance: one command creates a template module in ~/.eseq.d/modules and opens it
description: Spec: docs/attachable-packages-spec.md rev 2 §2. Retarget the existing new-script draft flow (ui/host_commands/scripts.rs, ui/edit_sessions.rs:848): create ~/.eseq.d/modules/<name>.lisp from a template with a module header (default prefix my.<name>) plus commented example, open as a file-backed source tab. Template drops the seven-name eseq.vanilla contract. Leaves the user one (import my.<name>) away from attaching it in *scratch*.

title: Linux baseline + attribution: expanded-editor multi-slider drag
description:
## Why

eseq-z85k.1 checked in the ExpandedStepSliderDrag project-92 probe and generally useful per-event work counters, but its implementing session ran on macOS. The required x86_64 Linux baseline and Linux CPU profile therefore remain unmeasured. This task completes only that host-specific evidence and attribution; it does not implement a performance fix.

## What to do

Run the checked-in release probe from commit 1b1ee16b on the Linux workstation for both its 1-expanded-track and 3-expanded-track configurations. Record median/p95 and the emitted per-event counts for full/subtree reruns, reevaluated roots, relayout reused/full/subtree, interpolation sub-samples, hit tests, and LayoutNode clones. Run with ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI and ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI plus a focused trace filter to identify dirty fields and affected buffers. Capture a CPU profile of the sweep using the profiling facility available on that host; if perf is unavailable, document the exact kernel/tool restriction and use a technically sound in-process or launch-time profiler rather than an attach workaround.

Record machine identity, CPU, memory, OS/kernel, backend, release profile, 220x110 viewport, visible buffers, and machine load conditions. Compare the Linux evidence with the provisional macOS evidence recorded on eseq-z85k.1, but base final ownership and fractions on Linux. Post the written attribution on eseq-z85k and create one fix child per confirmed owner. Explicitly decide H1, H2, H3, and any other observed owner. Do not land a behavior or performance fix in this task.
acceptance_criteria:
- The ExpandedStepSliderDrag probe passes on x86_64 Linux in release mode with at least 5 warmups and 20 measured samples for both 1 and 3 expanded tracks.
- Linux median and p95 are recorded separately with machine identity, backend, viewport, visible buffers, build profile, and load conditions.
- Per-event rerun, relayout, interpolation, hit-test, and LayoutNode-clone counts are recorded for both configurations.
- Focused UI traces directly confirm or refute the hypothesized expanded-track subtree fan-out.
- A Linux CPU profile backs a written cost attribution for H1/H2/H3 or documents an exact profiler restriction and uses a sound alternative.
- The final attribution is posted on eseq-z85k and one child is created per confirmed fix owner.
- No behavior or performance fix is included.
notes:
Completed on the x86_64 Linux workstation (omarchy, Intel i5-8250U, kernel
6.19.8-arch1-3-surface, release, 220x110). The checked-in probe passes on Linux
for both configurations, before (worktree at 1b1ee16b) and after (3260d893),
with 5 warmups and 20 samples each: 1 track 376.826/478.348 -> 41.482/45.255 ms,
3 tracks 457.304/622.519 -> 43.039/53.196 ms. Per-event rerun, relayout,
interpolation, hit-test and LayoutNode-clone counts recorded and identical to
macOS. Focused ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI traces confirm the expanded-track subtree
fan-out (49 velocity-dirty cycles before, 0 after). perf was unavailable at the
start (Arch extra/perf, root required) and perf_event_paranoid=2 limits
unprivileged sampling to user space; with no frame pointers in the release
profile, dwarf unwinding truncated to 1-4 frames, so the call-tree attribution
used an in-process SIGPROF sampler (pprof 0.15, 997 Hz, 1024-frame depth) around
an assertion-free replay of the same gesture. Attribution posted on eseq-z85k:
H1 confirmed and dominant (82%/68% of before UI CPU), H2 refuted (hit-testing
0.8%; clones were a consequence of H1), H3 refuted (no selection work in either
profile), and a new Linux-only owner H4 filed as eseq-z85k.3
(set-step-param-history x7 per event = 79% of the post-fix median). Tables added
to UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md. No behavior or performance fix landed.
close_reason: Linux baseline, focused traces, and CPU attribution recorded; H1 confirmed, H2/H3 refuted, new owner filed as eseq-z85k.3

title: Make fx-panel control subtree inputs track-invariant so same-instrument switches reuse the cached tree
description:
## Problem

The *fx* buffer root re-renders the entire custom-instrument UI on every track
switch (~87 ms for factory:core/drift on the Linux workstation, ~52 controls at
~1.7 ms each). It cannot be avoided today even though the destination panel is
structurally identical: every control already sits in a keyed subtree
(custom-ui-lego-knob-<scope>-<name>, custom-ui-lego-micro-num-*,
custom-ui-lego-micro-option-*, fx-param-row, ...), but the subtree body closes
over the parameter map `p`, and `p` is TRACK-ADDRESSED:

- :value-field is `track-<n>-instrument-param-<idx>-<name>`
  (state_values::shared::instrument_param_value_field)
- :value carries the current numeric value
- :text-value carries the current enum label
- :mod-targets carry per-track :source-value-field names

So the eseq-4kd subtree cache (try_reuse_cached_subtree deep-compares upvalues)
can never hit across a same-instrument switch. Because the tree differs, the
full relayout and the retained rebuild follow.

## Goal

The *fx* panel only ever shows the CURRENT track, so it can address 'the current
track's param N' instead of 'track T's param N'. Make the parameter descriptors
the fx panel hands to control subtrees track-invariant, so that switching
between two tracks with the same instrument produces an identical widget tree
and every control subtree cache-hits.

Sketch:
- add a current-track-relative field family (e.g. fx-instrument-param-<idx>-<name>)
  published alongside the existing per-track fields wherever those are published
  for the current track (state_values::param_fields_and_sync)
- have build_instrument_panel_value emit the invariant name in :value-field and
  in the mod-target depth/source fields
- stop putting value-derived entries (:value, :text-value) in `p` when a bound
  field exists, or bind them too, so the map compares equal across tracks

## Watch out for

p-locks, instrument key locks, mod targets, patch_learn (ui/patch_learn.rs names
these fields directly), the rack-slot panels (state_values/rack_panel.rs), and
the generic fx-param-row grid used by instruments WITHOUT a custom UI, which
reads :text-value for its dropdowns.

## Acceptance

- tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_end_to_end_perf drift medians drop
  materially and the probe's *fx* root rerun ms falls toward zero on a
  same-instrument switch
- the probe's existing correctness assertions still hold: the fx tile binds only
  the destination track, the panel identity is right, and a post-switch param
  edit reaches only the destination instance
- p-lock display, key locks, mod depth editing and the rack panels are covered
  by regressions

## Do NOT retry

Wrapping the whole instrument panel in one keyed subtree keyed by (track,
instrument). Measured under eseq-pgru: it makes things WORSE (fx rerun 126 ms ->
220 ms) because the cache never hits and store_subtree_render_cache deep-clones
every upvalue on each render.

title: UI performance: make selection/track-switch latency interactive on low-end hardware
description:
## Problem

eseq-pgru measured the reported same-instrument track switch on the x86_64 Linux
workstation (i5-8250U, release, production multi-pane layout, checked-in
drift-switch fixture). Baseline was 235.7 ms / 243.3 ms for the two directions.
Three shared VM/UI pathologies were fixed there (namespace-map clone per
reactive-get, filter-based find-first per rendered control, linear global_names
scan per reactive read), taking it to 149.2 / 159.3 ms — about 1.55x, not the
8x the bead asked for.

The remaining ~159 ms does not have one owner. It is roughly:

- ~87 ms   *fx* buffer root rerun (the whole custom-instrument UI re-renders)
- ~38 ms   side-effect layout refresh
- ~14 ms   track-switch state publication
- ~5 ms    epoch resync
- ~7 ms    the other (mostly invisible) buffer roots
- ~4 ms    frame construction + retained primitive refresh

Even a free fx render leaves ~72 ms, so no single change reaches 8x. This epic
collects the independent pieces.

## Goal

Get the same-instrument track switch on the eseq-pgru probe to an interactive
median on the SAME Linux machine, tracked by
tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_end_to_end_perf. Each child bead owns
one architectural layer and carries its own before/after on that probe.

## Reference

UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md, section 'Same-instrument track-switch probe (Linux)',
records the probe, the machine, the phase breakdown, the root cause, and two
dead ends that should not be retried.

title: [bug] All FFT-based effects broken on Linux (Convolution Reverb, Filter Table)
description:
All FFT-based effects are broken on Linux: Convolution Reverb and Filter Table
(both spectral and causal engines). Non-spectral dgen effects and instruments
work, so the break is specific to the spectral path. Exact audible symptom not
yet characterized (silence vs garbage vs dry passthrough) — capture it first.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT (explored 2026-08-25, inspection only, no tests run):

- Compile/load: cached spectral artifacts under .eseq/dgenlisp-cache/ have
  .c + .so + manifest; the conv reverb .so leaves only floorf and memset
  undefined and both are in abi/libsystem-symbols-v1-elf.txt. Spectral dylibs
  compile and pass the audit.
- Silent ABI skip: every generated spectral block guards on
  host->struct_size >= sizeof(DGenHostServicesV1) and skips the op on
  mismatch. The toolchain's dgen_runtime.h and the vendored
  audiograph/dgen_abi_v1.h define byte-identical structs (and a sha256 test
  pins them). Guard cannot fail.
- Compile-time IR prep: the cached partition-ir output
  (.eseq/dgenlisp-cache/ir-prep/*/ir.bin) is sane — finite, ~100% nonzero,
  |max|≈3.4, imag bin 0 = 0 per partition. The DGenLisp tool side works.
- Cross-platform codegen divergence: gh compare 68c6fba...ab969ed (macOS
  v0.1.0 pin vs Linux v0.1.2 pin) touches only DGenToolchainPolicy /
  DGenBinaryAudit / tests. CRenderer is unchanged; the emitted C is the same
  on both platforms.
- Obvious portable-FFT math bugs: audiograph/dgen_fft.c bit-reversal,
  butterflies, strided twiddle reuse, and the MAC all read correct, and the
  eseq-linux.9 unit tests pin all four callbacks to an f64 reference DFT
  (mutation-checked).
- Hop-gate codegen, dgen_simd_compat.h rounding intrinsics
  (vrndnq=roundeven etc.), the x86 optimizer barrier ("+x" constraint), and
  dgen_sanitize_f32x4 all read correct.

So the entire statically-checkable surface is clean, which localizes the bug
to the two things that actually differ per platform at runtime and have never
been validated together — exactly the gap eseq-linux.40 predicted ("a scaling
or bin-ordering error ... would show up as wrong gain or wrong spectrum, not
as a crash"):

H1 — the portable host-services FFT behaves differently from vDSP under the
way generated code actually drives it (one lazily-created static setup per
call site, in-place transforms on state-span memory, forward → 128-partition
complex MAC → inline non-@backend ifft with gain compensation baked against
vDSP's unscaled convention; filter-table's cepstral chain
log → ifft → fold → fft → exp additionally amplifies any FFT error
exponentially). The direct-callback tests can't see a composition-level
divergence.

H2 — the generated spectral C is miscompiled on Linux. CRenderer emits ARM
NEON intrinsics unconditionally; on x86_64 they run through the
dgen_simd_compat.h generic-vector shim, compiled by the hermetic clang-20 ELF
stage at -O3 -ffast-math. Upstream verified the Linux v0.1.2 release only
against toolchain/fixtures/scalar-synth.lisp — no spectral fixture has ever
been compiled AND numerically validated on Linux by anyone. Spectral effects
are the only heavy users of the inline-FFT bit-reversal chains, float-mask
hop gates, and vfmodq under that flag set.

H3 (long shot) — host-side spectral-specific driving on Linux: prewarm
(load_dylib_prewarmed) or init_state_entries seeding interacting badly with
the spectral branch gates, leaving the wet arm permanently gated off.

DIAGNOSTIC ORDER (cheapest discriminator first):

1. Characterize the symptom in-app or via the eseq-linux.40 test battery,
   which is now unblocked (toolchain is staged; dylib pipeline demonstrably
   works on this machine): spectral_effect_renders_finite_nonzero_audio_
   through_host_services, spectral_notch_phaser_depth_changes_signal,
   filter_table_causal probes, conv_reverb default_ir_prepares. Silence
   points at H3/gating; garbage or wrong gain points at H1/H2.
2. Discriminate H1 vs H2 without touching upstream: take one cached spectral
   .c from .eseq/dgenlisp-cache, recompile it with plain gcc at
   -O2 -fno-fast-math against the same headers, dlopen both, feed identical
   input + host table, diff outputs. Outputs differ → H2 (miscompile).
   Outputs agree but are wrong → H1.
3. For H1: swap the Linux table's four callbacks to rustfft-backed wrappers
   (rustfft is already a dependency) and A/B; or capture one real call
   sequence (sizes, buffers) from a session and replay it against vDSP on
   the Mac per eseq-linux.26 rider 5.

Related: eseq-linux.9 (portable FFT, closed), eseq-linux.40 (the deferred
end-to-end validation this bug proves out), eseq-linux.26 rider 5 (vDSP half
of the comparison), eseq-linux.49 (upstream prebuilt toolchain provenance).
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-26): not the FFT. CPAL honors BufferSize::Fixed only as a
hint on ALSA; PipeWire answers the 512-frame request with whatever
snd_pcm_avail_update reports (235 frames on this workstation), and audiograph
rendered that as a 235-frame slice. Generated DGenLisp code emits overlap-add
output only when a hop boundary lands on a process-block boundary, so a
hop-incompatible block silences the wet arm entirely while the dry arm keeps
passing. macOS never hit it: CoreAudio delivers the requested block.

Measured on the cached Convolution Reverb .so (delta IR, 100% wet):
peak 0.25 and 0.000000 error at 128/256/512 frames; peak exactly 0.0 at
235 and 300. The hop counter still fires at 235 (partition pointer advances) —
only the overlap-add read is gated.

H1/H2 both ruled out empirically:
- portable FFT matches an f64 reference DFT to 2.4e-5; unscaled round trip exact
- the cached generated C recompiled at -O0, -O2 and -O3 -ffast-math -march=x86-64-v3
  produces byte-identical output -> no miscompile
- driving the real live-graph node state (real Lexicon IR uploaded through
  GE_WRITE_NODE_STATE, enabled=1, mix cell correct, FTZ/DAZ on, 44.1k and 48k)
  renders a correct growing reverb tail

FIX (commit 1d433612): audio::FixedOutputBlocks renders exact block_size graph
blocks and serves the device out of that scratch. Allocation-free; no added
latency where the device already delivers whole blocks, up to block_size-1
frames on ALSA. Device-size observation moved to the device boundary so the log
still reports the real callback size.

FOLLOW-UP: transport.record_latency_seconds is still block_size/sample_rate.
On ALSA the adapter adds up to one more block of output latency; that default is
documented as user-tunable and was left unchanged deliberately.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
FIX IMPLEMENTED (uncommitted, working tree, branch eseq-linux).

Note first: adding ".SFNS-Regular" to the macOS font preference list is NOT a viable alternative. fontdue parses /System/Library/Fonts/SFNS.ttf but rasterizes every glyph to 0x0 ink (verified at 20px and 24px for H/S/x). Helvetica stays the macOS UI face, so the centering math had to absorb it.

Changes:
- glyph_atlas.rs: new free fn centered_text_baseline_px(cell_h, cap_height_px, scale) = cell_h*0.5 + cap*scale*0.5 — the single definition of where a proportional baseline goes. SizedFontCache gained a per-size cap_height() cache, measured from the rasterized ink of 'H'/'X' (flat-topped capitals; round ones overshoot the cap line) rather than read from OS/2, so it matches the pixels the atlas actually holds including hinting. Falls back to ascent*0.72 for a font that renders neither glyph.
- gpu_scene.rs + metal_backend.rs: both proportional layout caches now carry descent_px and cap_height_px, and both y_offset sites became
      let baseline_px = centered_text_baseline_px(mono_cell_h, layout.cap_height_px, scale);
      let y_offset = baseline_px - (layout.line_height_px - layout.descent_px) * scale;
- widget_render/mod.rs: proportional_text_baseline_offset now derives from the same helper, so baseline-aligned h-stacks track the glyphs they align to.
- TextMeasurer: ascent_px REMOVED (proportional_text_baseline_offset was its only caller and it no longer needs ascent), replaced by cap_height_px with a line_height*0.7 default. Impls updated in metal_backend, wgpu_app, hstack test stub, state_values tests stub.

Measured result, Helvetica at 2x, font-size 10 (em 20px), 'H': ink center was 7.5 vs box center 10.0 (-2.5 device px); now the baseline lands at 17.5 with cap 15.0, putting the ink center at exactly 10.0.

New regression test: ui::glyph_atlas::tests::capitals_center_vertically_in_their_layout_cell — scans the real atlas bitmap for ink rows and asserts H/S/R/1 land within 1.0px of the cell center across 3 sizes x 3 cell heights. Under the old line-box formula it fails at -2.5px.

Test updates: widget_render::hstack::tests::baseline_alignment_uses_rendered_label_and_number_picker_baselines had a second assertion that the two children's ROWS coincide. That was an accident of the stub measurer's rigged ascents (8pt*0.75 and 10pt*0.7 both landed on the same baseline); with cap-band centering two different font sizes centered in one cell legitimately get different baselines. Replaced with a check that the rows are NOT what bottom-edge alignment would give, which is what the test name actually claims.

Validation: cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp --no-fail-fast => 1778/1779 pass. The single failure, lang::sdf_codegen::tests::content_shader_corpus_emits_valid_wgsl, is PRE-EXISTING — verified failing at clean HEAD in a detached worktree, and this change touches no shader or content file. cargo nextest run -p sequencer -E 'test(/text|label|baseline|font|glyph|cap_height|scale/)' => 117/117 pass (includes metal_seq_fx_lisp_lego_text_readout_uses_optical_vertical_center).

Not done, still open: nothing has been committed, and the fix has not been eyeballed in the running app. The silent-macOS-font-fallback follow-up is unaddressed.

comments.text: Visually confirmed in the running app by Alec 2026-08-25: mixer strip-buttons and track-name badges now read as vertically centered. Closing.

title: Transport stop is not RT-safe: audio callback frees the scheduler snapshot
description:
IMPLEMENTED in 6aa57afd (branch eseq-linux). Design steps 1-4 all landed:

1. `crates/sequencer/src/sequencer/state/snapshot_handoff.rs` — new
   `SchedulerSnapshotHandoff`: a bounded lock-free `published` ring
   (crossbeam `ArrayQueue`, capacity 4, publishers supersede the entry the
   reader has not taken so retention stays at one snapshot) and a bounded
   `retired` ring (capacity 64). `refresh(&mut current, &mut version)` is the
   whole realtime side: pop newest, `mem::replace`, retire the outgoing Arc.
   Retire-ring-full falls back to the inline drop and bumps
   `retired_inline_count()` for the instrumentation bead to surface.
2. `audio/callback.rs:78` now calls `refresh` and never touches the published
   `Mutex` — so item 2 (non-blocking read) is satisfied WITHOUT arc-swap; no
   new lock-free-Arc dependency was needed.
3. `publish_transport_only()` in `sequencer_state/publish.rs`; wired into
   `start_playback`/`stop_playback`/`toggle_play`. Falls back to a full
   capture on a track-count disagreement, same guard as
   `publish_scheduler_track`. Shared transport capture factored into
   `capture_transport_snapshot()`.
4. `coalesce_publishes(F)` scope (depth counter + pending flag) wraps the
   whole `SongTransportMode::SongPlayback` stop arm, which was split out into
   `App::song_playback_stop` (and the capture arm into
   `arrangement_capture_stop`) so the closure can own the transition. The
   deferred publish runs after the resync's epoch bumps.
