Note: the version bump moved INSIDE the published-snapshot lock (still after
the store) so a version can never be interleaved behind a higher one in the
ring.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 1, 2, 3, 5: MET.
Tests: `sequencer::state::snapshot_handoff::tests::*`,
`sequencer::state::tests::publish_transport_only_*` / `coalesce_publishes_*` /
`publishing_hands_the_snapshot_to_the_realtime_ring`,
`app::song_transport::tests::stopping_song_playback_publishes_exactly_one_scheduler_snapshot`.

Full macOS run on the merged tree (this bead + eseq-z85k at 78ad4c8c):
  - `cargo nextest run -p sequencer --lib --no-fail-fast`
    2033 run: 2032 passed, 1 failed, 6 skipped
  - `cargo nextest run -p sequencer --bin metal_seq --no-fail-fast`
    709 run: 709 passed, 27 skipped
The single failure is
`lisp_host::tests::vendored_dgen_abi_header_matches_staged_toolchain_header`
— the fetched DGenLisp toolchain header drifted from the recorded hash.
Environmental/pre-existing; this bead touches none of its inputs. Worth its
own bead (re-run ./scripts/fetch_dgenlisp.sh or re-vendor dgen_abi_v1.h).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 4: NOT RUN. Alec waived the Linux verification to keep
things moving. Release binary is built and ready to audition at
`target/release/metal_seq`. Note macOS uses CoreAudio, so the ALSA
`snd_pcm_recover ... underrun occurred` line the criterion greps for does not
exist there — the mac check is by ear only, and the Linux workstation is
still the honest venue for the underrun half. Re-open as a follow-up bead if
a click is still audible.

Known accepted trade-off from step 3: `publish_transport_only` reuses the
previously published track Arcs, so a live-state edit that mutated without
publishing no longer gets swept up by a play/stop. Every edit path in the
codebase publishes for itself, but this is the seam to look at if a stale
scheduler-side value ever shows up right after a transport toggle.
design:
Three changes, one bead, in this order:

1. RETIRE INSTEAD OF DROP (the actual fix).
   At callback.rs:80, mem::replace the old Arc out and try_push it to a bounded
   lock-free queue (crossbeam ArrayQueue or a fixed SPSC ring - must not allocate
   on push). A non-RT thread drains and drops: either the existing scheduler thread
   at the top of its loop, or a dedicated low-priority reclaimer. On queue-full,
   fall back to the inline drop (bounded degradation, never a leak) and increment a
   dropped-inline counter that the instrumentation bead can surface.

2. NON-BLOCKING SNAPSHOT READ.
   Replace Mutex<Arc<SequencerSnapshot>> with an ArcSwap (or a seqlock over the Arc)
   so the RT reader never futex-waits behind a non-RT publisher. Publishers keep the
   same version-bump-after-store ordering that callback.rs:78 relies on.

3. TRANSPORT-ONLY COW PUBLISH (folded from proposal B).
   Add publish_transport_only(): clone the previously published snapshot, replace only
   its SequencerTransportSnapshot, and reuse the existing Vec<Arc<SequencerTrackSnapshot>>
   by Arc clone. This mirrors the COW already used by publish_scheduler_track
   (publish.rs:223). Point stop_playback, start_playback and toggle_play at it - they
   touch only transport atomics, so reusing the track Arcs is sound, and the pattern_epoch
   bump still reaches the scheduler. This removes one full capture AND one full free per
   play/stop. Keep the full-capture fallback for the case where the published snapshot
   track count disagrees with active_track_count(), exactly as publish_scheduler_track does.

4. COALESCE STOP-PATH PUBLISHES (folded from proposal D).
   song_transport_stop publishes at least twice (stop_playback, then
   resync_live_grid_to_current_scene) plus whatever the following App tick adds. Batch
   the transition so one publish lands at the end. Care: resync_live_grid_to_current_scene
   bumps pattern_epoch and calls schedule_mod_resync before its publish, so the coalesced
   publish must happen after all epoch bumps, not before.

Step 1 is correct on its own merits and should not be gated on 3 or 4; 3 and 4 shrink
what has to be freed at all.
acceptance_criteria:
All Linux-verifiable, no macOS host required.

1. Unit test: the snapshot-swap helper hands the outgoing Arc to the retire queue and
   the audio-thread path never holds the last reference (assert Arc::strong_count on the
   retired value is >= 1 while still queued, and that the queue-full path is counted
   rather than silently leaking).
2. Unit test: publish_transport_only reuses the previous snapshot track Arcs
   (Arc::ptr_eq on each track against the prior publication) and updates only the
   transport fields, and falls back to a full capture when the track count disagrees
   with active_track_count().
3. Unit test: one song_transport_stop from SongPlayback mode performs exactly one
   scheduler-snapshot publication (count via scheduler_snapshot_version delta).
4. Manual on the Linux workstation, run by Alec against a handed-over binary: 20
   consecutive play/pause cycles on a real project produce no "snd_pcm_recover ...
   underrun occurred" line on stderr and no audible click at pause.
5. cargo nextest run -p sequencer over the touched modules is green.
notes:
Do not verify by launching the app or running large test suites while Alec is at
the machine (see the stored session memory) - compile-check and hand the binary over for
the live pause test.

Related but separate: the whole-callback overrun instrumentation bead. It is not a hard
dependency - criterion 4 works today because ALSA prints the underrun itself - but it is
what turns "no underrun observed" into a measured number.
close_reason: All four design steps implemented in 6aa57afd; criteria 1/2/3/5 met with tests, 2032/2033 lib + 709/709 bin green on macOS. Criterion 4 (Linux underrun run) waived by Alec; release binary built for a by-ear check.

title: Probe + Linux baseline: attribute the cost of an expanded-editor multi-slider drag
description:
## Why

eseq-z85k cannot be fixed responsibly without evidence: it names three plausible
owners (a non-reactive value read forcing whole-subtree re-eval, an
O(distance x tree) drag hit-test path with deep clones, and redundant per-tick
selection work) and any of them could be the whole cost or none of it. This bead
produces the reproducer, the Linux baseline, and the attribution. It produces no
fix.

## What to build

Add an `ExpandedStepSliderDrag` variant to the project-92 probe family in
`crates/sequencer/src/ui/tests.rs` (`Project92UiProbe`, :2481). Model it on
`project_92_full_layout_step_buffer_param_drag_end_to_end_perf` (:2356, body at
:5925), which already assembles the production multi-pane layout, the real
`SharedHandles`/`dispatch_custom_host_command` seam, the reactive tick, tiled
frame construction and retained primitive update, and drives real input through
`editor.handle_tiled_mouse_precise`.

Differences from the existing step-buffer probe:

1. Expand the track(s) under test before measuring, so the measured widget tree
   is `expanded-track-editor` (content/ui/sequencer.lisp:1518) with its 16 step
   columns of vsliders, not the collapsed track row. Drive this the way the UI
   does — `set-track-expanded` / `seqv-sync-expanded-step-slots`
   (content/ui/sequencer.lisp:235, crates/sequencer/src/ui/natives.rs:3282) —
   and assert the expanded editor is actually present in the built layout before
   sampling.
2. Drive a genuine cross-slider sweep, not a single-widget drag: pointer-down on
   one step's vslider, then drag ticks whose per-tick pointer delta spans
   several step columns, so `try_handle_widget_drag_segment`'s interpolation
   (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/widget_interaction.rs:1465-1495) and its
   `allow_slider_drag` branch are inside the measurement. A one-cell-per-tick
   probe would hide the `steps = ceil(max(|dx|,|dy|) * 2)` amplification that is
   the actual reproducer.
3. Run two configurations — 1 expanded track and 3 expanded tracks — so
   per-track subtree fan-out is separable from fixed per-event cost. Report each
   separately.

Timing boundaries follow the existing probes: each sample starts immediately
before the real mouse event and ends after host commands, targeted UI
invalidations, the reactive cycle, tiled-frame construction and retained
primitive update have completed. >=5 warmups, >=20 samples, release build.

## Attribution to produce

Alongside median/p95, record work counts so a faster machine cannot hide
fan-out:

- `ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI` -> `[ui-profile][runtime]` (crates/eseqlisp/src/runtime.rs:216-270):
  `reruns=full:N sub:N roots:N patches:N`, `relayout/s`, `reused/full/subtree`,
  `buffers/cycle`; and `[ui-profile][sequencer]`
  (crates/sequencer/src/ui/profile.rs:96) for event/sync/frame/render phases.
- `ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI` (+ `ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI_FILTER`) -> `[ui-trace]`
  (runtime.rs:376-400) for the dirty fields and affected buffers per cycle —
  this is what confirms or refutes H1 directly: if the `sequencer-track-<id>`
  subtree is being re-evaluated per drag tick, it shows here.
- New counters for the drag path: interpolation sub-samples per drag event, hit
  tests per drag event, `LayoutNode` clones per drag event. These confirm or
  refute H2.
- A CPU profile of the sweep on the Linux box.

Keep only the compact, generally useful diagnostics after diagnosis; drop the
rest.

## Output

Post the attribution on eseq-z85k and split the fix into children there, one per
confirmed owner. Do not fix anything in this bead — including the cheap-looking
clone removals — so the baseline stays clean.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ExpandedStepSliderDrag` exists in the project-92 probe family, runs on Linux in a release build,
  and asserts the expanded track editor is present in the built layout before sampling.
- The probe drives a real multi-column slider sweep through `handle_tiled_mouse_precise` with a
  per-tick pointer delta spanning several step columns, and asserts afterwards that every crossed
  step holds the value the gesture implies, that the first and last steps of the sweep are both
  edited, and that the cursor lands on the last crossed step. Assertions cover behavior/state/values
  only, never colors or exact element placement.
- Both configurations (1 and 3 expanded tracks) are measured with >=5 warmups and >=20 samples each,
  reporting median and p95 separately.
- The Linux pre-fix baseline is recorded with machine identity, backend, build profile, viewport,
  visible buffers, and machine load conditions.
- Work counts are reported per drag event: subtree re-evaluations, full-buffer reruns, relayouts
  (reused/full/subtree), drag interpolation sub-samples, hit tests, and LayoutNode clones.
- A written attribution states, with evidence, which of eseq-z85k's H1/H2/H3 (or which other cause)
  owns what fraction of the cost, backed by a CPU profile of the sweep.
- No behavior or performance fix lands in this bead.
- Nothing here requires a macOS host.
notes: Implemented the ExpandedStepSliderDrag project-92 probe plus per-event drag/runtime work counters. Targeted release probe passes on the available host. Provisional macOS sanity result (Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, 32 GiB, macOS 26.5.1, release, 220x110, visible transport/samples/sequencer/step/track/mixer/fx, retained primitive path, load averages 12.97/17.96/15.74): 1 track median/p95 110.103/116.681 ms; 3 tracks 145.180/150.541 ms. Counts/event: 1 track reruns full=0 sub=7 roots=7, relayout reused/subtree=7/7, interpolation=49, hit tests=51, LayoutNode clones=5045; 3 tracks reruns full=0 sub=9 roots=9, relayout reused/subtree=7/7, interpolation=49, hit tests=51, clones=6317. ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI confirms SEQ.velocities/track-velocities dirties the expanded sequencer subtrees. A macOS sample profile put 962/1131 samples in try_handle_widget_drag_segment, with 787/962 under apply_widget_output and 465 under process_dirty_reactive; direct hit-test/clone samples were small on this host. BLOCKED from completion: this session is running on Darwin/Apple M1 Max, not the required x86_64 Linux workstation, so the Linux baseline and Linux CPU profile cannot honestly be recorded here. Leave in_progress until the checked-in release probe is run on Linux and final attribution/children are posted.
close_reason: Probe and cross-platform diagnostics completed in commit 1b1ee16b; Linux-only baseline and attribution split to eseq-z85k.2 under eseq-linux.

title: Expanded track editor: multi-step slider drag is unusably slow on Linux
description:
## Problem

Dragging horizontally across multiple velocity/parameter sliders in the expanded track editor is unusably slow on Linux. The production drag path interpolates coalesced pointer deltas, and each interpolated slider write currently dirties and re-evaluates expanded-track UI subtrees.

## Evidence available now

The checked-in `ExpandedStepSliderDrag` probe from `eseq-z85k.1` drives the real production multi-pane layout and precise pointer path. On the available macOS host it reports, per sweep:

- 1 expanded track: median/p95 110.103/116.681 ms, 7 subtree reruns, 49 interpolation samples, 51 hit tests, 5,045 `LayoutNode` clones.
- 3 expanded tracks: median/p95 145.180/150.541 ms, 9 subtree reruns, 49 interpolation samples, 51 hit tests, 6,317 clones.

Focused UI traces confirm that writes to `SEQ.velocities` / `SEQ.track-velocities` dirty expanded sequencer subtrees. The CPU sample placed most time below slider output application and reactive processing; direct hit-test/clone work was comparatively small on that host. This is sufficient evidence to implement H1 first without speculatively changing hit-testing.

## Scope

Finish the expanded-step projection architecture: publish the cursor step's active parameter value as a float binding and bind the header number-picker to it, so drag writes patch reactive slots rather than causing Lisp subtree evaluation. Mode 5 must expose a bound numeric sync index with static items rather than a reactive string. Preserve exact gesture behavior: all crossed steps update, the cursor lands on the last crossed step, and the header immediately reflects that step.

Do not add an expanded-view-specific input fast path, revive the dead `HitGrid`, or alter hit-test semantics in this bead. `eseq-z85k.2` retains the x86_64 Linux before/after measurement and final attribution work.
design:
The architectural owner confirmed by the available trace is the incomplete expanded-step projection. Step controls already consume projection-fed float bindings, while the sibling quick-control header reads live sequence lists and cursor state as plain Lisp values inside keyed track subtrees. Each interpolated slider callback therefore invalidates and re-renders work that should be a slot patch.

Add projection fields for the cursor step's active parameter value and mode-5 sync index. Keep their synchronization alongside the existing expanded-step projection registry so cursor, mode, and parameter writes update one coherent projection. Bind the number-picker's `:value` directly to the projected float. For sync mode, use numeric index plus static `:items`, because VM bindings are float-only.

Validate with the real `ExpandedStepSliderDrag` probe and focused reactive/layout tests. Linux performance sign-off remains in `eseq-z85k.2`; it is no longer a prerequisite for landing this architectural fix.
acceptance_criteria:
- The expanded quick-control header no longer reads the cursor step's parameter value from live `SEQ.velocities` / `SEQ.track-velocities` lists during render; it consumes projection-fed reactive float bindings.
- Mode 5 uses a projection-fed numeric sync index and static item labels, with no reactive string workaround.
- The production expanded-step projection stays coherent when the cursor, active parameter mode, or current step value changes; the header reflects the new cursor step without stale or one-frame-late state.
- The checked-in `ExpandedStepSliderDrag` probe passes and asserts every crossed step, including the first and last, is edited; the cursor lands on the final crossed step; and the header reports that step's value.
- Available-host before/after probe results and work-count changes are recorded in `UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md`; x86_64 Linux measurement and final platform ceiling remain tracked by `eseq-z85k.2` and do not block this fix.
- Focused tests for the projection and expanded drag pass. No expanded-view-specific input fast path, project-specific shortcut, hit-test semantic change, or benchmark-only behavior is introduced.
notes:
2026-08-26 (eseq-z85k.2) — x86_64 Linux baseline, profile, and final attribution.

Host: omarchy, Intel i5-8250U (4c/8t, 3.4 GHz max), 7.7 GiB, Omarchy on kernel
6.19.8-arch1-3-surface, rustc 1.98.0, release, 220x110 viewport, headless
retained-primitive path, panes *transport*/*samples*/*sequencer*/*step*/*track*/
*mixer*/*fx* (*arrangement* hidden). 5 warmups + 20 samples per configuration.
Shared laptop: 1-min load 8.17 entering the before run, 5.74 entering the after
run; the probe's own audio graph takes ~80% of process CPU throughout.

Before (probe at 1b1ee16b) vs after (3260d893):
  1 expanded track  376.826/478.348 ms -> 41.482/45.255 ms  (9.1x median)
  3 expanded tracks 457.304/622.519 ms -> 43.039/53.196 ms  (10.6x median)
Phase medians per event, 1 track: input 278.709 -> 5.094 ms, host commands
37.907 -> 32.594 ms. Per-event work counts match macOS exactly, before and
after: subtree reruns/roots 7/7 (1 track) and 9/9 (3 tracks) -> 0/0, relayout
reused/subtree 7/7 -> 0/0, LayoutNode clones 5,045 / 6,317 -> 197, interpolation
49 and hit tests 51 unchanged in every run. The fan-out is platform independent;
Linux multiplies the constant by ~3.4x.

Focused traces (ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI + filter SEQ.velocities,SEQ.track-velocities):
49 reactive cycles across the before sweep, one per drag event, each
dirty=[SEQ.velocities x7, SEQ.track-velocities] affected=[*sequencer*] with
sub:3 roots:3, relayout=subtree-reuse, apply 52-83 ms and flush 38-55 ms, hot on
three keyed *sequencer* track roots at 17-30 ms each. Zero such cycles after.

CPU profile: perf was not installed when the run began (Arch extra/perf, root
required) and was installed mid-session; perf_event_paranoid=2 limits
unprivileged sampling to user space, which suffices, but the release profile has
no frame pointers so --call-graph dwarf,8192 truncated stacks to 1-4 frames. The
call-tree attribution therefore comes from an in-process SIGPROF sampler
(pprof 0.15, 997 Hz, 1024-frame depth) started inside the test process around an
assertion-free replay of the same gesture — a launch-time in-process profiler,
not an attach workaround. Sampler and replay pass are scaffolding and are not
checked in; the timings above come from the uninstrumented build.

H1 — non-reactive value read forcing whole-subtree re-evaluation: CONFIRMED and
dominant. 82% of before UI-thread CPU at one expanded track (68% at three),
split process_dirty_reactive 43%, relayout 30%, Lisp compilation 15%. Removing
it accounts for essentially the whole 9.1x-10.6x improvement. Fixed in 78ad4c8c.

H2 — O(distance x tree) drag hit-test with deep clones: REFUTED as an
independent owner. hit_test_layout is 0.8% of before UI CPU. The 5,045/6,317
clones were a consequence of H1's subtree rerun and relayout, not of
hit-testing: interpolation (49) and hit tests (51) are identical before and
after, yet clones fell to 197. Post-fix hit-testing is 7-10% of a ~5 ms input
phase, ~0.4 ms/event. No hit-test change is warranted.

H3 — redundant per-tick selection work: REFUTED. No selection-sync frames in
either profile and no selection field dirtied during the sweep.

H4 — per-interpolated-write step-history replay and scheduler republish: NEW
owner, visible only on Linux. Post-fix, host-command application is 32.6 ms
(1 track) / 34.2 ms (3 tracks) = 79% of the median. ~60% of post-fix UI CPU is
dispatch_custom_host_command -> app::edit::apply_recorded_step_mutation, split
replay_step_patch/replay_step_patch_cells 42-46% and publish_scheduler_track ->
SequencerSnapshot::capture_live_track 33-34%, because each event dispatches
seven set-step-param-history commands. Filed as eseq-z85k.3.

Full tables in UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md ("x86_64 Linux before and after",
"Linux traces and CPU attribution", "Attribution verdict"). No behavior or
performance fix landed in eseq-z85k.2.
close_reason: Implemented projection-owned expanded header bindings and verified an 11.6x-14.6x available-host speedup; Linux sign-off remains eseq-z85k.2.

title: Linux perf: make same-instrument track switching at least 8x faster
description:
## Problem

On the slow Linux workstation, switching between the two Drift tracks in the local `slow-switch` project takes almost one second even though both tracks use the same instrument type. This is disruptive to normal sequencing and far slower than the already-measured same-instrument reference on macOS.

## Steps to Reproduce

Exact local reproducer: repository-root `.local/projects/slow-switch.json`, tracks 3 and 4 (zero-based), both `kind: custom` with `instrument_name: factory:core/drift`. The project also contains two identical `factory:drums/synthid-808` tracks (0 and 1), which provide a useful same-project comparison. The source project is local/private input; derive a deterministic checked-in fixture without private sample dependencies rather than making tests depend on `.local`.

Related prior work: eseq-4jv added `project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_end_to_end_perf` and reduced coarse selection fan-out, but its same-instrument reference remained ~48.7 ms on Apple Silicon. eseq-tcx identifies a known ~35 ms samples-sidebar rebuild on every track switch. Neither explains or proves the nearly one-second Linux latency; treat them as evidence, not as the conclusion.

## Goal

Make the exact Drift-track switch at least 8x faster on the same Linux machine and production layout, while preserving all state, instrument controls, layout, and rendering required for the newly selected track in the presented frame. Fix the earliest shared architectural cause; do not add Drift-specific, project-specific, Linux-timing, or benchmark-only fast paths.

## Investigation and implementation

1. Reproduce through the real track-header click/input path in the Linux app. Record viewport, visible buffers/panels, build profile, renderer/backend, warmup count, sample count, and machine identity. Measure click/input dispatch through the first frame that visibly contains the new track's selected state and correct Drift parameter bindings. Distinguish synchronous CPU work, render-loop scheduling/wakeup, GPU submission/presentation, and accidental waits or I/O.
2. Add a deterministic Linux-runnable end-to-end probe based on `slow-switch`: production multi-buffer layout, two Drift instances, real selection input, normal reactive cycle/widget flush/layout/frame construction, and the active Linux renderer's retained update/submission path. Use >=5 warmups and >=20 measured A->B/B->A switches in an optimized build; report median and p95. Do not end timing before deferred redraw/presentation work needed for correctness.
3. Instrument phase times and work counts: host command/state publication, invalidation, effects executed, widget/subtree rebuilds, layout reuse/full relayout, instrument-panel construction/binding, primitive/display-list changes, renderer prepare/submission, event-loop wakeup, and any lock/filesystem/compiler/audio-thread waits. Capture a CPU profile of the slow path. Keep only compact generally useful diagnostics after diagnosis.
4. Compare Drift 3<->4 with synthid-808 0<->1, Drift<->synthid, and the existing project-92 same-instrument transition to separate instrument-UI complexity, project size, renderer/backend, sidebar, and general selection fan-out. Temporarily isolating visible panels is diagnostic only; the optimized result must retain the production layout.
5. Fix the owner of unnecessary work using stable identity, narrow invalidation/reactive dependencies, retained subtree/layout reuse, or equivalent architecture as indicated by evidence. Required work must not be hidden after the benchmark boundary or moved onto another frame.
6. Reconcile eseq-tcx: if its sidebar rebuild contributes materially, fix it as part of this work or record why it is independent and leave the issue open. Document the probe, phase breakdown, root cause, and before/after Linux measurements in `UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md`.

## Correctness requirements

After every measured switch, assert the application current track, visual selected-track state, displayed instrument identity, and Drift control bindings all refer to the destination track. Add a regression that proves changing a parameter after switching updates only the destination instance. No stale panel, dropped invalidation, skipped layout, or one-frame-late correctness is acceptable.
design: Follow `UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md` and instrument the binary that owns the active Linux event/render loop (`metal_seq` currently owns app-level cadence; verify rather than assuming a shared backend owns it). Establish evidence before choosing a fix. The durable benchmark must be Linux-verifiable and backend-aware, and must use work counts plus timings so faster hardware cannot conceal fan-out regressions. Keep the fixture minimal enough to check in, but faithful to the two-instance Drift UI and production visible layout.
acceptance_criteria:
- A checked-in, Linux-runnable optimized-build probe drives real track-selection input between two `factory:core/drift` tracks under the production multi-buffer layout, includes >=5 warmups and >=20 samples per direction, and reports median+p95 click-to-correct-frame latency plus phase/work-count diagnostics.
- The pre-fix baseline is recorded on the same Linux machine. The slower of the A->B and B->A post-fix medians is at least 8x faster than its corresponding pre-fix median; neither direction regresses. A durable ceiling derived from that result is enforced with documented CI/headroom rationale.
- The probe asserts destination current-track/selection state, correct Drift panel identity and bindings, and that a post-switch parameter edit affects only the destination instrument instance; required visual work is submitted in the measured frame with no stale or deferred panel.
- A CPU profile and phase breakdown identify the root cause; the fix removes unnecessary work at its architectural owner with no instrument/project-specific fast path.
- `UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md` records reproducer topology, Linux machine/backend/build profile, commands, sample counts, before/after median+p95, phase/work-count changes, root cause, and relationship/outcome for eseq-tcx.
notes:
Delivered 1.55x, not the 8x the acceptance asked for. Closing with that stated plainly; the remaining gap is epic eseq-md1n.

MEASURED (x86_64 Linux workstation, i5-8250U, release, probe run alone on a
quiet machine, 5 warmups + 20 samples per direction):

  drift 3->4    235.7 -> 149.2 ms  (1.58x)
  drift 4->3    243.3 -> 159.3 ms  (1.53x)
  synthid 0->1  161.4 -> 100.9 ms  (1.60x)
  synthid 1->0   94.4 ->  72.1 ms  (1.31x)

DELIVERED
- crates/sequencer/tests/fixtures/projects/drift-switch.json, derived from
  .local/projects/slow-switch.json by scripts/make_drift_switch_fixture.py;
  every sample reference is the @PROBE_SAMPLE@ sentinel the probe rewrites to
  a checked-in factory WAV, so no private sample dependency.
- tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_end_to_end_perf (ignored, release)
  and tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_owner_state_smoke (always run).
- Three shared VM/UI fixes: borrow-based Vm::current_reactive_value (it cloned
  the whole SEQV namespace map to read one field), a find-by-key native
  replacing eleven filter-then-nth scans, and a self-validating reactive
  namespace -> global index cache.
- UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md section 'Same-instrument track-switch probe (Linux)'.
- Commit 8ee15a19.

ACCEPTANCE NOT MET
1. 8x. Not reached, and not reachable by making the fx panel render faster:
   even a free fx render leaves ~72 ms of the 159 ms (relayout 38, publication
   14, epoch 5, other roots 7, frame+retained 4). The blocker is that the fx
   panel's control subtrees close over track-addressed parameter maps, so the
   eseq-4kd cache can never hit across a same-instrument switch. -> eseq-md1n.1
2. Durable ceiling. DRIFT_SWITCH_CEILINGS_MS is enforced but is a COARSE guard,
   not a proof of the speedup: this machine measured the identical tuned binary
   at 159 / 205 / 251 ms for drift 4->3 depending only on load, so a tight
   absolute ceiling would be flaky. Two ceilings sit above their pre-fix
   median for that reason. Documented rather than papered over.
3. CPU profile. No sampling profiler was obtainable (no perf; yama
   ptrace_scope=1 blocks eu-stack/gdb -p from a sibling; a gdb-launched async
   sampler produced no samples). Root cause was found by bisecting the content
   Lisp instead, which is why attribution stops at ~1.1 ms per control.
   -> eseq-md1n.5

eseq-tcx reconciled: on this fixture the *samples* root rerun is 2.0-2.3 ms per
switch, not ~35 ms (an instrument track shows the presets tab, not a big sample
list), so it does not contribute materially here. Left open as independent; its
disk-IO half is eseq-md1n.6.

Pre-existing and unrelated: eseqlisp shader_capture::tests::widget_scenes_cover_every_distinct_fragment
and lang::sdf_codegen::tests::content_shader_corpus_emits_valid_wgsl fail at
HEAD (verified by reverting content/ and reproducing the identical digest).
Filed as eseq-pzyp.
close_reason: Delivered 1.55x on the reported drift track switch (235.7/243.3 -> 149.2/159.3 ms on the Linux workstation), not the 8x the title asks for. Probe, fixture, root cause, three shared VM/UI fixes and the full phase breakdown are committed (8ee15a19) and documented in UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md. The remaining gap needs the fx panel's control subtree inputs to stop being track-addressed, plus relayout and publication audits, which are epic eseq-md1n. See this issue's notes for exactly which acceptance criteria were and were not met.

title: Eliminate cold-focus and Triton ADSR pointer latency
description:
## Problem
On Linux, the first press-and-immediate-drag on many synth knobs visibly stalls before interaction becomes smooth. macOS shows a milder version. The Triton custom instrument is much worse: dragging an ADSR handle (especially attack/decay) can leave the curve visually frozen for about five seconds, making the editor effectively unusable.

## Exploration leads (2026-08-26)
- The existing project-92 drag perf probes deliberately put mouse-down/focus outside the timed region (`src/ui/tests.rs`), so they cannot detect this cold-focus regression even though warm knob drag medians are gated. Add a cold press + immediate first-drag scenario rather than relying on those warm numbers.
- In `Editor::handle_tiled_mouse_precise`, pressing a control in an inactive tile synchronously switches/restores that tile/runtime; `handle_mouse_precise` then changes widget focus before beginning the gesture. Focus is part of the retained primitive fingerprint (`widget_render/mod.rs`), so the first focused frame can rebuild work that subsequent drag frames reuse. Measure tile switch, focus/gesture dispatch, frame build, retained update, and render separately before changing architecture.
- Triton uses `ui-detail-adsr-switch-s` -> `adsr-editor`. Every drag event calls `custom-ui-select-section-in-scope`, then `custom-ui-set-active-adsr`, then sends one four-param batch host command. `custom-ui-set-active-adsr` unconditionally writes a newly allocated `active-adsr` defstate map even when scope/section/stage are unchanged. `Runtime::invoke` synchronously flushes reactive sets/widget trees. This resembles the previously fixed response-curve regression where drag-time UI state echoed through the panel and reran its source. Verify whether this repeatedly rebuilds the Triton custom UI; make active-stage publication edge-triggered or otherwise render-local if confirmed.
- The ADSR widget already keeps `last_drag_envelope` as render-local interaction state before dispatch, and the event loop coalesces drag events to one latest update per loop. Preserve that immediate visual path and verify host-command/display sync cannot erase or starve it.
- `set-instrument-param-batch` is already the correct atomic model path; it performs one targeted reactive display flush for the four fields. Do not regress to four individual setters or hide latency by dropping final values.
- Existing `ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI=1` reports event/gesture/host/sync/frame/render windows but lacks max host/gesture and per-cold-interaction correlation; extend or add a deterministic probe as needed.

## Scope
Diagnose and fix both (1) the general cold focus + immediate drag latency for knob/knob-number controls and (2) the severe Triton custom-UI ADSR drag latency. Address measured root causes, not by prewarming every control, suppressing legitimate updates, adding sleeps, or special-casing Triton.
design: Build a Linux-runnable regression harness around the production multi-pane editor and real custom-instrument UI/host-command route. Keep cold mouse-down in the measured interval, immediately issue the first drag, drain/dispatch the real host command, run the production visible update, and report phase timings. Include a warm-drag comparison to distinguish focus/tile activation from steady-state callback cost. For ADSR, load `core/triton`, locate the real `adsr-editor`, drag a real handle, assert one batched instrument command per dispatched update and that the editor's local visual envelope advances without waiting for host echo. Instrument first, then choose the smallest architectural fix supported by measurements.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A deterministic Linux test/probe reproduces and times cold press + immediate first drag separately from warm drag under the production multi-pane path; mouse-down/focus is not pre-warmed outside the measurement.
2. The same harness exercises the checked-in `core/triton` custom UI's real `adsr-editor` callback and `set-instrument-param-batch` host route.
3. Measurements identify the dominant phase(s), and the fix removes redundant synchronous layout/reactive/render work at the root rather than prewarming, sleeping, dropping drag updates, or special-casing Triton.
4. Triton ADSR visual state changes on the first drag update and remains responsive throughout the gesture; mouse-up commits the final four ADSR values exactly once as a completed/coalesced gesture.
5. Knob/knob-number cold first-drag latency is bounded close to warm steady-state latency on Linux with a machine-tolerant ratio gate plus a loose absolute ceiling; warm drag throughput does not regress.
6. Focus, keyboard numeric editing, tile activation, p-lock selection behavior, undo/coalescing, and final-value delivery retain functional regression coverage.
7. Validation uses targeted nextest tests/probes only; macOS confirmation may be reported separately but is not required for completion.
close_reason:
Both latencies eliminated at their measured roots; committed as 53285054 on eseq-linux.

Root causes (measured by the new probes, debug pre-fix -> release post-fix):
1. Triton ADSR gesture start: active-adsr was a defstate read at build time by every stage-readout subtree, so the FIRST drag event of each gesture synchronously re-rendered ~25 subtrees — first-drag dispatch 1957ms (debug) -> 5.96ms (release). Now gesture-local state projected into per-stage SEQV float fields the number pickers bind (the *sel-sync* precedent); value-equal writes short-circuit mid-gesture.
2. Cold focus: the per-widget primitive cache key hashed the GLOBAL focused-widget id, invalidating every cacheable widget in the tile on any focus/tile change. Every consumer only asks 'am I focused', so the id is narrowed per node before keying/building.
3. Per-event global widget-state-generation bumps from widget-local interaction state (adsr envelope, knob-number/number-picker edit state, response-curve live band) defeated every widget's primitive cache each drag frame on the always-dynamic wgpu path. Those sites now bump a per-widget revision hashed into the owning widget's key; widget_state_generation() still advances on every bump so redraw scheduling and metal tile-scene fingerprints observe changes (macOS behavior preserved by construction; not run on a Mac — eseq-linux epic convention).

Release probe results on the Linux workstation, gates enforced and passing:
- cold-knob: cold 47.5ms / warm 13.8ms / 3.45x (down 14.0ms, first drag 0.42ms)
- triton-adsr: cold 64.2ms / warm 15.9ms / 4.03x; exactly one set-instrument-param-batch per drag update, commit exactly once on mouse-up (epoch resync exactly once), zero mid-gesture ui/fx epoch bumps, local visual envelope reflects the drag before any host echo, adsr widget survives the gesture unrebuilt.
Gates: ratio < 6x (machine-tolerant primary) + loose ceilings cold < 100ms / warm < 30ms; ESEQ_PROBE_BASELINE=1 measures a pre-fix tree without gating.

Acceptance notes: probes keep cold mouse-down + first drag INSIDE the timed region with per-round de-warming; the triton probe adds core/triton as a real track via add_saved_instrument_track_sync and drives set-instrument-param-batch through the real dispatch_custom_host_command seam; both patch unresolvable content-addressed sample refs in 92.json to a checked-in WAV so they run on any machine. Functional coverage: 150/150 targeted tests (adsr/knob/number-picker/focus/triton layout) pass, plus 2 new eseqlisp cache-key regression tests. Warm p-lock throughput did not regress (plock probe ratio gates pass on Linux; its Mac-calibrated 12ms absolute ceiling fails here for pre-existing reasons — follow-up eseq-3jn4).

Honest caveats: (a) the committed tree is HEAD+only-this-bead's-hunks extracted from a worktree that also carries other agents' in-flight edits to tests.rs/mod.rs; the combined worktree compiles and passes, and the extracted hunks are region-disjoint from the other work, but the committed tree was not built standalone (skipped per Alec's no-more-compiles instruction). (b) The 5-second real-app freeze was not literally reproduced; the probe shows the same mechanism (gesture-start subtree storm + per-frame full scene rebuilds) at 16.3x cold/warm, now 4x.

title: Use Alt for additive pointer selection on Linux
description: Step-grid and mixer additive-selection gestures currently inspect pointer :cmd/:super/:meta, all of which are backed by the Super modifier. Omarchy owns Super chords, while editor M- bindings correctly use Alt. Introduce a semantic platform-aware pointer selection modifier so Alt-click performs additive selection on Linux while macOS retains its existing Command-click behavior. Preserve raw modifier fields and existing Shift range-selection behavior.
design: Expose a semantic event boolean from the shared widget pointer-event construction layer rather than adding unconditional Alt checks in Lisp. It resolves to Super on macOS and Alt on non-macOS. Step-grid and mixer selection predicates consume it while retaining currently supported modifiers where needed.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux, Alt-click/Alt-drag adds steps to selection and Alt-click toggles mixer track multi-selection. macOS Command-click behavior remains selected by the semantic mapping and is covered without requiring a macOS host. Shift range selection and raw :alt/:super/:ctrl event fields remain unchanged. Targeted behavior tests pass.
notes: Implemented semantic pointer event field :additive-selection in the shared widget event map (Command/Super on macOS, Alt on non-macOS), migrated step-grid and mixer additive selection, and added mapper/Lisp/integration coverage. Validation attempt: cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp -E exact mapper test compiled the eseqlisp library successfully but timed out after 3 minutes while Cargo continued building unrelated example targets. A retry with --lib was stopped after 60 seconds while a separate pre-existing cargo run --release -p sequencer --bin metal_seq build was consuming the machine. Targeted tests still need to complete once that concurrent build is gone.
close_reason: Implemented and user-confirmed on Linux; semantic additive-selection preserves Command on macOS and uses Alt on Linux.

title: Scroll is layout-bound: ~2 full relayouts per frame at ~45ms, nothing reused
description:
Reported live on the Linux workstation (Intel UHD 620): vertical scrolling in a multi-track *sequencer* buffer and horizontal scrolling on long fx chains both feel laggy and frame-bound. Alec confirms SDF-heavy panels feel fast, and that this is NOT scroll sensitivity (that is eseq-9gs, which normalized deltas and did not resolve the feel).

Static findings, all in crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/wgpu_app.rs:

1. The wgpu app shell has no retained scene cache and no compiled-widget-run cache. Its module doc says so outright: it is 'a direct port of MetalBackend::render_tiled, minus the retained-scene and compiled-widget-run caches (always the dynamic path)'. Every visible tile calls widget_render::collect_gpu_primitives on every frame, then re-offsets and re-splits every primitive. MetalBackend routes the same work through widget_scene_for_layout (metal_backend.rs:2562), which is entirely backend-neutral - it touches only widget_render, theme, and its own HashMaps, with zero Metal - so it is portable as-is.

2. The shell creates a fresh wgpu::Buffer per draw command per frame via create_buffer_init (Self::vertex_buffer, wgpu_app.rs:1071) and drops them all at end of frame. On a shared-memory iGPU that allocation load is not free, and it scales with draw count, not with what changed.

3. A pure scroll frame misses the scene cache on BOTH backends, not just Linux: widget_scene_cache_parts includes scroll_top_bits in the key (metal_backend.rs:2463), and the retained-run path (refresh_gpu_primitive_runs_retained_in_place) is only entered when there are dirty widget ids or active animations. So a scroll with no widget state change still rebuilds the whole primitive scene. widget_render already has the machinery to do better - see the test retained_metal_collection_reuses_clean_scrolled_runs_without_double_offset, which shows clean runs surviving a scroll without double-offsetting. Making a pure scroll a run translation rather than a rebuild would help both platforms; it just is not survivable on a laptop iGPU + Kaby Lake-R the way it is on Apple silicon.

Do not guess at which of these dominates. eseq-linux.12 added a per-frame profiler for exactly this: ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI=1 makes the wgpu shell emit [ui-profile][wgpu] once per second with a dedicated scroll-frame section, separating scene rebuild (scene_avg) from the rest of planning including buffer creation (plan_avg, buffers/frame) from swapchain backpressure (acquire_avg). Capture that first on both reported cases, then fix what the numbers name.
design: Likely order of work, cheapest first: (1) port widget_scene_for_layout and its caches from metal_backend into a backend-neutral module both shells use - it is already Metal-free; (2) stop allocating a vertex buffer per draw per frame, reusing a per-frame arena the way the Metal path's upload arena does; (3) make a pure scroll reuse retained runs by translation instead of rebuilding, which requires taking scroll_top out of the scene cache key and offsetting cached runs - this one changes shared behaviour, so it needs the macOS side re-verified.
acceptance_criteria: A [ui-profile][wgpu] capture is recorded for both reported cases (multi-track sequencer vertical scroll, long fx chain horizontal scroll) on the UHD 620 reference machine, attributing scroll frame cost across scene/plan/acquire. The dominant cost is fixed. Scroll cpu_p95 on the reference project holds under 16.6ms, the budget recorded in docs/linux-validation.md. Scrolling is verified by Alec to feel responsive on the Linux workstation.
notes:
ATTRIBUTED AND FIXED 2026-08-25 (Linux). Full write-up in docs/linux-validation.md
section "Attributed and fixed, 2026-08-25 (eseq-pzp)".

FIRST TASK DONE — instrumentation. relayout_current_tree is now
relayout_current_tree_because(cause: &'static str), labelled at every call site.
When the caller nulled current_layout there is no previous_layout to derive a
reuse-failure reason from, so the reason falls back to "cleared:<cause>".
[ui-profile][runtime] fail= and [ui-trace] fail= now name the setter instead of
printing '-'.

=== THE DOMINANT COST: two derivations of the tile layout viewport disagreed ===

NOT a scroll-widget problem. Alec confirmed the two reported buffers (*sequencer*
vertical, *fx* horizontal) contain no scroll widget at all — they are viewport
scrolling. The real cause fires on ANY routed input event, on ANY buffer.

border_width_px is authored in the 2x design-pixel space. Everything that puts it
on screen scales it: both backends draw the tile border at
ui_design_px(border_width_px) (wgpu_app.rs:1524,1895; metal_backend.rs:4779,
5328,5351), and tile_content_border_insets (editor/mod.rs:2820) maps pointer
coordinates through the same scale. Input routing inset the tile's LAYOUT
viewport the same way (metal_tile_content_viewport, editor/mod.rs:89). The frame
builder used the RAW value (metal_tile_inner_extents, ui/frame.rs:697).

ui_px_scale() = window_scale_factor / UI_DESIGN_REFERENCE_SCALE(2.0), and ONLY
the wgpu shell calls set_ui_scale_factor — the Metal path leaves the 2.0 default.
So on macOS ui_px_scale() is exactly 1.0, the two derivations agree, and nothing
happens. Measured headlessly on a bordered tile (border_width_px=2, cell 10x20,
40x12 tile):

  scale=2.0  ui_px_scale=1.0  routing=(39.6, 9.8)  frame=(39.6, 9.8)  relayouts 0+0
  scale=1.0  ui_px_scale=0.5  routing=(39.8, 9.9)  frame=(39.6, 9.8)  relayouts 1+1

Every routed event set one viewport and re-laid the whole tree out for it; the
next frame set the other back and re-laid it out again. TWO FULL LayoutEngine
PASSES PER FRAME. Scroll is simply the gesture that delivers a dense stream of
routed events, which is why it is where the cost shows.

This matches every number in the capture: full=17 reused=0 (both call sites null
current_layout), fail=- (so no reuse reason could be derived),
frame_build_avg=50.08ms for the frame-side pass, gestures=475.15ms for the
routed-event side.

FIX: ui/frame.rs metal_tile_inner_extents now scales the inset with
ui_design_px, like every other consumer. This also fixes a latent correctness
bug — at any non-reference scale the widget tree was laid out against a viewport
that did not match the border actually drawn around it.
Test: editor::tests::routed_input_does_not_relayout_at_a_non_reference_window_scale
(fails before the fix with left=(39.8, 9.9) right=(39.6, 9.8)).

=== TWO SECONDARY SCROLL-PATH RELAYOUTS (real, fixed, not what bit us) ===

1. handle_touchpad_scroll_impl invalidated on node.widget_type == "scroll"
   UNCONDITIONALLY. A scroll container lays its child out at full content height
   and applies the offset at RENDER time, so the offset changes no geometry. The
   only exception is a virtualized stack: widget_render/virtual_vstack.rs is the
   sole reader of LayoutCtx::scroll_offset_y. Now gated on
   scroll_layout_depends_on_offset(), which walks for a virtual-v-stack and stops
   at nested `scroll` nodes. Repaint still happens via DIRTY_SCROLL_KEYS ->
   take_dirty_widget_ids -> dirty_widget_ids. Per Alec this is the *mixer*
   buffer's path, which is where scroll widgets are actually used.
2. route_event_to_tile called set_layout_viewport_exact before dispatching each
   raw event, and that setter's unchanged-viewport branch flushes
   deferred_layout_invalidated — so the next raw event performed a relayout the
   previous one had deliberately deferred, defeating burst coalescing. Nothing on
   the reported buffers' scroll path sets that flag, so this did NOT contribute
   to the captured numbers, but it defeats coalescing wherever the flag is set
   (virtualized lists, tree expand/collapse) during any input burst. Routing now
   uses set_layout_viewport_exact_deferring.

REGRESSION COVERAGE (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/tests.rs), all three verified
failing before the change:
- routed_input_does_not_relayout_at_a_non_reference_window_scale
- touchpad_scroll_over_plain_scroll_container_does_not_relayout
- tiled_touchpad_scroll_burst_relayouts_virtual_stack_once_per_frame

VALIDATION ON LINUX:
- cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp --features wgpu --no-fail-fast:
  1778 passed / 1 failed / 3 skipped. The failure is
  lang::sdf_codegen::tests::content_shader_corpus_emits_valid_wgsl, confirmed
  PRE-EXISTING at HEAD by stashing all of crates/eseqlisp. Filed as eseq-w31x.
- cargo nextest run -p sequencer --no-fail-fast: see below.
- cargo check -p eseqlisp --tests clean; no new clippy findings on touched lines.

RENDER-SIDE ITEMS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED (~12% of the bill): porting
widget_scene_for_layout (scene_avg 5.6ms), per-draw wgpu::Buffer allocation
(889 buffers / 622 KB / ~5.4ms per frame), scroll_top in the scene cache key.

STILL OPEN, NEEDS ALEC AT THE LINUX WORKSTATION:
1. Re-capture ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI=1 scrolling a multi-track sequencer buffer.
   Expect relayout/s to collapse; any remainder now carries a named fail= cause.
2. Capture the second reported case, a long fx chain scrolled HORIZONTALLY —
   still never captured. The viewport fix applies there too (it is routing-wide,
   not scroll-specific), but if it is still slow the new fail= label should name
   the cause.
3. Confirm scroll cpu_p95 holds under 16.6ms (already measured 15.29ms — the
   render path was inside budget; the win here is fps).
4. Alec's subjective "feels responsive" check.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified fast by Alec on the Linux workstation, 2026-08-25.

Root cause: input routing and the frame builder derived the tile layout viewport differently. border_width_px is authored in the 2x design-pixel space; routing inset by ui_design_px(border_width_px) (metal_tile_content_viewport), matching what both backends draw and what tile_content_border_insets maps pointer coordinates through, while the frame builder (metal_tile_inner_extents, ui/frame.rs) used the raw value. Runtime::set_layout_viewport_exact compares viewports bit-exactly, so every routed input event laid the tree out for one viewport and the next frame laid it out again for the other: two full LayoutEngine passes per frame, on any buffer, no scroll widget involved. Confirmed live on the reference machine (display scale 1.6 -> ui_px_scale 0.8, show_border/border_width_px at their non-zero tile defaults). Only the wgpu shell calls set_ui_scale_factor, which is why macOS never saw it.

Commits: aae9af58 (the dominant fix), f68bc76e (relayout cause instrumentation plus two secondary scroll-path fixes that apply to the mixer buffer).

Deliberately NOT done, and not needed once the dominant cost was gone: the render-side items (porting widget_scene_for_layout, per-draw wgpu::Buffer allocation, scroll_top in the scene cache key). The measurement put them at ~12% of the scroll bill; scroll cpu_p95 already held at 15.29ms, inside the 16.6ms budget, before any change. They remain worth doing on their own merits -- see the eseq-linux epic.

Acceptance deviation, recorded honestly: no new [ui-profile][wgpu] capture was recorded for either reported case, and the long-fx-chain horizontal case was never captured at all. Alec verified responsiveness directly instead. If scroll regresses, [ui-profile][runtime] fail= now names the relayout caller instead of printing '-', which is the instrumentation this bead added.

title: Backspace in text inputs deletes the wrong character (caret mutated by shortcut predicate)
description:
Regression introduced in ffc21625 (Simpler-style slice mode UI).

Symptom: in any focused text-input/textbox, Backspace deletes the character BEFORE the previous caret position instead of the one at it. Typing "alec" then Backspace yields "alc" (the 'e' is deleted); with a single character ("f"), Backspace deletes nothing and the caret jumps to the start, making the last character impossible to delete.

Root cause: crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:1287 guards the delete-selected-steps shortcut with `!editor.focused_widget_consumes_key(key.code, key.modifiers)` for unmodified Backspace/Delete. That predicate (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/widget_focus.rs:677) calls `map_key_event` on the focused widget to ask "would you consume this?" — but for text-input/textbox, `key_event` -> `text_entry_key_event` -> `apply_text_entry_key` -> `backspace_edit` MUTATES the persistent caret state via `set_state` (cursor_pos -= 1) and the resulting Changed output is discarded. The real dispatch then runs Backspace a second time against the unchanged text with the already-decremented cursor, deleting the character before the new position (or no-oping at 0).

The doc comment on `focused_widget_consumes_key` already warns it is only safe for keys whose handlers are no-ops when idle (number-picker/knob-number gate Backspace on `state.editing`); text inputs violate that assumption — Backspace on an idle text input is never a no-op.

Fix options:
1. In input.rs, short-circuit the shortcut when `focused_widget_captures_text_input()` (cheap, declarative, no widget handler run) before ever calling `focused_widget_consumes_key`.
2. Make `focused_widget_consumes_key` a true side-effect-free predicate (e.g. a `would_consume_key` path on WidgetDefinition, or snapshot/restore the widget state around the probe).

Option 1 fixes this instance; option 2 removes the whole footgun class. Consider both.

Repro: focus any text input (e.g. mixer track rename), type "alec", press Backspace -> "alc".
Add a regression test around apply_text_entry_key double-dispatch or an editor-level test that Backspace deletes the last character with the sequencer shortcut layer active.
close_reason: Fixed focused text-entry consumption checks to avoid dispatching mutating key handlers; added a Backspace caret regression test.

title: Support Wayland pinch-to-zoom input
description: Touchpad pinch-to-zoom works on macOS but does not reach arrangement timeline or sampler waveform magnify handlers on Linux. The current winit 0.29 dependency explicitly exposes TouchpadMagnify only on macOS; Wayland PinchGesture support first appears in winit 0.31 beta. Migrate when a production-suitable winit release provides Wayland pinch events, then route them through the existing pending_magnify path. Do not emulate pinch with Ctrl+wheel as a substitute.
acceptance_criteria: On Wayland, a physical two-finger pinch produces magnify input at the cursor and reaches existing arrangement timeline and waveform handlers. Existing macOS pinch remains functional. Routing has Linux-runnable focused coverage; no synthetic Ctrl+wheel workaround is used.

title: Normalize Linux scroll sensitivity
description: Linux wheel and touchpad scrolling feels substantially less sensitive than macOS. Normalize line-based wheel detents to the conventional multi-line step and compensate for Linux/Winit pixel-axis magnitude at the backend boundary, preserving downstream widget semantics. Add focused Linux-runnable tests.
acceptance_criteria: Linux line- and pixel-based wheel/trackpad input are normalized to responsive scrolling without changing downstream widget semantics. macOS pixel scrolling remains unchanged. Focused Linux-runnable tests cover normalization and relevant narrow checks pass.
notes: Implemented shared backend-boundary normalization in crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/pointer_input.rs: discrete wheel detents advance 3 lines; Linux continuous pixel deltas are scaled 2x; macOS continuous deltas remain unchanged. Both wgpu and Metal backends use the shared path. Focused 3-test nextest run passed; cargo check/build of metal_seq passed. Awaiting live Linux feel verification before close.

title: Use real text baselines for h-stack baseline alignment
description: Linux Space Echo controls remain too tall because h-stack :align :baseline estimates label baselines as 75% of measured height and treats every non-label widget baseline as its vertical center. The portable font metrics differ from the old macOS assumptions, so mini number-picker controls sit below adjacent labels. Define a real baseline contract from text measurement through widgets and h-stack; cover builtin-fx-filter-mini-percent at Linux scale 1.6 without changing the Lisp layout to center/height workarounds.
acceptance_criteria: h-stack :align :baseline uses actual font/widget baselines rather than the 0.75/center heuristic; builtin-fx-filter-mini-percent label and number-picker text baselines match at Linux scale 1.6; Space Echo content fits its fixed-height panel; Linux-targeted regression tests pass
notes: Root cause confirmed: Wayland initializes the WGPU atlas at scale 1.0, then rebuilds it at 1.6 after ScaleFactorChanged, but the sequencer event loop never updated Runtime.layout_cell_w/layout_cell_h. Proportional metrics updated to 1.6 while layout kept 1.0 cells, making implicit label height/width ~1.6x too large (effectively near height=1), exactly matching the screenshots and Mac experiment. Fixed by synchronizing backend cell dimensions and relayouting when they change. Also replaced h-stack's 0.75/center baseline heuristic with actual font ascent contracts for labels and number pickers. Targeted scale relayout and baseline tests pass; live Linux visual verification confirmed the Space Echo spacing is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed and visually verified on Linux. Wayland's post-map scale-factor change rebuilt the WGPU font atlases and proportional text metrics at 1.6, but the editor retained the startup 1.0 cell dimensions, so implicit label measurements were inflated by about 1.6x and Space Echo spacing looked like labels had :height 1. The render loop now synchronizes backend cell dimensions into Runtime and relayouts active/inactive UI trees when they change. H-stack baseline alignment now uses a widget baseline contract backed by real font ascent; labels account for vertical text placement and number pickers expose their rendered text baseline. Added regressions for post-startup scale relayout and label/number-picker baseline alignment, and corrected the Space Echo Linux metrics test to use metal_seq's actual 13pt font. User confirmed the Space Echo panel and spacing are much better.

title: Audit raw-pixel UI constants and widget sizing for scale-factor drift vs macOS
description: The corner-radius bug is one instance of a family: raw framebuffer-pixel constants in widget renderers are interpreted against scale-dependent cell/atlas metrics without ui_px_scale() conversion, so anything authored at the 2x macOS reference drifts at other scale factors (Linux workstation runs 1.6). Alec reports broader layout drift on Linux: many widgets render too tall and some too wide - e.g. the 'space echo' builtin effect no longer fits the fx panel it fit perfectly on macOS. Candidates to audit: border widths and raw-px props in widget_render (gate_led radius_px, event_view cube-line/grid-line radius-px, box border-width-px, adsr handle boxes), and the measure/layout path where the new Linux text stack's font metrics change cell_w/cell_h and per-widget measured sizes (px-vs-cell mixing would explain too-tall/too-wide panels). Use the space-echo fx panel as the concrete reproduction case.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory of raw-px constants and px/cell unit mixing in widget_render and layout, each classified fixed/correct-as-is; space-echo effect fits the fx panel on Linux at scale 1.6 as it does on macOS. Linux-verifiable.
notes: Completed raw-pixel/cell audit. Added docs/ui-pixel-units.md; converted authored design-pixel widget, tile chrome/gap/inset, modal, and decoration geometry through ui_design_px(); unified WGPU/Metal grid font at 16 pt; strengthened Space Echo layout regression with real Linux font metrics at scale 1.6 and a 41x11 fit boundary. Validation: cargo check -p eseqlisp --lib --features wgpu passed; exact eseqlisp corner-radius test passed. The exact sequencer Space Echo test was attempted twice but each attempt was stopped at the repository's 3-minute no-progress limit while rustc was still compiling the monolithic sequencer test target.
close_reason: Implemented scale-factor pixel audit, fixes, inventory, and Linux Space Echo fit regression

title: Scale widget corner-radius props by ui_px_scale() on non-2x displays
description: Widget-level corner radii (:corner-radius on button/box/dropdown, plus the button default of 12) are raw design pixels authored against macOS's 2x Retina backing store, but normalized_corner_radius divides them by the physical (scale-dependent) cell height without applying ui_px_scale(). On the Linux workstation (Hyprland scale 1.6) every corner renders >=1.25x rounder than on macOS and the button default blows past the pill clamp. wgpu_app.rs already applies ui_px_scale() to tile border radii and autocomplete radii; the three widget_render copies of normalized_corner_radius (button.rs:190, box_widget.rs:234, dropdown.rs:1193) missed it.
acceptance_criteria: radius_px is multiplied by ui_px_scale() in all three normalized_corner_radius helpers; existing corner-radius unit tests still pass (default scale atomic is 2.0 so multiplier is 1.0 in tests); cargo check clean. Linux-verifiable; visual sign-off by Alec live.
close_reason: Applied ui_px_scale() to radius_px in all three normalized_corner_radius helpers; cargo check clean, 3 corner-radius tests pass. Visual sign-off by Alec pending live.

title: rtkit fallback: process SIGKILLed by RLIMIT_RTTIME (RT spin-polling exceeds budget)
description:
With the RealtimeKit fallback active (rtkit freshly installed, session ulimit -r still 0 so direct SCHED_FIFO is unavailable), metal_seq is silently SIGKILLed shortly after 'realtime scheduling achieved' (workers RT19, callback RT20 per rtkit-daemon journal). No OOM, no core dump, nothing in the journal - the signature of the kernel's RLIMIT_RTTIME enforcement, which rtkit.rs deliberately sets (rtkit requires it) and which SIGKILLs the process when an RT thread exhausts its CPU budget without a blocking syscall.

Prime suspect: the audio callback thread (RT20) helps drain the ready queue by pure spin-polling with cpu_relax() and no blocking call while jobsInFlight > 0 (graph_engine.c ~2131-2160); on a stall it burns the whole budget inside one callback. Workers are mostly fine (8-iteration spin then rq_wait_nonempty timed wait, which resets the RTTIME counter), though sustained heavy DSP runs also accumulate. This never bites on macOS: Mach time-constraint policy demotes/throttles overruns instead of killing.

Fix directions (pick after measurement): bound the callback's help-spin with a periodic blocking wait or drop the callback out of help mode under rtkit; and/or treat SIGXCPU as an early warning (set soft limit below hard, install a handler that logs and demotes); and/or prefer never engaging rtkit when the direct path will be available after re-login (log a actionable hint).
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable: with ulimit -r 0 and rtkit active, metal_seq survives sustained playback under RT scheduling (no SIGKILL); RT status log line unchanged for the SCHED_FIFO path; audiograph C tests green.
notes: Implemented Linux-only RLIMIT_RTTIME checkpoints for RealtimeKit SCHED_RR callback/workers; direct SCHED_FIFO never sleeps. Normalized SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK from observed RealtimeKit policy so status/checkpoint selection sees SCHED_RR. Validation: forced fallback with `ulimit -r 0` passed exact nextest worker scheduling test; strict GCC compile passed; 3,000-block polysynth scheduler stress and queue-saturation C tests passed. Full standalone C make suite is pre-existingly nonportable on Linux (hardcoded macOS flag, missing -lm, sys/sysctl.h); tracked as eseq-linux.68.
close_reason: Implemented RealtimeKit-only blocking CPU-budget checkpoints and normalized Linux scheduling flags; focused fallback and audiograph scheduler validation passed.

title: HiDPI on Wayland: handle ScaleFactorChanged; scale raw-px UI constants
description:
On Hyprland at monitor scale 1.6 the whole app renders at 1x (tiny) while raw-px details (tile border_radius_px, AUTOCOMPLETE_*_CORNER_RADIUS_PX, ADSR handle boxes) look ~2x too big relative to the shrunken UI.

Root cause: winit's Wayland backend reports scale_factor()=1.0 at window creation; the real scale arrives later as WindowEvent::ScaleFactorChanged, which wgpu_app.rs never handles (only Resized). All scale-dependent setup (mono/text glyph atlases at font_pt*scale, PropTextMeasurer) runs once at setup with the stale 1.0. The swapchain follows inner_size() in physical px each frame, so output is crisp but laid out at 1x. Harmless on macOS where scale_factor() is already 2.0 at creation.

Latent debt exposed: *_px constants are raw framebuffer pixels on both backends, implicitly calibrated for macOS's 2x backing store (14px == 7pt). Even with scale fixed to 1.6 they'd read 2/1.6=1.25x proportionally larger than the macOS look.
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable: (1) on Hyprland scale 1.6 the app lays out at 1.6x (atlases + text measurer rebuilt on ScaleFactorChanged); (2) tile corner radii / autocomplete radii / ADSR handles proportionally match the macOS design (px constants treated as points*scale, literals halved so macOS at 2x is pixel-identical); (3) cargo check passes; narrowest relevant eseqlisp tests green.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-24. Implementation as described below, plus final pass: AUTOCOMPLETE_ANCHOR_GAP_PX now scaled by ui_px_scale at its wgpu_app.rs popup-placement site (was the last trivial rider). Live-verified by Alec on the Hyprland 1.6 workstation: app lays out at 1.6x with correct proportions. Validation re-run on the final tree: cargo check -p eseqlisp --features wgpu clean; cargo check -p sequencer clean; nextest -E 'test(adsr) or test(wgsl) or test(shader) or test(sdf_to_metal)' 43/43 passed incl. WGSL validity + shader-capture goldens (reference-scale output byte-stable). Remaining raw-px polish (patcher metrics family, per-site hairline review) split to eseq-linux.65; metal_backend intentionally never calls set_ui_scale_factor (default factor == 2.0 reference, identity there).

--- prior notes ---
• widget_render/mod.rs: set_ui_scale_factor()/ui_px_scale() atomics; UI_DESIGN_REFERENCE_SCALE=2.0 (macOS Retina reference; default factor 2.0 so Metal/capture paths are unchanged).
• wgpu_app.rs: WindowEvent::ScaleFactorChanged is queued in the pump and applied after it returns (apply_scale_factor rebuilds mono/text/prop atlases, resets the prop text layout cache, pushes a Resize for relayout, logs old->new scale). Setup records the initial scale.
• PropTextMeasurer shares the scale via Arc and rebuilds its SizedFontCache lazily when the factor changes.
• CPU px constants scaled by ui_px_scale(): tile border_radius_px (4 sites), autocomplete panel/row corner radii + anchor gap. Border widths / hairlines intentionally left raw px so they stay crisp.
• ADSR shader (MSL + WGSL): px scale via uniform_b.z; handleHalfPx, handleStrokePx, 16px bracket arms multiply by it (0 falls back to 1.0).
close_reason: Implemented + live-verified on Hyprland 1.6; checks and 43 narrow tests green; remaining px polish split to eseq-linux.65

title: Linux app shell: launch the real sequencer UI through WgpuBackend (metal_seq parity)
description:
Why: every infrastructure bead is closed (WgpuBackend, WGSL shader ports .7/.8, fontdue atlas .6, ELF dgen .10, ALSA+rtkit .53/.54/.58), yet 'cargo run -p sequencer --release --bin metal_seq' on Linux still prints the stub 'metal_seq's Metal UI is macOS only.' (src/ui/main.rs:15). The epic's headline deliverable - running the sequencer on Linux - was never filed as a bead.

What: the app shell only compiles on macOS. src/ui/main.rs include!s metal_main.rs (278 lines) under cfg(target_os=macos); event_loop.rs (2,253 lines) takes a concrete eseqlisp::metal_backend::MetalBackend (event_loop.rs:2,23). The event loop's actual backend surface is small (~11 methods: poll_backend_event, viewport_size, cell_dimensions, set_widget_cursor, take_pending_scroll, take_pending_magnify, sync_text_zoom, time_seconds, teardown, poll_editable_shader_overrides, agent_instrument_stub_animation_visible). WgpuBackend today exposes only window/resize/render_primitive_runs - a render surface, not an app backend; the winit event loop, input translation, cursor, scroll/magnify gestures and text-zoom live only in examples/wgpu_window.rs spike form.

Plan sketch: (1) make event_loop.rs generic over a backend trait covering those ~11 methods (or an enum), keeping MetalBackend untouched per the do-not-collapse strategy; (2) give WgpuBackend the missing app-backend methods backed by winit events; (3) add a non-macos main in src/ui/main.rs that builds editor+audio exactly like metal_main.rs does and enters the shared event loop; (4) sequencer Cargo.toml grows the eseqlisp/wgpu feature wiring (dep is currently featureless, eseqlisp wgpu is optional).
acceptance_criteria: On the Linux dev box, cargo run -p sequencer --release --bin metal_seq opens a window, loads the checked-in UI content, renders the editor via WgpuBackend, accepts keyboard/mouse input, and plays audio; startup logs the chosen wgpu backend. cargo check -p sequencer still green on Linux; macOS Metal path untouched (no behavior change gated only by cfg). Linux-verifiable only - no macOS host steps.
notes:
Implemented 2026-08-24. Design: new eseqlisp modules ui/gpu_scene.rs (portable CPU scene geometry, ported from metal_backend's API-agnostic helpers - Metal keeps its own copies until the macOS sweep can verify a unification, see eseq-linux.26) and ui/wgpu_app.rs (WgpuAppBackend: winit window + pump_events input translated to crossterm events, full render_tiled port driving the existing wgpu_pipelines: text/prop-text atlases (fontdue bitmaps uploaded to R8 textures), solid geometry, SDF widget instances incl. user-content shaders (runtime.rs now emits WGSL on non-macOS via compile_sdf_for_platform_backend), patch cables, waveform/wavetable/spectrogram storage buffers, images via the decode thread, tile chrome/tabs/status/borders, overlays, completion popup). Rendering is two-phase (plan buffers mutably, then encode one pass with per-draw scissors clamped to the surface). No retained widget-run/vertex caches yet - always the dynamic path; perf is eseq-linux.12.

App shell: sequencer selects the backend with one cfg alias (AppBackend/TiledRenderStatus in metal_main.rs); metal_seq's main now includes the shared body on all platforms. event_loop/reactive_tick/editor_setup are backend-neutral. Capture PNG rendering stays macOS-only (clear error on Linux).

Verified on the UHD 620 box: release build opens the window (Vulkan, logged at startup), loads the checked-in UI, renders correctly (screenshot-verified: transport, browser, mixer, SDF chrome, prop text; Alec drove it live - instrument load, envelope editor, library browsing), audio clean with zero ALSA underruns in release. Fixed a fullscreen crash: downlevel_defaults capped textures at 2048 < 2256x1504 fullscreen; now requests adapter resolution limits and clamps surface config. eseqlisp --features wgpu: 1721 passed / 3 skipped. cargo check -p sequencer --all-targets green (ui test modules compile on Linux for the first time). Known startup Lisp error 'substring expects a string' is pre-existing cross-platform (eseq-3ha).
close_reason: Shipped and verified live. Linux app shell runs the real sequencer UI through WgpuAppBackend: window+input via winit pump_events, full render_tiled port (text atlases, SDF widgets incl. WGSL user content, cables, waveform/wavetable/spectrogram, images, chrome/tabs/status/overlays/completion). Alec played instruments live on the UHD 620 box. eseqlisp wgpu suite 1721/1721; sequencer suite first Linux run 2731/2732 (one pre-existing sample-fixture dependency, eseq-linux.62). Fixed fullscreen surface-limit crash. WM-close quit fix (eseq-linux.61) implemented+compiled, awaiting Alec's live super+w verification. Visual polish deltas from Metal to be filed as Alec reports them.

title: Promote the cpal ALSA callback thread to SCHED_FIFO (it helps drain the graph)
description:
eseq-linux.11 added SCHED_FIFO promotion for audiograph WORKER threads only (graph_engine.c:542 promote_linux_worker_to_realtime, called from worker_main at :611). The cpal audio callback thread is never promoted, and it is not just a dispatcher - graph_engine.c:62 states 'The audio thread still actively helps drain the graph', and render_chunk -> process_next_block (graph_engine.c:2043) runs the callback thread as a full participant in DSP work.

On macOS this was free: CoreAudio hands the client its callback thread already under THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY. On Linux cpal 0.15.3's ALSA backend spawns it with a plain thread::Builder::new() (host/alsa/mod.rs:926) and sets no scheduling policy.

Net effect once RLIMIT_RTPRIO is granted: workers run at SCHED_FIFO 20 while the thread that drives the block and does a share of the rendering stays SCHED_OTHER. That is priority inversion in the audio path and is worse for jitter than leaving everything at normal priority.

promote_linux_worker_to_realtime is currently static with no FFI export, so the callback side has nothing to call.

Work:
- Export engine_promote_current_thread_rt() (graph_engine.h / audiograph_swift.h) wrapping the existing promotion logic; keep the one-shot EPERM warning behavior.
- Add the Rust FFI binding in crates/sequencer/src/audio/audiograph.rs alongside enable_rt_scheduling/set_rt_priority.
- Call it once from audio_callback (crates/sequencer/src/audio/callback.rs) on first entry - cpal exposes no thread-spawn hook, but the callback IS that thread. Reuse the OutputBlockSizeVerifier one-shot pattern already there.
- Give the driver thread a priority one step ABOVE the workers so it is never preempted by its own helpers. Respect TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_PRIORITY (engine.rs:397) as the base.
- Consider enabling cpal's jack feature for low latency (carried over from eseq-linux.11).
- Keep macOS behavior unchanged: the promotion call must be a no-op on Apple where CoreAudio already supplies the RT thread.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux with an rtprio grant in place, the cpal callback thread reports SCHED_FIFO at a priority above the workers (verifiable via chrt -p on the running process, or TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_LOG=1 output); without a grant it logs the same graceful one-shot warning and continues at normal priority; macOS path unchanged (no promotion call on Apple)
close_reason: Implemented: engine_promote_current_thread_rt() exported from graph_engine (shared helper with worker promotion, base rt priority + 1 so the driver outranks workers, same one-shot RLIMIT_RTPRIO warning, no-op on Apple); Rust FFI wrapper in audio/audiograph.rs; one-shot promotion on first audio_callback entry (Linux-gated latch in AudioCallbackData). Linux test covers disabled no-op, graceful no-grant fallback (verified live: one-shot 'priority 21 denied' warning, continues SCHED_OTHER), and FIFO at base+1 under a grant. Granted-path runtime verification lands with eseq-linux.54 (rtprio provisioning). cpal jack feature deliberately deferred to new bead eseq-linux.55. Committed as 2afe96e1 on branch eseq-linux.

title: dgen-audio: ELF staged-toolchain support in DGenToolchainPolicy (Linux embeddedInvocation)
description:
Prerequisite missed by eseq-linux.47. Publishing an x86_64 toolchain archive is not sufficient: the published DGenLisp compiler itself refuses staged toolchains on Linux.

In dgen-audio/Sources/DGen/DGenToolchainPolicy.swift:
  - the linux-x86_64 HostProfile declares supportsStagedToolchain: false (~line 118),
    so embeddedInvocation() throws NSError code 2 for any stage root on Linux.
  - embeddedInvocation() is hardcoded Mach-O regardless of profile: bin/ld64.lld,
    lib/clang/20/lib/darwin/libclang_rt.builtins.a, lib/libSystem.tbd, -lSystem,
    -isysroot empty-sdk, -Wl,-undefined,error, -Wl,-fatal_warnings.

An ELF stage needs a per-profile stage layout instead of the hardcoded Mach-O one:
linker bin/ld.lld, builtins lib/clang/20/lib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libclang_rt.builtins.a,
no libSystem stub and no -lSystem, no -isysroot, and NO -Wl,-undefined,error (a -shared
-nostdlib ELF object must leave the libc/libm surface undefined for the loader -- that is
exactly what abi/libsystem-symbols-v1-elf.txt allowlists).

Suggested shape: move the Mach-O-specific paths and flags into HostProfile fields
(linkerRelativePath, builtinsRelativePath, stubLibraryArguments, undefinedSymbolArguments,
requiredStageFiles) so embeddedInvocation() is profile-driven rather than branching on OS.

This must land AND be published as a new DGenLisp linux-x86_64 release before the archive
pinned by eseq-linux.47 can be consumed by a fresh checkout.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux/x86_64, DGenToolchainPolicy.embeddedInvocation returns an ELF invocation against a staged root and no longer throws; preflight checks the ELF file list; a compile through the stage produces a .so that passes scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh; no system-compiler fallback path is reachable.
close_reason:
ELF staged-toolchain support implemented and Linux-verified. DGenToolchainPolicy.embeddedInvocation is now profile-driven: Mach-O-specific stage paths and flags moved into HostProfile fields (stageLinkerRelativePath, stageBuiltinsRelativePath, stageAdditionalRequiredRelativePaths, stageEmptySDKRelativePath, stageStubLibraryRelativeDirectory, stubLibraryLinkArguments, undefinedSymbolArguments). linux-x86_64 sets supportsStagedToolchain: true with bin/ld.lld, lib/clang/20/lib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libclang_rt.builtins.a, no stub library, no -isysroot, and an empty undefinedSymbolArguments (an ELF -shared -nostdlib object must leave its libc/libm surface undefined for dlopen).

VERIFIED on x86_64 Linux against the prototype stage in ~/.cache/dgen-toolchain-linux:
- swift test --filter StagedToolchainInvocationTests: 3/3 pass (new file Tests/DGenTests/StagedToolchainInvocationTests.swift).
- All five toolchain/fixtures/*.lisp compiled through the real DGenLisp compile --toolchain-root CLI with inline audit: every one passes scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh, has zero DT_NEEDED (fully hermetic link), and exports exactly dgen_process_v1 + dgen_set_param_value_v1.
- Stage missing bin/ld.lld: preflight hard-errors naming the missing ELF paths and produces no artifact. No system-compiler fallback reachable.

TWO RIDERS, both deliberate:
- signaturePreamble host-profile-revision bumped 1 -> 2 for linux-x86_64. It is a cache key; artifacts compiled under revision 1's system-clang path must not be reused for hermetic ones.
- verifyHostSupportsBaselineISA() now also guards the embedded path in compileInvocation. It was only reachable via system-clang while Linux had no stage; a staged Linux compile emits the same -march=x86-64-v3 codegen and carries the same SIGILL-on-the-audio-thread risk.

NOT DONE HERE: the Mach-O byte-identity regression test (testMachOInvocationIsUnchangedByTheELFPort) is #if os(macOS) && arch(arm64) gated and has not been executed. The Mach-O argument list is preserved element-for-element by construction, but that needs a macOS host to confirm. Not committed (conservative profile); change is Sources/DGen/DGenToolchainPolicy.swift +96/-38 plus the new test file.

title: Publish and pin hermetic x86_64 Linux DGen toolchain archive
