REVERSED the same day once the numbers were measured:
  Linux binary  64 MB on disk, 62 MB compressed in git (binaries barely compress)
  macOS binary  4.1 MB
  .git total    191 MB -- so one blob was already a third of all history
  cadence       DGenLisp is expected to change WEEKLY OR MORE
  => roughly 3 GB of permanent history per year. Untenable at any binary size.

SETTLED shape: publish per-target artifacts from dgen-audio; eseq commits only
content/dgenlisp.lock (url + sha256 + upstream commit + glibc floor) and fetches
into a gitignored path. Repo growth per update is zero, and a contributor still
needs neither a Swift toolchain nor the dgen-audio checkout -- which was the
property that motivated the original tracked-binary choice.

Rejected alternatives and why:
  stage from a sibling checkout  -- the existing dgen-toolchain pattern, but it
      requires every contributor and CI to have dgen-audio plus Swift, losing
      the zero-setup property.
  keep tracking, shrink first    -- even at a hoped-for 15 MB, weekly updates
      are ~780 MB/year and need periodic history rewrites.
  git LFS                        -- keeps clones small but adds LFS setup for
      every contributor and CI, plus quota, plus a migration rewrite.

Chain: .33 (build old-glibc + publish, upstream) -> .35 (lock + fetch, eseq)
       -> .34 (excise the blob from unpushed history) -> unblocks pushing the
       branch, which .24 needs for the macOS handoff.

STILL TRUE from the first decision, do not undo: the Swift runtime MUST be
statically linked (eseq-linux.15 solved this), and there are two targets, not
one -- static linking never collapses macOS and Linux into a single binary.

title: Implement Vim d$ delete-to-end-of-line motion
description: In the eseqlisp text editor's Vim normal mode, d$ should delete from the cursor through the remainder of the current line, matching the existing standalone $ motion.
acceptance_criteria: In Vim normal mode, pressing d followed by $ deletes from the cursor to end of line through one undoable edit; focused regression tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented the Vim d$ operator (including operator counts) through the normal undo/kill-ring edit path and added focused undo coverage.

title: Add OS clipboard copy and paste in text-only mode
description: Text-only editor mode must support macOS Cmd+C and Cmd+V, including pasting text from the operating-system clipboard and copying the current editor selection.
acceptance_criteria: In text-only mode, Cmd+C copies selected text to the OS clipboard and Cmd+V inserts OS clipboard text through the editor's normal edit path; focused tests cover both shortcuts.
close_reason: Preserved native Cmd-C/Cmd-V through sequencer input normalization so text-only buffers reach the existing OS clipboard commands; added focused regression coverage.

title: [bug] Project switch leaves stale jaki sequencers / def-processes from the previous project
description:
Repro: open project A that defines jaki sequencers / processes (def-sequencer, defprocess/def-process, channels, conductor attachments), then load project B. The Lisp-host process authoring registry (SharedProcessAuthoring in crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/shared_state.rs: defs / instances / channels / patches / conductors / outlet_handles / pending_channel_writes / channel_write_echo) is not reset on project load, so project A's sequencers and process defs are still registered and can still run/schedule under project B.

Expected: loading a project clears all authored process/jaki state that belongs to the outgoing project before evaluating the incoming project's Lisp, the same way pattern/scene state is swapped.

Work:
- Find the project-load path in the UI/event loop and audit which Lisp-host state it resets today.
- Add a reset for SharedProcessAuthoring (and any downstream published snapshot / scheduler-visible process chain state) on project switch.
- Decide what happens to package-level (non-project) def-sequencers loaded from content/ — those presumably should survive the swap; only project-authored ones should be cleared. May need a provenance tag on ProcessDef/instances.
- Test: load project A with a jaki sequencer, switch to project B, assert the authoring snapshot contains none of A's defs/instances/channels.

title: Loud tick errors: notice on first per-generator failure, park until source changes
description: lookahead.rs tick eval currently unwrap_or(empty) — errors are discarded 16x/bar. Report the first failure per generator through a bounded notice channel (push_notice pattern, song_runtime.rs:319) and park the generator (skip ticking) until its body/requires change. Applies to all published sequencers regardless of the requires work.
close_reason: Closed

title: defscene declarations cross via a published table (was: two-arg __defscene-resolve)
description: IMPLEMENTED as a published declaration table instead of a two-arg resolve: the defscene default is an arbitrary runtime expression, so the compiler cannot embed its value into the shipped read. __defscene-register now also publishes (name -> ProcessLiteral) into SequencerState::published_scene_slot_declarations; __defscene-resolve and __defscene-set fall back to that table on a local-table miss. Slot values still cross via SharedSceneSlotSnapshot. Removal staleness: a defscene deleted from the authoring file leaves its published declaration behind until restart (acceptable; declarations are defaults only).
close_reason: Closed

title: requires seam: PublishedSequencer carries module names; scheduler loads them before tick compile
description: Add requires: Vec<String> (validated module names) to PublishedSequencer and its serialization. register_published_sequencer loads each named module through the runtime's module system (the scheduler runtime already has set_scoped_module_load_path, shared_state.rs:411) BEFORE compiling the tick lambda; a module that fails to load fails registration with the module name in the error. def-sequencer accepts :requires (list of module-name symbols/strings) and publishes it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Published sequencer program record: def-sequencer works from UI-runtime (file-backed) buffers
description: def-sequencer published from a file-backed buffer ships only its :tick source; the scheduler VM is built from *scratch* + builtin libraries, so any tick that references a package (alez.jaki.core), file-local helper, or defscene declaration silently fails every tick (lookahead unwrap_or(empty)). Fix by making the published record self-contained DATA instead of shipping file source: (a) requires: module names loaded into the scheduler runtime via the already-wired module load path before tick compile, (b) defscene reads carry their own default across the seam, (c) publish-time free-symbol verification that fails loudly, (d) tick errors surfaced via notice + generator parked. Jaki already ships figures as quoted data, so it only needs alez.jaki.core in requires. Repro + diagnosis: scheduler runtime = build_scheduler_scratch_runtime (lookahead.rs:77) + register_published_sequencer (shared_state.rs:947); module load path already present in scheduler VM (shared_state.rs:411); defscene declaration table is per-VM (sequencer_natives.rs:74) while slot VALUES already cross via SharedSceneSlotSnapshot.

title: Editor autocomplete for (import …): complete package and module names
description:
Typing an import in the ESeqLisp editor gives no completion today. `(import alez.j` should
pop the completion list with `alez.jaki.surface`, `alez.jaki.core`, and every other module
under packages that are actually installed. Every installed package name and every module
inside it should be completable, at any dotted depth.

Scope:
- Complete the module-name argument of `(import NAME …)`.
- Candidates = installed package names + every module reachable under their roots
  (and the factory/user module roots), spelled as dotted module names.
- Progressive dotted prefixes work: `a` -> `alez…`, `alez.j` -> `alez.jaki.core`,
  `alez.jaki.` -> the modules beneath it.
design:
Existing seams:

- crates/eseqlisp/src/mode.rs:226 `completion_match` is the dispatcher. It already
  branches on the prefix (`:` -> `contextual_keyword_candidates`, else
  `completion_candidates`). Add a third branch: when the cursor sits in the module-name
  position of a `(import …)` form, return module candidates instead of runtime symbols.
  Detect that the same way `contextual_keyword_candidates` finds its enclosing form
  (walk back to the open paren, check the head symbol is `import` and the cursor is in
  argument 1).
- crates/eseqlisp/src/mode.rs:763 `symbol_prefix` already treats `.` as a symbol byte
  (is_symbol_byte only excludes delimiters/whitespace), so `alez.j` comes through as one
  prefix and the existing `starts_with(prefix_lower)` filter does the right thing. Verify
  rather than assume.
- Candidate source: `crate::package::PackageCatalog` — `packages()` gives installed
  package names, `module_roots()` gives (path, module_prefix) pairs. Modules are files on
  disk under those roots; `lang/modules.rs:174 module_relative_file_candidates` documents
  the file<->module-name mapping to invert (flat `a/b.lisp` and nested spellings, plus the
  `ui/` prefix on the factory root, and the `eseq.` prefix strip in
  `module_file_candidates`).
- Plumbing: the catalog is scanned in crates/sequencer/src/app_paths/mod.rs:250 and only
  its module roots reach the runtime (`Runtime::set_module_load_path`,
  runtime.rs:1952). The editor has no view of package/module names today. Either
  (a) walk the configured module load roots at completion time and cache the result, or
  (b) push a module-name list into the Runtime alongside the load path. (a) keeps the
  sequencer crate out of it; cache the walk and invalidate on the same signal that
  invalidates the symbol cache (`invalidate_symbol_cache`) so typing is not doing IO per
  keystroke.

Open question: whether to also complete `:refer (…)` symbol lists from the target
module's export registry (`lang/modules.rs:71 inspect_exports`). Nice follow-up, not
required here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Typing `(import alez.j` opens the completion popup listing `alez.jaki.core` and
  `alez.jaki.surface` (given those modules are installed).
- Typing `(import ` with no prefix, or a one-char prefix, lists installed package names.
- Completion covers user, package, and factory module roots.
- Accepting a candidate (Tab) inserts the full dotted module name.
- Module completion does not fire outside the module-name position of an `import` form
  (e.g. `(import foo :refer (x` must not offer module names).
- Completion does not do filesystem IO on every keystroke (walk is cached).
- Tests live alongside the existing completion tests in crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/tests.rs
  and crates/eseqlisp/src/mode.rs tests.
notes: 2026-08-25: now load-bearing for the Scripts-tab retirement (docs/attachable-packages-spec.md rev 2 §2): with plain (import …) in *scratch* as the blessed attachment mechanism, autocomplete over the load path IS the script-discovery story. Bumped P2→P1; eseq-mods.17 depends on this.

title: Fix sample-browser waveform resolution after sample-store path move
description: The sample browser's waveform preview still opens persisted sample paths such as samples/<sha256>.wav relative to the old repository layout. After samples moved to the user/sample-store tier, waveform loading logs ENOENT even though the sample exists in the configured store. Route browser waveform lookup through the canonical AppPaths/sample-store resolver (the same content-addressed resolution used for sample playback) rather than reading the persisted relative path directly. Audit adjacent browser preview paths so waveform and audio preview cannot diverge.
acceptance_criteria: A browser row whose persisted sample_path is samples/<sha256>.wav loads its waveform from the configured user sample store; no read is attempted against the obsolete repository-relative samples/ directory; audio and waveform preview resolve the same sample; a focused regression test covers a non-working-directory sample-store root and fails under direct relative-path lookup; missing/corrupt samples still produce a clear non-panicking diagnostic.

title: Published sequencers never GC: stale defs tick forever, scheduler load grows monotonically
description: SYMPTOM: scheduler thread degrades over a session, worst after re-evaluating *scratch*; Instruments shows 70%+ under invoke_sequencer_tick. EVIDENCE (jaki_perf_probe, commit b4411cdf): per-tick cost is FLAT (~0.26ms release) across 6000+ beats and repeated re-evals — the VM/jaki lisp does not degrade. But total load scales linearly with registered sequencer count (1 def=267ms per 256-beat window, 13 defs=1347ms). MECHANISM: SequencerState::publish_sequencer (process_chain.rs:15) upserts by id=fnv(name) and the ONLY removal path is the manual seq-unpublish-sequencer native (ui/natives.rs:5652). Nothing prunes on buffer re-eval, project load, or new-project — every (jak "name" …)/(def-sequencer "name" …) ever evaluated in a session keeps ticking (and emitting!) on the scheduler forever; renaming a sequencer leaks the old one. Debug builds multiply the per-tick constant ~20-50x, so a dozen stale defs saturates the scheduler. FIX SKETCH: reconcile instead of upsert — tag PublishedSequencer with source provenance (e.g. the file path passed to eval_source_transactional) and an eval generation; after a successful eval of that source, drop entries from the same source that were not re-published in that generation. Same-name upsert stays for hot-reload. Also consider: surface published-sequencer list + unpublish in UI; scale jaki memo caps (memo-store 16 / len-memo 32 shared across ALL patterns) with pattern count or key them per-pattern id to avoid thrash once many patterns coexist legitimately.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text: Root cause of the reported scheduler pinning found and FIXED (03e87ab1): it was NOT primarily stale published defs — jaki/locate mapped cycle-length over the whole super-cycle period every tick per route, and real patterns (multi-fig + cyc + every + align, 5 routes) overflowed the 32/16-entry shared memo caps → permanent thrash → 44.5 ms/tick (measured with the user's exact patterns; 0.45 ms/tick after caching the per-pattern (lens total pd) table by pattern id in a new lens-memo). This bead's GC issue is still real and still worth fixing (stale defs tick+emit forever, linear load growth — measured 5x at 13 defs) but it is now secondary. jaki_perf_probe is trimmed to a ~2s run using the real-world pattern shape.

title: Remove playback latency from instrument-rack slot controls
description: Instrument-rack slot gain and base-note/transpose edits can take roughly a second to become audible while transport is playing. Investigation confirms this is the same broad stale-snapshot/competing-writer class as eseq-wtp, but through the rack event path. Gain/pan/mute setters update the live rack state and directly push the slot panner, while every rack trigger later calls `push_rack_slot_panner_params` using `RackSlotSnapshot` values captured for scheduler/lookahead playback. A queued trigger can therefore overwrite a newer live gain/pan/mute edit with its stale slot baseline. Base-note/transpose has no direct runtime push: it is read from the captured rack slot when a note is fired, so newly triggered notes continue using the old offset until a new scheduler snapshot is published and stale lookahead events drain. The UI intentionally marks `rack_control_snapshot_dirty` and publishes the large scheduler snapshot only at pointer release, which explains why these controls feel delayed; the source already contains a mute-specific comment acknowledging stale per-trigger panner clobbering. Fix the rack control ownership/publication model so live defaults and per-step p-lock/macro overrides compose correctly without stale queued events or broad snapshot work on every pointer tick.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Rack slot gain changes affect currently audible rack output immediately and remain at the edited value across subsequent triggers. 2. Rack slot pan, mute, and solo have equivalent immediate behavior and are not clobbered by queued rack events. 3. Base-note/transpose changes affect the next note triggered after the edit; already sounding notes need not be retuned, but no one-second/lookahead drain is required. 4. Slot parameter p-locks and rack macros still override the live default on their intended steps and restore to the newest live default afterward. 5. Correctness does not depend on pointer release, transport restart, pattern launch, or unrelated edits. 6. The solution does not rebuild/publish a full scheduler snapshot for every drag tick; direct controls remain responsive in large projects. 7. Deterministic regression coverage queues rack events, edits live gain and base note, then proves stale events cannot restore the old values. 8. Add a focused interaction/performance check if the base-note handler full-panel refresh remains on the pointer-rate path.
notes: Related bug: eseq-wtp (bus sends), which has the same immutable-snapshot versus live-control ownership conflict. Rack-specific findings: `app/synth.rs::set_rack_slot_gain` directly pushes the slot panner; `audio/rack.rs::fire_rack_resolved` resolves gain/pan/mute/base-note from the event rack snapshot and pushes panner parameters on every trigger before firing notes; `ui/host_commands/rack.rs` sets `rack_control_snapshot_dirty`; `ui/event_loop.rs` publishes the scheduler snapshot only on pointer release. The handler comment for rack mute explicitly says per-trigger panner pushes clobber a new value from a stale snapshot. Base-note additionally calls `refresh_instrument_panel_reactive` for every change, which may add UI-side drag cost and should be measured rather than assumed to be harmless. This is related to eseq-wtp architecturally, but needs rack-specific treatment because transpose is note-trigger data while gain is a continuous live graph parameter.

title: Make bus send edits audible immediately during playback
description: While transport is playing, dragging a track bus-send knob often updates the UI but produces no audible/backend change. The new value only takes effect after a pattern/clip launch or another pattern mutation, even when that mutation belongs to a different track. Investigation found two competing writers for the same send gain nodes. The UI command path (`set-track-bus-send` -> `SetTrackSends` -> `apply_track_bus_sends`) updates `TrackParams.sends` and directly pushes the new amount to the live graph. However, scheduler lookahead calls `resolve_track_send_params` for triggered steps and emits both send channels on every event, using the baseline captured in its immutable `SequencerSnapshot`. `command_mutates_sequencer_state` deliberately excludes `SetTrackSends` from snapshot publication because mixer drags were designed as direct graph updates. Therefore an already queued or subsequently scheduled event writes the stale captured baseline over the live knob edit. Any unrelated pattern command publishes a fresh full snapshot/epoch, explaining why launching another track clip makes the send suddenly register. Fix the ownership/publication model so scheduler p-lock restoration observes the current live baseline without requiring expensive full snapshot publication on every drag tick and without stale queued events overriding newer edits.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Dragging any track-to-bus send while transport is playing changes the audible send level immediately and continuously. 2. Subsequent scheduled events do not overwrite the edited value with a stale baseline. 3. No pattern/clip launch, transport restart, or unrelated track edit is required for the value to take effect. 4. Bus-send p-locks still apply on locked steps and restore to the latest live baseline afterward, including when the baseline changes while lookahead events are already queued. 5. Behavior is correct with multiple tracks, multiple buses, scenes/patterns, and both zero/nonzero starting sends. 6. The fix preserves the intended mixer-drag performance property: do not use broad full scheduler snapshot publication per drag tick as a workaround. 7. Deterministic regression coverage reproduces the race between a live `SetTrackSends` update and scheduler-generated send parameter events, and proves unrelated pattern publication no longer changes correctness.
notes: Code findings: `crates/sequencer/src/ui/host_commands/routing.rs` applies `SetTrackSends`; `crates/sequencer/src/app/command.rs` explicitly classifies `SetTrackSends` as not mutating scheduler-visible state, with a comment claiming event scheduling cannot observe mixer fields; but `crates/sequencer/src/scheduler/params.rs::resolve_track_send_params` reads `snapshot.tracks[*].params.sends` as the baseline and emits it to both runtime gain targets. That function is appended in multiple paths in `scheduler/lookahead.rs`, including inactive and active step/event routes. Pattern commands publish a new immutable scheduler snapshot, which accounts for the reported cross-track clip-launch trigger. Existing tests prove p-lock -> captured-baseline restoration, but do not cover changing the live baseline after snapshot/lookahead creation. The bus-send p-lock/runtime-target implementation appears to have introduced this contradiction (commit 7df3dad4). A robust design likely needs a lightweight/live baseline authority or generation-aware dispatch; simply publishing the full snapshot on every knob event would violate the existing performance intent and may still leave stale already-queued events.

title: Stop auto-evaluating *scratch* while editing
description: The *scratch* authoring buffer currently appears to evaluate/publish changes as the user types. Preserve edits without executing them until the user explicitly invokes eval-buffer, including Jaki/def-sequencer authoring.
notes: Implemented in commit d37a0741. *scratch* text/cursor sync is now draft-only; a successful eval-buffer authoring transaction publishes source to the scheduler. Projects persist draft and last evaluated source separately (legacy projects treat their sole buffer as evaluated), and runtime rebuild/startup evaluation uses only evaluated source.
close_reason: Scratch editing is side-effect free until successful eval-buffer

title: Precompile Lisp sequencer tick bodies in the scheduler VM
description:
## Problem

Pure-Lisp `def-sequencer` tick bodies (notably Jaki) are published from the UI VM as source text and executed in the scheduler VM. `ScratchControlRuntime::invoke_sequencer_tick` currently calls `Runtime::eval_str` for every scheduler boundary, reparsing/compiling the same body on the scheduler thread before executing it.

A profile of Jaki playback attributes 3.71 s / 53.2% of samples to `schedule_playing_lookahead -> invoke_sequencer_tick -> Runtime::eval_str -> VM::eval_str/execute`, with 3.39 s in core-native invocation beneath that path. This is avoidable scheduler-thread work and makes Lisp-native sequencers disproportionately expensive.

## Implementation direction

Use the same scheduler-VM compilation/cache model as graph-based neural sequencer updates (`CompiledGraphUpdate` / `graph_update_callback`):

- Compile a published tick source into a scheduler-VM callable once, rather than evaluating source on every tick. A zero-argument closure around the body should preserve the existing `seq-*` context-native contract.
- Cache the callable with the sequencer's stable identity and exact source, or compile it while reconciling/registering the published definition if that gives cleaner ownership.
- Invoke the cached scheduler-VM callable at each boundary.
- Recompile/replace it when authoring republishes changed source, and correctly discard VM-owned values whenever the scheduler runtime is rebuilt/reset.
- Preserve the UI-VM/scheduler-VM split: do not attempt to move or retain closures created in the UI VM. Jaki helpers and pattern values must still be resolved/built scheduler-side.
- Produce a clear registration/compilation error for malformed or non-callable tick source without leaving a stale callback active.

Prefer a sequencer-specific compiled callback type/cache over broadening `RegisteredAccumulatorCallback` semantics unless a careful refactor demonstrates that accumulators/MIDI FX need the same lifecycle. Avoid source-string evaluation in the real-time lookahead path.

## Evidence

Profile excerpt:

```text
3.71 s  53.2%  schedule_playing_lookahead
3.71 s  53.2%  ScratchControlRuntime::invoke_sequencer_tick
3.71 s  53.2%  eseqlisp::runtime::Runtime::eval_str
3.71 s  53.2%  eseqlisp::lang::vm::VM::eval_str
3.70 s  53.1%  VM::execute_from / execute / execute_with_frames
3.39 s  48.6%  register_core_natives closure -> VM::invoke
```

Relevant code: `crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/shared_state.rs`; reference design: `crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/eseq/graph_update.rs`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repeated invocations of one unchanged published Lisp sequencer tick do not call `eval_str` or compile/parse source after the initial scheduler-VM compilation.
- Tick behavior, emissions, RNG advancement, generator state, and fractional scheduling remain unchanged for Jaki and ordinary source-authored `def-sequencer` definitions.
- Republishing the same sequencer ID with changed tick source causes exactly one new compilation and subsequent ticks execute the new body; failed replacement cannot silently execute stale code.
- Scheduler runtime rebuild/reset cannot reuse a callable owned by an old VM.
- A targeted regression test proves compile-once/invoke-many and hot-reload behavior without relying only on wall-clock timing.
- Run the deterministic scheduler lookahead routing regression and the relevant exact Lisp-host/Jaki tests.
- A before/after release profile or focused benchmark demonstrates that `Runtime::eval_str` is absent from the steady-state `invoke_sequencer_tick` scheduler path.
notes: Implemented in commit 16cbc6f5. Published tick bodies compile into scheduler-VM zero-argument closures at registration; source/id cache invokes the VM callable thereafter, caches failed compilation, removes stale registrations on failed replacement, and is recreated with each ScratchControlRuntime. Exact compile-count/hot-reload regression plus Jaki and deterministic scheduler routing tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated scheduler-VM tick precompilation and hot reload

title: R1c: prove the DMG on a machine with no dev checkout
description:
Spec: docs/release-packaging-spec.md section 5.

Run the R1 acceptance matrix. This is the slice that finds the bugs R1 exists
to find -- expect a list of findings, not a clean pass on the first try.

CRITICAL: testing on the build machine is INSUFFICIENT. The Dev arm's
`find_package_dir` walks `current_exe()` ancestors looking for a `crates/`
directory, so a sibling checkout on the same machine can mask exactly the
failure this rung is meant to catch. Use a second Mac, a fresh VM, or at
minimum a clean user account with no checkout anywhere in the exe's ancestry.

Matrix:
- Mount, drag to /Applications, remove quarantine, launch. Window opens.
- Clean user account: `~/Library/Application Support/<bundle-id>/` and
  `~/.eseq.d/` are created and populated; NO write is attempted inside the
  bundle (content-tiers section 4.1 forbids it and a read-only bundle makes it
  a hard failure).
- Factory instruments and effects load.
- A new DGen instrument compiles, auditions, saves, and survives restart --
  using ONLY the bundled toolchain, with no Xcode and no Command Line Tools.
- App moved to another directory still launches.
- A tester who has never seen the repo installs and makes sound from the
  README alone.

Section 4.6 names one dev-only path already found (the per-frame shader
override metadata call). There are likely others; file what turns up rather
than patching silently, so the class stays visible.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every matrix item above passes on a machine with no dev checkout in the
  executable's ancestry, and the environment used is recorded in the bead.
- Findings filed as beads; anything blocking install is fixed before close.
- README install instructions verified by someone other than the author, or
  explicitly noted as unverified.

title: R1b: dist/macos/build.sh -- assemble ESeq.app, Info.plist, icon, and an unsigned DMG
description:
Spec: docs/release-packaging-spec.md sections 3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7.

Produce the artifact. Plain shell under `dist/macos/`, no Xcode project.

Product shell decisions to ratify and then wire (spec section 3):
- CFBundleIdentifier: recommended `com.universalsequences.eseq`. DECIDE ONCE.
  AppPaths::Release routes user data to
  `~/Library/Application Support/<bundle-id>/` and artifacts to
  `~/Library/Caches/<bundle-id>/`; changing it after any tester saves a
  project orphans their library and forces a migration.
- Names: product is ESeq, bundle `ESeq.app`, CFBundleName/DisplayName `ESeq`,
  CFBundleExecutable stays `metal_seq` (renaming the Cargo bin target touches
  probes, tests and docs for no user-visible gain).
- CFBundleShortVersionString from the crate version (0.1.0); CFBundleVersion
  from the short git hash for R1. R2 swaps in a CI run number -- Sparkle in R3
  requires CFBundleVersion to increase monotonically.
- LSMinimumSystemVersion 11.0, matching `minimum_macos` in the staged
  toolchain's VERSION.json. arm64 only.
- AppIcon.icns is REQUIRED for R1: a generic icon is the loudest "this is not
  a real app" signal to a first tester. Source artwork in dist/macos/.

Script steps:
1. cargo build --release for `metal_seq` and `eseq`.
2. Verify `crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain` exists; it is ~140 MB,
   gitignored, and produced by `./rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh`. ABORT LOUDLY with
   that command in the message -- a bundle shipped without it cannot compile
   anything, and the failure would surface much later as a confusing runtime
   error. Record the stage's VERSION.json in the build log.
3. Assemble the tree in spec section 4.4: Contents/MacOS/{metal_seq, eseq,
   DGenLisp}, Contents/Resources/{AppIcon.icns, dgen-toolchain/, content/
   copied verbatim}.
4. Generate Info.plist.
5. Ad-hoc sign (`codesign -s -`) so it launches without a Developer ID. R3
   replaces ONLY this step.
6. Emit `ESeq-<version>-<hash>.dmg` (hdiutil; or create-dmg if a window
   layout is wanted -- Ghostty uses create-dmg and R3 will want it).

Output to `dist/out/`, gitignored.

Depends on eseq-4tr.1: without the Release arm the assembled app exits before
opening a window, so there is nothing to verify.
acceptance_criteria:
- `dist/macos/build.sh` produces a mountable DMG containing ESeq.app.
- Missing staged toolchain aborts with the rebuild command in the error, not
  a silently incomplete bundle.
- The app launches from /Applications after `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`
  and opens a window.
- Info.plist carries the ratified identifier, names, both version keys, icon,
  and LSMinimumSystemVersion.
- `strings` on the shipped binaries reveals no path into the build machine's
  home directory or checkout.
- README documents install + quarantine removal for a tester who has never
  seen the repo.

title: R1a: construct AppPaths::Release -- arm detection, skip the dev chdir, gate dev-only paths
description:
Spec: docs/release-packaging-spec.md section 4.1-4.3, 4.6.

Code-only slice, fully testable in the workspace before any bundle exists.
Nothing constructs `AppPaths::Release` today.

1. Add `init_release()` / arm selection. `AppPaths::release(contents_macos,
   contents_resources, application_support, caches, user_lisp_root)` already
   exists and every accessor already consumes it correctly -- only the
   constructor and root derivation are missing.

2. Select the arm at RUNTIME from `std::env::current_exe()`: if the exe sits
   in `.../Something.app/Contents/MacOS/`, take Release with roots derived
   from that ancestor; else Dev. One binary, both behaviors, `cargo run` from
   the workspace unaffected. A build-time feature flag is REJECTED in the
   spec: it makes the bundled binary untestable from the workspace, which is
   the debugging loop R1 depends on.

3. Skip `paths::enter_sequencer_dir()` on the Release arm.
   `crates/sequencer/src/ui/main.rs:105` chdirs into the crate dir. In a
   bundle `find_package_dir` fails every branch (SEQUENCER_ROOT -> cwd ->
   current_exe ancestors containing `crates/` -> CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) and
   returns Err("sequencer crate directory not found"), which propagates out
   of main -- THE BUNDLED APP EXITS BEFORE OPENING A WINDOW. Expect this as
   the first symptom.

4. Release arm ignores `ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT` (already a documented rule
   in the toolchain spec), and should ignore `SEQUENCER_ROOT` /
   `ESEQLISP_ROOT` for the same reason.

5. Gate `poll_editable_shader_overrides` off on Release. It reads
   `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/shaders/button_surface.metal` every frame from
   `crates/sequencer/src/ui/event_loop.rs:311`. It degrades gracefully today
   (returns false, logs once) so it is not a crash -- but it is a per-frame
   fs::metadata on a path that can never exist in a bundle.

6. RESOLVE THE LAYOUT CONFLICT (spec section 4.4, open question 3). The
   toolchain spec's Bundle Layout shows `Resources/runtime/eseqlisp/init.lisp`
   and `Resources/factory/...`. The CODE disagrees: `factory_root()` returns
   `contents_resources` directly, so `core_dir()` is `Resources/core`.
   content-tiers-spec.md is rev 2 and newer and matches the code. Correct the
   toolchain spec (or change the accessors) -- do not ship the ambiguity, and
   do not leave it for the dist script to guess.

`ensure_user_tier()` is already correct for first run on a clean account and
needs no change.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test constructs the Release arm from a synthetic `.app/Contents/MacOS/`
  exe path and asserts every AppPaths accessor resolves under Contents/ or
  the App Support / Caches roots -- no path escapes into the checkout.
- A test asserts the Dev arm is still selected for a workspace binary, so
  `cargo run` and every existing test is unaffected.
- Release arm ignores ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT / SEQUENCER_ROOT /
  ESEQLISP_ROOT; asserted, not assumed.
- Startup does not chdir on the Release arm.
- Exactly one bundle layout is documented; toolchain spec and
  content-tiers-spec agree with the code.
- Scoped tests only (`-p sequencer`), per AGENTS.md.

title: Release packaging: installable artifact (R1 unsigned DMG -> R2 CI tip -> R3 signed)
description:
Spec: docs/release-packaging-spec.md rev 1.

Turn the workspace build into something a person installs. Three rungs:

- R1: unsigned/ad-hoc .app in a DMG, built locally. No Apple account, no CI,
  no second machine. This is what developer friends install.
- R2: same artifact built in GitHub Actions on every main commit (tip channel).
- R3: Developer ID signed, notarized, stapled, Sparkle updates -- already
  owned by eseq-toolchain.3 and the toolchain spec Phase 5.

Only R1 is scoped into children here. R2 is sketched in spec section 6; R3 is
a pointer to the existing bead.

Why R1 exists as a separate rung: ESeq compiles and loads dylibs at runtime.
Unsigned means no hardened runtime, so library validation never constrains
those dylibs and the disable-library-validation question does not arise. R1
removes the most uncertain part of R3 rather than deferring it -- but per spec
section 2.2, R1 passing is NOT evidence R3 will pass. Its value is real
testers on the product while signing work proceeds in parallel.

The diffuse half of this work is already done: a scan of non-test code found
ZERO relative-path filesystem accesses; everything resolves through AppPaths.
What remains is concentrated in the named places in spec section 4.

title: Package sample ingest is never called: installing a package contributes no samples
description:
`crates/sequencer/src/package_samples.rs` is complete, `pub`, and unit-tested,
but `ingest_installed_packages` has ZERO call sites outside its own tests.
Nothing in startup, no host command, and notably not
`package_install::install_git_package` (which stops at cloning + Lisp
validation) ever invokes it. `uninstall_package_samples` is likewise
uncalled.

Consequence: the whole sample-attribution feature is inert. A package that
ships `samples.jsonl` contributes nothing at runtime; the browser's origin
chips ("Yours" / "Factory" / package name, `content/ui/browser.lisp:679`)
can only ever show `user`. Confirmed against the live library: every row in
`sample_provenance`, `sample_tag_origins`, and `sample_titles` has
origin `user` (13783 / 49170 / 13768 rows, zero `pkg:` or `factory`).

This is the seam between eseq-tiers.6 (Lisp packaging) and eseq-lc0 (sample
store): each shipped its half and the wire between them was never run. The
supporting pieces all exist and work -- `eseq package index` builds
`samples.jsonl` from a pretty `samples/` tree with directory-derived tags
(`sample_manifest.rs:71`), ingest validates every payload and source ref
BEFORE mutating, and `remove_origin` makes reinstall idempotent.

Where it should be called (decide in the bead):
1. At startup, after `ensure_user_tier()`, alongside
   `AppPaths::module_load_roots()` -- which already scans the same dir and
   reports invalid packages without aborting boot. Symmetry argues for
   ingest reporting failures the same lenient way.
2. From `install_git_package` / a matching uninstall path, so the DB changes
   when the filesystem does rather than at next launch.

(1) alone is simplest and self-healing; (2) alone leaves a hand-copied
package dir invisible. Startup ingest is the safer default, but it must be
cheap when nothing changed -- ingest currently does `remove_origin` then
re-merges every line for every installed package unconditionally, which is
fine for two packages and not for twenty. Consider skipping a package whose
`samples.jsonl` hash is unchanged since last ingest.

Depends on eseq-tiers.7: until the name formats agree, no package can be
both loadable and a sample provider, so this cannot be tested end to end.
acceptance_criteria:
- Installing a package that ships `samples.jsonl` makes its samples queryable
  with origin `pkg:<identity>`, without a manual step.
- Uninstalling (or deleting the package dir) removes exactly that origin's
  provenance/tag/title rows and leaves user claims on the same hashes intact.
- Re-running ingest with an unchanged package is idempotent and does not
  duplicate rows; unchanged packages are not needlessly re-merged.
- A malformed package is reported, not fatal -- matching the existing lenient
  `PackageCatalog::scan_reporting` behavior at boot.
- The browser origin chips show the package and filter by it. End-to-end
  test, not a unit test on package_samples.rs.
close_reason: Implemented startup and install-time package sample reconciliation with manifest digest caching, stale-origin cleanup, lenient error reporting, and end-to-end coverage.

title: Package manifest name format is mutually exclusive between the Lisp loader and the sample ingester
description:
Both readers parse the SAME file (`<pkg>/manifest.json`) and their `name`
validators cannot both be satisfied:

- `crates/eseqlisp/src/package.rs:223` `validate_package_name` REQUIRES an
  author-scoped `author/name` (splits on `/`, returns module prefix
  `author.name`). No slash => "name must be author-scoped".
- `crates/sequencer/src/package_samples.rs:127` `validate_package_name`
  REJECTS `/` (allows only ascii-alnum plus `. - _`). Its tests use dotted
  names like `one.pack` and build origin `pkg:one.pack`.

So `alec/jaki` loads as a Lisp package but can never contribute samples, and
`jaki` ingests samples but is rejected by the module loader. There is no name
that satisfies both, which means NO package can currently be both a Lisp
package and a sample provider.

The CLI already picks a side: `eseq package install AUTHOR/NAME GIT_URL`
(`crates/sequencer/src/bin/eseq.rs`) is author-scoped, and
`install_git_package` takes that identity. The Lisp form is the
user-facing one.

Proposed fix: `author/name` is the single distribution identity. The sample
side stops validating the raw manifest field and instead derives its origin
from the already-validated module prefix, i.e. origin = `pkg:author.name`.
That keeps origin strings free of `/` (worth preserving: `sample_provenance`
origins appear in queries and UI chips, and instrument ids reject
`pkg:someone/mine` at
`crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/instrument_storage.rs:1102`), while
giving one identity end to end.

Watch for: `validate_source_id` in package_samples.rs requires package source
ids to be namespaced under `<origin>/`, so changing the origin string changes
what a package's `samples.jsonl` source ids must look like. Any fixture or
doc example must move together.
acceptance_criteria:
- One package identity format documented and enforced: a single validator (or
  one deriving from the other) so `author/name` is valid for BOTH the module
  loader and the sample ingester.
- A test installs one package that ships both `src/*.lisp` and
  `samples.jsonl` and asserts the Lisp module imports AND its samples land
  with the expected `pkg:` origin. This is the case neither side covers today.
- docs/sample-store-spec.md states the identity format and the origin string
  derived from it.
notes:
Verified 2026-08-21 with a real install: eseq package install alec/hello file://<repo> clones to <packages>/alec.hello -- the on-disk directory is ALREADY the dotted module prefix, not the slashed identity. So pkg:<dir name> == pkg:alec.hello is the derivation with the least new machinery, and it matches the dotted names package_samples.rs tests already assume (one.pack). Also verified eseq package index works: a samples/drums/kick/thump.wav tree yields {"hash":..,"path":"drums/kick/thump.wav","title":"thump","tags":["drums","kick"]} -- directory segments become tags, Strudel-style, as specced.

Implemented author/name as the sole manifest identity; package sample origins now derive from the validated module prefix (pkg:author.name). Added install/import/sample-ingest integration coverage and documented the mapping. Targeted nextest checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated package identity unification

title: Prevent topology edits from briefly muting unaffected tracks
description: Topology mutations caused short transport-wide gaps: rack-track creation, sampler/custom rack slot add/replace/delete, single-track deletion, and in-place instrument replacement. The audio callback globally cleared events, reset every voice pool, gated off every custom engine, and re-anchored host clock; the scheduler also cleared lookahead immediately. Preserve unaffected voices, routes, delayed events, scheduler horizon, and clock phase. Rack edits must retain event-compatible pattern epochs; single-track deletion must drain to an atomic frontier and remap surviving flat/rack runtime identities; same-count instrument replacement must reconcile only changed runtime. Deterministic regressions cover rack sampler/custom edits, deletion frontier/remapping, instrument-swap epoch publication, and additive-track behavior.
close_reason: Implemented seamless single-track/rack/instrument topology reconciliation: rack edits retain valid event epochs, deletion drains lookahead to an atomic frontier and remaps surviving callback state, and same-count instrument swaps no longer globally gate off/reset unaffected voices. Eight targeted regressions pass. Multi-track/group deletion remains separately tracked as eseq-l8i.

title: Preserve instrument clock phase when adding tracks during playback
description: Adding a track while transport is playing often resets clock-driven instruments (including LFOs and DGen clock inputs). Their phase remains wrong until transport restart, preventing seamless live jamming. Root invariant: transport phase belongs to transport state and must survive both additive and destructive topology refreshes; topology reset must not re-anchor the host clock. Add a deterministic regression proving a continuously playing clock retains phase through topology work and resets only on an actual stop/play edge.
close_reason: Implemented: host clock phase now has dedicated transport-owned runtime state and topology reconciliation cannot re-anchor it; deterministic stop/play-edge regression passes.

title: Keep effect parameter targets valid after reordering an effect chain
description: Reproduction: create or load a two-scene project with a custom instrument whose only effect is Str8 Delay. While Scene 2 is active, add Filter Table as a second effect and move Filter Table into the first slot so Str8 Delay shifts to the second slot. Editing any Str8 Delay parameter in Scene 2 then fails: the control does not move and the console reports command failed: InvalidTarget("effect parameter does not exist"). Switching to Scene 1 makes the same knobs work; switching back to Scene 2 makes them fail again. This scene-dependent behavior suggests that effect-chain reordering leaves one scene snapshot, rendered control, command target, effect identity, or parameter lookup bound to stale slot metadata. Diagnose the effect-chain identity and per-scene publication invariant, and fix it at the shared reorder/targeting layer rather than special-casing Str8 Delay or Filter Table.
acceptance_criteria: 1. After adding/reordering Filter Table before Str8 Delay while Scene 2 is active, every Str8 Delay parameter remains editable in Scene 2 and updates the intended DSP instance. 2. Switching between Scene 1 and Scene 2 preserves valid parameter targeting in both scenes; neither scene retains stale pre-reorder slot metadata. 3. Parameters on Filter Table and other reordered effects target the correct effect rather than a stale slot. 4. Repeated reordering in both directions does not produce InvalidTarget errors or route edits to the wrong effect. 5. Saving and reloading the reordered two-scene project preserves order and parameter editability in both scenes. 6. Focused regression coverage reproduces a reorder from a non-primary active scene and verifies command targeting before and after scene switches through the shared owner path.
notes: Observed console error: command failed: InvalidTarget("effect parameter does not exist"). Exact report: the project has two scenes; the effect was added and reordered while Scene 2 was active. Str8 Delay knobs fail only in Scene 2, work immediately after switching to Scene 1, and fail again upon returning to Scene 2. This is strong evidence of scene-local stale effect-slot/parameter target state.
close_reason: Resolved rendered effect controls by carrying live effect node identity and resolving it after chain reorders; added second-scene/repeated-reorder and UI callback regression coverage.

title: Prevent transport-wide silence when adding tracks during playback
description: Adding a track while the project transport is running can interrupt audio for every track even though the transport remains in the playing state. Two observed variants need to be treated as one topology-mutation investigation: (1) after adding a track, playback can remain silent until the transport is stopped and started again; (2) in a project containing an instrument rack and a custom instrument, adding a sampler track temporarily mutes everything for roughly a second and then playback recovers without a restart. This is not limited to instrument-rack edits or to the newly added track. Audit all add-track/topology publication paths for atomic ordering between scheduler snapshots, topology/pattern epochs, route construction, and audio-side visibility. Fix the shared invariant rather than patching individual track kinds.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Adding sampler, custom-instrument, and rack-backed tracks while transport is playing does not silence or audibly interrupt existing tracks. 2. The transport continues scheduling both existing and newly added tracks without requiring stop/play. 3. Behavior is correct in mixed projects containing instrument racks, custom instruments, and samplers. 4. A deterministic regression test exercises add-track topology mutation during active scheduler playback and proves no stale epoch/snapshot window drops events across tracks. 5. Existing rack slot edit/hot-swap behavior covered by eseq-6r5 remains correct.
notes: Likely related to closed bug eseq-6r5, fixed in b86cc011, where rack slot edits published the scheduler snapshot before bumping topology/pattern epochs and caused the audio callback to drop all stale-pattern-epoch events until restart. The new report demonstrates that track addition has either a similar ordering defect or another non-atomic topology transition outside the paths fixed there. Reported screenshot path (ephemeral): /var/folders/w0/m727twr50851tbqdlkbl_c1c0000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_3Fq9dB/Screenshot 2026-08-21 at 9.41.01 AM.png.
close_reason: Completed in c8d1d582: additive track topology now publishes atomically without invalidating existing event epochs; scheduler/audio extend at the existing frontier while destructive edits retain full reset behavior. Targeted mixed-track, scheduler lookahead, rack hot-swap, and track deletion regressions pass.

title: Custom (dgen) effect knob changes apply several triggers late; builtins and instrument params are instant
description:
Turning a knob on a **custom (dgen-compiled) effect** does not change the sound
until several more triggers have passed. The value eventually lands, so it is
not dropped forever -- it is applied late.

## Repro

- Custom effect `content/effects/shimmerpitch` on a track. Turn `mix` (or any
  other param) while audio is running.
- The change is not audible immediately; after a few more note triggers the
  sound catches up to where the knob already was.
- Same shape reported for delay and midi-fx params.

## The discriminator (this is the useful part)

| Target | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Custom / dgen-compiled effect (shimmerpitch) | **DELAYED** |
| Builtin effect (filterbank) | instant |
| Instrument patch params | instant |

So this is not the knob widget, not the reactive/UI layer, and not the generic
param pipeline -- all three would break instrument and builtin params too. It
is specific to how a **custom effect slot's param reaches the audio graph**.

Suspected recent regression per the reporter.

## Code path

`App::send_slot_param` (crates/sequencer/src/app/effect_params.rs:517)
  -> early-returns when `desc.params[param_idx].host_control.is_some()`
     (this is the split: builtins take a different route, which is exactly the
     route that works)
  -> `push_fx_param` (crates/sequencer/src/app/fx_chain.rs:1138)
       with `slot.node_id.load(Relaxed)`,
            `slot.modulator_node_id.load(Relaxed)`,
            `slot.resolve_node_idx(param_idx)`
  -> `params_push_wrapper(lg, ParamMsg { logical_id, idx, fvalue })`

## Ranked hypotheses

1. **Silent drop on a stale/zero node id.** `push_fx_param` computes `target`
   and returns with NO logging when `node_id == 0` or
   `node_param_idx == u32::MAX` (fx_chain.rs:1151-1158). If a custom effect
   slot's `node_id` / `resolve_node_idx` is stale or not yet published, every
   knob move is silently discarded, and the value only lands when some LATER
   event re-sends the full param set -- which would look exactly like "it
   catches up after a few triggers". **Check this first**: log or assert on the
   drop path and confirm whether custom-effect knob moves are reaching
   `params_push_wrapper` at all.
2. **Value-delta suppression comparing against a stale shadow.**
   `docs/fx-value-delta-spec.md` work was explicitly about skipping redundant
   fx param sends. If the dedupe compares the new value against a shadow that
   is not updated on the custom-effect path, changes get suppressed until
   something forces a resend. See `refresh_macro_base_shadow_for_slot`
   (effect_params.rs:871).
3. **The dgen node latches params at a sparse boundary** (hop/frame/trigger)
   rather than draining the param queue per block. Would explain the
   trigger-shaped granularity directly.

Hypotheses 1 and 3 are distinguishable by whether the ParamMsg is enqueued at
all: if it is enqueued promptly, the lateness is on the dgen consumption side
(3); if it never enqueues, it is (1).

## Bisect candidates

Recent commits on the fx param path:
  9928d5ef feat(bus): gut the bus gate step sequencer (eseq-fru)
  8caccf1b fix(effects): stop Space Echo aborting on Play from a zeroed sample-rate slot
  c58a1105 Add host-integrated Filter Table effect
  5b412acc refactor(sequencer): split graph push/send/dispatch wrappers into audio/graph_dispatch.rs
Plus the fx value-delta work: 73aad513, d6a9c822.

## Ask

- Fix so a custom-effect knob move is audible in the same block budget as a
  builtin-effect knob move.
- Add a regression test that turns a param on a dgen-compiled effect and
  asserts the value reaches the audio graph within one block -- not just that
  the app state changed. The whole bug is that app state was already correct.
- If `push_fx_param` is silently dropping sends, make that path loud (debug
  assert or trace) rather than a bare `return`; it hid this bug.
acceptance_criteria: Turning a param on a custom dgen effect (shimmerpitch mix) is audible with the same latency as a builtin effect param; a regression test asserts a dgen-effect param edit reaches the audio graph within one block rather than only asserting app state; any silent-drop path in push_fx_param is made loud.

title: Perf-probe project fixtures are untracked: probes cannot run on a fresh clone
description:
The documented perf probes read project fixtures that are **not in git**.

`crates/sequencer/src` references:
- `projects/92.json`   — project_92_step_interactions_end_to_end_perf,
                         project_92_arranged_step_interactions_end_to_end_perf,
                         project_92_mixer_track_badge_switch_reports_layout_work
- `projects/pianohold.json` — pianohold_step_selection_end_to_end_perf,
                         arrangement_view_interactions_end_to_end_perf
- `projects/arrtest3.json`

`crates/sequencer/projects/` is gitignored (root .gitignore
`crates/sequencer/projects/`), and none of these three files is tracked.
`git ls-files crates/sequencer/projects` returns 18 unrelated personal
projects (brokenriddim, garage, plocka, ...) that were committed before the
ignore rule landed — gitignore does not retroactively untrack.

**Consequence: every perf probe documented in UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md can
only run on one developer's machine.** On a fresh clone they fail or skip.
That silently voids the regression guardrails those probes are supposed to
provide (the checked-in pre-tuning medians and 10x ceilings), and it is a
direct contributor to the eseq-4tl problem: an agent cannot establish a
baseline for tests whose fixtures do not exist in the repo.

## Work

1. These three are **test fixtures, not user data**. Track them under the
   crate (e.g. `crates/sequencer/tests/fixtures/`), not under the gitignored
   `projects/`.
2. Check their size before committing — `crates/sequencer/projects/` totals
   188 MB across 263 files, so at least confirm these three are reasonable to
   version. If any is too large, decide deliberately (trim it, generate it, or
   mark the probe as requiring a local fixture and SKIP loudly rather than
   fail obscurely).
3. Point the probes at the fixture path through `AppPaths` rather than a
   relative literal — this is also a T1 (eseq-tiers.1) requirement.
4. `git rm --cached` the 18 zombie tracked projects; they are personal music
   and not referenced by anything.
5. Add a check that fails loudly and legibly when a probe fixture is missing,
   so the next person sees "fixture not found" rather than a confusing
   assertion failure.

Blocks eseq-tiers.3: T2 moves `projects/` out of the repo entirely, which
forces this decision anyway.
acceptance_criteria: 92.json, pianohold.json and arrtest3.json (or trimmed equivalents) are tracked in the repo as test fixtures outside the gitignored projects/ dir; every probe in UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md runs from a fresh clone; probes resolve fixtures via AppPaths, not relative literals; a missing fixture fails with a legible 'fixture not found' message; the 18 zombie tracked personal projects are git rm --cached.
notes: Tracked 92.json, pianohold.json, and arrtest3.json under crates/sequencer/tests/fixtures/projects; probes now resolve and load fixtures through AppPaths with a loud missing-fixture assertion; removed 18 zombie personal projects from the index. Validation: fixture presence/parse test, AppPaths path tests, and project-92 owner-switch smoke probe pass.
close_reason: Completed and validated perf-probe fixture migration

title: Sample store: derived index + package sample/tag contribution
description:
Spec: docs/sample-store-spec.md rev 1.

Once packages exist, many parties contribute samples and — more importantly —
*statements about* samples (titles, tags, sources, provenance). Today all of
those live in one mutable SQLite file that is the sole system of record. That
does not survive contact with packages.

Core design: **the index is derived; the facts are files.** samples.db becomes
a rebuildable index over per-tier line-oriented text; packages ship a generated,
hash-keyed samples.jsonl and never a .db file. The pretty directory tree stays
the authoring form and ingests into TAGS (Strudel's {"bd": [...]} map is tags
with ordering, not a second addressing scheme), so there is no parallel
namespace to maintain.

Two schema facts carry it: samples.hash is TEXT UNIQUE (portable identity
already exists) and tags.name is UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE (string merge key, and
normalize_tags already implements the policy). Every INTEGER PRIMARY KEY is a
local surrogate and must never be shipped.

## Findings that shaped the spec

- **The stored file is a transcode, and its name is not its own hash.**
  sample_import::import_one decodes the source and writes a canonical WAV, but
  names it {hash}.wav where hash is sha256 of the ORIGINAL source bytes
  (sample_import.rs:190). So the store is content-*named*, not
  content-*verified* — a stored file cannot be checked by re-hashing it, and
  package ingest is a transcode, not a cheap clonefile.
- **Deleting samples.db today loses 49,170 hand-made tag assignments
  permanently.** Nothing else records them. This is the real fragility and M1
  fixes it independently of packages.
- **Path-derived tags do not exist yet** — stage_one always sets
  tags: Vec::new(); only batch_tags reach insert_sample_with_tags.
- **source_refs collides globally**: UNIQUE(provider, ref_kind, ref_value) has
  no source_id, so two packages citing the same Discogs release collide by
  construction. Correct resolution is to converge on one source row, but ingest
  must do it deliberately rather than failing the insert.

## Slices

- M1 user facts of record: write curation to samples.jsonl alongside the DB +
  an index rebuild. Exit: deleting samples.db loses nothing. **No package
  dependency — do this first, it is the fragility fix.**
- M2 provenance + path-derived tags: sample_provenance table (a TABLE not a
  column — two packages can legitimately ship the same hash), backfill existing
  rows as 'user', derive tags from path segments on import.
- M3 manifest format + `eseq package index`: generate/read samples.jsonl,
  verify shipped payloads against their hashes.
- M4 package ingest: scan ~/.eseq.d/packages/*/samples.jsonl, merge under
  pkg:<name> provenance, namespace source ids, dedupe source_refs, refcount
  before removing any file on uninstall.

M1+M2 are standalone. M3+M4 land with eseq-mods.6 / eseq-tiers.6.

## Open questions (spec section 8)

1. Tag attribution on uninstall — sample_tags has no origin column, so
   uninstalling a package cannot retract exactly its tags without also removing
   the same tag the user applied by hand. Add an origin, or accept residue?
2. Journal format — append-only event log vs rewritten snapshot. Leaning
   append-only with compaction.
3. Should the store filename become the hash of the STORED bytes? Would make
   the store self-verifying but rewrites 13,783 filenames and every sample_path
   in 262 projects, which tiers.2 explicitly declined. Probably no; the spec
   records the reasoning so it is not relitigated.
acceptance_criteria: M1: deleting samples.db loses no curation (rebuildable from store + samples.jsonl). M2: sample_provenance populated, path segments become tags on import. M3: eseq package index generates a hash-keyed samples.jsonl from a pretty tree; payloads verify. M4: installing a package merges its samples/tags/sources under pkg:<name> provenance with namespaced source ids and deduped source_refs; uninstall retracts them and refcounts before deleting any stored file. M5: the browser can filter to one installed package and compose it with tags/favorites, and rows show provenance badges. M6 (discretionary, gates nothing): source graph surfaced.
notes:
## Attribution added to the spec (section 7), 2026-08-20

Browse-by-package is in scope and cheap. There are TWO attribution axes and
they must not be conflated:

- **Axis 1, delivery/provenance** — which package/tier put this file on this
  machine. `sample_provenance(sample_id, origin)`. This is what powers
  "browse by package". Depends on nothing else.
- **Axis 2, credit** — who made the sound / what record it came from.
  `sample_origins` -> `sources` / `source_contributors` / `source_refs` /
  `source_assets`.

**Axis 2 is dormant at BOTH ends and must not be assumed live.** Nothing
reads it: SampleDb::query selects only id/hash/title/favorited, filters only
on tags/text/favorites, and ui/browser.rs never mentions sources,
release_title, or source_assets. And almost nothing writes it: of 13,760
sample_origins rows, **13,741 are method='legacy_migration' and only 19 are
'local_sample_import'** (providers: 13,741 legacy_ipfs vs 637 youtube, 303
discogs). It is a one-time import of a previous system's data with a
near-dead write path. source_contributors is 0 rows -- artist is baked into
the source title string ("George Benson - In Flight").

Consequence: axis 2 was split out as its own DISCRETIONARY slice (M6) that
gates nothing. Browse-by-package (M5) needs only M2's sample_provenance and
ships without any of it. If sources are ever revived, packages are the
natural producer -- credited at authoring time via manifest source lines --
rather than retrofitting metadata inference onto local import.

**Rejected: provenance as a reserved tag** (`pkg:<name>` as a row in `tags`).
Tempting because it rides all existing tag machinery for free (query,
adjacent_tags, chip UI) with zero new code. Rejected because tags are
user-editable opinions and provenance is a fact -- as a tag it could be
deleted or falsely applied, and it entangles uninstall with the section 6 tag
attribution question. Instead: keep the table, expose it as a browser facet
that renders like a chip. query gains an `origins: &[&str]` EXISTS clause in
the same shape as the tag clauses; SampleRow carries origins for the
provenance badges content tiers 4.1 already requires; adjacent_tags stays
tag-only (package co-occurrence is not meaningful).

New open question 3: licensing. Distributing sample packs makes license terms
a real field. Per-package default with per-source override is the obvious
shape, but browser display and install-time warnings are undecided.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix every broken test in the repo and re-measure suite speed
description:
Tests are becoming a bottleneck again on two axes: **broken tests** and **wall
clock**. The expensive failure mode is a broken test that is *pre-existing*:
an agent that hits it cannot tell whether it caused the failure, so it clones a
worktree at HEAD (or at the merge base), rebuilds from scratch, and re-runs the
suite just to answer "was this already red?". That is a full cold build plus a
full test run burned on a question a green suite would answer for free.

## Goal

1. **Zero known-broken tests on main.** Every test either passes or is removed /
   fixed / explicitly `#[ignore]`d with a bead id in the ignore reason. No
   silent red.
2. **Re-measure how fast the suite actually is** and re-attack the slow tail.

## Work

### A. Inventory the current red
- Run the full suite from a clean checkout of `main` (release and debug — they
  fail differently) and produce a complete list of failing / flaky / hanging
  tests, per crate.
- For each one: fix it, delete it if it no longer describes intended behavior,
  or `#[ignore = "eseq-XXX: <why>"]` it and file the child bead. Ignoring
  without a bead id is not an acceptable outcome.
- Flaky counts as broken. Re-run the suite N times (or use nextest retries in a
  diagnostic pass) to separate deterministic red from flake.

### B. Make "is this pre-existing?" cheap
The worktree-clone dance exists because there is no cheap ground truth. Once
main is green, add one:
- a committed baseline of known-red/ignored tests, or
- a CI job that publishes the last-known-good result for the merge base, or
- a documented one-liner for the narrow "check this one test at HEAD" case
  that does not require a full cold rebuild (shared target dir / sccache /
  reusing the existing worktree per `eseq-test-workflow` conventions —
  **never** `git stash`).
Whatever the mechanism, write it into `CLAUDE.md` so agents reach for it
instead of cloning.

### C. Re-measure and re-attack speed
- Time the suite per crate and per test binary; produce a ranked list of the
  slowest targets and the slowest individual tests.
- Compare against the previous tuning pass (25 min -> 105 s, achieved via lazy
  `OnceLock` cells + pid-unique dylibs) and identify what has regressed or what
  new cost has been added since.
- Attack the tail: dylib compilation, project-fixture loading, per-test audio
  engine construction, and anything doing real filesystem or codegen work that
  could be shared or memoized across tests.
- Record the before/after numbers and the command used, so the next regression
  is measurable rather than felt.

## Notes
- Follow the repo test conventions: scoped tests (`-p sequencer`, not
  package-wide), no package-wide `cargo fmt`, use worktrees rather than
  `git stash`.
- Prior context: the earlier slowness diagnosis found lazy `OnceLock` cells and
  pid-unique dylibs were the two big wins; check whether either has eroded.
acceptance_criteria: Full suite on main is green in both debug and release (or every exclusion is #[ignore]d with a bead id in the reason); a documented cheap mechanism exists to answer 'is this failure pre-existing?' without cloning a HEAD worktree and cold-rebuilding, and is written into CLAUDE.md; the enlarged-stack requirement is root-caused (deep frame chain identified, production crash risk assessed) and reduced to one uniform, self-applying mechanism with one documented number, with stack overflow surfacing as a named failing test rather than an aborted binary; per-crate and per-test timings are recorded with a ranked slow list and before/after numbers for any speed work done.
notes:
## D. Root-cause the "needs a bigger stack or it crashes" gotcha

Several test families only passed on hand-enlarged stacks, causing whole test binaries to abort before results were reported. The pre-fix state had 13 UI sites at 64 MiB, 6 state-values sites at 32 MiB, a 16 MiB scheduler production/test constant, and a documented RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 shell rule. Required work: identify the deep frame chain; assess production risk; reduce cheap depth; establish one uniform self-applying budget; and make overflows report as named failures.

## Completion (2026-08-20)

Completed implementation and validation. Fixed deterministic test drift, DGen temp-output races, hardcoded instrument sample rates, release-only debug assertions, sound-palette containment, and scheduler stack coverage. LLDB identified recursive Expression clone/compiler traversal; clone is iterative, and remaining production-risk compiler recursion is child eseq-4tl.1. Unified the stack budget at 16 MiB via .cargo/config.toml and sequencer::REQUIRED_THREAD_STACK_SIZE. All ignored tests now include eseq-4tl in their reason.

Debug: 4,272 passed / 32 skipped in 191.09s test wall (192.06s process). Release: 4,270 passed / 32 skipped in 48.13s test wall (48.90s process), with an immediate second release run also green. Tail tuning reduced debug from 248.77s to 192.06s. Full details are in docs/test-suite-performance.md.

Instrument probes passed for flutefab, treatedpiano1, saxaphone-pm, and simplest-piano. The sound-palette Metal capture was inspected at /tmp/eseq-4tl-sound-palette-modal.png.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria complete; eseq-4tl.1 remains as the documented production-risk follow-up for removing compiler recursion.

title: Perf: group/track selection relayout is sluggish when the fx + instrument panels change owner
description:
Selecting a group or a track in the step sequencer feels sluggish when the fx
panel / instrument panel has to change shape. The cost appears to be panel
teardown + relayout (clearing a track's fx chain to show a group's fx chain and
vice versa), not the selection state change itself.

## Reported scenario (reproduce this exactly)

Project topology:
- 1 group + 6 tracks outside the group
- all groups expanded in the step sequencer (not collapsed)
- group 1 has 8 tracks
  - track 1 of the group: instrument rack with 1 instrument slot
  - track 2 of the group: plain sampler
  - remaining tracks: ordinary instrument tracks
- group 1 has an effect chain of ~5 effects

Observed ranking, slowest first:
1. group selected -> select track with an **instrument rack**  (worst)
2. track 1 in group -> select **the group itself**
3. group selected -> select **sampler** track (faster, but not instant)
4. track with instrument X -> track with the same instrument type (fastest —
   no relayout needed; this is the "no work" reference point)

The gap between (4) and (1)-(3) is the budget we are leaving on the table.

## What the implementer must do

1. **Build a realistic profile test first.** Follow `UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md`
   end to end (sections 1-4 especially). The fixture MUST have the production
   layout of buffers visible — the full sequencer + fx panel + instrument panel
   + mixer/whatever the real window shows — not a single isolated buffer.
   Measuring one buffer in isolation will give a number that does not match the
   user-visible latency and will send the tuning in the wrong direction.
   Drive the real click/selection input path (not an internal helper), and time
   through: host command -> invalidation -> reactive cycle -> widget-tree flush
   -> layout -> tiled frame -> retained Metal update.
2. Save a project fixture matching the topology above (or extend an existing
   one) so the probe is deterministic and checked in.
3. Report median + p95 over >= 20 samples in `--release`, with warmups, for each
   of the four transitions listed above, and check the pre-tuning medians into
   the harness like the existing probes do.
4. Split the latency into phases and record work counts (effects executed,
   dirty widgets, relayouts, primitive runs rebuilt). Expect the root cause to
   show up as counts, not milliseconds.
5. Fix the earliest architectural cause. Suspects to check, not conclusions:
   - fx panel children being destroyed/recreated rather than keyed and reused
     when the fx-chain owner changes (track <-> group)
   - instrument-rack panel construction doing full-subtree layout per selection
   - selection writing a coarse `defstate` that fans out to every visible panel
   - full relayout where in-place subtree layout reuse would do
6. Add a regression guardrail (10x-style ceiling as in the existing probes) and
   document the probe + reference timings in `UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md`.

Relevant starting points: `crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp` (group/track
selection state), `seq-panels.lisp`, `seq-layout.lisp`, `effects.lisp`,
`crates/sequencer/src/ui/tests.rs` (existing probe harnesses to copy).

Prior art in memory: "Subtree scene-switch perf" (356->60ms via index-aware deps
+ nested subtrees) and "Full-layout selection perf" (Cmd+A 41.5->4.2ms via
in-place subtree layout reuse + binding-table delta) are the closest analogues.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in release probe with the production multi-buffer layout measures the four selection transitions (track->group, group->instrument-rack track, group->sampler track, same-instrument track->track) with median+p95 over >=20 samples; pre-tuning medians recorded; each transition materially faster after tuning with a regression ceiling enforced; UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md documents the probe and reference timings.
notes: Probe built (project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_end_to_end_perf). Root cause found: selected-bus defstate read in render by every sequencer/arrangement row + group blocks + mixer strips -> full re-renders per selection. Fixed via *sel-sync* SEQV projection (seq-core-state.lisp) + binding conversions. Owner-flip medians 108/134/111 -> 17/45/20ms. Verifying + docs next.
close_reason: Shipped 97c8eebe. Probe project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_end_to_end_perf checked in with pre-tuning medians 145/139/170/48.5ms and enforced ceilings 80/75/110/75ms; tuned medians 51.2/45.6/75.8/48.7ms via the *sel-sync* SEQV selection-visibility projection (seq-core-state.lisp) replacing render-time selected-bus reads in every row/group/strip. UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md documents the probe + timings. Follow-ups filed for the remaining *fx* panel reconstruction and *samples* sidebar re-render.

title: Live-keyboard suppression regressed GUI-only buffers (piano roll, sample browser)
description:
REGRESSION from eseq-4o9 (text-editing focus should suppress sequencer/roll/live-keyboard shortcuts).

REPRO (user, 2026-08-20): arm a track, focus the *piano-roll* tile (or the *samples* sample browser) and press home-row keys. No notes fire. Focusing *sequencer* or *mixer* works.

ROOT CAUSE: eseq-4o9 made live keys OPT-IN per major mode. crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:103 editor_accepts_live_keyboard_input gates on Editor::active_mode_accepts_live_keys (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:5499), which requires BufferMode::Named(m) with m.live_keys. Only four modes ever opted in: seq-mixer-mode (mixer.lisp:1686), eseq.seq-grid-mode/seq-grid-mode (seq-grid-mode.lisp:80, used by *sequencer* and *metal*), seq-fx-mode and seq-plock-panel-mode (effects/buffers.lisp:264/280).

Every other effect-buffer never calls set-buffer-mode-for, so it keeps the default non-Named mode and silently lost live keys: *piano-roll* (piano-roll.lisp:515), *samples* (browser.lisp:1828), *arrangement* (arrangement.lisp:1695), *transport* (transport.lisp:700), *patch-mixer* (mixer.lisp:1652), *macro-mappings* (macros.lisp:252), *patch-macros* (patch-macros.lisp:191). These are GUI-only buffers with no text pane, so there was never anything for them to protect.

FIX DIRECTION: the opt-in list is the wrong axis for GUI buffers. A widget-only buffer resolves to ViewMode::UiOnly (editor/mod.rs:322 widget_only_scratch_buffer_should_show_ui, applied at mod.rs:2959/4778), which already means 'no text pane exists here'. Let editor_accepts_live_keyboard_input accept when the mode opts in OR the active buffer is UiOnly, keeping every focus-level suppression intact (minibuffer/prompt, focused text-input/textbox/patcher-text-edit, editing number-picker). That preserves all three eseq-4o9 symptoms' fixes, which were about TextOnly/Both code buffers, and is self-maintaining for future GUI buffers.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Armed track + focused *piano-roll* / *samples* / *arrangement* / *transport*: home-row keys fire live notes.
- Roll mode + focused number-picker: digits still type into the picker.
- Roll mode + code buffer: ';' still inserts a semicolon, no SequenceRoll.
- Armed track + code buffer: home-row keys still insert characters, no KeyboardTrigger.
- Browser search field focused in *samples*: typing still types.
- Regression test covers a UiOnly buffer accepting live keys and a TextOnly buffer refusing them.
close_reason: Fixed in crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs: editor_accepts_live_keyboard_input now admits ViewMode::UiOnly buffers alongside modes that declare :live-keys, so widget-only buffers (piano roll, sample browser, arrangement, transport, patch-mixer, macro tables) get live keys without each having to register a major mode. All focus-level suppression is unchanged, so the three eseq-4o9 symptoms (number-picker digits, ';' in a code buffer, home-row in a code buffer) stay fixed — those buffers are TextOnly/Both. Regression test widget_only_buffers_accept_live_keys_without_a_mode_opt_in covers UiOnly accept / opt-in-less text buffer reject / TextOnly reject. input::live_keyboard_tests 49/49 pass. NOT yet verified by the user in the running app.

title: Context menu opens at the wrong position when the clicked widget is inside a scrolled container
description:
Right-clicking a mixer track/group whose content is scrolled inside its viewport buffer opens the context-menu panel far from the pointer (observed: well to the LEFT of the click). Unscrolled clicks anchor correctly.

Likely cause: mouse events reach widgets in CONTENT space — widget_interaction.rs adds widget_layout_scroll_left() / total_scroll_top() (and the scroll widget's offset_y) to the local pointer position before dispatch — and box_mouse_info() (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/box_widget.rs:126) hands that value straight through as the event's :col/:row, documented as 'absolute pointer position in tile-local layout cells'. But context-menu places its panel against current_frame_viewport() in tile/frame space (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/context_menu.rs, anchored_panel_rect + layout_children). Any scroll/pan offset between the hit node's container and the tile frame is therefore added to the anchor and never subtracted back. Confirm which offset produces the horizontal shift (the mixer strip area pans horizontally; the tile buffer also scrolls vertically) — the flip-left branch of anchored_panel_rect may also be firing on an out-of-range anchor.

Call sites: crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp %open-track-menu / %open-group-menu pass :col/:row straight into :anchor-col/:anchor-row.
acceptance_criteria:
- Right-clicking a track/group header anchors the context menu at the pointer regardless of the horizontal or vertical scroll position of any ancestor container.
- Holds for the mixer badge/strip menu and the group-header menu, expanded and collapsed strips.
- The anchor coordinate space (content vs frame) is documented, and a regression test covers a non-zero scroll offset.
close_reason: Fixed: current_frame_viewport now reports the frame in content space (LayoutEngine::content_scroll), so frame-anchored widgets clamp/flip in the same space as the pointer anchor. Commit 9e7fa476.

title: Text-editing focus should suppress sequencer/roll/live-keyboard shortcuts
description:
Global sequencer key handling ignores text-editing focus in three places, so typing hijacks the transport/live keyboard.

## Symptoms
1. Roll mode + focused number-picker: digits set the roll rate instead of typing into the picker. Focus should win.
