2. Roll mode + code/text buffer: `;` triggers the sequence roll, so comments cannot be typed.
3. Armed tracks + code/text buffer: home-row keys fire live-keyboard notes while typing.

## Root cause
The "am I typing?" predicate is too narrow and applied unevenly.

- `crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:78` `focused_widget_captures_text_input` matches only `text-input` / `textbox` / patcher-text-edit. A `number-picker` in edit mode (`number_picker_edit_state(widget_id).editing`, see input.rs:847/915) is NOT text input by this predicate, so symptom 1 slips through.
- `crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:413` `is_active_roll_rate_key` checks only `roll_mode` + no modifiers, with no focus/buffer test at all; `crates/sequencer/src/ui/event_loop.rs:827` uses it as an OR-gate to enter the recording path.
- `crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:428` `should_route_to_live_keyboard` (the one real gate) checks focused-widget text capture but never the active buffer's `ViewMode`. In a code buffer (`ViewMode::TextOnly` / `Both` with text focus) there is often no focused widget at all, so symptoms 2 and 3 pass straight through into `handle_recording_key`.
- The sequence-roll hold binding is resolved even earlier (`event_loop.rs:823` `buffer_mode_keybinding("*sequencer*", key)`) and is OR'd in ahead of any focus test.

## Proposed fix: one "text mode" predicate, checked once at the seam
Introduce a single `editor_is_text_editing(&Editor) -> bool` in `input.rs` that is true when ANY of:
- `focused_widget_captures_text_input` (existing),
- the focused widget is a `number-picker` with `number_picker_edit_state(id).editing`,
- the minibuffer prompt / prompt text is active,
- the active buffer's text pane has keyboard focus (i.e. `ViewMode::TextOnly`, or not `UiOnly` with no focused widget) — note `active_buffer_accepts_global_ui_shortcuts` (input.rs:99) already encodes the `UiOnly` half of this and should be expressed in terms of the new helper.

Then gate on it in the three places above:
- `is_active_roll_rate_key` returns false when text-editing.
- `should_route_to_live_keyboard` returns false when text-editing (already partially true; widen to the new predicate) — this covers live notes AND the roll-rate/hold paths since they all funnel through it.
- the `sequence_roll_binding` OR in `event_loop.rs:836` must not bypass the gate; keep Release handling for already-held notes so a note held before focus changed still gets its note-off (`held_note_for_key` path must stay exempt).

Rule of thumb to encode in the doc comment: **focus supersedes mode.** Sequencer shortcuts are only live when the keyboard is not owned by a text/numeric editor.

## Acceptance
- Roll mode on + number-picker editing: digits type into the picker, roll rate unchanged.
- Roll mode on + code buffer focused: `;` inserts a semicolon, no `SequenceRoll` command emitted.
- Tracks armed + code buffer focused: home-row keys insert characters, no `KeyboardTrigger` sent.
- Note-off for keys pressed BEFORE entering text mode still fires (no stuck notes).
- All existing gates keep working in `*sequencer*` UI-only buffers.

Tests: extend `mod live_keyboard_tests` in `crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:1961` with cases per symptom.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in major-mode live keys, editor-focus suppression, and regression coverage; targeted tests pass.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
## Vim interaction (asked during triage)

Gating this seam FIXES vim rather than regressing it.

Today a note-key press returns `RecordingKeyOutcome::Consumed` (input.rs:1803) and `event_loop.rs:883` skips `editor.handle_key` when consumed. So with tracks armed + a code buffer focused, vim NORMAL-mode motions (h/j/k/l/w/b) are already swallowed by the live keyboard and never reach vim. This is a 4th symptom of the same bug.

### Predicate choice — matters only in vim normal mode
- **A: `key_starts_text_insert`** (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:5706, currently private). Already vim-aware: false in Normal, true in Insert; also handles read-only, UiOnly, save/minibuffer prompts. Fixes symptoms 1-3 but leaves normal-mode motions eaten by armed tracks.
- **B: buffer-focus based** (recommended). Suppress whenever a text pane owns the keyboard, regardless of vim mode — in Normal mode vim genuinely wants ';', 'j', 'd' for itself.

Take B. It is consistent with the rest of input.rs: `global_sequencer_navigation_available` (input.rs:140) and `shortcut_context_allows_sequencer_tab_switch` (input.rs:194) already gate on ViewMode / `active_buffer_accepts_global_ui_shortcuts`. The live-keyboard seam is the only shortcut family that never got that gate.

Trade-off to accept: roll/live-play stop working while a code buffer has focus — switch panes rather than pressing Esc. Cmd/Ctrl-modified shortcuts are unaffected either way (`should_route_to_live_keyboard` already bails on those modifiers, input.rs:443).

Extra acceptance case: tracks armed + code buffer in vim NORMAL mode -> h/j/k/l perform vim motions and trigger no notes.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
## REVISED DESIGN — opt-in, not opt-out (supersedes the A/B choice above)

Emacs-style `define-mode` buffers break the 'is this a text mode?' framing entirely.

### Why both earlier predicates fail
`define-mode` + `mode-bind-key` modes are read-only text buffers that bind BARE keys:
- `dired-mode` (crates/eseqlisp/init.lisp:70-74): binds g / q / - / RET
- `buffer-list-mode` (init.lisp:190): `:on-key buflist-handle-key`
- `seq-script-picker-mode` (crates/sequencer/ui/seq-script-picker.lisp:127)

Confirmed collision: dired's `g` is the live-keyboard G note (input.rs:1494). With any track armed, `g` in dired fires a synth and dired-refresh never runs.

- **Predicate A (`key_starts_text_insert`) is OUT**: it returns false when `active_buffer().read_only` (mod.rs:5717), so every dired-style mode stays broken.
- **Predicate B (ViewMode-based) is OUT**: the sequencer's OWN buffers are read-only `define-mode` buffers too — `eseq.seq-grid-mode/seq-grid-mode` (seq-grid-mode.lisp:80), `seq-mixer-mode` (mixer.lisp:1669), `seq-fx-mode` (effects/buffers.lisp:264), `eseq.effects.buffers/seq-plock-panel-mode` (effects/buffers.lisp:280). These WANT live keys. No text-vs-not test separates dired from the grid.

### Recommended: invert the default
Add `:live-keys true` to `define-mode` (crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/natives.rs:273), **defaulting false**. Only the sequencer's own modes declare it. Then `should_route_to_live_keyboard` asks exactly one question: does the active buffer's mode claim live keys?

Benefits: no 'am I typing' heuristic at all; code buffers, dired, buffer-list, the script picker, and any FUTURE mode get their keys back by default rather than needing to be added to an ever-stale exclusion list.

Layered on top, within an opted-in mode:
1. focused text-input / textbox / patcher-text-edit still wins (existing `focused_widget_captures_text_input`)
2. number-picker with `number_picker_edit_state(id).editing` still wins (symptom 1 — the new part)
3. held-note Release stays exempt via `held_note_for_key` so nothing sticks

### Scope of the collision
Live-keyboard chars (input.rs:1485): a w s e d f t g y h u j k l o — covers most of vim normal mode AND dired's g.
Roll-rate keys (data.rs:338): digits 1-9 — collides with number-picker numeric entry and any digit binding a mode defines.

### Added acceptance cases
- Track armed + dired focused: `g` refreshes dired, no note fires.
- Track armed + buffer-list focused: `:on-key` handler receives the key.
- Roll mode on + `*sequencer*` grid focused: rate digits and roll hold STILL work (no regression on opted-in modes).

### Migration note
Audit every `define-mode` call site for whether it needs `:live-keys true`; grep shows ~8 registrations across init.lisp, mixer.lisp, seq-grid-mode.lisp, effects/buffers.lisp, seq-script-picker.lisp.

title: Delete % semantics + update specs
description: Spec §6 step 4. Remove is_private_name (crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/modules.rs:44) and both warning sites (compiler.rs:1275 qualified-access warning, compiler.rs:1979 override warning); every named module now uses export semantics unconditionally (zero export forms = exports nothing, meaningful rather than legacy mode). Delete the opt-in coexistence branch from .1. Grep the tree for surviving %-prefixed lisp symbols — should be zero in named modules. title: Convert the ui tree module by module
description: Spec §6 steps 2-3. Run the .2 script over every named module under crates/sequencer/ui, one module or coherent family per commit (mixer, seqv, effects.*, arrangement, ...). After each commit: cargo test -p sequencer (scoped; the state_values tests drive lisp by name and are the canary for Rust-driven-name breakage), plus a UI boot smoke check if available. 1176 symbols / ~3848 occurrences total. Headerless eseq.vanilla files are NOT converted (they stay fully public, spec §2.6). If a module fails conversion for a reason the script cannot express, file a discovered-from bead and skip it rather than hand-hacking; the epic closes only when zero named modules carry % semantics.
notes: Implemented in commit e6855beb. Converted 67 of 68 named UI modules to explicit exports and stripped owned % private names; normalized qualified :refer entries and fixed migration handling for qualified definitions. crates/sequencer/ui/legacy/mixer.lisp was skipped per bead instructions because malformed nesting hides most apparent definitions from the migration; follow-up eseq-xpt.6 was filed as discovered-from. Validation: module_export_migration tests (5), main reverse-order UI boot, builtin FX load, mixer widget-tree load, five Lisp parse/load canaries, and git diff --check all pass.

title: Resolve %/bare name collisions
description: Spec §6 step 2c. ~25 global-upper-bound candidates where a stripped %name would collide with an existing bare definition (e.g. %selected-track vs selected-track, %close vs close, %number-knob vs number-knob). Only same-module pairs are true collisions — run the .2 script's collision report per module to get the real list. For each true collision, hand-rename the PRIVATE half to something more specific (it is private; its name is cheap to change) in its own commit, keeping tests green. Do not rename the public half — Rust may drive it by name.
close_reason: Closed

title: Migration script: generate exports, strip %
description: Spec §6 step 2. A tools/ bin (warn+migrate posture like the alias-era .13 bin) that converts ONE module (or dotted family) at a time: (a) collect the module's unprefixed module-level definitions and emit an (export ...) block under the imports; (b) strip % from every occurrence of the module's own private names, module-scoped; (c) rewrite tree-wide qualified references to this module's former %-names (spec §6 step 3); (d) REFUSE to convert a module where stripping collides with an existing bare definition — print the colliding pair and exit nonzero; (e) --dry-run mode printing the diff. Must handle all definers (def/defn/defstate/defmacro/defhook) and % occurrences inside strings/comments conservatively (skip comments, flag strings for review — Rust drives some names as strings). Test the bin on ui/mixer.lisp with --dry-run and eyeball before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: export form: Rust semantics + enforcement
description: Implement spec §2-§3 in crates/eseqlisp. (a) modules.rs: per-module export-set storage + helpers. (b) compiler.rs: compile top-level (export sym ...) — bare unqualified symbols only, list-shaped elements are errors (reserved for re-export §5), error inside function bodies, error in headerless eseq.vanilla files; multiple forms union; position-independent. (c) vm.rs eval_module_source: end-of-unit validation — every exported name must be defined in the module, else load-time error naming the symbol + form location. (d) Enforcement at existing choke points: :refer of non-exported = hard compile error; qualified M/name of non-exported = warning (reuse the %-warning slot compiler.rs:1275); override of non-exported = warning (slot compiler.rs:1979). (e) OPT-IN COEXISTENCE (spec §6 step 1): a module with zero export forms keeps legacy %-semantics; any export form switches it to export semantics and its %-names become plain names. (f) REPL: export appends to current module's set. (g) Verify spec §7.2: runtime by-name lookups (VM::resolve_global_read_index, Rust-driven names like mixer-v2-*/seq-ctrl-g) bypass visibility — enforcement is compile-time only; add a test proving a non-exported symbol still resolves by name from the host. Unit tests for all of a-g in the style of the existing modules/compiler tests. Scoped tests: cargo test -p eseqlisp.
close_reason: Closed

title: Module exports: private-by-default + (export ...), retire % prefix
description:
Replace %-prefix module privacy with export lists: private by default, public symbols declared in position-independent top-level (export sym ...) forms, mirror of import. Spec: docs/module-export-spec.md (rev 1, ratified decisions: qualified access to internals WARNS for hackability; :refer of non-exported is a hard error; exporting an undefined symbol is a load-time error). Parent spec docs/module-system-spec.md rev 3 §2 decision 4 is superseded at migration end.

Scale measured 2026-08-19: 1176 unique % symbols, ~3848 occurrences in crates/sequencer/ui; 25 global-upper-bound collision candidates where stripped %name matches an existing bare definition.

FOR THE OVERNIGHT AGENT: work the children strictly in id order (.1 -> .5); each is gated on the previous. Per-module/per-slice commits are explicitly authorized by the user for this epic (commit, do NOT push). House rules: scoped cargo tests only (-p eseqlisp / -p sequencer, never package-wide fmt), NEVER git stash (use worktrees if needed), never git checkout shared files. If a step hits a wall, file a discovered-from bead with findings and stop rather than improvising around the spec.
close_reason: All 6 children complete (.1-.6). Export migration shipped: PR #52 merged from workflow/eseq-xpt; commits e6855beb, d177c7ee (.4), 5b0d7b75 (.5), 0ff05b3b + f785442a (.6). % privacy prefix retired in favor of private-by-default plus explicit (export ...) forms.

title: Gut the bus gate step sequencer feature
description:
Remove the bus gate step sequencer entirely. Buses currently carry a step sequencer (\`bus.gate_sequence\`) that gates/mutes the bus per step. The editing UI for it was removed, but the feature and its key bindings survive, causing a recurring UX trap: Ctrl-A ("select-all-bus-steps") + Backspace ("delete-selected-bus-steps") in bus-grid.lisp can silently delete all gate steps for a bus, muting it with no visible way to recover. Gutting the feature also removes per-block gate evaluation from the audio path (small perf win).

Scope (from grep, 2026-08-19):
- Key bindings + orphaned UI: crates/sequencer/ui/bus-grid.lisp (host-command "select-all-bus-steps" at :160, "delete-selected-bus-steps" at :163); check step-grid-interactions.lisp / main.lisp for references.
- Host commands: crates/sequencer/src/ui/host_commands/bus_steps.rs (whole module: toggle-bus-step, set-bus-step-*, select-*, delete-selected-bus-steps, move/shift, set-bus-sequencer-param) + registration in host_commands/mod.rs and dispatch.rs.
- App/model: bus.gate_sequence + publish_bus_gate_runtime in src/app/{mod.rs,edit.rs,history.rs,projects.rs}; ui/state_values/track_and_mixer.rs; ui/natives.rs.
- Engine: src/sequencer/state/bus_pattern.rs, scenes.rs, sequencer_state/repository_edit.rs; audio/{stream,callback,render,state,engine}.rs gate evaluation.
- Serialization: project.rs — decide how to handle existing saved gate_sequence data (ignore/drop on load; keep loading old projects without error).
- Tests: src/ui/tests.rs, src/sequencer/state/tests.rs, src/audio/tests.rs.

Acceptance:
- Ctrl-A/Backspace in bus context no longer mutes a bus; the commands are gone.
- No gate_sequence evaluation in the audio callback.
- Old project files still load (gate data silently dropped).
- Scoped tests pass (-p sequencer).
close_reason: Gutted end to end in 9928d5ef: bus-grid.lisp + host_commands/bus_steps.rs deleted, BusGateSequence and all SEQ.bus-step* reactive values removed, gate evaluation out of the audio callback (BusGateRuntimeState -> BusEffectRuntimeState, effect slots only). Old projects still load; new test in project.rs covers the dropped gate_sequence field. Scoped tests: sequencer --lib and --bin metal_seq green apart from 8 failures confirmed pre-existing at HEAD via worktree.

title: Persist custom track names across project save/load
description:
**Symptom:** Load an instrument-rack preset (a .sound with a preset name) onto a track, save the project, reload — every rack track comes back as "Layer Rack". Any renamed/preset-named track loses its name on reload, which makes multi-rack projects unreadable.

**Root cause:** ProjectTrack (src/project.rs:1353) serializes only id/color/collapsed/kind — the display name (app.tracks[idx]) is never written. On load, names are re-derived from ProjectTrackKind: Sampler -> sample title, Custom -> instrument name, Rack -> hardcoded "Layer Rack" (app/projects.rs:3491 legacy by_pitch path, and the v-current Rack path derives similarly). The runtime name set by replace_track_instrument_container_with_rack (app/projects.rs:1668, preset display name) exists only in memory.

**Fix sketch:**
- Add `name: Option<String>` to ProjectTrack + ProjectTrackWire with skip_serializing_if None (backward + forward compatible, no version bump needed — old files just have no name and keep derived defaults).
- On save: write app.tracks[idx] for every track (or only when it differs from the derived default, but always-write is simpler and unambiguous).
- On load: after each track is created (all ProjectTrackKind arms incl. both rack paths), if saved name is Some and non-empty, overwrite app.tracks[idx] with it.
- Also confirm group/bus names already persist (ProjectBusChannel has name — buses are fine).

**Acceptance:**
- Round-trip test: create rack track, set a custom name, save, load, name survives.
- Load-rack-preset -> save -> load keeps the preset name.
- Old project files (no name field) still load with derived names.

This is independent of any rename UI — it fixes the preset-name loss immediately.
close_reason: Persisted optional track display names on project save/load with rack and legacy compatibility coverage

title: Transport goes silent after drag-drop sample audition into an instrument rack containing a sampler
description:
Repro: while the transport is playing, drag and drop a sample into an instrument rack that contains a sampler (auditioning the sample). The transport keeps moving (playhead advances) but ALL tracks stop producing sound — not just the rack's track. Pressing pause and then play again restores playback.

Needs exploration/root-cause: something in the sample-audition/hot-swap path appears to stall or wedge the audio-side scheduling for every track (voice pool wipe? route close? preflight latch?) while the UI-side transport keeps running. Possibly related to known patterns: stop-resync wiping latched override pins (latch-override-pin-stop-bug), idle-route close zeroing voice gain (scene-switch-voice-mute-bug), or the instrument swap/rebind path (docs/instrument-swap-spec.md).

Scope: instrument rack (slot-based v1), sampler in a slot, drag-drop audition. Check whether the same happens on a plain (non-rack) sampler track.
close_reason: Fixed in b86cc011: rack slot edits published the scheduler snapshot before bumping topology/pattern epochs, so the audio callback dropped every event (all tracks) stamped with the stale pattern_epoch until pause/play republished. Reordered in replace_layer_rack_slot_source, delete_rack_slot, convert_track_instrument_container_to_rack, replace_track_instrument_container_with_rack; regression test added.

title: Saving an instrument rack (with Filter Table in a chain) as a sound preset writes a corrupted .sound
description:
REPRO (user, 2026-08-19): Take a working track with a custom instrument (core/drift preset "Lush Shark Pad") and an effect chain including a Filter Table plus builtins (Str8 Delay, Space Echo, Filterbank, 2x Compressor). Group the track into an INSTRUMENT rack (slot-based rack, not drum rack v2). Save the rack as a sound preset. The written .sound is corrupted.

EVIDENCE — checked-in example: crates/sequencer/sounds/lush-filter-tab-pad.sound (version 8). Concrete anomalies visible in the JSON:
1. track.slots[0].instrument_name is "core/drift/" — a trailing-slash path with the leaf (preset/instrument name) missing. Something truncated or joined the name wrong during rack capture (track_sound_state.loaded_preset still knows "Lush Shark Pad").
2. custom_effects is ["Filter Table","builtin:Str8 Delay","builtin:Space Echo","builtin:Filterbank","builtin:Compressor","builtin:Compressor",null,null] — every builtin carries the "builtin:" prefix EXCEPT "Filter Table", which is serialized as if it were a custom DGenLisp effect. Filter Table is in builtin_effect_names() but NOT builtin_insert_names() (effects/mod.rs pinned-lists test ~line 1502) — likely the classifier used at save time consults the insert list, so Filter Table falls through to the custom branch, and load-time resolution of a custom effect named "Filter Table" then fails or mangles the slot. Suspect the bug generalizes to any builtin_effect_names-only effect (check "Convolution Reverb" too).
3. Param tables are wildly inflated and cross-contaminated: the Str8 Delay slot claims num_params 104, Space Echo 106, Filterbank 188, and the instrument slot 190 — far beyond those effects' real param counts — and the SAME 72-entry block of ids 1000000064..1000000135 appears verbatim in the instrument slot AND the first four effect slots' param_node_indices. That 1e9-range block looks like a shared/global (macro- or rack-scope?) param-node id space being appended into every slot's capture. Also present: 4294967295 (u32::MAX) unmapped sentinels and six-digit node ids (140382..140406) in the Filter Table slot. The two Compressor slots look sane (21 params) — so the contamination correlates with the mis-classified/mis-captured slots.
4. The Filter Table slot at least keeps its "table":"fltab:notch-mesa" reference.

TASK:
- Reproduce: build the track as above (any custom instrument + Filter Table + a couple of builtins), group into an instrument rack, save the rack as a sound preset; confirm the written file shows the anomalies (and characterize what loading it actually does — silent wrong sound, load error, or crash).
- Root-cause the rack save path: writer is project.rs save_sound_preset (project.rs:2505), called from app/projects.rs:1949; the interesting part is how the rack branch captures per-slot instrument_name, the custom_effects names (builtin classification), and param_node_indices for each slot. Compare against the single-track (non-rack) sound save, which the user reports works.
- Fix so a rack save round-trips: correct instrument_name capture, Filter Table (and any builtin_effect_names-only builtin) serialized with the builtin: prefix / correct classification, per-slot param tables containing only that slot's params with correctly-scoped node indices.
- Decide/handle existing corrupted files: at minimum loading one must not crash; a load-time repair for the mis-prefixed "Filter Table" name is nice-to-have. Delete or regenerate the checked-in lush-filter-tab-pad.sound example as appropriate.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Regression test: build a rack containing a custom instrument + Filter Table + at least one prefixed builtin, save as sound preset, reload into a fresh project — instrument name intact, all effects present with correct types, per-slot param counts match the live descriptors, no 1000000064+/u32::MAX ids leak into unrelated slots.
2. The repro above, done by hand in the app, yields a preset that loads back to a sounding rack equivalent to the saved one.
3. Loading a pre-fix corrupted file does not crash.
4. Scoped tests for the touched modules pass (-p sequencer).
close_reason: Root cause: rack-slot chains save custom_effect_names verbatim, and the DGenLisp-builtin writers stored bare names, so 'Filter Table' loaded as a missing custom effect. Fixed in 1df9d906: shared builtin classifier (native + dgen) used by every rack-slot writer plus the save-side conversion; load side accepts bare names so pre-fix files repair; added the missing rack-slot Filter Table/conv-reverb IR restore; repaired lush-filter-tab-pad.sound. Regression test app::graph::tests::rack_preset_round_trips_dgen_hosted_builtins. Bead anomalies 1 and 3 (trailing-slash instrument name, inflated param tables / 1e9 id block) were false alarms - every working .sound has them.

title: Note-positional drum rack pad grid: cells map to MIDI notes, not insertion order
description:
INTENT (from user screenshots, 2026-08-19): The drum rack pad grid must work like Ableton's — each pad cell IS a fixed MIDI note position, and pads render sparsely at their note's cell. Today, dragging a sample onto the bottom-left cell creates a pad labeled C5 (the note mapping works), but the pad then RENDERS in the top-left cell, because the grid draws pads[bank*16 + cell] in insertion (chronological) order. The label and the position contradict each other.

CURRENT CODE (all UI-side; the data model already carries pad_note per pad and needs no change):
- crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp:1756-1775 — %pad-grid-bank / %pad-grid-banks / %pad-index / %pad-at: banks of 16 over the ORDERED pads vec; %pad-grid-banks counts len(pads)+1 over 16.
- crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp:1910-1913 — %pad-grid-row draws row 0 at the TOP, cell = row*4+col.
- crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp:1814-1833 — %drop-on-empty-pad asks pad-note-for-cell for a note.
- crates/sequencer/ui/drum-rack-v2.lisp:222 — pad-note-for-cell: wants the raw pad-vec index as the note, falls back to next-free on collision.
- docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md — "ordered; pad grid position = index" is the line this feature obsoletes; pads stay an ordered vec in the project model, only the grid's addressing changes. Update the spec's UI section to describe note-positional layout.

NEW LAYOUT MODEL:
- A visible page shows 16 consecutive MIDI notes in a 4x4 grid. Within a page: BOTTOM-left cell = lowest note of the page; notes ascend left-to-right, then bottom-to-top (Ableton convention). This inverts the current row order — top row currently renders first.
- Pages are OCTAVE-ALIGNED: page k starts at note 12*k, so the bottom-left cell of every page is a C, and shows notes [12k, 12k+16) — 16 notes spanning an octave and a third, with a 4-note overlap between adjacent pages (this is what keeps bottom-left = C; a non-overlapping 16-stride cannot). Clamp the top page so no cell addresses a note > 127. If the implementer finds octave-overlap pages fight some existing invariant, the fallback is Ableton's row-scroll (page start moves in 4-note rows); either way bottom-left of the default page positions must land on C — plain 16-note strides (0,16,32…) are NOT acceptable.
- Cell -> note is now a pure function of (page, row, col). Rendering a cell looks up the pad whose pad_note equals that note (nil = empty cell). Pads whose note falls outside the visible page are simply on another page — sparse is correct, no compaction.
- %pad-cell keeps its current anatomy (drop targets, replace-on-occupied, click = select + trigger, choke badge); only the pad it resolves for a cell changes.

DROP SEMANTICS:
- Dropping on an EMPTY cell maps the new pad to EXACTLY that cell's note — no next-free fallback (an occupied cell can't be hit by the empty-drop path, so collision is impossible). pad-note-for-cell's index-as-note heuristic dies with the old addressing. Lazy-pad drops (empty cell claims a track, commit f98dc020) must keep working with the exact-note semantics.
- Drops that DON'T name a cell (mixer group-header drop, track-badge drag, move-track-to-group) keep the existing lowest-free-note behavior from the spec — out of scope here.

PAGE STATE / NAVIGATION:
- Keep the existing prev/next selector UI (sequencer.lisp:1915) but page over the fixed note range, showing something note-meaningful (e.g. the octave label "C3" or "C3–E4") instead of "1/2".
- Default page when a rack panel opens: the lowest page containing an occupied pad (a rack whose kit lives at C5 must not open onto four empty octaves); an empty rack defaults to the C3-ish middle. Note %pad-grid-bank is currently a single global defstate shared across racks — per-rack (keyed by group id) is preferred; at minimum re-derive the default when the selected rack changes.
- Page count/navigation must no longer derive from len(pads): the navigable range is the note range (all octaves 0..127, or at least every page from lowest-occupied to highest-occupied plus headroom for placing new pads on any octave).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Dropping a sample on the bottom-left cell of the visible page creates the pad AND renders it in that same cell, labeled with that cell's note (a C when it's the page's bottom-left).
2. A rack whose pads live at scattered notes (e.g. C5 + F#5) renders them sparsely at their note cells with empty cells between; no pad ever renders at a cell whose note differs from its pad_note.
3. Bottom-left of every page is a C; notes ascend left-to-right, bottom-to-top; page navigation reaches any pad in an existing kit and shows note/octave labels.
4. Opening the *fx* panel for a rack with pads only at C5 shows the page containing C5 without manual paging.
5. Existing behaviors survive: pad click = select + trigger, occupied-cell drop replaces the member's sound in place, lazy-pad empty drop claims a track at the cell's note, nudge-pad-note moves the pad to the neighboring cell (possibly across a page edge).
6. docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md UI section updated: grid position derives from pad_note, not vec index.
close_reason: Closed

title: Drum rack v2: every member-add path must map a pad (mixer drops produce unreachable padless members)
description:
Dropping a sample onto a drum rack's mixer group-header strip adds a member track but no pad mapping, so the sound is invisible in the pad grid and unplayable via pad-play/arming. Root cause (verified 2026-08-19): ProjectRackPad entries are ONLY created by attach_track_to_group when pad_note is Some (app/edit.rs:2583-2585), and the only non-test callers passing Some are 'add-track-rack' creation-with-sample (ui/host_commands/tracks.rs:145-165, first pad only) and kit load (app/projects.rs:1845). The mixer drop path — drop-on-group-header (ui/mixer.lisp:1192-1249) → 'add-track-sample' with no :pad-note → tracks.rs:315-341 reads pad-note=None → attach_track_to_group(..., None) — appends to group.members with no pad. Same for 'move-track-to-group' / track-badge drag (mixer.lisp:179-185). Since the grid renders exclusively from rack.pads (build_rack_pads_value, ui/state_values/steps_and_pattern.rs:526-553; %pad-at in ui/sequencer.lisp:1770-1773) and pad/key resolution goes only through rack_pad_track (project.rs:1043-1047, input.rs:1562-1573, silently ignoring unmapped notes), a padless member is unreachable: 3 sample members can render as member rows while all 16 pad cells sit empty.

Fix: when a track joins a group that has a rack config, auto-assign the next free pad note (from DRUM_RACK_FIRST_PAD_NOTE upward, skipping taken notes) in EVERY attach path — sample/instrument drop on the group header, move-track-to-group, badge drag, and any future add-to-group entry — ideally centralized inside attach_track_to_group itself (rack group + pad_note None → auto-assign) so callers can't get it wrong, while still honoring an explicit pad_note when provided (the 'pad-note' payload plumbing at tracks.rs:319 / host_commands/mod.rs:488-501 already exists). Also handle existing damage: projects already saved with padless rack members should be repaired on load (assign free pads in member order) or at minimum surfaced — decide and note. Undo of the attach must remove the auto-created pad too (pads remap via remap_after_member_removed, project.rs:1117-1126).
acceptance_criteria: Dropping a sample or instrument onto a drum rack's mixer group header creates a member WITH a pad mapping: it appears in the pad grid with its badge, is playable by pad click and armed key, and choke selector renders (no 'no pad' placeholder); move-track-to-group into a rack maps a pad likewise; explicit pad-note payloads still win; pads exhausted (16 mapped) is handled gracefully (defined behavior, no panic); loading a project saved with padless members yields playable pads or a documented surfaced state; undoing the add removes both member and pad; regression tests cover the group-header drop path end-to-end and the auto-assign-next-free-note logic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Filter Table: type dropdown selection is a no-op (regression)
description:
Regression in the Filter Table builtin effect panel: the filter-table TYPE dropdown (top-left, e.g. 'Procedural Shapes') no longer applies a selection. Repro: open a Filter Table effect on a track, click the type dropdown — options render correctly — click a different option: nothing happens. The spectrum visualizer does not change, the dropdown's displayed selection does not change, no error is shown. The neighboring phase-mode dropdown ('Min Phase') and knobs may or may not share the fault — verify both while diagnosing.

Observed 2026-08-18 on main with local working-tree changes. Note: crates/sequencer/ui/effects/builtin/filter-table.lisp has uncommitted modifications in the working tree (rack-panel/capture-fixture work also touched ui/state_values/rack_panel.rs and ui/capture-fixtures/rack-filter-table-panel.lisp) — first bisect whether the regression comes from those local edits or is already on committed main. Likely suspects: the dropdown's on-change handler / reactive binding in filter-table.lisp no longer reaching the host command that swaps the table type, or the host command failing silently (check ui/host_commands/effects.rs and reactive sync paths). Related recent work: filter-table feature branch merged in PR #50, plus dylib-cache exclusive-lease changes (eseq-599).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting any option in the Filter Table type dropdown updates the displayed selection, swaps the underlying filter table (spectrum visualizer redraws to the new family), and the change is audible/persisted with the effect state; a regression test (widget/capture or host-command level) covers dropdown selection applying the type change; root cause noted on the bead (local-edit vs committed regression).
notes: Root cause is confined to the pre-existing local rack-panel refactor, not committed main: filter-table.lisp passed a second map to merge, but merge accepts a target map followed by key/value pairs. The resulting set-filter-table-source/engine commands omitted :path/:engine, so host dispatch had nothing to apply. Corrected calls to (merge target :path path)/(merge target :engine engine), including drop metadata, and added track-panel regression assertions for complete dropdown command payloads. Existing live-graph tests cover table upload/persistence and engine recompilation.
close_reason: Fixed the local Filter Table command-payload regression and added dropdown callback coverage; targeted UI and live-graph checks pass.

title: PDC: p-locked sends flam — send edges excluded from the latency plan when baseline amount is 0
description:
Repro: add a latency-inducing effect anywhere in the project (e.g. Filter Table, which raises total mix latency), then p-lock a track's bus send (baseline send amount 0) and trigger a step. The sample audibly flams — plays twice, offset by exactly the project latency — even when the destination bus has NO fx. The direct track path is compensated; the send path is not.

Likely root cause (verified in code, confirm with a render): compute_latency_plan's topology builder (crates/sequencer/src/app/graph/latency.rs ~295-301) collects a track's send edges as params.sends() filtered by send.amount > 0.0. A p-locked send leaves the BASELINE amount at 0 while the send gain node is opened at trigger time by the p-lock, so:
- the send edge is dropped from LatencyTopology.tracks[i].sends → no send_pad is computed/applied to that edge's PDC node (the per-send pdc node created in bus_routing.rs apply_track_bus_sends),
- the track may also be excluded from the destination bus's input-latency max (latency.rs ~84-98: bus_inputs takes the max over tracks whose output or sends target the bus), skewing bus_pads too.
Result: the send arm reaches the bus (and then MIX) ahead of the compensated direct arm by the track's chain latency delta — heard as a flam at exactly the latency amount.

Also audit the adjacent cases while in here:
- Does apply_track_bus_sends even create the send nodes when baseline amount is 0? (If yes — which the audible flam implies — the plan and the graph disagree about which edges exist; make the plan follow the GRAPH edges, not the baseline value.)
- Latched/overridden send values (latch override pins) and scene-switch transients: any path where the effective send amount differs from params.sends() baseline has the same hole.
- A send p-lock on a track routed to a bus PRIMARY output (not just MIX) — same math via output_pads.

Fix direction: treat a send edge as present for latency purposes whenever its nodes exist in the graph (i.e. the send is configured at all), regardless of the current baseline amount — a padded silent edge costs one small delay node that's already allocated (the per-send pdc). That also removes a latency-plan rebuild when a send amount crosses zero (check whether crossing 0 today triggers a plan recompute mid-play — an audible pad jump on the first p-locked step would be a second bug from the same filter). Keep the amount>0 filter ONLY if it's needed to avoid counting never-configured default send slots — distinguish 'send slot exists with amount 0' from 'no send configured', or include all edges that apply_track_bus_sends materializes.

Coordination: eseq-81r (post-fx volume / post-fader sends) rewires what sends tap but keeps the send-edge pdc topology; whichever lands second re-verifies this test. Recent commit dde2066f (post-PDC sidechain taps and bus meters) is adjacent context.
acceptance_criteria: Render-level regression test: project with a known-latency effect on track A (or anywhere raising mix latency), track B sends p-locked (baseline 0) to an fx-less bus; rendering a single impulse trigger yields ONE aligned impulse at master (cross-correlate direct-only vs direct+send renders: peak offset 0, no secondary peak at the latency amount) — test fails before the fix with a secondary peak; same test green with baseline send amount > 0 (already-working case stays working); latched/override send values covered by at least one test or an explicit note ruling them out; no audible pad discontinuity when a send amount crosses zero during playback (plan does not churn per p-lock step); existing latency.rs + graph tests pass

title: Mixer: post-fx volume + post-fader meters and sends for tracks and buses
description:
Two coupled problems with the same root: (a) mixer meters show pre-fx level, (b) the volume fader is applied PRE-fx, so raising a track's volume drives its fx chain harder (e.g. slams tape saturation) instead of just scaling the track's output. Desired (standard DAW behavior): fx chain sees a fixed gain stage; volume is applied post-fx as the track's final output control; meters are post-fx/post-fader; bus sends tap post this volume (post-fader sends).

Current wiring (verified):
- Track (app/graph/node_build.rs create_track_shell): voice_sum -> pan_id (stereo_panner; push_track_volume in app/params.rs writes STEREO_PANNER_PARAM_VOLUME here, plus pan/mute/solo) -> [track fx chain inserts between pan and fx_out] -> fx_out_id (a second stereo_panner, currently pass-through; TrackShell.delay_id == fx_out_id) -> pdc -> output. Track mixer meters read the PAN node's peak state (ui/state_values/meters_and_modulation.rs read_track_peak_levels over pan_ids) — hence pre-fx. Bus sends tap delay_id (= fx_out) outputs (bus_routing.rs apply_track_bus_sends), i.e. post-fx but the volume that should precede them is upstream of the fx.
- Bus (app/graph/bus_routing.rs ~line 24-146): gate -> volume (gain node; push_bus_volume) -> [bus fx chain] -> pdc -> peak-meter node; verify exactly where the bus fx chain inserts relative to volume — the audible symptom says volume is upstream of the fx there too.
- Master/mix bus (audio/engine.rs ~172-260): mix_gate -> mix_volume -> mix_meter -> DAC, with the Mix bus FX chain feeding the bus; apply the same post-fx placement if it has the same problem.

Implementation sketch (track): move the volume application from pan_id to the existing post-fx fx_out_id stereo_panner — i.e. push_track_volume (and any scene/snapshot/p-lock writers of STEREO_PANNER_PARAM_VOLUME for the track main panner — grep for other writers, e.g. scene apply, project load, latch/override pin paths) target fx_out_id instead. Keep PAN itself where it is unless trivial to move (out of scope to relocate pan/mute semantics; note below). Sends already tap fx_out output, so they become post-fader for free once volume lives in fx_out. Meters: read fx_out's panner peak state instead of pan's (fx_out is NOT currently watchlisted — add add_node_to_watchlist for it, and remove pan from the watchlist if nothing else reads it). Bus: move the volume gain node to sit after the bus fx chain (or retarget which node push_bus_volume writes), and confirm the bus meter taps after it; bus sends-to-other-buses (if any) follow the same rule.

Watch out for:
- Mute/solo currently live on the pre-fx pan node. Post-fx mute is the DAW norm (mute kills the output AND the sends instantly); decide and document — simplest consistent choice: move muted/muted_by_solo to fx_out along with volume so mute/solo also gate the sends (today they do, since pan is upstream of everything; keep that property).
- Volume p-locks / scene parameters / rack contexts: rack slot mixers (slot_pan_id) and rack per-slot gain staging are explicitly OUT of scope — only the track main fader, bus fader, and master. But make sure scene switch, project load, undo restore, and latched-override paths that push volume all hit the new node (grep STEREO_PANNER_PARAM_VOLUME and push_track_volume callers).
- PDC/sidechain taps: recent commit dde2066f ('Fix post-PDC sidechain taps and bus meters') touched adjacent wiring — rebase on that and keep sidechain tap points semantically unchanged (sidechain taps should keep tapping what they tap today unless they tapped the fader node itself).
- Meter display should be post-PDC or pre-PDC consistently with today's bus meter behavior; pick post-fader/pre-PDC (fx_out output) for tracks so meter timing matches the existing feel, and note the choice.
- Existing projects: no serialization change — same volume values, new application point. Audible change for tracks using nonlinear fx is the POINT, but call it out in the handoff.
acceptance_criteria: With a saturating effect (e.g. tape/roar) on a track, sweeping the track volume changes output level WITHOUT changing the saturation character (verify by render: normalized spectra at two volume settings match within tolerance; today they differ); mixer track meter responds to fx output (e.g. a compressor/limiter visibly reduces the meter; muting the fx chain changes the meter); same verified for a bus with fx; sends scale with the track volume fader (post-fader: fader at -inf silences the send); mute/solo still silence both main out and sends; volume p-locks and scene switches still apply (targeted test); master chain behavior consistent; graph tests in app/graph/tests.rs extended for the new topology; scoped nextest suites for graph + state_values pass
notes:
Moved track volume, mute, and solo-mute to the existing post-FX fader node; track meters now read/watch that node, making existing bus sends post-fader. Verified bus FX hosts already terminate at post-FX volume and meters remain downstream; Mix bus already follows the same topology. Added graph regressions, including a live-graph signal test proving the track fader scales and silences the bus send/meter. Checks: cargo check -p sequencer --bin metal_seq; targeted nextest graph tests (3 passed).
Committed as cff8646d (Move mixer faders and meters post FX). Isolated-index validation against clean HEAD passed metal_seq check and all 3 targeted graph tests.
close_reason: Implemented post-FX track faders, post-fader track metering/sends, and topology regressions; confirmed existing bus/master post-FX ordering.

title: Conv reverb: async IR prep on a worker thread + busy spinner on the panel
description:
Dropping a sample onto the Convolution Reverb builtin freezes the whole UI: the set-convolution-reverb-ir host command runs prepare_ir synchronously on the main thread (crates/sequencer/src/effects/conv_reverb.rs — WAV decode, windowed-sinc resample of both channels, then a DGenLisp subprocess per channel for partition-ir; easily hundreds of ms to seconds on a cold cache). Make IR prep fully asynchronous with visible busy state.

Implementation — reuse the existing async-compile pattern (app/effects.rs ~3169: worker thread + std::sync::mpsc + PendingCompile polled by poll_pending_compile with an expected_node_id staleness guard):

1. In the set-convolution-reverb-ir path (and the track/bus/rack set_conv_reverb_ir* variants in app/effects.rs), capture path/reference/host_sr and the target's expected node_id, spawn a worker thread running prepare_ir, and register a pending-IR-prep entry (either extend PendingCompile with a new target variant or a parallel small struct polled from the same tick). Support multiple simultaneous preps (different instances) — unlike pending_compile's single slot — or explicitly serialize with a queue; either is fine, document the choice.
2. On completion, back on the main thread: re-validate the target still holds the same node_id (drop the result with a status message if the slot changed/removed), then run the existing apply path (apply_prepared_conv_reverb_ir_to_node) — tensor writes, record_prepared_ir, undo recording all stay main-thread. On error, surface the message via editor.status_message; the instance keeps its previous IR.
3. Supersede: a second drop on the same instance while a prep is in flight cancels/ignores the older result (compare a per-request sequence number, not just node_id).
4. Busy state: expose per-instance 'ir-loading' to the UI (alongside :ir-name in ui/state_values/effects_panel.rs) and show a spinner/progress treatment in the IMPULSE RESPONSE drop box in crates/sequencer/ui/effects/builtin/convolution-reverb.lisp (e.g. dim the name, animated indicator, 'Loading…' label) for track, bus, and rack-slot contexts. Clear on completion or error.
5. Project load (app/projects.rs restore_conv_reverb_ir_track/_bus/rack) currently blocks per instance too — route restores through the same async path so loading a project with several conv reverbs doesn't stall the UI; instances play dry (or with default IR) until their IR lands, which is acceptable.
6. Instance creation's bundled-default-IR load (app/effects.rs ~1708) can stay synchronous if it's fast from cache, but verify; if it measurably janks, route it through the same path.

Coordination with eseq-hsk.1 (related, NOT blocked): whichever lands second inherits a small merge — shape re-prep (set-convolution-reverb-ir-shape) must also go through the async path with the same supersede semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Dropping a large uncached sample onto the conv reverb leaves the UI fully interactive (no frame hitch beyond normal; verify by dropping while a knob drag or playback UI is animating); a spinner/loading state shows on the effect panel until the IR is applied, in track, bus, and rack contexts; rapid successive drops apply only the last one; deleting the effect or switching the slot mid-prep drops the result without panic or misapplied tensors; prep errors show a status message and keep the prior IR; project load with multiple conv reverb instances does not block the main thread; existing conv_reverb + effects tests pass

title: Show bus-send p-lock indicators and playback automation
description: Steps with track bus-send p-locks need the standard p-lock indicator, and track send knobs must follow the effective p-lock value at playback steps like synth parameter controls do, returning to the pattern baseline afterward.
notes: Added track-send locks to standard step p-lock render classification, and queued targeted StepBatch invalidations from send-lock knob edits so indicators appear immediately. Send knob bindings now use the same display-step precedence as synth/effect params (selected step, then playback playhead, then baseline); reactive playhead transitions refresh sends in FX/step/mixer views and restore baseline after leaving the lock. Added exact Metal tests for indicator kind and selected/playback/baseline knob values. AppCommand authoring regression and cargo check remain green.
close_reason: Implemented send p-lock step indicators and playhead-driven knob automation with regression coverage.

title: Route bus-send p-lock command through recorded step edits
description: SetTrackBusSendPlock is classified as recorded history but try_apply_command returns UnsupportedCommand because the command is missing from the recorded step-edit routing match. Add it to the proper step mutation path and test the actual AppCommand authoring flow.
notes: Root cause confirmed from user diagnostic: history_policy classified SetTrackBusSendPlock as recorded, but resolve_step_command had no matching ResolvedStepCommand variant, so every selected-step knob update returned EditError::UnsupportedCommand before writing a lock. Added BusSendPlock to recorded step resolution, affected-step tracking, labels, execution, pattern-pool persistence, and undo snapshot flow. Added an exact AppCommand regression proving try_apply_command succeeds and stores both live and pooled lock state. Scheduler event and Metal binding regressions still pass; cargo check -p sequencer --tests passes.
close_reason: Routed SetTrackBusSendPlock through recorded step editing and verified authoring-to-pool persistence.

title: Conv reverb panel: start/length/transpose controls
description:
Extend the Convolution Reverb builtin panel (crates/sequencer/ui/effects/builtin/convolution-reverb.lisp) with IR shaping controls next to the existing IMPULSE RESPONSE drop box and mix/gain knobs:

- START knob/number: seconds into the source sample, 0..source-duration (host exposes the loaded sample's duration on the fx dict, e.g. :ir-source-secs, so the range is meaningful; fall back to a fixed 0..30s range if unknown).
- LENGTH knob/number: seconds, 0.05..max supported IR length (read the max from a host-provided value rather than hard-coding 1.49, so the longer-IR bead extends it for free).
- TRANSPOSE knob: -24..+24 semitones, integer detents, 0 default, displayed as e.g. '+5 st'.

Behavior: knobs edit live UI state freely, but the expensive re-prep (host command set-convolution-reverb-ir-shape from eseq-hsk.1) fires only on knob release / commit, not per drag tick — follow the existing builtin-fx knob commit pattern used elsewhere (percent-knob/number-knob in eseq.effects.builtin.dynamics) and whatever debounce seam eseq-hsk.1 exposes. Show the committed region as text under the IR name (e.g. '0.80s + 2.00s · +5 st'). Controls apply to all three contexts the drop box already handles (track slot, bus, rack slot) via the same :track/:bus/:slot meta. When a new sample is dropped, reset start/transpose to defaults and length to min(sample length, max). Values come from the persisted per-instance shape state so the panel reflects reality after project reload.

Also update the values plumbing in crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/effects_panel.rs (which already surfaces :ir-name) to surface the shape fields and source duration.
acceptance_criteria: Panel shows START/LENGTH/TRANSPOSE with sensible ranges; dragging a knob does not spawn re-prep per tick (verify by log/trace: one prep per release); committed change audibly swaps the IR and is one undo step; values persist across project save/load and match the audible IR; works on track, bus, and rack-slot instances; a UI capture fixture or state_values test covers the new fields

title: Conv reverb IR shaping: start/length/transpose in the prep pipeline + persistence
description:
Add per-instance IR shaping settings to the Convolution Reverb: start_sec (offset into the source sample), length_sec (region length; capped at the effect's max IR length), and transpose_semitones (resample the region by 2^(semi/12) — tape-style: pitch and duration change together; +5 semitones makes it shorter/brighter). Implementation lives in crates/sequencer/src/effects/conv_reverb.rs:

1. Extend prepare_ir(path, host_sr) to prepare_ir(path, host_sr, &IrShape) where IrShape { start_sec, length_sec, transpose_semitones }. Apply in prepare_ir_uncached AFTER decode/channel-split, in source-sample time: slice [start, start+length) (clamp to file bounds; pad with zeros if the region runs past EOF), apply short fade-in/fade-out at the slice edges (reuse the existing 256-sample fade idea from fit_to_ir_len; also fade-in at start when start > 0 to avoid a click), THEN resample by (host_sr/src_sr) * 2^(-semi/12) using the existing windowed-sinc resample(), then normalize and fit_to_ir_len as today. Defaults (start=0, length=max, transpose=0) must reproduce today's byte-identical behavior for the bundled default IR.
2. Fold IrShape into ir_cache_key so shaped variants cache independently (bump the cache-salt string, e.g. eseq-conv-ir-cache-v2). Keep the ESEQIR01 binary format unchanged.
3. Per-instance state: alongside the existing IR_REFS/IR_NAMES/IR_DATA node maps, record the current IrShape per node_id, with accessors mirroring ir_ref_for/record_prepared_ir; clear in clear_instance.
4. Host command + apply path: extend the set-convolution-reverb-ir flow (app/effects.rs apply_conv_reverb_ir_to_node and the track/bus/rack set_conv_reverb_ir* variants, ui/host_commands/effects.rs) with a new host command (e.g. set-convolution-reverb-ir-shape) that re-prepares the current IR with new shape values and bulk-rewrites the four tensors via the existing apply_ir_to_node. Re-prep must run off the UI thread or at minimum be debounced — it shells out to the DGenLisp tool (~partition per channel), so never run it per knob tick.
5. Undo/redo: shape changes go through the same undoable pattern as IR swaps (see the existing prepared-IR undo retention via IR_DATA and app/edit.rs conv usages) — one undo step per committed shape change (knob release), restoring both the prior shape values and prior tensors.
6. Persistence: serialize IrShape next to ir_ref in the project format (app/projects.rs restore_conv_reverb_ir_track/_bus and their save counterparts; also the rack-slot path). Older projects without the fields load with defaults. Follow the project-version conventions used by recent v7/v8 bumps.
7. Rack preset save/load (see korgbass1.rackpreset flow) must round-trip the shape too if it currently round-trips ir_ref — verify and cover.

Non-goals: no UI in this bead (child bead covers the panel); no change to K/N/HOP or max IR length; no independent time-stretch (transpose is resample-style only).
acceptance_criteria: prepare_ir with default IrShape produces identical partitions to today (cache-key aside); a shaped prep of a known WAV (e.g. start=0.8s, length=1.0s, transpose=+5) yields an IR whose nonzero span and content match an offline reference slice+resample within tolerance (unit test on the pre-partition samples, no DGenLisp needed); shape changes rewrite tensors on a live node and are undoable as one step; save/reload of a project restores ir_ref + shape and audibly identical tensors; existing conv_reverb tests still pass; cargo nextest -p sequencer conv_reverb scope green

title: Convolution reverb upgrade: IR region, transpose, longer IRs
description: The builtin Convolution Reverb is currently too basic to be usable as a sound-design tool: dropping a sample always crops the first ~1.49s (fixed IR_LEN = K*HOP = 65536 samples @ 44.1k) with no control over which part of the sample becomes the impulse, its length, or its pitch. Goal: drop any sample (e.g. percussion), then set start offset (seconds into the sample), length (seconds), and transpose (semitones) and have the IR rebuilt from that region. All shaping happens offline in the Rust IR-prep pipeline (crates/sequencer/src/effects/conv_reverb.rs prepare_ir) before partitioning — the dgenlisp DSP (conv_reverb_dsp.lisp) is unchanged except where longer IRs require a bigger K. Children: (1) shaping model + offline pipeline + persistence, (2) panel UI controls, (3) longer max IR length so e.g. a 2s region actually fits.

title: Fix bus-send p-lock playback
description: Bus-send controls accept selected-step edits, but playback remains at the zero pattern baseline when the locked step fires. Trace the authoring command through scheduler snapshot/event dispatch and fix the underlying playback path; add an end-to-end scheduler regression.
notes:
Reproduced the scheduler path with an end-to-end lookahead regression: zero baseline -> 0.8 send lock at step 1 -> zero baseline at step 2 is present in emitted realtime parameter events. The observed failure was the transport/full reactive refresh overwriting selected-step send bindings with the unchanged baseline, making the lock appear absent. Full synchronization now reapplies selection-aware send values after baseline mixer/track synchronization. Targeted scheduler and Metal UI binding regressions pass; cargo check -p sequencer --tests passes.
User supplied definitive diagnostic: each knob edit logs command failed: UnsupportedCommand. The scheduler path is valid, but the AppCommand was not accepted by recorded edit routing.
Definitive follow-up fix in eseq-yn0: SetTrackBusSendPlock had been omitted from resolve_step_command, causing UnsupportedCommand before any lock was authored. Now fixed and covered by exact AppCommand regression.
close_reason: Verified send p-lock realtime events and fixed full-refresh UI overwrite that made locks appear absent.

title: Fix bus-send knob editing with selected steps
description: Track bus-send knobs snap back or appear uneditable when steps are selected because p-lock edits are followed by baseline-value reactive synchronization. Make the displayed binding selection-aware while preserving pattern baselines and p-lock semantics.
notes: Fixed selection-aware send control projection: exactly one selected step displays its send p-lock, deselection restores the pattern baseline, and multi-step edits publish the edited value instead of immediately syncing the unchanged baseline. Added targeted reactive binding regression. Validation: cargo check -p sequencer --tests; targeted metal_seq nextest passed.
close_reason: Fixed selected-step bus-send knob editing and added regression coverage.

title: B1: feed mix_latency into the recording offset
description:
Recording compensates the wrong number, so notes land early by whatever PDC
is adding.

record_latency_seconds (sequencer/state/core.rs:87) is set exactly once, at
stream build, to block_size/sample_rate (audio/stream.rs:27-33, whose comment
admits CPAL exposes no portable output latency and calls it a value users must
tune). It is consumed by record_beats_at_instant
(state/sequencer_state/transport.rs:74-88). It knows nothing about PDC.

Meanwhile LatencyPlan::mix_latency (app/graph/latency.rs:65) -- the planner's
actual total output delay -- is computed and discarded; grep finds no reader
outside latency.rs.

Net effect with a spectral Filter Table on MIX: you hear the beat ~46ms late,
play in time with what you hear, and the note is stamped ~46ms early.

Work:
- refresh_latency_compensation (latency.rs:352) already runs every frame, is
  change-detecting, and holds Arc<SequencerState>; have it publish the plan's
  mix_latency instead of dropping it (the `plan` binding at latency.rs:319 is
  local and only pads are extracted today)
- do NOT reuse the same atomic: stream.rs:30 blind-writes it, so the device
  and PDC terms would clobber each other. Keep two atomics -- device set once
  at stream build, PDC updated per frame -- and subtract the sum at the read
  site. Both are lock-free.
- sample rate is needed for samples->seconds; App has it via the stream config

Also worth doing: the same total belongs in front of the user (eseq-lat.7).
notes: The UI-facing half of publishing mix_latency is eseq-lat.8; do the publish once and serve both.
close_reason: Fixed in 2ba836ba. record_latency_seconds keeps the device term; new pdc_latency_seconds atomic carries the graph term, republished by refresh_latency_compensation; record_beats_at_instant subtracts the sum via total_record_latency_seconds. Publish happens before the pad change-detection so a plan that moves the mix total without moving any pad still updates. Tests: take_notes_compensate_graph_latency_on_top_of_device_latency, a_lone_latent_track_moves_the_mix_total_without_moving_any_pad.

title: A2: declare latency in the 12 latent dgen effects
description:
With the mechanism from eseq-lat.1 in place, declare the actual values. The
planner then compensates all of them with no further work -- that machinery
already exists and is tested (latency.rs:614-658 proves alignment through the
real C engine).

Latency == the WINDOW argument of the `buffer` node, not the hop:

  crates/sequencer/effects/*/dsp.lisp
    2048: spectral-bloom, spectral-bloom-mod, spectral-shatter,
          spectral-vox, spectral-xenovox, spectral-notch-phaser
    1024: spectral-bin-freeze, spectral-cloud-gate, spectral-cumsum-soothe,
          spectral-vocoder-shift, spectral-stft-identity
  crates/sequencer/src/effects/conv_reverb_dsp.lisp:25
     512: Convolution Reverb  (buffer inL 512 512, @N 1024)

Conv reverb is a dgen builtin (effects/dgen_builtin.rs:13-30, source
include_str!'d by conv_reverb.rs:39), so it takes the same declaration as the
bundled effects.

Excludes the lookahead dynamics -- their latency is param-dependent, see
eseq-lat.6.

Add a drift test: for each bundled dsp.lisp, parse the largest
`(buffer _ N hop)` window and assert it equals the declared latency. Catches
someone changing the FFT size and forgetting the declaration, without needing
compiler support. Note the parse must tolerate `def`'d constants (e.g. HOP in
filter_table_dsp_spectral.lisp:24) -- either resolve them or skip and assert
only on literal windows.

title: A1: let effects declare their latency
description:
Replace the name-keyed latency match with a declared value.

Why declaration and not compiler inference: the dgen compiler is an external
Swift binary vendored here as a prebuilt artifact (tools/DGenLisp, built from
$HOME/code/swift/dgen). It already knows every `buffer` node's size/hop and
could fold a graph-level latency into the manifest -- but that is an
out-of-repo change plus a manifest schema bump plus plumbing, and cannot land
from this repo alone. Revisit later; declaration should remain the override.

The cheap in-repo seam: `param` is already a general metadata carrier that
reaches the manifest, hidden params included. DGenParam carries
name/default/hidden/role (lisp_host/dgen/dgen_manifest.rs:48-60, parsed at
:213-229), and from_lisp_manifest (effects/mod.rs:7190) receives the full
param slice BEFORE it filters hidden params out of the UI list (:7195). So

    (param __latency @default 2048 @hidden true @role latency)

works today with zero compiler change. Cost is one memory cell per effect.

Work:
- add `latency_samples: u32` to EffectDescriptor (effects/mod.rs:2348)
- read the @role latency param in from_lisp_manifest, before the hidden filter
- set it in the hand-built builtin_* constructors too (mod.rs:6211+, 6620+)
- make EffectDescriptor::latency_samples (mod.rs:2388) prefer the field

Simplification this unlocks: each Filter Table engine has its own lisp source
(dsp_source_for), so the spectral source declares 2048 and the causal source
declares 0, and the descriptor is rebuilt per engine on swap. The name-keyed
arm and its dependence on the filter_table::ENGINES registry should be able to
retire entirely -- verify the descriptor really is rebuilt on the swap path
(apply_compiled_effect_to_slot_sync) before removing it.

Keep the per-node escape hatch in the signature; Filter Table proves some
effects need it.

title: Latency: make PDC cover every latent effect
description:
The plugin-delay-compensation machinery built for the Filter Table
(app/graph/latency.rs, effects/pdc_delay.rs) is correct and verified
end-to-end through the real C engine, but it compensates exactly ONE effect.

EffectDescriptor::latency_samples (effects/mod.rs:2388) is keyed by effect
NAME and has a single arm: "Filter Table". Everything else returns 0. Thirteen
effects are genuinely latent and report zero, so they sum out of phase against
everything else -- the exact failure PDC exists to prevent, with no symptom
except a smeared mix:

  window 2048 (46ms @44.1k): spectral-bloom, spectral-bloom-mod,
    spectral-shatter, spectral-vox, spectral-xenovox, spectral-notch-phaser
  window 1024 (23ms): spectral-bin-freeze, spectral-cloud-gate,
    spectral-cumsum-soothe, spectral-vocoder-shift, spectral-stft-identity
  window 512  (12ms): Convolution Reverb
  param-dependent: limiter (0-20ms, default 3), compressor (0/1/10ms)

Separately, the planner's computed total output latency (LatencyPlan::
mix_latency, latency.rs:65) is used for NOTHING outside the file -- not the
UI, not the transport, and notably not the recording offset, which instead
uses record_latency_seconds derived purely from the output block size
(audio/stream.rs:27-33). So a project with a spectral effect is heard ~46ms
late while recorded notes are stamped ~46ms early.

Convention worth preserving: latency == the WINDOW argument of the dgen
`buffer` node, not the hop. See filter_table_dsp_spectral.lisp:2,21
("One-window (N) latency"), which also routes its dry path through the same
STFT so the internal mix stays aligned.

Related existing issue: eseq-dtx.10 (wire rack-slot PDC pads).

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text: From eseq-lat.4: the conv reverb wet path's measured latency is hop-1 = 511 samples, not 512 (delta-IR fit residual 1.6e-5 at 511 vs 6.4% at 512 — the hop buffer's completed block is visible on the sample that fills it). PDC beads that declare this effect's latency should use 511; the same off-by-one may apply to other buffer/OLA effects like Filter Table spectral.

title: Isolate runtime state across simultaneous instances of the same DGen effect
description:
## Problem
Opening multiple instances of the same DGen effect can cause them to share mutable memory because the effect dylib cache returns a single cached source+dylib combination. Multiple effect engines then execute against aliased dylib state, causing cross-instance corruption or audio behavior.

Instruments avoid analogous aliasing through DGenLisp polyphony/voice slots, but blindly compiling effects with a fixed polyphony such as 8 would reserve memory for instances that may never exist and may impose an arbitrary instance limit. Effects need correct isolation without speculative fixed over-allocation.

## Investigation and design
Evaluate the appropriate ownership model before implementation. The leading design is a lease-aware dylib cache: a cached compiled artifact/load instance may be leased by at most one live effect instance; when the same source/build identity is requested while already leased, create/load a genuinely independent dylib image with independent mutable state. Released leases should be safely reusable where appropriate.

Confirm the platform dynamic-loader semantics and DGen-generated state layout: merely calling dlopen again on the same path may return the same image and continue aliasing, so independent instances may require unique artifact paths/load identities or a deeper runtime-state separation. Compare this design against explicit DGen runtime contexts or voice-slot allocation, and choose the simplest robust architecture. Do not adopt fixed effect polyphony unless investigation demonstrates it is the correct ownership model.

The cache must distinguish immutable compilation reuse from mutable loaded-instance ownership, handle concurrent requests and failures correctly, and clean up leases/artifacts without invalidating active effects.

## Acceptance criteria
- Two or more simultaneous instances of the same DGen effect have independent mutable DSP state, histories, buffers, and parameters, with no cross-instance memory aliasing.
- A regression test demonstrates independent processing/state for at least two instances created from identical source.
- The selected architecture is documented in the implementation, including why lease-aware dylibs, runtime contexts, or DGen voice slots were chosen.
- Dynamic-loader identity semantics are explicitly validated; repeated loading cannot silently resolve to shared mutable globals.
- Creating, removing, and recreating effect instances safely acquires/releases resources without affecting another live instance.
- Cache behavior remains efficient for the common single-instance case and does not rely on arbitrary fixed polyphony or unbounded artifact leakage.
- Compile/load errors do not strand leases or poison otherwise usable cache entries.
acceptance_criteria:
- Multiple live instances of identical DGen effect source process with fully independent mutable state and parameters.
- Tests reproduce the previous aliasing and verify isolation plus acquire/release/recreate lifecycle behavior.
- The implementation evaluates and documents lease-aware dylib instances versus DGen runtime contexts/voice slots.
- Loader identity is handled robustly rather than assuming repeated dlopen calls create independent state.
- The single-instance path avoids fixed speculative polyphony and unnecessary resource growth.
notes:
Implemented lease-aware exclusive dylib cache in crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dylib_cache.rs.

Root cause: DGenLisp-generated C has file-scope 'static float tN_g[VOICE_COUNT*SCRATCH_STRIDE]' scratch arrays with voiceIndex hard-coded 0 for effects. The cache shared one artifact dir per key via refcounted leases, and dlopen of the same path returns one dyld image, so all simultaneous instances aliased the same mutable scratch -> data races under audiograph worker threads.

Design chosen (over fixed effect polyphony and toolchain runtime contexts): leases are now EXCLUSIVE (one live lease per artifact dir). When every matching artifact for a key is live-leased, the manager clones the artifact directory (file copy, no recompile) under a fresh artifact id and dlopens the clone -> distinct path/inode -> independent dyld image with private statics. Released artifacts become free and are reused, bounding disk to the simultaneous-instance high-water mark. Clone failure falls back to compilation; compile failures publish nothing (unchanged). workspace_default() now returns the global singleton manager so all acquirers of one cache root share one lease table (per-process is sufficient: dlopen images are per-process). Slice E6 'one compilation per key' preserved (racing loser clones the winner's artifact).

Also fixes cross-engine instrument scratch collision (two engines, same source, same voice v) since instruments go through the same acquire path.

Tests (all pass, real toolchain): simultaneous_acquires_get_independent_dylib_images (loader identity: distinct dirs, dylib paths, process_fn addresses; release->reuse without growth), racing_threads_on_one_key_share_one_compilation (updated), concurrent_instances_render_independently (two threads render identical source concurrently, outputs must equal sequential golden), second_lease_on_live_artifact_is_refused.
close_reason: Closed

title: Filter table preset dropdown stays stale until transport starts
description: Selecting a filter-table preset updates DSP sound and visualizers immediately, but the preset dropdown does not display the new selection until playback starts. Diagnose the reactive state publication/render invalidation path and add a regression test.
close_reason: Fixed Filter Table source/mode/engine panel metadata updates by routing them through typed post-event panel-tree invalidations, which force the stopped-transport reactive cycle; added dropdown prop refresh regression coverage.

title: Add explicit Filter Table import analysis modes
description: Replace the single ambiguous sample-import path with intentional pipelines for structured wavetables, single-cycle waveforms, ordinary audio textures, and impulse responses. Each mode needs appropriate framing, windowing, DC policy, normalization, spectral smoothing, reference-frequency behavior, and deterministic errors.
design: Automatic detection may recommend a mode but must not hide destructive assumptions. Preserve source analysis as an offline operation and produce the same validated magnitude-table model for every mode. Make DC removal and normalization explicit per mode rather than universal.
acceptance_criteria: The UI/import API exposes or reliably proposes each mode without silently misclassifying input; structured wavetables use periodic aligned frames without Hann windowing; arbitrary audio uses a leakage-controlled STFT and selectable time/novelty framing; single-cycle and IR inputs have distinct documented behavior; tests cover mono/stereo, short/long, silent, malformed, and non-integer-cycle inputs.
notes: Ordinary audio and wavetables are mathematically different inputs. Raw rectangular windows are appropriate only for known periodic cycles; arbitrary audio requires windowing. Several analyzed reference tables contain deliberate DC energy, so unconditional per-frame DC removal should be evaluated rather than assumed.
close_reason: Four explicit analysis modes shipped on feature/filter-table (uncommitted): wavetable (aligned 2048 cycles, rectangular, DC kept, non-multiple length = deterministic error — folds .4 legacy-path gap), single-cycle (periodic resample any length, x64), audio (Hann STFT, 64 evenly spaced windows, DC removed; novelty framing documented as extension), impulse-response (first 2048 samples w/ half-Hann truncation fade, no normalization, explicit-only). recommend_mode proposes, never silently misclassifies; chosen mode persists in the table ref (#ft-mode tag) so save/reload/undo reproduce identical analysis; set-filter-table-mode host command + panel mode button for track/bus (read-only in racks). REFERENCE_HARMONIC=24 now a named constant pending eseq-dtx.6. Verified: filter_table 21/21, app::effects 21, app::edit 51, plus project/graph/latency suites; cargo check clean. Notes: rack slots lack a drop/re-analysis target (pre-existing); perceptual smoothing left to eseq-dtx.3.

title: Correct Filter Table wavetable framing and interpolation bounds
description: Fix two correctness defects before expanding import/editor functionality. Structured 2048-sample-cycle wavetables must be split on exact cycle boundaries and frame-resampled without windows that straddle adjacent cycles. DSP table interpolation must clamp endpoint reads so frame=1 and the final harmonic bin never gather beyond the tensor.
design: Represent frame selection explicitly rather than deriving arbitrary sample offsets. Keep structured-wavetable analysis separate from arbitrary-audio STFT analysis. Clamp interpolation indices before both gathers instead of relying on backend out-of-range behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Known 256x2048 mono wavetables import as 64 selections/interpolations of whole aligned cycles; arbitrary frame-count wavetables have a documented deterministic mapping; exact frame and frequency endpoints remain in bounds; focused tests fail under the previous unaligned/OOB behavior and pass after the fix.
notes: Local analysis of 89 Kilohearts filter wavetables found all were 256x2048. The current evenly spaced window-start algorithm aligns only 4 of 64 windows for a 524288-sample source; median table spectral error was about 1.8%, typical worst-row error 5.3%, and worst observed row 54.5%. This evidence is for behavioral benchmarking only; do not include third-party assets.
close_reason: Fixed both defects on feature/filter-table (uncommitted). Structured wavetables (len = exact multiple of 2048, >=2048) split on cycle boundaries; frame f maps to fractional cycle f*(K-1)/63 via linear interpolation of two adjacent whole aligned cycles; K=1 repeats; non-multiple lengths keep legacy path (deferred to eseq-dtx.5). DSP peek-vec clamps position and base row before both gathers (frame last=63, harmonic last=1024) so frame=1.0/final bin select exactly the last row. Files: effects/filter_table.rs, effects/filter_table_dsp.lisp, docs/filter-table-effect-spec.md. Tests: cargo test -p sequencer --lib filter_table, 10/10 pass; framing tests verified fail-before; endpoint test is a regression guard (old OOB gather carried zero weight so numerics matched — defect was the undefined read).

title: Add effect latency reporting and plugin delay compensation
description: Filter Table's STFT path has a known 2048-sample latency, but the audiograph currently has no effect-latency contract or path compensation. Add a general per-node latency API, compensate parallel/serial graph paths correctly, and have Filter Table report N. This must be graph-level support, not a Filter Table timing workaround.
close_reason: Graph-level latency contract + PDC shipped on feature/filter-table (uncommitted). EffectDescriptor::latency_samples() declares per-effect latency (Filter Table=2048, others 0); new effects/pdc_delay.rs stereo ring-delay node inserted on every real summing edge (track fx-out->destination, send taps, bus->MIX); pure planner in app/graph/latency.rs computes pads (serial accumulation, max-alignment at joins); change-detecting App::refresh_latency_compensation() reconciles every frame + after routing changes, covering undo/redo/load/scene-switch. Filter Table dry path shares the STFT so internal mix stays aligned; 2048 reported outward once. Verified: latency 8 tests (incl. real-engine impulse alignment), pdc_delay 4, filter_table 11, graph/effects/command/edit suites — all pass; cargo check clean. Deferred: rack-slot chain joins computed in plan but pad wiring not connected (RACK_SLOT_JOIN_UNCOMPENSATED marker, follow-up bead); pads clamp at 16383 with log; bypass-toggle shift caveat documented in spec Known-limits.
