title: Add Filter Table built-in effect
description: Port the dgenlisp Filter Table prototype into a production-quality built-in sequencer effect, following the Convolution Reverb host-wrapper architecture. Include wavetable/sample loading and offline magnitude preprocessing, stereo processing, mix/latency behavior, persistence/UI integration, and focused validation.
acceptance_criteria: A Filter Table built-in can be added and restored; bundled/default and user-dropped audio tables are preprocessed into per-frame magnitude responses; stereo DSP applies frame morph, cutoff shift, resonance contrast, and latency-compensated mix; host/UI integration exposes the controls and file interaction; focused tests cover preprocessing, persistence, and DSP behavior.
notes:
Experimental V1 implemented on feature/filter-table: stereo N=2048/HOP=512 DGenLisp response with mandatory IR window; offline magnitude preprocessing for dropped audio; procedural default; host-managed tensor writes; track/bus/rack creation; project persistence and undo/redo mementos; custom UI, layout regression, and production-path visual capture. Frame, cutoff, resonance, and mix expose all four host modulation lanes; output intentionally does not. Frame/resonance/mix carry percent units so typed values such as mix=33 map to 0.33. Remaining production gaps are tracked in children eseq-dtx.1 (graph latency/PDC), eseq-dtx.2 (minimum phase), and eseq-dtx.3 (smoothing/anti-aliasing).
Fixed custom Filter Table knob integration: controls now use param-mod-wrapper and modulation-aware value/min/max/write routing, render selected-source ranges, and write depth params in mods mode. Added a regression that proves four wrappers render, output does not, and frame writes the depth cell; inspected /tmp/metal-seq-filter-table-mods-panel.png.
Fixed silent runtime modulation: Filter Table declared @mod destinations but read raw params, bypassing DGen's generated modulation resolver. DSP now reads (mod frame/cutoff/resonance/mix), clamps additive results to valid domains, hop-holds response controls, and leaves mix sample-rate responsive. Added an offline DSP regression proving Mod 1 changes rendered mix output.
Reworked resonance after listening feedback: removed mean-relative exponential scaling that could explode narrow peaks. Resonance now applies bounded power contrast plus RMS makeup capped at +6 dB, making it spectral-selectivity control rather than output gain. Extended offline effect probe support with validated tensor overrides and added a real default-table render regression covering low-res audibility and high-res peak bounds.
Added Filter Table visual diagnostics. Generalized wavetable-viewer with a revisioned zero-copy published-bank registry and a non-negative magnitude domain while preserving file-backed waveform behavior; Metal buffers now update safely on bank replacement. Filter Table publishes its 64x1025 bank for track/bus/rack UI, displays a 16-row sampled overview with frame-morph highlight, and uses a read-only EQ8 spectrum overlay showing pre-FX audio plus the target frame/cutoff/resonance response. Added cutoff-translation, registry lifecycle, layout, and Metal primitive regressions. Inspected /tmp/metal-seq-filter-table-visualizers-final2.png and mods capture.
Fixed visualization liveness regression found in the app. The panel passed snapshot tests because it read static :value map entries; live controls update value-field reactive slots instead. Frame/cutoff/resonance visual props now bind through instrument-param-base-value. Added normalized-wave support inside wavetable-viewer so the ReactiveRef is passed directly (reactive arithmetic had caused the custom panel to be rejected), and strengthened the layout regression to mutate live frame/cutoff slots and assert both widget props update. Production capture now loads without a Filter Table UI error.
Implementation committed on feature/filter-table as c58a1105 (Add host-integrated Filter Table effect). Concurrent crates/eseqlisp/src/runtime.rs tracing edits were intentionally excluded.
Session 2026-08-17 (agent-coordinated): children .4, .1, .5, .6, .3, .7, .8 all implemented and CLOSED on feature/filter-table; all work UNCOMMITTED pending review (~3130 insertions, 7 new files + 11 bundled .fltab presets). .2 (minimum-phase) deliberately deferred — may need dgen-side renderer work and the dgen repo is owned by another agent. New follow-ups: eseq-dtx.9 (effect dylib not reentrant for same-source concurrent renders), eseq-dtx.10 (rack-slot PDC pad wiring). Needs human ears/eyes: factory-preset listening (probes in session scratchpad ft-presets/), smoothing defaults (30ms one-pole, 1/6-octave audio smoothing), in-app editor pass. Verified: filter_table 53, app::effects 23, app::edit 51, project 36, latency 9, pdc_delay 4, effects 269, app::graph 69; cargo check --lib --bins --tests clean.

title: Fix adsrexp retrigger after completed release
description: A second adsrexp note can skip attack after the preceding release reaches zero: release leaves phase_hist at 1, the next gate bypasses reset because env is already zero, and attack_done reads the stale phase before the new attack phase is initialized. Gate the completion check on a genuinely continuing attack and add a repeated-note runtime regression.
acceptance_criteria: Two separated notes through one adsrexp instance both execute full attacks, including when the first note completed release and left phase at 1; existing single-note curve test passes; instrument probe remains finite.
notes: Root cause confirmed: after a completed release, phase_hist remains 1 while env is zero. A fresh gate correctly bypasses de-click reset, but attack_done read that stale phase and transitioned directly to decay before phase_start could reset it. Fix requires attack_done to apply only when prev_stage was attack and this frame is not a retrigger. Added deterministic two-note render regression: first and second six-frame attack/decay prefixes match and both peak at 1. Validation: both focused adsrexp nextest tests pass; repeated-note instrument_probe peak 1.0, no non-finite samples/state; diff check clean.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
FIXED in dgen (branch dgenlisp-train, working tree on top of 403ec9e).

Root cause (gradients): with a spectral (isolated-pass) loss, the scalar history BPTT recurrence runs as a detached backward block wrapped in one reverse frame loop. A trainable phasor frequency emits a temporalGradStore/Scan/Read tape whose ops are block boundaries; they split the backward partition in node-ID order MID-RECURRENCE: carry-cell reads landed in one block (ran as a plain forward loop -> recurrence truncated to garbage) while carry-cell writes were stranded in a frame-parallel block after the scan. Every gradient crossing a history filter (SVF cutoff/resonance/drives/mix levels) came out ~10-100x too small with unreliable sign, so Korg1 Adam climbed. Minimal reproducer: one env-modulated phasor -> polyblep saw -> one SVF (M6); same seed FD-checked correct without the trainable pitch path (M4).

Fix: Sources/DGen/Blocks/BlockFormation.swift — consolidateScalarBPTTBackwardBlocks detects the fragmented carry read/write layout and rebuilds it via the (generalized) tensor detached-BPTT consolidation: sandwich eviction of post-tape consumers, tail re-segmented into ID-contiguous runs, forward deps hoisted out of 'after' blocks.

Verification: full Korg1 fdcheck at 65536 now 30/33 sign-match (was 18/33); filter params match FD to ~1-5% (resonance -0.545 vs -0.544). Remaining mismatches (pulse_width, analog_drift, lfo_*) are the deterministically micro-jagged directions (log-eps near-dead-bin leakage as edges shift): autograd matches TIGHT central FD (verified at +/-0.01 cent) — landscape property, not an adjoint bug. 50-epoch legacy Adam on the exact repro: training loss 5.125 -> 4.77 (was 5.13 -> 13.6), independent CPU score 0.5859 -> 0.5325, improvement 9.11%.

Scoring unification: legacy path now reports the same independent CPU log-MR-STFT scorer (TrainSpectralScorer) as CMA for abs_distance/improvement, seed-vs-final, with seed retention if the canonical score regresses. Documented in dgen docs/TRAIN_SUBCOMMAND_NOTES.md (Fixes 2026-08-15).

Regression tests: TemporalGradientCompositionTests testTrainablePhasorComposesWithSVFSpectralGradient + testEnvModulatedPhasorAndCutoffComposeWithSVFSpectralGradient (fail at baseline, pass with fix); SVFBPTTScratchTests testFullVoiceManyTargetsGradientsWithTrainableDetune XCTExpectFailure removed (now genuinely passes).

title: dgen: flip --filter-surrogate default to none; fix or retire the freq SVF surrogate
description: Validated 2026-08-14 (tb303 + monologue synthetic round-trips): the default freq surrogate objective ranks the ground-truth params WORSE than the seed (monologue: truth 8.38 vs seed 5.92; tb303: loss at truth 9x the none-path), backward loss disagrees with forward realize() by 33%, cutoff autograd is sign-flipped and ~150-185x under-scaled vs FD, envelope decay grads ~2000x under-scaled, and the global window-1 target delay is structurally wrong for dry/wet-mixed topologies (tb303 post_tone comb: 15dB bright tilt). Perf case has collapsed: surrogate 2.3s/epoch vs BPTT 1.0-1.5s, and BPTT GPU exec is only ~0.3s/epoch (recompile dominates; epoch-cache spec is the real lever). eseq now passes --filter-surrogate none explicitly (learn_job.rs build_argv, uncommitted). Action in dgen: flip TrainOptions default to none, then decide retire vs fix (fix list: backward pass w/ forward-backward loss mismatch as reproducer; per-branch latency instead of global target shift; hop-hold +5dB HF error on snappy sweeps; -60dBc leakage floor; high-Q wrap). If kept, polish-epochs>0 mandatory and abs_distance reported from polish phase.

title: Train-only analytic ADSR lowering (closed-form envelope, duration-differentiable)
description:
Patch-learn cannot learn envelope attack from 0 and only weakly learns durations: in the eseq adsr macro the stage machine (gte/gswitch) carries no gradient, so autograd only sees the intra-window ramp slope 1/attack_samples; at attack_ms=0 the max(1.0, attack_ms*0.001*sr) clamp makes the gradient identically zero (hard stuck point). FD sees the improvement; autograd reports 0 (validated 2026-08-14, surrogate audit).

Fix: a train-only lowering pass in dgen (Sources/DGenLisp/, same pattern as ExcitationLowering — TrainPlanner.makePlan step) that swaps (adsr gate trig a d s r) for a closed-form envelope in sample index t. This is sound because ExcitationLowering already guarantees a known one-shot: gate = (accum < gate_frames), single trigger at t=0, no retriggers. Shape: attack = min(1, t/attack_samples) or a soft-blended ramp so d/d(attack) is nonzero through the ramp AND the stage boundary is differentiable; decay/release as the existing settle-time exponentials, with soft stage windows instead of hard gte 0.999 switches. Render/checkpoint subprocesses keep the real macro (unswapped source), same as the SVF surrogate handoff.

Payoff: (a) real, correctly-signed duration gradients for attack/decay/release incl. attack-from-0; (b) removes 3 make-history cells per envelope from the BPTT tape (typical patch has 2+ envelopes) — genuine training speedup with EXACT forward semantics under the training excitation, unlike the freq SVF surrogate (biased approximation, now disabled via --filter-surrogate none).

Validate with the rung round-trip harness from this session: render known-config target via train-render, seed attack=0, confirm recovery of a 0.5s filter-env attack; DGENLISP_TRAIN_FDCHECK sign/ratio for all envelope params. Stopgap until built: seed attack params with a few-ms floor in eseq so at least the slope gradient flows.
acceptance_criteria: FD-vs-autograd sign match and sane ratio for attack/decay/sustain/release on tb303+monologue patches; round-trip recovers a 0.5s filt_attack from a 0 seed; per-epoch time does not regress; rendered checkpoints still use the real adsr macro
notes: Implemented in dgen: train-only AnalyticADSRLowering inserted after excitation/modulation lowering, with one shared sample counter, closed-form attack/settle decay/release, two-sample differentiable stage windows, and +1-sample differentiable duration floors. Render AST remains the real adsr macro. Added focused DGenLisp tests and re-vendored crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp (sha256 8d21cdbc474926d06f456e565579e196a5beebdc881e6d93282e51f81f6cc189). Validation: focused tests pass; tb303 FD check filt_attack -0.054836 vs -0.050592, filt_decay -0.40614 vs -0.41571, filt_sustain -0.26441 vs -0.08564 (all sign matches); release was effectively zero for that target/crop. Remaining acceptance validation before close: monologue/all-envelope FD, attack=0 -> 0.5s round-trip, and epoch timing comparison.

title: Validate dgenlisp train flow with rung-style known-config round-trip (tb303 + korg1)
description: Patch-learn on a tb303-basic bass sound walked cutoff far up despite a near-correct start. Validate the whole eseq raw-dgenlisp -> differentiable lowering -> train flow the way SynthID rungs did: render a target from a KNOWN param config via train-render, perturb params, train, measure param recovery. Also audit surrogate fidelity (SVF freq-sampled surrogate, envelope/adsr handling) vs the real forward path.
close_reason: Validation complete via 3 opus agents: flow works with --filter-surrogate none (exact recovery both patches); default freq surrogate is the bug (follow-ups filed); eseq now passes none explicitly.

title: Recording undo transaction must close at transport stop/pause
description: The 'Record take' undo transaction opens when the recording flag turns on and only commits when it turns off. Pausing the transport leaves it open, so multiple play passes (and interleaved knob edits captured in the scene snapshot) collapse into one undo entry: undo after recording wipes the whole recorded pattern plus later edits. Fix: scope the transaction to (recording armed AND transport playing) — commit on stop/pause or disarm, reopen on the next play pass.
close_reason: Recording undo transaction now scoped to (armed && playing) via App::sync_recording_history_boundary; event loop diffs that conjunction per frame. Regression test: app::graph::tests::transport_pause_splits_recording_into_separate_undo_entries

title: First recorded note after transport restart lands at stale playhead position
description: RecordClockAnchor is only published by the audio callback while playing and never invalidated on stop. A key press in the window between Play and the first playing audio block samples the stale anchor (last played beat + wall-clock elapsed since stop), so the first live-recorded note lands deep in the pattern instead of step 0. Fix: invalidate the anchor (timestamp_nanos=0 sentinel) on the stop transitions in stop_playback/toggle_play_no_publish so sample() returns None and the press falls back to the freshly-reset track playheads.
close_reason: RecordClockAnchor::invalidate() on stop transitions; press during play-start race now falls back to reset playheads. Test: stop_invalidates_the_record_clock_anchor_until_republished

title: P-lock indicator no longer shown on off steps
description: Regression: off steps no longer render their p-lock indicator. Users often select off steps to p-lock e.g. warp bpm in samplers. Worse, p-locks get added to off steps accidentally and are invisible, causing confusing parameter movement in the sampler UI. Restore the p-lock indicator on off steps.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cannot choose a variant when selecting a p-lock-free step on a track that has p-locked steps
description: Regression: previously, selecting a step with no p-locks on a track where other steps have p-locks offered a quick variant chooser — the whole point of variants. That affordance is gone. Restore the ability to quickly choose a variant for a step with no p-locks.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decision: sounds/ + samples/ project-path migration strategy
description: Existing projects pool-reference sounds/ and samples/ by path. Moving them out of the repo (T2) needs a project-path migration or resolve-time fallback chain. Decide before T2. Spec: content-tiers 7.2.
close_reason: Resolved 2026-08-20; recorded in docs/content-tiers-spec.md section 7 question 2. Measured over all 262 saved projects: sounds/ has ZERO project references (it is a browsable library dir read by list_sound_presets / written by save_container_preset), so moving it needs no migration. samples/ is referenced only via sample_path and is ALREADY content-addressed (samples/<sha256>.wav, 366 occurrences in the first 80 projects); sample_name is display-only metadata. DECISION: no project migration AND no fallback chain -- sample_path is an identity with a directory prefix stapled on, so the resolver uses one rule (strip the prefix, resolve the hash against the sample store). This is the permanent design, not legacy compat: it gives portable projects across machines and tiers, which section 4.0 already promises for packages. New saves may stamp sample:<hash>; that is save-side, never a rewrite pass. Naming question 4 also resolved: content/ not assets/.

title: T1+T2: AppPaths coverage, then the repo split into content/
description:
Merged bead: was eseq-tiers.1 (T1) + eseq-tiers.3 (T2), combined 2026-08-21 because T1's completeness is only PROVEN by T2 -- an incomplete AppPaths conversion looks green until the roots flip and something cannot find its files. One agent does both, in two mandated commits.

PHASE 1 (T1, commit 1): every content lookup goes through AppPaths with ZERO behavior change. instrument_storage.rs (~10 relative INSTRUMENTS_DIR/EFFECTS_DIR sites), paths.rs init candidates, ui/ loads, presets, sample-assets. Audit for runtime writes into factory content dirs (forbidden per content-tiers 4.1). Exit: grep-clean for relative content-path literals, tests green, app runs identically.

PHASE 2 (T2, commit 2): git mv factory content (ui, instruments, effects, defmacros, midi-fx, presets, kits, processes, impulses, core eseqlisp lisp) into a top-level content/ dir; demos to crates/eseqlisp/examples/; projects/recordings/samples.db/sounds out of git into .local/; flip the AppPaths Dev roots. Mostly renames.

Spec: docs/content-tiers-spec.md rev 2, sections 3 + 3.1 + 3.2 + 5 + slice T1/T2. The dir is content/ NOT assets/ (section 7 q4). The section 3 layout predated measurement -- follow 3.1's corrections, not the original block.

WORK IN THE MAIN CHECKOUT ON A BRANCH, NOT A WORKTREE: samples/ (12G), projects/ (188M), samples.db, sounds/, sample-assets/ and recordings/ are all gitignored and exist only in the main checkout. A fresh worktree has none of them, so content resolution -- the entire subject of this bead -- cannot be verified there. T1's 'zero behavior change' exit is unverifiable against an empty library.
acceptance_criteria: Commit 1 (T1): grep-clean for relative content-path literals; every content lookup resolves through AppPaths; no runtime writes into factory content dirs (project.rs:2635 create_dir_all(SOUNDS_DIR) fixed); scoped tests green; app behavior unchanged. Commit 2 (T2): factory content lives under a top-level content/; projects/recordings/samples.db/sounds are out of git in .local/ and gitignored; the 18 zombie tracked projects are git rm --cached; impulses consolidated to one home; sample-assets landed in the USER tier not content/; ui/capture-fixtures stayed with the crate; app runs and finds all content from the flipped Dev roots; full suite green from a fresh clone.
notes:
T1 audit target found while resolving tiers.2 (2026-08-20): project.rs:2635 list_sound_presets calls create_dir_all(SOUNDS_DIR) where SOUNDS_DIR is the RELATIVE literal "sounds" (project.rs:27). save_container_preset (project.rs:2513) writes there too. This is the forbidden runtime-write-into-a-relative-content-dir pattern from content-tiers 4.1 and becomes a hard failure inside a signed bundle. Also note sounds/ is NOT referenced by any of the 262 saved projects, so moving it is a constant change with no migration.
  Inventory measured 2026-08-20; spec section 3 corrected (new 3.1 + 3.2).    
  The section 3 target layout predated any measurement of the tree and was    
  wrong in several places. Do NOT follow it verbatim.                         
                                                                              
  Measured, tracked-file counts:                                              
  instruments 17M/407 | effects 4.5M/129 | ui 1.6M/145 | presets 772K/25      
  defmacros 172K/32 | midi-fx 52K/13 | kits 352K/3 | processes 4K/1           
  projects 188M/18 | recordings 3.9G/0 | samples 12G/0 | sounds 448K/15       
  impulses (top level) 10M/25 | crates/sequencer/assets 7.1M/26               
  sample-assets 3.1M/0 | filter-tables EMPTY/0                                
                                                                              
  Corrections to the section 3 layout:                                        
                                                                              
  1. **sample-assets/ is NOT factory content.** Gitignored in BOTH the root   
  and crate .gitignore; 3.1 MB of untracked local artwork backing             
  source_assets. It goes to the USER tier with samples/, not into content/.   
  The spec previously listed it under assets/ — that was wrong.               
  2. **IRs have two homes**: top-level impulses/ (10M, 25 tracked) and

title: Audit remaining Cmd/Super-hardcoded shortcuts for Linux equivalents
description:
Copy/paste (eseq-linux.79) is one instance of a systemic problem: many global shortcuts gate on KeyModifiers::SUPER only, so they are unreachable on Linux where the compositor owns the Super key. After eseq-linux.79 lands the shared platform-primary-modifier helper, sweep the remaining hardcoded SUPER sites and route each through it (macOS: Cmd unchanged; Linux: Ctrl).

Known sites from a grep of crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs (line numbers as of eseq-linux HEAD 2ec8432d; re-grep for KeyModifiers::SUPER when starting):
- sequencer_tab_shortcut_index (input.rs:261): Cmd+1..9 tab switching (modifiers == SUPER exact match).
- Cmd+F sample-browser focus (input.rs:364).
- Cmd+, preferences (input.rs:413).
- Cmd+I (input.rs:1429) and Cmd+D duplicate outside the arrangement (input.rs:1436).
- Cmd+A select-all path (see test at input.rs:3884) and any other Char matchers guarded by contains(SUPER).
- Also sweep crates/eseqlisp for SUPER-only gates outside the widget paths that already accept SUPER|CONTROL (wgpu_app.rs:3061 and metal_backend.rs:9706 branch on super_key() — determine whether those are macOS-only paths or shared).

Per-site care, not a mechanical replace:
- Linux Ctrl equivalents may collide with existing CONTROL bindings (the text editor keymap is emacs-flavored: Ctrl+F/B are page motion, Ctrl+A/E line motion, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+Q quit, Ctrl+W kill, Ctrl+Y yank, Ctrl+K kill-line — see crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/commands.rs bind_defaults). A global Cmd+F -> Ctrl+F mapping must not shadow text-mode page motion: each converted shortcut needs the same context guards the SUPER version had (focused_widget_captures_text_input, minibuffer/prompt checks), and where a genuine conflict exists in a text context, the text binding wins. Document any shortcut left mac-only because its Ctrl slot is taken.
- normalize_command_shortcuts (input.rs:529) and the exact-match sites (modifiers == SUPER) need the same raw-vs-normalized tracing noted in eseq-linux.79.
- Deliverable includes a short table in the bead notes (or docs/) listing each shortcut, its macOS chord, its Linux chord, and any intentional divergence — this feeds the eseq-2k9p.4 keybinding reference.

Depends on eseq-linux.79 for the shared helper and its test patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Every global shortcut that works with Cmd on macOS has a working Linux chord (Ctrl-based via the shared helper) or a documented, deliberate mac-only exception. Grep shows no remaining bare contains/== KeyModifiers::SUPER gates in crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs outside the shared helper. No existing CONTROL binding in text mode is shadowed (page motion, save, quit, kill/yank still work in the editor on Linux). Focused nextest coverage exercises at least tab switching, Cmd/Ctrl+F, and Cmd/Ctrl+D on both platform shapes. A shortcut table macOS-chord/Linux-chord/divergences is recorded in the bead notes or docs.
notes:
Shortcut audit (2026-08-26):

| Action | macOS | Linux | Context / divergence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Select sequencer tab 1..9 | Cmd+1..9 | Ctrl+1..9 | UI buffers only; text/minibuffer/prompt focus wins |
| Focus sample browser search | Cmd+F | Ctrl+F | UI buffers only; Ctrl+F remains editor page-forward in text mode |
| Toggle recording | Cmd+, | Ctrl+, | Minibuffer/prompt retains input |
| Select all steps | Cmd+A | Ctrl+A | UI shortcut contexts only; text mode retains editor Ctrl+A line-start |
| New instrument editor | Cmd+I | Ctrl+I | UI shortcut contexts only |
| Duplicate mixer pattern | Cmd+D | Ctrl+D | Mixer only; arrangement duplication uses the same primary D via eseq-linux.79 |
| Toggle track mods | Cmd+M | Ctrl+M | Text-entry widgets retain input |
| Group tracks | Cmd+G | Ctrl+G | Existing global grouping action |
| Double/halve pattern | Cmd++/Cmd+- | Ctrl++/Ctrl+- | UI shortcut contexts only |
| Sequencer history | Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z | Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z | Already used the shared primary helper; text and focused patcher history win |
| Copy/paste (steps, arrangement, editor) | Cmd+C/V | Ctrl+C/V (Ctrl+Shift+C/V also accepted for clipboard) | Landed in eseq-linux.79; audited here |
| Patcher create/connect | Cmd+Enter / Cmd+Up | Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+Up | Focused patcher only |
| Patcher cable segmentation | Cmd+Y | Ctrl+Y | Linux text mode retains editor Ctrl+Y yank |
| Patcher agent | Cmd+K / Cmd+Shift+K | Ctrl+K / Ctrl+Shift+K | Linux text mode retains editor Ctrl+K kill-line |
| Disable patcher drag alignment | Cmd+drag | Ctrl+drag | Pointer gesture now uses the shared primary helper |

Intentional non-shortcut SUPER sites left unchanged: winit-to-crossterm translation reports the physical Super key; pointer callback maps expose raw `super`; `:drag-modifier :super` explicitly requests the physical key; text-input paths already accept Super or Control. The Metal and wgpu `super_key()` branches are raw modifier translation, not macOS-only shortcut gates.
close_reason: Completed in 11107e6e: routed remaining sequencer and patcher Cmd shortcuts through the platform-primary modifier, preserved Linux text-editor Ctrl bindings, added platform-shape/context coverage, and recorded the shortcut audit table in notes.

title: Account for the fixed-block adapter in record latency on ALSA
description: audio::FixedOutputBlocks (eseq-linux.73) adds up to block_size-1 frames of output latency on hosts that do not deliver whole blocks (ALSA/PipeWire). transport.record_latency_seconds is still block_size/sample_rate, set in audio/stream.rs build_output_stream. Decide whether the default should account for the adapter on Linux, or stay the documented user-tunable estimate. Not urgent: it is already an estimate and the graph's own PDC compensation is summed separately.

title: Vendored dgen ABI Source-sha256 matches only the Linux toolchain stage; the test is red on macOS
description:
Found on a macOS host running eseq-linux.26 rider 4.

sequencer lisp_host::tests::vendored_dgen_abi_header_matches_staged_toolchain_header FAILS on macOS at HEAD (78ad4c8c, branch eseq-linux):

  staged  73baeab623bb7f2aa1f4971e1117ea3757769731f49e7d2f8967bd0a6f3a0e50
  recorded 5c3333cb92db268a82a8e0e618ed17566e05b112824023a5b75a2f93a29d5b38

The test hashes tools/dgen-toolchain/include/dgen_runtime.h -- a per-target,
gitignored staged artifact -- and compares it against ONE Source-sha256 comment
recorded in crates/sequencer/audiograph/dgen_abi_v1.h. The two pinned archives
do not ship the same header, so a single recorded hash cannot satisfy both
targets:

- content/dgen-toolchain.lock pins arm64-apple-macos to
  dgen-toolchain-20.1.8-arm64.tar.gz sha 3f5a813d..., unchanged since b398927f.
  Its staged include/ holds only dgen_runtime.h, and that header still does
  #include <arm_neon.h>.
- Commit 2f5a3cd9 (Fetch the hermetic Linux DGen toolchain by lock file) added
  the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu pin and, in the same commit, bumped
  dgen_abi_v1.h's Source-sha256. Its own message says the upstream header
  changed only in its intrinsics section: '#include <arm_neon.h> became
  #include "dgen_simd_compat.h", plus an asm-barrier macro'. So the recorded
  hash was updated to the LINUX stage's header while the macOS pin stayed on
  the older archive.

Consequence: the workspace suite is green on Linux (4508/4508 at 7396708d) and
red on macOS on this one test, and it will stay red on every Mac until the two
targets are reconciled. Nothing about the ABI itself is wrong -- the vendored
section (context struct, host-services struct, both export prototypes) is
byte-identical between the two headers per 2f5a3cd9's own analysis. The bug is
the pin/assertion shape, not the contract.

Two candidate fixes:
1. Bump the arm64-apple-macos archive pin to the toolchain build that carries
   the same dgen_runtime.h as the published Linux stage, restaging via
   ./rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh from a dgen-audio checkout. Keeps one hash;
   requires the mac archive to be rebuilt and re-vendored.
2. Make the assertion per-target: record one Source-sha256 per lock target and
   compare against the one matching the host, or hash only the vendored ABI
   section rather than the whole upstream header (which is what dgen_abi_v1.h
   actually copies -- the intrinsics section it explicitly does not vendor is
   the only part that differs).

Option 2 is the one that survives the next intrinsics-only upstream change.

Reproduce on a Mac:
  cargo nextest run -p sequencer --lib -E 'test(=lisp_host::tests::vendored_dgen_abi_header_matches_staged_toolchain_header)'
acceptance_criteria: The vendored-ABI drift test passes on both arm64-apple-darwin and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with the archives content/dgen-toolchain.lock pins, and an intrinsics-only change to the upstream header no longer breaks one platform while leaving the other green.
close_reason: Hash the vendored ABI section rather than the target-specific whole header, with regression coverage proving intrinsics-only differences are ignored while ABI changes remain detectable.

title: Content-package import flow: hand-cloned packages register on load; live detection with a modal
description: What is the flow for importing a package carrying content (presets, instruments, samples)? Target: cloning a well-formed package into ~/.eseq.d/packages/<name> is sufficient — its content shows up on next launch, and ideally an already-running session detects it and offers a nice modal ('package detected — with N samples, M presets') to register it. Current state (verified 2026-08-26): modules already work this way (packages_dir is scanned into module_load_roots at startup); samples do NOT — reconcile_installed_package_samples (package_samples.rs, samples.jsonl manifest → sample DB) is only called from the git-install path (package_install.rs:214), so a hand-cloned package's samples silently never ingest. Gaps: (1) run sample reconcile at startup, (2) define how packages declare presets/instruments and register them into the browsers, (3) the live-detection + modal flow. Related: eseq-mods.18 (Packages tab, v0.2).
notes: 2026-08-26 decision: both flows stay. The CLI path (eseq package install = clone + validate + atomic publish + sample reconcile) is fine as-is; this bead's job is making the hand-clone path equally first-class — startup reconcile closes the samples gap, and the live-detection modal is the polish layer on top. No plan to retire either flow.

title: [bug] File drag-and-drop does not work on Linux
description: Dropping files onto the window does nothing on Linux, so the sample-import gesture is dead there (likely the winit Wayland file-drop gap; verify against the compositor/backend in use, and check whether X11/XWayland behaves differently). Blocks the revamped sample import flow (eseq-2k9p.7) from being cross-platform.
notes: Root cause confirmed: winit 0.29 implements DroppedFile through XDND on X11 but has no Wayland data-device implementation. The Linux wgpu app now explicitly creates an X11/XWayland event loop, allowing the compositor to bridge native Wayland drags to winit's existing DroppedFile -> BackendEvent::FileDrop -> SampleImportSession path. Added a Linux display-backed regression proving the event loop is X11. Validation: exact nextest regression passed; exact existing backend event test passed; CFLAGS=-D_GNU_SOURCE cargo check -p sequencer --bin metal_seq passed. Existing unrelated compiler warnings remain.
close_reason: Fixed in 3260d893. title: Give the Lisp VM a sampling profiler: per-function attribution for UI renders
description:
## Problem

eseq-pgru had to localise a 126 ms panel render by hand-bisecting content Lisp
(stub a helper, rerun the probe, diff the medians) because no CPU profile was
obtainable:

- perf is not installed on the Linux workstation
- eu-stack / gdb -p cannot attach: yama ptrace_scope=1 requires the tracer to be
  an ancestor of the tracee, and a sibling sampler is denied
- a gdb-launched async interrupt/backtrace loop in batch mode did not produce
  samples

That worked, but it cost hours and it only finds costs large enough to show
through a stubbed-out helper. It found three real pathologies
(namespace-map clone per reactive-get, filter-based find-first per control,
linear global_names scan per reactive read) and then hit a floor of ~1.1 ms per
rendered control that could not be attributed further.

## Goal

An in-process, env-gated sampling or instrumenting profiler in eseqlisp that
attributes VM execution time to Lisp function names, so 'why does one control
cost 1.1 ms' is answerable in one run. The VM already has the pieces:
reactive_exec_timings gives per-effect attribution, and chunks carry names —
what is missing is per-call-frame attribution below the effect boundary.

Should compose with the existing ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI / ESEQLISP_TRACE_UI /
ESEQLISP_PROFILE_CLONES switches and cost nothing when unset.

## Acceptance

- running the drift probe with the switch on prints a ranked per-function
  attribution of the *fx* root rerun
- overhead when the switch is unset is unmeasurable on the drift probe
- documented in UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md next to the existing profiling switches

title: Audit side-effect layout refresh (~38ms/switch): halve it
description:
## Problem

Editor::refresh_runtime_side_effects costs ~38 ms on every same-instrument track
switch on the Linux workstation (side_effects_ms in
tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_end_to_end_perf). About 18 ms of that
is inactive-tile layout refresh (inactive_layout_refresh_ms); the rest is the
remainder of refresh_runtime_side_effects, including
sync_reactive_bindings_for_visible_layouts.

This is the second-largest phase after the *fx* root rerun and, unlike the rerun,
it is not obviously required work: the *sequencer* tile is the active one and its
tree barely changes on a track switch (the *sel-sync* projection means only the
row highlight fields move), yet the ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI record shows
reused=0 full=N subtree=0 with fail=cleared:layout-snapshot — every visible tile
takes a FULL relayout, none is reused or partially relaid out.

## Investigation

- why layout snapshots are 'cleared' rather than reused across a track switch
  (editor/mod.rs refresh_visible_layouts_* / cached_layout_widget_tree_revision)
- whether targeted subtree relayout can apply when only bound float fields moved
- what sync_reactive_bindings_for_visible_layouts costs and whether it must walk
  every widget of every visible layout every frame
- tiles whose buffer did not change should not relayout at all

Note eseq-md1n.1 may remove most of the *fx* tile's share by making the fx tree
identical across a same-instrument switch; this bead owns the cost that remains
for the tiles that genuinely did not change.

## Acceptance

- side_effects_ms and inactive_layout_refresh_ms on the drift probe both at least
  halve
- inactive visible tiles still keep their dirty work across active-tile
  relayouts (the existing UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md rule)
- the probe's in-frame assertions still pass on every sample; no visible update
  is deferred to a later frame

title: Audit track-switch state publication (~14ms/switch): halve it
description:
## Problem

The reactive_tick 'track switch — rebuild everything' branch costs ~13.5-14 ms
per switch on the Linux workstation, measured as the track_switch_ms phase of
tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_end_to_end_perf (see
UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md, 'Same-instrument track-switch probe (Linux)'). That is
pure host-side publication: it runs sync_track_name_state, sync_pattern_state,
build_steps_value, sync_piano_roll_state, sync_step_param_lists,
sync_track_mixer_state, sync_bus_mixer_state, the peak/modulator field syncs,
build_effects_value, build_midi_effects_value, build_instrument_panel_value,
build_accumulator_names, the two param-sync revisions, build_step_has_plocks and
sync_sidebar_browser — unconditionally, for every track change.

A further ~5 ms lands in epoch_sync_ms right after it, because clearing the step
selection bumps fx_epoch and the fx-epoch branch then rebuilds
effects/midi-effects/instrument-panel/bus-effects AGAIN in the same frame. The
probe reports fx_epoch_updates=20/20 for every measured switch.

## Goal

At least 2x on track_switch_ms + epoch_sync_ms without dropping any state the
destination frame needs. Likely levers: do not rebuild what the immediately
following fx-epoch branch is about to rebuild; skip syncs whose inputs did not
change (the ParamSyncRevision precedent already exists); and stop
sync_sidebar_browser from re-reading the preset bank off disk on every switch
(visible_preset_items_for_track -> load_instrument_presets does a
read_to_string + serde_json parse of e.g. the 132 KB content/instruments/core/drift.presets
on every track change).

## Acceptance

- track_switch_ms and epoch_sync_ms on the drift probe both at least halve
- no phase moves the work later: the probe's in-frame correctness assertions
  (destination current track, sel-sync highlight fields, fx binding identity,
  panel identity) still pass on every sample
- the drift-switch ceilings in DRIFT_SWITCH_CEILINGS_MS are lowered to match

title: Instrument whole-callback overrun, not just render_chunk
description:
The only audio-callback overrun warning today is at
crates/sequencer/src/audio/callback.rs:627:

    if render_elapsed.as_millis() >= 10 { eprintln!("audio: slow render_chunk; ...") }

It times render_chunk only. Everything before render_start is invisible: the scheduler
snapshot swap (callback.rs:80), sync_sampler_voice_pool / sync_custom_engine_pool /
sync_rack_voice_pools, the keyboard-trigger drain, the BPM and mod-reset param pushes.
That is exactly where the transport-stop underrun lives (see the RT-safety bead), so the
symptom users hear has no corresponding log line.

cpu_load_pct is computed over the whole callback (callback.rs:781) but it is smoothed and
only printed inside trace heartbeats, so it does not identify a single blown block.

Also: eprintln! inside the audio callback is itself an RT violation - it locks stderr and
can allocate. The existing line 627 warning is already doing this. Any new instrumentation
must not repeat it.
design:
Time the whole callback, split into pre-render and render phases, and report from a
non-RT thread:

1. In the callback, record callback_start.elapsed() at the end (callback_start already
   exists at callback.rs:58) plus a pre-render split taken just before render_start.
2. Publish into lock-free atomics/counters on SequencerState: worst-block micro for each
   phase, a count of blocks exceeding the block budget (block_size / sample_rate), and the
   snapshot-retire-queue-full counter from the RT-safety bead.
3. A non-RT thread (the scheduler loop is already polling at 1-2ms) reads and logs those
   counters, rate-limited. Nothing in the callback prints.
4. Replace the existing eprintln! at callback.rs:627 with the same counter mechanism so the
   RT thread stops writing to stderr at all.
5. Keep it always-on and cheap (two Instant::now calls plus a few relaxed atomic stores);
   gate only the reporting verbosity behind the existing trace_audio / TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_TRACE
   style flag.
acceptance_criteria:
All Linux-verifiable.

1. Unit test: the phase accounting records pre-render and render separately and the
   over-budget counter increments when a synthetic block exceeds the budget.
2. Grep assertion (or test) that crates/sequencer/src/audio/callback.rs contains no
   eprintln!/println! on the per-block path.
3. Manual on Linux: running a project and pausing 20 times reports the worst pre-render
   and render block times, and the counters attribute any over-budget block to a phase.
4. cargo nextest run -p sequencer over the touched modules is green.
notes:
Companion to the transport-stop RT-safety bead: this is what turns "no underrun
observed" into a measured before/after number for the snapshot-retire change. Not a hard
blocker for that bead - ALSA prints the underrun on its own - so the two can land in either
order.

Do not verify by launching the app or running large test suites while Alec is at the machine.

title: Dropdown: draw the selected-item checkmark as vector/SDF instead of the "✓" glyph
description:
Dropdown menus mark the selected item with a "✓" (U+2713) emitted as a ProportionalText primitive at crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/dropdown.rs:1110 (column reserved by check_col_width at :1025). Like the disclosure triangles (eseq-linux.70), this glyph is missing from the Noto Sans face the proportional atlas resolves to on Linux, and fontdue has no per-glyph fallback, so it renders as a tofu square. Replace the text glyph with a drawn checkmark next to the selected item.

The dropdown menu is Rust-rendered (overlay primitives), not content lisp, so this cannot directly reuse the lisp sdf-stdlib materials path. Draw it with existing overlay primitives — e.g. two stroked segments via GpuPrimitive::Quad/Triangle (widget_render/mod.rs:747), or whatever thin-line primitive the overlay layer already supports — sized off menu_font_size so it scales with the menu.
design: Keep the same check_col_width layout slot and check_color; only the mark's rendering changes. Match stroke weight to the menu text weight so it does not read heavier than the labels. If a shared Rust-side helper falls out of this (checkmark path builder), note it for the other Rust-side tofu sites (tree.rs:795, timeline.rs:640, number_picker.rs:732), but they are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable: dropdown.rs no longer emits "✓" text for the selected item; the selected item shows a drawn checkmark in the existing check column; action menus (action_menu=true) still show no mark; existing dropdown tests stay green (assert behavior/state, not colors/exact placement per UI test policy). Visual sign-off by Alec on the Linux workstation.
notes: Implemented a backend-paired SDF checkmark overlay sized from menu_font_size, preserving the existing check column/color and suppressing marks for action menus. Added behavioral coverage and validated all dropdown unit tests plus WGSL shader parsing (12 passed). Alec completed Linux visual sign-off.
close_reason: Implemented, tested, committed as e28ad4ee, and visually approved on Linux.

title: Replace disclosure-triangle glyphs with reusable SDF symbols (mixer + sequencer groups/drum racks)
description:
The collapse/expand controls for groups and drum racks render the Unicode triangles "▸" (U+25B8) / "▾" (U+25BE) as button labels. On Linux the proportional UI font resolves to Noto Sans, which lacks the Geometric Shapes block, and fontdue has no per-glyph fallback, so they render as .notdef tofu squares. Alec also dislikes how the font glyphs rendered on macOS, so the fix is to stop using text glyphs entirely and draw the symbols as SDFs.

What to do:
1. Add reusable symbol SDF functions to content/core/sdf-stdlib.lisp (the sdf/* macro module) — e.g. a triangle primitive plus disclosure-right/disclosure-down helpers built on it. There is currently no triangle in the stdlib (only circle/rect/rounded-rect/line + ops).
2. Use them to replace the glyph labels in both buffers:
   - Mixer buffer: group + drum-rack collapse button at content/ui/mixer.lisp:1495 ((button (if (get group :collapsed) "▸" "▾") ...) inside the group badge).
   - Sequencer buffer: group + drum-rack collapse button at content/ui/sequencer.lisp:2167 ((button (if (eseq.drum-rack-v2/collapsed? gidx) "▸" "▾") ...)).
design:
Buttons currently take text labels; SDF rendering in content flows through named materials (sdf/layer in content/ui/materials.lisp) referenced via :background. Likely shape: define the triangle SDF in sdf-stdlib, define collapse-indicator materials in materials.lisp, and give the buttons an empty/space label with the material background — or whatever cleaner hook exists for icon buttons. The SDF DSL compiles per-backend via lang/sdf_codegen.rs emitters, so a stdlib function works on both wgpu and Metal for free.

Adjacent rider (optional, same stdlib function rotated): the pad-page prev/next buttons at content/ui/sequencer.lisp:2022 and 2031 use "◂"/"▸" and have the same missing-glyph problem. Other tofu sites (tree.rs:795, timeline.rs:640, number_picker.rs:732) are Rust-side and out of scope here; dropdown checkmark is its own bead.
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable: sdf-stdlib gains reusable symbol function(s); mixer.lisp:1495 and sequencer.lisp:2167 collapse buttons no longer contain U+25B8/U+25BE text; collapsed/expanded state still toggles the indicator between right- and down-pointing; existing eseqlisp tests stay green (per UI test policy, assert behavior/state/size, not colors or exact placement). Visual sign-off by Alec on the Linux workstation — hand over the binary, do not launch repeatedly.
close_reason: Implemented reusable triangle/disclosure SDFs and replaced mixer/sequencer collapse glyph controls; targeted collapsed mixer/sequencer UI load/layout test passes.

title: Window close request (super+w / WM close) does not quit the app on Linux
description:
Found during eseq-linux.59 live testing (Alec, 2026-08-24): pressing super+w (Omarchy/Hyprland close-window) does nothing; the eseq window stays open and the process keeps running.

Mechanics: the WM sends a close request, winit delivers WindowEvent::CloseRequested, and WgpuAppBackend (like MetalBackend) translates it into a synthetic Ctrl+C crossterm key event. That key then rides the normal editor key path, where it evidently does not reach a quit - most plausibly it is consumed by mode/modal routing, or Ctrl+C simply is not bound to quit in this keymap (the translation predates any Linux run, so it was never exercised against a real WM close).

Fix sketch: give the backend an explicit close-requested flag surfaced to the event loop (or a BackendEvent::Quit variant in eseqlisp::backend) instead of impersonating a keystroke; the loop already has a TickFlow::Quit path via editor.should_quit(). Verify whatever is chosen also matches what the macOS red-button close does, and that a project-dirty state still gets whatever confirmation flow exists.

Workaround meanwhile: quit from inside the app, or kill the process.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux, super+w (or any WM close request) exits metal_seq cleanly: audio engine shuts down through the normal run_event_loop teardown path (no orphan process, no abort). Linux-verifiable.
close_reason: Implemented explicit BackendEvent::Quit handling for wgpu and Metal window close requests, routed through metal_seq's normal editor quit and backend teardown path. Added a Linux wgpu regression test. Committed as 38a48bb1.

title: rtkit fallback: zero-config realtime promotion when direct SCHED_FIFO is denied
description:
Decision from 2026-08-24 discussion: yes to rtkit. Direct pthread_setschedparam stays the first choice (full priority 20/21, needs an rtprio grant per eseq-linux.54), but when it returns EPERM the engine should fall back to RealtimeKit instead of giving up, so a packaged eseq (Omarchy/Arch, Debian, Flatpak) is realtime out of the box with zero terminal setup - the same mechanism PipeWire's own threads use on a stock desktop.

Mechanism (per rtkit's contract):
- D-Bus system-bus call org.freedesktop.RealtimeKit1.MakeThreadRealtime(tid, priority) on /org/freedesktop/RealtimeKit1. The TID must belong to the calling process, but ANY thread in the process may make the call.
- Before calling, the process must set RLIMIT_RTTIME to at most rtkit's RTTimeUSecMax property (default 200ms per burst). Safe for our threads - they block on the ALSA device / block-start condvar every period, which resets the accounting - but an overrunning RT thread gets SIGKILLed, so set it deliberately and document it.
- Read MaxRealtimePriority property (commonly well below our base 20) and clamp: workers at min(base, cap-1)-ish, callback one above them within the cap, degrading to equal priorities if the cap leaves no headroom. Keep callback >= workers always (the eseq-linux.53 invariant).
- rtkit grants SCHED_RR, not SCHED_FIFO. Verification text, the rt_log lines, and the eseq-linux.54 achieved-policy banner must accept/report RR-via-rtkit as success.

Design constraints:
- Do NOT make blocking D-Bus calls from the audio callback thread. The callback's first-entry one-shot (callback.rs) should publish its TID (gettid) and let a non-RT helper (or the control thread) perform the rtkit negotiation for it and for each worker TID. Workers can likewise publish TIDs from worker_main on EPERM rather than each speaking D-Bus.
- Keep the dependency footprint deliberate: a small hand-rolled libdbus/zbus/dbus-crate client on the Rust side, or sd-bus in C - pick one and justify. The C engine currently has no D-Bus dependency; doing the D-Bus work in Rust and passing priorities/TIDs across the FFI keeps graph_engine.c vendored-clean.
- Fallback ladder end state: direct SCHED_FIFO (full priority) -> rtkit SCHED_RR (capped, zero-config) -> SCHED_OTHER with the existing one-shot warning, which should then also mention that rtkit was tried/unavailable.
- No rtkit on the bus (headless box, D-Bus absent): fail silently into the existing warning path, never block startup.

Related: eseq-linux.54 (provisioning + achieved-policy banner; its decide-rtkit item is resolved by this bead), eseq-linux.56 (root README must describe the out-of-the-box rtkit behavior vs the optional full-priority grant).
acceptance_criteria: On a stock PipeWire desktop with NO rtprio grant (RLIMIT_RTPRIO hard=0), starting eseq gets the audiograph workers and the cpal callback thread promoted via rtkit to SCHED_RR (chrt -p shows RR; callback priority >= workers within rtkit's cap) with RLIMIT_RTTIME set; with a grant in place the direct SCHED_FIFO path still wins at full priority; with neither (no rtkit on bus) the one-shot warning fires and audio continues at normal priority; the callback thread never performs blocking D-Bus IPC itself
notes: Post-close review fixes landed as 89812ae6: (1) callbackReported pending marker now stored before invoking the rtkit hook so a preempted SCHED_OTHER callback thread cannot clobber the helper's recorded result; (2) promote() caches only connection/property/transport failures — per-call MakeThreadRealtime method-error replies (e.g. rtkit thread quota) no longer permanently disable the fallback for later threads, notably the callback which asks last. Validated: 68/68 audio module tests green.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the zero-config RealtimeKit fallback

title: bundled_factory_assets_match_their_recipes fails on Linux: baked filter-table assets drifted from recipes
description: effects::filter_table_presets::tests::bundled_factory_assets_match_their_recipes fails deterministically on x86_64 Linux (observed in 3 consecutive full workspace nextest runs, 2026-08-24, e.g. at HEAD 2afe96e1): 'swoop-low: baked file has drifted from its recipe — regenerate the factory assets' (filter_table_presets.rs:2185). Unrelated to the eseq-linux.51 staging race — it failed identically in every run with the fix in place, and Alec confirmed it fails for a separate reason. It is the only failing test in the Linux workspace runs (3727/3728 passing, 10 skipped).
