title: Root README: add Linux section (requirements, build/run, realtime audio provisioning)
description:
The root README.md still says "macOS - Apple platforms only (Metal renderer, CoreAudio output)" and has no Linux instructions, while the eseq-linux branch runs on Linux (wgpu renderer, cpal/ALSA output). Anyone cloning on Linux gets no guidance and, notably, glitchy audio unless they perform the RLIMIT_RTPRIO provisioning dance from eseq-linux.54.

Add a Linux section to the ROOT README covering everything a dev needs to run eseq locally on Linux:

- System requirements: Rust toolchain, clang (DGenLisp compiles DSP at runtime), ALSA dev libs, mesa vulkan driver for wgpu (note the GL fallback behavior once eseq-linux.12 settles it); soften/replace the "Apple platforms only" line.
- Build/run: cargo run invocation for the Linux binary, plus ./scripts/fetch_dgenlisp.sh (lock-file pinned compiler fetch per content/dgenlisp.lock; ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL=/abs/path overrides with a locally built compiler; anything missing the tool hard-fails naming the fetch command).
- Realtime audio provisioning (the glitch-avoidance dance): whatever mechanism eseq-linux.54 ships (limits.d drop-in with rtprio/memlock + realtime group membership + re-login, or systemd LimitRTPRIO, or rtkit), how to verify (chrt -p on the running process, or TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_LOG=1 showing workers at SCHED_FIFO base priority and the cpal callback thread at base+1, per eseq-linux.53), and what the one-shot "SCHED_FIFO priority N denied" warning means: audio still runs at normal priority but glitches under load are expected.
- Audio environment knobs worth knowing: TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT, TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_PRIORITY (base; callback runs base+1), TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_LOG, TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_WORKERS, TINYSEQ_AUDIO_TRACE. Note cpal talks plain ALSA; on PipeWire desktops that routes through pipewire-alsa (say what to expect for device selection/latency).
- Dev workflow need-to-knows: cargo nextest is the expected runner (install command; the 16 MiB RUST_MIN_STACK test stack budget is applied automatically by .cargo/config.toml - do not add local overrides); some tests are cfg(target_os="macos")-gated so Linux counts differ from the macOS baseline in docs/test-suite-performance.md; keep Cargo target dirs off /tmp on tmpfs-rooted boxes (small tmpfs cannot hold one).
- GPU expectations: renderer is tuned for Apple GPUs (UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md); on an iGPU expect a different perf regime until eseq-linux.12 establishes the Linux frame budget; mention how to check which wgpu backend was chosen once .12 adds the startup log.

Depends on eseq-linux.54 because the docs must describe the provisioning mechanism .54 actually chooses.
acceptance_criteria: Root README.md has a Linux section a fresh Linux dev can follow end-to-end: system deps, build, fetch DGenLisp, run, provision rtprio, verify SCHED_FIFO via chrt or TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_LOG=1, plus the dev need-to-knows (nextest runner and stack budget, audio env vars, macOS-gated test caveat, iGPU perf expectations); the 'Apple platforms only' claim is gone
notes: Also mention in the Linux section: the app requires a native Wayland session (winit Wayland backend). HiDPI/fractional scaling (e.g. Hyprland monitor scale 1.6) is handled via WindowEvent::ScaleFactorChanged + wp-fractional-scale-v1; running under X11/XWayland is unsupported/untested and will not pick up the compositor scale (eseq-linux.63).
close_reason: README.md rewritten in commit be8ae78b: per-platform system requirements (Wayland-only session, ALSA/windowing dev libs, Vulkan driver + gpu_adapter assert with ESEQ_GPU_BACKEND/ESEQ_ALLOW_GPU_FALLBACK, JetBrains Mono), corrected DGenLisp story (hermetic toolchain via both fetch scripts, ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL override), realtime-audio section (FIFO->rtkit->OTHER ladder, limits.d recipe, RT_LOG/chrt verification, denial-warning meaning, TINYSEQ_* knobs, pipewire-alsa note), and dev notes (nextest + 16MiB stack budget, macOS-gated test caveat -> docs/linux-validation.md, tmpfs target dirs, iGPU perf). 'Apple platforms only' claim is gone.

title: Provision RLIMIT_RTPRIO on Linux: the SCHED_FIFO path is denied on every dev/user box today
description:
eseq-linux.11 shipped the SCHED_FIFO code path (and eseq-linux.53 extended it to the cpal callback thread), but nothing grants the process permission to use it, so it is dead code on an unconfigured host. Measured on the Linux dev box 2026-08-24 with a direct C probe:

RLIMIT_RTPRIO soft=0 hard=0
pthread_setschedparam(SCHED_FIFO,20) -> rc=1 (Operation not permitted)

No rtkit-daemon.service on the box, no rtprio line in /etc/security/limits.conf or limits.d, and the user is not in a realtime/audio group (groups: alec docker input wheel). Every audiograph worker therefore takes the EPERM branch at graph_engine.c:571 and runs at normal priority. The one-shot warning is the ONLY signal, and it names the fix but nothing performs it.

Work:

- Ship a limits.d drop-in for the realtime group (rtprio 95, memlock unlimited) plus documented group membership, or a systemd user-unit LimitRTPRIO, whichever fits how eseq is launched on Linux. This remains the full-priority path for dev boxes and power users even once rtkit lands.
- Document the requirement in the audiograph README next to the existing RT notes so it is not rediscovered by a glitch report. (User-facing docs on the ROOT README are tracked separately in eseq-linux.56.)
- Surface the outcome at startup: the engine.rs banner currently prints the REQUESTED SCHED_FIFO priorities regardless of whether promotion actually succeeded. Report the ACHIEVED policy, not the requested one. Design the report so it can also express the rtkit outcome (SCHED_RR at a capped priority) once eseq-linux.58 lands.

DECIDED 2026-08-24: the rtkit fallback question is resolved YES and moved to its own bead, eseq-linux.58 (zero-config promotion for packaged installs). This bead stays scoped to host provisioning + docs + the achieved-policy banner.

ORDERING HAZARD (resolved): eseq-linux.53 landed 2026-08-24 (commit 2afe96e1), so granting rtprio now promotes the callback thread to base+1 above the workers; the previous inversion hazard is gone.
acceptance_criteria: On a provisioned Linux host, audiograph workers AND the cpal callback thread verifiably run at SCHED_FIFO with the callback one step above the workers (chrt -p / TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_RT_LOG=1); the startup banner reports the policy actually achieved rather than the one requested; the provisioning step is documented in crates/sequencer/audiograph/README.md (root README docs are eseq-linux.56)
notes: Packaged-distribution UX (2026-08-24 discussion): once eseq ships as a signed distro package (Omarchy/Arch, Debian, Flatpak), the limits.d+group route means every end user does terminal setup + re-login before RT works. rtkit avoids that entirely: any PipeWire desktop already runs rtkit-daemon, and per-thread MakeThreadRealtime D-Bus calls promote with zero user action (it is how PipeWire's own threads go RT on stock installs). So the 'decide whether to add rtkit fallback' item should lean YES for the packaged future. Caveats to design for: rtkit caps the granted priority (may be below our requested base 20 / callback 21 - accept what is granted, keep callback >= workers within the grant), it requires the caller to set RLIMIT_RTTIME first (safe for threads that block on the device each period; overrun means SIGKILL), and Flatpak can ONLY use rtkit (no file caps). Fallback order: direct pthread_setschedparam (full priority, needs rtprio grant) -> rtkit (capped, zero-config) -> SCHED_OTHER with the existing one-shot warning. setcap cap_sys_nice+ep in a package postinst is the blunter zero-config alternative with Debian precedent but no Flatpak story.
close_reason: Implemented in 9d9da036: shipped PAM limits.d provisioning and documentation, added achieved native scheduling status for workers/callback (including SCHED_RR), and validated worker/callback reporting plus the CPAL startup banner on Linux. This session has RLIMIT_RTPRIO hard=0, so it verified the truthful SCHED_OTHER fallback; the documented re-login is required to exercise the installed FIFO grant.

title: Parallel nextest processes sweep each other's dylib-cache staging dirs, bypassing the leasing system
description:
7 DGen tests fail under a parallel workspace run and pass under --test-threads=1. The app
is not affected: it uses the dylib leasing system, which parallel tests bypass.

MECHANISM (crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dylib_cache.rs, sweep_cache_root ~line 864):
manager construction sweeps every staging dir under the current schema tier except those
whose artifact-id starts with this process's pid. Under nextest each test is its OWN
PROCESS sharing .eseq/dgenlisp-cache/, so process B's sweep deletes process A's in-flight
staging dir while A's linker is still writing into it:

  ld.lld: error: cannot open output file
    .eseq/dgenlisp-cache/3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/staging/<pid>-<ts>-0.tmp/dgen_effect_*.so
    No such file or directory

The doc comment above the function states the assumption that fails: 'Nothing can be leased
at manager construction, so all staging dirs are orphans -- except ones created by *this*
process (another live manager instance sharing the root may be mid-compile)'. That reasons
about a second manager inside one process; it does not account for a second process.

OBSERVED 2026-08-24 on x86_64 Linux, all 7 green under --test-threads=1:
  app::effects::tests::filter_table_editor_session_edits_audition_save_and_restore
  app::effects::tests::filter_table_asset_loads_as_source_with_deterministic_reference
  app::effects::tests::filter_table_engine_toggle_recompiles_and_preserves_state
  app::effects::tests::sidechain_effect_descriptor_uses_other_tracks_as_options
  app::graph::tests::rack_preset_round_trips_dgen_hosted_builtins
  effects::filter_table::tests::bundled_dsp_smoothing_preserves_steady_state
  lisp_host::tests::digitone_bellington_high_note_remains_finite
Failure count varies run to run (16 on a cold cache, 8 warm), which is the race window
narrowing as fewer compiles are needed -- another reason the raw count is not a stable
signal.

This surfaces on Linux only because Linux only just started compiling DGen patches at all
(eseq-linux.47); the same race is latent on macOS.

FIX SHAPE: the sweep needs liveness, not pid-identity. Options: skip staging dirs younger
than some age; take an advisory lock (flock) on a staging dir for the duration of a compile
and only sweep unlocked ones; or give tests a per-process cache root so they never share
staging. The last is the cheapest and narrowest if the goal is only to unblock the suite,
but it hides the underlying race rather than fixing it -- if two eseq instances can ever
share a cache root in production, prefer the lock.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TESTS: eseq-linux.32 adds a Linux CI job running the full suite. On a
fresh runner the cache is always cold, which is the worst case for this race, so CI will be
flaky from day one unless this is fixed or tests are given isolated cache roots.
acceptance_criteria: A full parallel workspace run on x86_64 Linux shows none of the 7 listed tests failing with the 'cannot open output file' staging diagnostic, across at least 3 consecutive runs starting from a cold .eseq/dgenlisp-cache. If the fix is per-process cache roots rather than liveness-aware sweeping, sweep_cache_root's doc comment is corrected to state that it is unsafe for multiple processes sharing a root.
close_reason: Fixed by flock-based staging liveness in dylib_cache.rs (commit 0fdd3bd3). A compile holds an exclusive advisory flock on a sibling <artifact-id>.tmp.lock from before the staging dir exists until it is renamed/cleaned; the sweep only deletes staging whose lock it can acquire (or whose lock file is gone), with fd/path inode re-verification closing the create-vs-unlink race. Validated: 3 consecutive full parallel workspace nextest runs on x86_64 Linux from cold .eseq/dgenlisp-cache — all 7 listed tests green every run, zero 'cannot open output file' diagnostics. Only failure each run was the known unrelated bundled_factory_assets_match_their_recipes asset drift.

title: Factory filter-table assets fail exact-equality against their recipes on Linux (1-2 ULP f32 drift)
description:
effects::filter_table_presets::tests::bundled_factory_assets_match_their_recipes fails on
x86_64 Linux. It is NOT the parallel dylib-cache artifact that accounts for the other Linux
DGen test failures: it fails identically under --test-threads=1, in 0.13s, with no DGen
compilation involved at all.

MEASURED 2026-08-24 (preset swoop-low, recomputed vs baked):
  array length      65600 both sides
  differing         212 elements (0.32%)
  max abs diff      2.7e-07
  relative diff     ~1e-07 across the board, i.e. 1-2 ULP of f32
  first divergence  index 1031 (left 0.38371944, right 0.3837194)

The first ~1000 elements are bit-identical, which is what makes this cross-platform float
drift rather than a wrong recipe: the computation agrees until rounding accumulates. The
baked assets under content/ were generated on Apple Silicon; the recipe recomputed on
x86_64 lands 1-2 ULP away in 0.3% of samples. assert_eq! on Vec<f32> then fails.

Plausible sources, in likely order: differing FMA contraction between arm64 and x86-64-v3,
libm transcendental implementations differing between platforms, and vectorization width
changing the summation order in the recipe's accumulation.

FIX SHAPE (decide deliberately, do not just loosen the assert):
  a) compare with a stated f32 tolerance instead of exact equality -- correct if the assets
     are a cache of a deterministic-in-spirit computation;
  b) make the recipe bit-reproducible across platforms (explicit FMA control, fixed
     summation order, own the transcendentals) -- correct if bit-identical factory content
     across platforms is a product requirement;
  c) bake per-platform assets -- almost certainly wrong, listed to be rejected explicitly.

Option (a) is probably right, but the tolerance must be justified in the test rather than
tuned until green.

PROVENANCE: found while verifying eseq-linux.47. It was inside the 66-failure count
eseq-linux.12 recorded, which attributed the whole set to the missing toolchain stage; with
the stage published that attribution turns out to have been true for all but this one.
acceptance_criteria: bundled_factory_assets_match_their_recipes passes on x86_64 Linux and on Apple Silicon macOS, with the chosen fix documented in the test (a stated tolerance and why it is that value, or a bit-reproducibility guarantee), not by regenerating assets for one platform.
close_reason: Documented the cross-platform libm contract and replaced exact asset equality with a justified 32*f32::EPSILON relative-error bound; targeted Linux nextest passes.

title: CLAUDE.md cheap clean-HEAD recipe is unsound: dead toolchain export + shared target dir runs the wrong binary
description:
Two defects in the "Cheap clean-HEAD check" recipe in CLAUDE.md (also mirrored in AGENTS.md).

1. It exports
     ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT="$root/crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain"
   which does not exist in any Linux checkout (gitignored ~147 MB stage, never
   produced for Linux -- see eseq-linux.30). app_paths warns and ignores a
   non-directory override, so it is inert-but-misleading; the patcher harness no
   longer reads it at all after eseq-linux.37. Either drop the export or make the
   recipe set it only when the stage exists.

2. Sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR between the disposable worktree and the working
   checkout SILENTLY POISONS the working checkout. Observed 2026-08-24:

     - ran the recipe against /tmp/eseq-head-test with
       CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/alec/code/eseq/target
     - afterwards, two consecutive `cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib` runs from
       /home/alec/code/eseq executed the HEAD-built test binary, not the working
       tree: panics reported source lines exactly 226 lower, matching the line
       delta of the uncommitted edit. Tests that pass in the working tree reported
       as failing.
     - `touch` on the edited source forced a rebuild and the failures vanished.

   Cargo reuses the same unit fingerprint for the two checkouts, so whichever ran
   last wins. Anyone using this recipe to "check whether a failure is pre-existing"
   can get the exact opposite answer. The recipe should either use a separate
   target dir for the worktree, or say explicitly that the working checkout must be
   rebuilt (touch a source file / cargo build) after each worktree run.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md no longer instruct exporting a path that does not exist, and the clean-HEAD recipe cannot silently make the working checkout run the worktree binary.
close_reason: Updated CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md to remove the dead DGen toolchain override and use a dedicated clean-HEAD target directory, preventing cross-worktree Cargo artifact poisoning. Committed as 14930a5b.

title: Training unavailable on Linux: degrade the Learn path gracefully instead of failing
description:
Implements the epic's scope decision (user, 2026-08-23) that the DGenLisp "train"
subcommand is out of scope for Linux because it is Metal-based upstream. Porting
the optimizer is NOT in scope here and must not be attempted.

CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (user): an earlier version of this bead said to disable a UI
control. THERE IS NO CONTROL TO DISABLE. Patch Learn is reachable only by manually
running M-x open-learn-patch from an instrument patcher buffer. content/ui/main.lisp:31
says so explicitly:

    ;; Deliberately command-only for now: Patch Learn has no button in the patch
    ;; editor. Invoke this while the instrument patcher buffer is active.
    (def open-learn-patch ()
      (host-command "open-learn-patch"
        (dict :patcher-buffer (current-buffer-name))))

So this bead is NOT about hiding a button. It is about making the command itself
say clearly that training is unavailable on this platform, instead of opening the
Learn UI and failing later once a job is actually launched.

ENTRY POINT AND THE PATTERN TO COPY:
  crates/sequencer/src/ui/host_commands/learn.rs:22  "open-learn-patch" arm
That handler ALREADY has the right shape for a precondition failure -- it emits a
status line and returns early:

    editor.handle_host_event(HostEvent::Status(
        "Open Patch Learn from an instrument patcher buffer".to_string(),
    ));
    return;

Add a platform check in the same style, as the FIRST check in the arm, before the
instrument-session lookup. A message naming the platform and the reason is enough;
match the existing terse status-line voice rather than writing a paragraph.

WHERE TO GATE: at open-learn-patch, not at start-learn-job. Opening is the earliest
point and stops the user before they configure a target and parameters. The actual
launch is further along at crates/sequencer/src/ui/event_loop.rs:1821
(launch_learn_job); gating there would let someone set up a whole job first and
only then be told it cannot run. Gate early. The sibling commands in
host_commands/learn.rs COMMANDS (set-learn-target, configure-learn, start-learn-job,
stop-learn-job, replan-learn-job, apply-learn-result, close-learn-patch) become
unreachable through normal use once open is gated -- decide whether that is
sufficient or whether start-learn-job deserves a defence-in-depth check too, and
say which you chose.

DO NOT REMOVE THE COMMAND FROM M-x. crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/tests.rs:15930
asserts open-learn-patch appears in collect_mx_candidates(), and a command that
silently vanishes is worse UX than one that explains itself. Keep it listed and
let it report.

KEEP MACOS BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED. Use a cfg or capability check, not a removal.
Leave content/ui/patch-learn.lisp, the patch-learn capture fixture, and the
state_values tests intact -- they exercise UI state, not the trainer, and must keep
passing on both platforms.

STILL WORTH DOING FIRST: establish what actually happens today on Linux when the
command is run and a job is launched, and record it in the notes. The Linux
DGenLisp is compile-only, so the train subprocess will fail or be rejected -- find
out which, and what learn_job.rs does with that (surfaces an error, retries, or
leaves the job pending forever). That is the evidence this bead was needed.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux, M-x open-learn-patch reports that training is unavailable on this platform and does not open the Learn buffer; the command remains listed in collect_mx_candidates() and state_values/tests.rs:15930 still passes; the check lives in the open-learn-patch arm of host_commands/learn.rs and matches the existing early-return status-line pattern; whether start-learn-job also got a defence-in-depth check is stated either way; the pre-change Linux behaviour is recorded in the notes; macOS is gated by cfg/capability rather than removal and its behaviour is unchanged; patch-learn fixtures and state_values tests pass on both platforms; no optimizer porting was attempted
notes:
Pre-change Linux probe (2026-08-24): the pinned DGenLisp-linux-x86_64 accepts the host's train argv. With --plan-only and an explicit pitch it emits a valid plan event and exits 0. Without --plan-only it emits the plan, then stderr reports 'train-render error: runtimeError("Metal backend is unavailable on this platform; use the C backend (DGenConfig.backend = .c)")', emits a terminal JSON error ('train-render exited 1'), and exits 1. learn_job.rs forwards the JSON error as LearnEvent::Error followed by Exited; poll_learn_job publishes the error phase, clears preview state, and removes the pending job. It does not retry or remain pending. Implementation choice: gate open-learn-patch first on Linux and also gate start-learn-job as defence in depth against direct/custom command dispatch; macOS remains enabled via cfg.

Review (2026-08-24, reviewer): commit 6324773b accepted, no fixes needed. Verified on Linux: `cargo nextest run -p sequencer -E 'test(learn_job::)'` is 9/9 green including the new patch_training_reports_its_linux_platform_requirement; COMMANDS still lists open-learn-patch so collect_mx_candidates() is unchanged; state_values/tests.rs:15954 reaches Patch Learn through crate::host_commands::open_patch_learn_buffer directly, not through the gated dispatch arm, so that test is unaffected; the new code is rustfmt-clean (the rest of learn_job.rs has pre-existing drift). Independently corroborated the pre-change probe: the pinned Linux DGenLisp binary contains the exact string 'Metal backend is unavailable on this platform; use the C backend (DGenConfig.backend = .c)'. LearnLaunchKind::Train has exactly one call site (host_commands/learn.rs:193, the gated start-learn-job arm); the three Plan launches are all downstream of the gated open. The non-Linux cfg arm was compile-checked out of tree with the cfgs flipped, since it cannot be built here.

Reviewer caveats recorded, neither a defect in this change: (1) ui/main.rs:12 includes metal_main.rs only on macOS, so the whole ui/ tree - host_commands/learn.rs included - does not compile on Linux today (cargo nextest lists 0 tests in bin/metal_seq here). The gate is therefore correct-but-dormant on Linux and only becomes observable once the wgpu UI port lands; it could not be exercised end to end on this host by any implementation of this bead. (2) training_unavailable_reason() keys on cfg(target_os = \"linux\") while the actual blocker is Metal, i.e. macOS-only; a hypothetical third target would report training as available and fail at runtime. Left as-is deliberately - the bead asked for a message naming the platform, and no third target exists in this repo - but note ui/main.rs uses not(target_os = \"macos\") for the same Metal reasoning.
close_reason: Reviewed: Patch Learn is gated at open-learn-patch with a status-line early return, plus a defence-in-depth gate at start-learn-job; macOS unchanged via cfg; learn_job tests 9/9 green on Linux.

title: Hermetic dgen toolchain is arm64-only; Linux compiles fall back to the system compiler
description:
Found 2026-08-23 while validating the Linux DGenLisp binary.

content/dgen-toolchain.lock pins a single archive with no platform or arch dimension:
  archive       dgen-toolchain-20.1.8-arm64.tar.gz
  llvm_version  20.1.8
  dgen_abi_version 1

The staged stage directory crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain/ is gitignored (~147 MB) and is EMPTY on this Linux box -- nothing has ever staged an x86_64 equivalent, and the pinned archive is arm64 anyway.

Despite that, compiling through the Linux DGenLisp succeeded and emitted a working .so. That means the Linux path silently fell back to the SYSTEM compiler rather than the hermetic clang/lld stage. Reproduced with:

  DGenLisp compile t.lisp -o out --name patcher_dgen_compile_test \
    --sample-rate 44100 --voices 12
  -> out/patcher_dgen_compile_test.{c,json,so}, processAbi dgen-host-abi-v1

WHY THIS MATTERS: hermeticity is the whole point of the staged toolchain -- pinned LLVM version, reproducible codegen, no dependence on whatever clang a contributor happens to have. On Linux that guarantee is currently absent and, worse, absent SILENTLY: the build succeeds, so nobody notices that two machines can produce different audio binaries from identical source.

SCOPE:
 • Give content/dgen-toolchain.lock a platform/arch dimension (archive + sha256 per target) rather than one flat entry.
 • Establish where an x86_64-linux toolchain archive comes from -- built upstream in dgen-audio, or fetched. Coordinate with eseq-linux.15, which touches rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh (the script that stages the archive and maintains this lock).
 • Decide the fallback policy explicitly and implement it: either hard-fail when no matching stage exists for the host target, or warn loudly. Silent fallback is the actual bug here.
 • DGenLisp already accepts --toolchain-root and honours DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_STAGE_ROOT; eseq passes ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT. Verify the whole chain reports, rather than swallows, a missing or wrong-arch stage.

This is independent of whether the DGenLisp binary itself is committed -- it is about the compiler the binary invokes.
acceptance_criteria: content/dgen-toolchain.lock carries per-target archive identities; a missing or wrong-arch toolchain stage produces a clear diagnostic instead of a silent system-compiler fallback, with a test covering that path; the source of an x86_64-linux toolchain archive is documented in the bead notes even if staging it is deferred; compiling a patch on Linux either uses the hermetic stage or fails loudly saying it cannot
notes: Implemented hard-fail policy in eseq. The x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu archive must be produced and published upstream from /home/alec/code/dgen-audio, currently linux-c-backend at ae25e9d9913ac745c653b6c7df4236b1a42b32f8, by extending scripts/build-toolchain.sh. That upstream script currently hardcodes an arm64-apple-macos LLVM/clang/ld64 stage, so publishing/staging the Linux archive is deliberately deferred; content/dgen-toolchain.lock has no Linux archive identity and Linux now fails clearly instead of selecting /usr/bin/clang. Validation: cargo check -p sequencer --lib --quiet passed; bash syntax and Linux missing-target diagnostic checks passed; git diff --check passed. The targeted nextest run was stopped during sequencer test-binary compilation after exceeding the repository's three-minute budget, and a retry caused the pi harness session to disappear; no tests had started, /tmp retained about 3 GiB free, and no OOM/core dump was recorded.
close_reason: Completed in b398927f: target-qualified lock/staging, mandatory checked toolchain handoff on Linux, wrong-target validation, and cache preflight prevent system-compiler fallback. Linux archive publication remains deliberately deferred and its upstream source is recorded in notes.

title: cargo-nextest is not installed on the Linux dev box, but CLAUDE.md mandates it
description:
CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section says 'Prefer cargo nextest run' and the cheap clean-HEAD check recipe invokes 'cargo nextest run' directly. On the Arch/x86_64 box this fails:

  error: no such command: `nextest`

Consequence, measured 2026-08-23: falling back to plain 'cargo test' shares one process across tests and produces two spurious failures that do not reproduce in isolation -- hot_reload::tests::relative_load_falls_back_to_installed_content_roots and widget_render::waveform::tests::tui_render_highlights_the_active_slice_marker. A worker following CLAUDE.md verbatim hits an unknown-command error; a worker improvising with 'cargo test' gets a red suite with two red herrings in it and may waste a session chasing them.

Also note the CLAUDE.md claim 'As of 2026-08-20 there are no known pre-existing failures: full debug is 4,272 passed / 32 skipped' is a macOS number. The Linux reality on eseqlisp alone is 1,654 passed / 41 failed. That line should be qualified per-platform so nobody reads a red Linux suite as their own regression.

SCOPE:
 • Install cargo-nextest on the Linux box (cargo install cargo-nextest, or the distro/binary release).
 • Confirm the two race-y tests pass under nextest's process-per-test isolation without any source change -- that is the evidence they are isolation artifacts, and it lets the sibling beads be scoped as real cleanups rather than urgent breakage.
 • Update CLAUDE.md AND AGENTS.md (they are independent files, not symlinked -- mirror the edit) to record the per-platform baseline: what green looks like on Linux today, and that it is currently NOT green pending eseq-linux.14.
acceptance_criteria: 'cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp --features wgpu' executes on Linux; the hot_reload and waveform tests pass under nextest with no source change; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md both record a per-platform test baseline and no longer present the macOS pass count as unqualified
notes: cargo-nextest 0.9.143 is available at /home/alec/.cargo/bin/cargo-nextest. On x86_64 Linux, the two exact shared-state regressions passed under nextest (2 passed, 1700 skipped). The acceptance run 'cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp --features wgpu' completed green (1699 passed, 3 skipped, 60.783s). title: Shipped :tick bodies drop quasiquote/unquote markers
description: compile_quoted_expression (crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/compiler.rs) flattens Expression::Quasiquote/Unquote/UnquoteSplicing into their inner form, so a def-sequencer :tick containing `(a ,b) ships to the scheduler VM as (a b) -- a live call form instead of a template. compile_quoted_expression_preserving_quotes already solves the same problem for 'quote by re-emitting it as a (quote x) list; the analogous fix needs the parser to accept the (quasiquote x)/(unquote x) list spellings so the shipped text round-trips. Found while fixing the defscene shipping lowering (PR #57 review): the lowering now correctly rewrites only the unquoted holes, but the markers still do not survive serialization.

title: load_system_ui_font picks a condensed face on Linux (NimbusSansNarrow)
description:
glyph_atlas::load_system_ui_font() has a macOS preference list (SFPro-Regular, .AppleSystemUIFont, Helvetica) and nothing for Linux - it falls straight through to Query{families: [Family::SansSerif]}.

Probed on this box: SizedFontCache::new(1.0) resolves to NimbusSansNarrow-Regular. That is a *condensed* face, so every proportional advance is materially narrower than a normal sans.

This is not just cosmetic. SizedFontCache::measure_text feeds PropTextMeasurer, which is the layout::TextMeasurer the widget layout uses, so label widths, alignment and cells-per-character estimates all shift. patcher/tests.rs:20605 rendered_label_width_cells is still #[cfg(target_os = "macos")], so nothing guards the Linux value.

Needs a Linux preference list (DejaVu Sans / Noto Sans / Liberation Sans / Cantarell / Inter) before the generic SansSerif fallback.
acceptance_criteria: load_system_ui_font names a Linux preference list; a test asserts the resolved UI face is not condensed, or the rendered_label_width_cells guard is extended to Linux with a bounded expectation
close_reason: Closed

title: aubio-sys fails to build on Linux (strncasecmp implicit declaration under -std=c99)
description:
`cargo check -p sequencer` fails on Linux: aubio-sys 0.2.1 compiles its vendored aubio C sources with `-std=c99`, which hides POSIX declarations under glibc. `aubio/src/utils/strutils.c:39` then errors with 'implicit declaration of function strncasecmp' (an error, not a warning, under modern GCC/C23 defaults).

Reproduced during review of eseq-linux.4 on Arch (gcc, glibc). macOS is unaffected because Apple libc exposes strncasecmp regardless of the std level.

This blocks building the sequencer crate at all on Linux, so no workspace-wide build or test run is possible there yet.

Options: set CFLAGS/-D_GNU_SOURCE or -std=gnu99 via a build override, patch/vendor aubio-sys, or move to a maintained fork.
acceptance_criteria: aubio-sys compiles on Linux: 'cargo build -p aubio-sys' (or the equivalent isolated build) succeeds with no implicit-declaration error from strutils.c. NOTE: this bead alone does NOT make 'cargo check -p sequencer' pass -- crates/sequencer/audiograph/dgen_host_services.c:14 independently fails on a missing Accelerate/Accelerate.h, which is eseq-linux.9. Verify by confirming the aubio-sys build-script failure is gone and that the NEXT build-script failure reported is the Accelerate one, not an aubio one. Whole-crate 'cargo check -p sequencer' green is the acceptance of eseq-linux.9, which lands second.
notes: Vendored aubio-sys 0.2.1 and patched its header detection to include POSIX <strings.h> when available. Validation: cargo build -p aubio-sys passes on Linux; cargo check -p sequencer proceeds to the expected Accelerate/Accelerate.h failure tracked by eseq-linux.9.
close_reason: Patched vendored aubio-sys to detect/include strings.h; isolated aubio-sys build passes on Linux.

title: SDF lighting cost: 5x field evaluation per pixel from finite-difference normals
description:
The generated SDF lighting path is the most likely first perf wall on
non-Apple GPUs, and it is fixable entirely in the emitter - no content
changes.

crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/sdf_codegen.rs:640-710 computes the surface normal
by FINITE DIFFERENCES: it evaluates the SDF field at four offset positions
(left, right, up, down) to derive dx/dy, then builds
normalize(float3(dx, dy, 1.0)). So every lit widget evaluates its ENTIRE SDF
expression 5 times per pixel. On top of that, per pixel:
  - 2x normalize (normal, light vector)
  - 2x dot (diffuse, specular)
  - 1x pow() for Blinn-Phong specular (:701-707)

This is not a rare path. content/ui/materials.lisp puts :lighting on
slider-material and slider-material2, so every slider and knob in the UI
pays it.

On Apple silicon this never surfaced (GPU sits ~10%). On an Intel UHD 620 -
roughly 6-8x less ALU, immediate-mode blending instead of TBDR, and DDR4
bandwidth shared with the CPU and the audio engine - this is the term most
likely to dominate.

Options, cheapest first:
  1. Cache the base SDF evaluation and reuse it across the 4 offset taps
     where the expression allows - may cut 5 evaluations toward 4.
  2. Analytic normals for the primitive shapes that have them
     (rounded-rect, circle), falling back to finite differences only for
     arbitrary composed fields.
  3. Replace pow() with a cheaper specular approximation.
  4. A quality tier: emit flat shading (drop :lighting to its :color term)
     under a runtime/backend flag. Lets the Linux target ship before the
     optimization work lands, and gives low-end hardware an escape hatch.

Measure before choosing. Build a shader-cost probe on a representative
sequencer buffer (many sliders and knobs visible) and compare frame time
with lighting on vs forced flat, on BOTH macOS and the UHD 620 box, before
committing to an approach.

Do this work in the emitter so it benefits the Metal target too.
acceptance_criteria: Frame time measured with lighting on vs forced flat on UHD 620; chosen mitigation lands in sdf_codegen.rs and benefits both backends by construction; a flat-shading quality tier exists as a low-end fallback. The macOS half of the frame-time comparison moved to eseq-linux.26.
close_reason: Reviewed ab41d330; emitter tests, wgpu build, and UHD 620 release probe pass

title: Audio on Linux: verify cpal/ALSA block size, add SCHED_FIFO RT worker priority
description:
Audio is close to free but has two real gaps.

cpal (probably fine): usage is vanilla - crates/sequencer/src/audio/stream.rs
:145 cpal::default_host(), :150 StreamConfig with
:153 BufferSize::Fixed(block_size), f32 output. Dev box confirms ALSA 1.2.16
headers present and PipeWire's pulse server running.
  - VERIFY: BufferSize::Fixed is closer to a suggestion on ALSA than on
    CoreAudio. Confirm the requested block size actually lands, and that the
    audiograph's fixed-block assumptions hold if it does not.
  - Consider enabling cpal's `jack` feature for low latency.
  - Check device enumeration in stream.rs:176-190 (supports_f32 probing)
    behaves sanely against ALSA's virtual devices.

RT thread priority (a real gap): crates/sequencer/audiograph/graph_engine.c
already guards Mach with `#if __has_include(<mach/mach.h>)` (:21), and
crates/sequencer/src/audio/engine.rs:392 sets
`mach_rt_default = cfg!(target_os = "macos") && workers > 0`. So it degrades
SAFELY on Linux - but "degrades" means the audio graph worker threads run at
normal priority and will glitch under load.
  - Add a Linux path: pthread_setschedparam with SCHED_FIFO, mirroring what
    thread_policy_set THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY does at
    graph_engine.c:579.
  - Needs rtkit (via D-Bus) or a limits.conf rtprio grant; handle the
    permission-denied case gracefully and log it, matching the existing
    WARN at graph_engine.c:584.
  - Wire the existing TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_MACH_RT env flag (engine.rs:393) or
    introduce a neutral name covering both platforms.
  - graph_engine.c:567 also uses mach_timebase_info for timing; needs a
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: Audio plays on Linux at the requested block size; worker threads acquire RT priority where permitted and log clearly where not; xrun-free under a representative project load
close_reason: Closed

title: dgen host services: drop Accelerate/vDSP (4 symbols) for a portable FFT
description:
crates/sequencer/build.rs unconditionally emits
`cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework=Accelerate`, and
crates/sequencer/audiograph/dgen_host_services.c:14 does
`#include <Accelerate/Accelerate.h>`. Neither exists on Linux.

Good news: the vDSP surface is narrow. Only 4 symbols across 11 call sites:
  vDSP_create_fftsetup
  vDSP_fft_zip
  vDSP_zvma
  vDSP_Length

The DGen ABI v1 host-services table is vDSP-backed; generated DGen dylibs
themselves stay libSystem-only and never link Accelerate, so this is
confined to the host.

Scope:
- Replace the FFT with a portable implementation (kissfft or pffft vendored
  into audiograph/, or expose rustfft through the host-services table -
  rustfft 6.2 is already a sequencer dependency).
- Replace vDSP_zvma (complex vector multiply-add) - trivial to hand-write.
- Make the Accelerate link in build.rs conditional on target_os = macos.
- Keep the ABI v1 host-services table layout byte-identical so existing
  generated dylibs stay valid.

Also confirm the split-radix / packed-complex convention vDSP_fft_zip uses
matches whatever replaces it - this is the classic place to silently get
scaling or bin ordering wrong. Add a numeric test comparing outputs before
switching macOS over.

Related: the eseq-toolchain epic covers shipping the embedded dgen toolchain.
acceptance_criteria: audiograph builds and links on Linux with no Accelerate; 'cargo check -p sequencer' succeeds on Linux (this is the bead that finally turns the sequencer crate green there -- verified 2026-08-23 that Accelerate is the second of exactly two build-script blockers, the first being eseq-linux.16); numeric test shows the replacement FFT matches vDSP output within tolerance; ABI v1 host-services table layout unchanged
notes:
Implemented on branch eseq-linux.

SHAPE: dual-backend rather than a single replacement. Apple targets keep the
vDSP calls byte-for-byte unchanged; everything else gets audiograph/dgen_fft.c,
a hand-written iterative radix-2 in-place split-complex FFT plus the
multiply-accumulate. build.rs now emits the Accelerate link only when
CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS == "macos", but compiles dgen_fft.c on every target so the
comparison tests run on both hosts. Chose this over rustfft/kissfft/pffft: the
callbacks take raw split-complex float pointers straight out of the generated
dylib's state span and run inside the audio callback, so a Rust or vendored
backend would have meant either an allocation-free wrapper anyway or copying
into interleaved buffers per block. The whole thing is ~150 lines of C.

CONVENTIONS PINNED (the "classic place to silently get it wrong" the bead
warns about) -- all three taken from vDSP_fft_zip's / vDSP_zvma's documented
pseudocode:
  - unscaled in BOTH directions, so a forward/inverse round trip scales by N.
    Generated spectral gain compensation is tuned to exactly this.
  - natural DFT bin ordering, no real-FFT packing: unlike vDSP_fft_zrip, bin
    N/2 is its own bin and is never folded into the imaginary part of bin 0.
  - vDSP_zvma is D = A*B + C wired C == D, i.e. accumulate with an ordinary
    (non-conjugated) complex product.
  - one setup serves every transform at most as long as the length it was
    created for, because generated code caches one lazily created static setup
    per call site. The portable twiddle table is therefore indexed by the
    TRANSFORM's length, not the setup's -- mutation-tested: mis-indexing it by
    the setup's length is caught only by
    portable_fft_setup_serves_shorter_transforms.

ABI: dgen_abi_v1.h untouched; a test asserts struct_size still equals
sizeof(DGenHostServicesV1). Existing generated dylibs stay valid.

VALIDATION (Linux): cargo check -p sequencer --lib green -- the first time the
sequencer crate has compiled on Linux. dgen_fft.c and dgen_host_services.c
compile warning-free under gcc and clang at -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic
-Wconversion. 10 new tests in
crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_host_services_tests.rs pass, all
comparing against a naive f64 DFT; two deliberate mutations (inverse direction
flipped, twiddle stride mis-indexed) were confirmed to fail them.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately:
  - `cargo check -p sequencer` including bins is still red, but no longer on
    anything in this bead: the remaining 8 errors are all
    MetalBackend/TiledRenderStatus in the metal_seq bin (eseq-linux.7/.8).
    The lib target, which is what the Accelerate blocker gated, is green.
  - End-to-end spectral render through a real generated .so -- filed as
    eseq-linux.40. Blocked on eseq-linux.30: tools/dgen-toolchain/ is unstaged
    on Linux (the pinned archive is arm64-only), so effect compilation
    hard-fails before any dylib exists. 73 of the 2017 lib tests fail for that
    reason and for Mach-O-only audit fixtures (eseq-linux.10); none of them
    reach the FFT. 1944 pass.
  - The vDSP half of the numeric comparison -- handed to eseq-linux.26 as
    rider 5. The host_services_* tests drive whatever backend the platform
    ships, so running that module once on a Mac pins vDSP to the same
    reference the portable path is already pinned to, which is what turns
    "both match the reference" into "the replacement matches vDSP".
close_reason: Portable radix-2 split-complex FFT in audiograph/dgen_fft.c serves the four ABI v1 host-services callbacks off Apple; macOS keeps vDSP and build.rs links Accelerate only on target_os=macos. ABI table layout untouched. cargo check -p sequencer --lib is green on Linux for the first time (remaining bin errors are metal_seq/eseq-linux.7-.8, not build-script). 10 new tests pin all four callbacks to a naive f64 DFT taken from vDSP's documented pseudocode -- unscaled both directions, natural bin ordering, non-conjugated product, setup reusable for shorter transforms -- and were mutation-checked. macOS half of the vDSP comparison handed to eseq-linux.26 rider 5; end-to-end spectral render filed as eseq-linux.40 (blocked on the unstaged Linux toolchain, eseq-linux.30).

title: Port 25 widget fragment shaders to WGSL (~2165 lines)
description:
Port the per-widget fragment shaders to WGSL. ~2,165 lines of MSL across 25
widget modules in crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/. Depends on
eseq-linux.2 (backend-tagged trait) and the WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE port in
eseq-linux.7, since each of these is concatenated onto that preamble.

By MSL volume:
  sound_glyph 364, mod 247, button 224, response_curve_editor 158,
  adsr_editor 158, matrix 128, phaser_notch 126, modulator_curve 87,
  knob_number 84, roar_shaper 80, multiband_meter 64, roar_filter 63,
  vslider 51, tree 49, plus box_widget knob number_picker scroll timeline
  hslider toggle text_input dropdown.

Note the overlap with eseq-linux.3: some of these hand-written shaders do
work the SDF DSL can already express. Where that is true, consider deleting
the hand-written MSL and moving the widget to a defwidget :shader instead of
maintaining two translations. Evaluate per widget; do not force it.

Same hazards as eseq-linux.7 - no implicit conversions in WGSL, fast-math
and half-precision assumptions, texture sampling. Expect a subset to compile
cleanly and render wrong.

Suggested approach: build a per-widget visual regression harness (render one
widget in isolation, macOS vs Linux, pixel diff) before porting in bulk.
crates/eseqlisp/src/bin/eseqlisp_capture.rs may already be a starting point.
acceptance_criteria: All 25 widgets render correctly on Linux under wgpu, judged self-consistently rather than against a macOS reference; any widget migrated to the SDF DSL instead is noted in the bead; deterministic per-widget captures produced and committed for the same fixed scene set as eseq-linux.7. The per-widget pixel diff vs macOS is NOT part of this bead -- it is eseq-linux.25.
notes: Implemented in commit 35843072. Ported all 29 distinct retained-mode widget fragment bodies to WGSL without SDF migrations. Added Naga parse/validation coverage and schema-v2 deterministic Linux captures for every distinct body; visually reviewed the contact sheet. Validation: exact WGSL validation test, every-scene paint/repro test, and shader_capture_cli determinism test all pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Port the 8 core MSL pipelines in metal_backend.rs to WGSL (~1150 lines)
description:
Port the 8 hand-written MSL pipelines in crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/metal_backend.rs
to WGSL. ~1,149 lines of MSL. Mechanical but real.

  :100  SHADER_SRC                    text quad (vert + frag)
  :147  PROP_FRAG_SRC                 proportional text fragment
  :171  IMAGE_SHADER_SRC              image_vert / image_frag
  :247  PATCH_CABLE_SHADER_SRC        patch_cable_vert (:292) / frag (:467)
  :513  WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE        instance struct, varyings, SDF utils
  :572  DEFAULT_WIDGET_VERTEX_SHADER  widget_vert
  :762  WAVETABLE_SHADER_SRC          wavetable_vert / wavetable_frag
  :924  WAVEFORM_SHADER_SRC           waveform_vert / waveform_frag
  :1170 LIVE_SPECTROGRAM_SHADER_SRC   live_spectrogram_vert / frag

Plus crates/eseqlisp/shaders/button_surface.metal (96 lines), the only
standalone .metal file.

The WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE is the important one - it defines the shared
WidgetInstance struct, WidgetVaryings, and the SDF utility functions that
every per-widget fragment shader (eseq-linux.8) is concatenated onto. Port
it first and get it right.

Known translation hazards beyond type renames:
- WGSL has no implicit numeric conversions; MSL mixes int/float freely.
- [[stage_in]] / [[buffer(n)]] / [[vertex_id]] / [[instance_id]] ->
  @location / @group+@binding / @builtin.
- Texture sampling model differs substantially (separate sampler objects).
- MSL fast-math and half precision defaults may be silently relied on.
  Expect "compiles fine, renders differently" on a subset.

Suggested order: text quad first (proves the glyph atlas end to end), then
image, then widget preamble + default vert, then patch cable, then the three
audio-visualization pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 pipelines render correctly on Linux under wgpu, judged self-consistently (no artifacts, correct geometry/order/color relationships) rather than against a macOS reference; WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE equivalent verified before widget shaders land; deterministic whole-frame captures produced and committed for the fixed scene set so the macOS comparison can run later. The macOS visual diff is NOT part of this bead -- it is eseq-linux.25.
close_reason: All 8 core MSL pipelines ported to WGSL in ui/wgsl_shaders.rs plus shaders/button_surface.wgsl; wgpu pipelines in ui/wgpu_pipelines.rs; widget preamble verified (naga + rendered end-to-end via button_surface, and the 63-shader SDF corpus now assembles onto it); deterministic captures for the fixed 8-scene set committed at tests/fixtures/shader-capture/goldens/wgsl-linux-x86_64. Commit 16c172f7. Follow-up: eseq-linux.44.

title: Give host-resolved slot params a real identity instead of a rebind heuristic
description:
Follow-up from the PR #56 review (commit 13c5149c).

Host-resolved slot params -- the sampler's `slice` / `sens` / `slice base`
tail -- carry `node_param_idx == u32::MAX`, so
`ParamNodeId::from_slot_param` returns `None` and they get no
`ParamNodeId` at all. Every other param relies on that id to reject
p-lock and key-lock rows left behind by a previous binding; for host
params that check is a no-op, and a stale value at the slice tail
silently forces a step into slice mode, rewriting start/end and
sometimes muting the step outright.

WHAT SHIPPED (the stopgap)

Both descriptor sync paths now drop host-resolved rows when the slot is
rebound to a different node:

  - `EffectSlotSnapshot::sync_to_descriptor_with_modulator`
  - `EffectSlotState::sync_descriptor_with_modulator`

guarded on `self.node_id != 0 && != node_id` so a project load (a first
bind, not a rebind) still restores saved slice p-locks. Helper is
`effects::is_host_resolved_param`. Test:
`effects::tests::rebinding_drops_host_resolved_plocks_but_a_first_sync_keeps_them`.

WHY IT WANTS REVISITING

1. It is a heuristic on the WRONG side of the seam. The read path
   (`resolved_sampler_host_param_value` in both `scheduler/params.rs` and
   `audio/params.rs`) still does a raw `slot.plocks[step][138..140]`
   lookup with no identity check, unlike `slot_has_explicit_plock`
   directly below it. Correctness now depends on every writer having been
   scrubbed rather than on the reader being able to tell.

2. It sits in the SHARED sync paths, not sampler-specific ones. Today the
   sampler tail is the only host-resolved param in any descriptor, so the
   blast radius is nil -- but anything added with `node_param_idx ==
   u32::MAX` silently inherits "dropped on rebind", which may not be what
   that param wants.

3. `node_id == 0` as the "first bind" signal is load-bearing and
   undocumented outside the comment at the guard.

PROPOSED DIRECTION

Give host-resolved params a positive identity so the existing machinery
works uniformly -- e.g. a `ParamNodeId` variant keyed on the slot's
`node_id` with a sentinel `node_param_idx` -- then make
`resolved_sampler_host_param_value` go through `plock_identity_matches`
like everything else and delete the sync-path guard.

CAUTION: `EffectSlotSnapshot::param_node_id` feeds neural param binding
and modulation routing. Making host params return `Some(..)` there would
expose them as bindable/modulatable targets. Audit those consumers before
changing `param_node_id` itself; a separate host-param id accessor may be
the safer shape.

title: Audit panel/handler pairs that pass list indices for divergent resolution
description:
Generalized from the eseq-c7q.3 review (commit 3d99cc44). That review found the
sampler slice edit handler resolving slice sensitivity WITHOUT p-locks and rack
macros while the panel resolved it WITH them. Both sides then indexed into a
"same" marker list that was not the same list, so a marker edit could address
the wrong marker.

THE RULE: any host command that carries an INDEX into a panel-rendered list must
resolve that list by exactly the same path the panel used to render it. Divergent
resolution silently retargets the edit; there is no error, just the wrong item.

Values are safe, indices are not. A command carrying the value (or a stable id)
cannot desync this way, which is also the preferred fix wherever the payload can
carry one instead.

WORK

Audit the panel/handler pairs in crates/sequencer/src/ui/host_commands/ for
commands whose payload includes an index, ordinal, or position into a list that
some panel renders. For each, confirm the handler's resolution path matches the
panel's (same p-lock layer, same rack-macro layer, same filtering/sorting, same
fallbacks). Start from the ones whose lists are p-lock- or macro-sensitive,
since that is where the known defect lived.

Where a pair diverges, prefer changing the payload to carry a value or stable id
over patching the handler to duplicate the panel's resolution -- duplicated
resolution is what rots next time either side gains a layer.

Record the audited pairs in the bead so this does not have to be redone blind.

title: defscene readers do not repaint on scene switch
description: Scene-slot readers are re-dirtied only by an authoring set! (sequencer_natives) and by undo/redo (ui/event_loop). Nothing invalidates the '__scene-slot' reactive namespace when the live pattern changes, so a panel bound to a defscene slot keeps showing the previous scene's value after a scene switch until some other write happens. State is correct (scene_slot_overrides_survive_a_scene_switch_round_trip); only the UI is stale. Fix: on scene switch, invalidate every slot the runtime reads with the newly-current scene's epoch. Found reviewing eseq-o1a.5.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
Review of 2120a504 (no rev- tab was spawned for this bead; reviewed from the
main eseq session). The design is right and well tested — the invalidation is
hooked into sync_pattern_state, which is the single funnel for pattern state
into the UI runtime, and epochs are deliberately process-wide monotonic
(scene_slots.rs:6-19), so they are sufficient to distinguish two scenes whose
slot values happen to be equal. Dropping the broad SEQ/current-pattern edge in
favour of the qualified per-slot source is the correct targeting.

ONE PLAUSIBLE HOLE — not verified by running it, needs a repro attempt before
this bead closes.

queue_reactive_namespace_invalidation only iterates
subscribed_injected_reactive_fields, i.e. sources whose `dependents` is
non-empty (vm.rs, the new helper). If a scene switch happens while a slot has
NO live reader, nothing is queued for it and the source node keeps the previous
scene's generation. mark_source_dependents_dirty then early-returns whenever
value_change_scope finds the generation unchanged, so:

  1. scene A, slot `amount` override epoch 7 -> source node stores 7
  2. the reader's effect is torn down (tile closed, or the buffer re-evaluated
     during authoring, which rebuilds effects)
  3. switch to scene B -- zero subscribers, nothing queued, node still stores 7
  4. reader remounts and renders B's value correctly by direct read; the node's
     stored generation is still 7 and nothing re-stamps it on read
  5. switch back to scene A -- queued generation is 7, equals the stored 7, so
     mark_source_dependents_dirty early-returns and the reader keeps showing
     B's value

Step 2 is the reachable part: hot reload replaces module subtree effects, so a
plain edit-and-eval of the panel buffer empties the dependents momentarily.

Candidate fixes, cheapest first:
- Stamp the source's generation at read time, so track_reactive_read on a slot
  records the epoch it actually resolved. Self-healing regardless of subscriber
  churn.
- Use the resolved slot VALUE as the generation instead of the epoch. Then the
  comparison in value_change_scope means exactly what the UI cares about, and
  the detached case cannot desync; equal values across scenes correctly skip
  the repaint.
- Queue every DECLARED slot rather than only subscribed ones. Simplest, but
  gives up some of the targeting this bead was written to gain.

The existing test (pattern_sync_repaints_defscene_readers_with_the_current_
scene_epoch) keeps a live reader across the switch, so it does not cover this.
A regression test would tear down the effect buffer between the two switches.

title: Slice by beat division

Review of b1340609 (fixes in 3d99cc44). Implementation met the criteria -- override layer, resolved() semantics, hash-keyed serialization, detected onsets never persisted, edit-sampler-slice handler on the track-parameter gesture. Two defects found and fixed:

1. Stale overrides survived a sample swap. Generalizable: any host command that takes an INDEX into a panel-rendered list must resolve that list exactly as the panel did. Worth checking other panel/handler pairs that pass indices rather than values.

title: Correct jaki live-channel spec section 3: drag release DOES trigger a buffer eval
description:
docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md section 3 ("Verified repo facts", each
claimed read on 2026-08-21) states at lines 73-75:

  "The text writeback does **not** trigger evaluation. `pending_inline_writeback`
   (`editor/mod.rs:697, 8916`) is undo coalescing only. So today's 'recompile on
   release' is the author's own eval keystroke, not a side effect of the drag."

This is false, and has been since commit 15319e90 ("Implement inline code
widgets", 2026-07-10), which introduced `finish_inline_widget_writeback` calling
`evaluate_buffer_transactional`. Today `pending_inline_writeback` is undo
coalescing AND an eval trigger: mouse-up unconditionally re-evaluates the whole
buffer (`crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:6678` → `mod.rs:9020`). See
eseq-jo7.18 for the full trace.

WORK

1. Correct the section 3 bullet, citing `mod.rs:6678` and `mod.rs:9020`.
2. Re-check every downstream decision that leaned on the false premise. At
   minimum:
   - section 6, payload-epoch design — its cost model assumes no drag-driven eval.
   - section 8 "Divergence" (~line 486): "between a live write and a text
     writeback the widget already ..." — reassess when release also evals.
   - ~line 594: "undoing a drag restores the text but not the channel until the
     next eval" — with a release-time eval in the picture this reads differently
     and may already be a different bug.
   - the section 9 table row "plain re-eval after a drag ... a no-op" (~line 309)
     — it is not a hypothetical, it happens on every release.
3. Note in the spec whether the section 10 tiers change the answer, since
   eseq-jo7.18 blocks on that call.

title: Channel-bound inline widgets should not force a full buffer eval on mouse release
description:
Releasing the mouse on ANY inline widget in a scratch buffer runs a full buffer
evaluation, even when the widget is channel-bound and the drag already committed
its value live. Observed as a "Lisp reload ok (no changed symbols; no roots
rerendered)" flash on every knob/slider release in a `jak` body.

MECHANISM (read 2026-08-22)

- `Editor::handle_mouse` mouse-up branch calls `finish_inline_widget_writeback()`
  (`crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:6678`).
- That fn (`mod.rs:9020`) pops `pending_inline_writeback`, finishes the typing
  undo group, then calls `evaluate_buffer_transactional(buffer_id)` — a full
  macro-expand + eval of the whole buffer.
- `pending_inline_writeback` is set in `apply_widget_output` (`mod.rs:8950`) for
  ANY widget whose `on-change` is `INLINE_WRITEBACK_CALLBACK`, with no regard for
  whether the widget resolved a `__inline-runtime-target`.
- Yet `apply_widget_output` has ALREADY done the live commit ten lines earlier
  (`mod.rs:8956`): `inline_widget_runtime_target(anchor_id)` →
  `runtime.invoke(target, [:inlet, value])`. For a `:chan`-marked widget that
  target is the channel handle bound with inlet "set" by
  `bind-channel-widgets` in `content/packages/alez.jaki/src/surface.lisp:60`.
- So for channel-bound widgets the release re-eval is pure overhead: it re-runs
  `jak` → `channel-register` → `__jaki-declare-value-channels` → rebuilds the
  `def-sequencer` tick-source string, to land on a value the channel already has.
- The message reads "no changed symbols" because `jak` registers a STRING-named
  sequencer, so nothing enters `ReloadReport.changed_symbols`
  (`crates/eseqlisp/src/hot_reload.rs:572`).

PROPOSED FIX

Make the release-time eval conditional on the widget having no runtime target.
Widen `pending_inline_writeback` from `(BufferId, SourceAnchorId)` to carry an
"evaluate on release" flag (or a small enum). Set it false when
`inline_widget_runtime_target` resolved — the live invoke IS the commit, and the
text rewrite only exists for file persistence and undo. Set it true otherwise:
an unbound inline widget's new literal can only take effect through an eval.
`finish_inline_widget_writeback` then always finishes the undo group and only
conditionally evaluates.

Wins: no spurious minibuffer flash, no `eseq-wlc` momentary-timing hit on every
knob release, and much less of the anonymous-channel churn `eseq-jo7.14` sweeps.

OPEN DESIGN POINT — decide before implementing

After skipping the eval, the buffer literal and the channel agree, but the
COMPILED tick-source still holds the pre-drag literal. That is correct while the
channel is the read path (spec Tier A, late resolution). It is NOT obviously
correct for Tier B / early resolution (`eseq-jo7.5`), where the value is
substituted structurally at build time and a rebuild may genuinely be required.
So the skip may have to be per-tier rather than blanket. Settle this against
docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md sections 5 and 6 first; see eseq-jo7.19
for the spec correction this depends on.
