title: Strip __source-origin wrappers from shipped capture residue
description:
Expansion residue quoted at capture sites carries the read-time `(__source-origin <start> <end> "<revision>" <form>)` wrapper that dvs.1 inserts around every macro call. Evidence (probe against both 6c9435ef and its parent de0f707f, so this predates dvs.4):

  (def-process p :every (k 5) :run (k 6))
  => :every (__source-origin 22 27 "8598839462071891009" (target-set! 5))
     :run   (__source-origin 33 38 "8598839462071891009" (target-set! 6))

Two problems:

1. Shipped run_source is no longer a pure function of the authored form. The wrapper embeds authoring-buffer byte offsets and a per-revision hash, so editing anything earlier in the buffer changes the shipped text of every macro-using def-process in it. Rule 2 of docs/procedural-macro-spec.md relies on the opposite ('same source -> same expansion, always, so hot-swap identity -- diff by source, preserve :state by name -- keeps working and a re-eval never produces spurious diffs').

2. Structurally-parsed clauses see the wrapper, not the form. :every, :target, :listen and the every/after/on/tap trigger are parsed by process_dsl_parse.rs, which has no __source-origin case; a macro in those positions yields an unparseable declaration. It only survives today because no checked-in content puts a macro there.

Fix: strip __source-origin wrappers when quoting/serializing capture residue (or before parsing declaration clauses), keeping them only on the authoring VM's evaluated path where the diagnostic is actually consumed. Likely lands with eseq-dvs.6 (source mapping), which owns the wrapper's contract.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sequencer h-scroll: fill track rows clip trailing chrome; gate root width to max(viewport, content)
description:
# Sequencer horizontal-scroll artifact: fill rows narrower than their content

## Symptom

In the `*sequencer*` buffer, when the tile viewport is narrower than a track
row's intrinsic content and the user scrolls horizontally, the track-actions
"..." button (and any trailing chrome) renders OUTSIDE the track container's
rounded border. The border stops at viewport width while the row's fixed-width
children (header + step grid) overflow past it.

Desired semantics: track container width = max(viewport width, content width).
When the viewport is wider than the content, the row still stretches to fill
the viewport (current working case must be preserved).

## Root cause (traced)

- Tile horizontal scrolling is applied AFTER layout: the tree is laid out
  against the viewport, then translated by `content_scroll`
  (`crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:4259` sync_layout_content_scroll; scroll
  bounds from `max_extent_bounded_exact` in `max_horizontal_scroll`,
  `mod.rs:6894`). Layout never knows scrolling exists.
- `LayoutEngine::layout` (`crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/layout.rs:278`) measures with
  `root_constraints()` where `max_width = terminal_cols` (`layout.rs:309`).
- `:width :fill` on a box resolves to exactly `constraints.max_width`
  (`crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/box_widget.rs:328`, guarded by
  `constraints.max_width.is_finite()`), i.e. exactly viewport width.
- So the track-row box (`content/ui/sequencer.lisp:1674`) gets viewport width;
  its inner h-stack's fixed-width children overflow, the `:flex 1` spacer
  collapses to 0, and `track-actions` lands past the box's right edge, outside
  the painted border. Same applies to `group-block`
  (`content/ui/sequencer.lisp:2230`).

## Agreed fix: gated root-constraint widening (opt-in, *sequencer* only)

Widen the ROOT constraint to max(viewport, natural content width), gated so
only buffers that opt in pay the cost (layout perf was just hard-won; do NOT
apply globally):

1. Opt-in seam: a `:fill-content`-style marker on the buffer root (e.g. wrap /
   tag the `*sequencer*` root v-stack at `content/ui/sequencer.lisp:2265`).
   Only a root carrying the marker triggers the extra pass.
2. Natural width pre-pass: `LayoutEngine::natural_content_width`
   (`layout.rs:659`) already measures with INFINITE max_width, and the `:fill`
   branches in box/h-stack measure only fire when `max_width.is_finite()` — so
   under that pass fill boxes fall through to content-sized measurement. That
   IS the "contents width" wanted here.
3. In `layout()`, when gated on: `natural = natural_content_width(tree)`, then
   use `max_width = terminal_cols.max(natural)` for `root_constraints()` and
   the same value for the fill-root width in `root_rect` (`layout.rs:320`).
4. Every `:fill` down the chain (root v-stack stretches fill children to inner
   width per vstack layout; `track-row`; `group-block`) then resolves to the
   same max(viewport, widest-content) width → all row borders align at the
   widest row's width, "..." sits inside the border, and scroll bounds follow
   automatically from laid-out extents.

## Gotchas / must-handle

- Targeted relayout: `relayout_node_at_path` / `measure_node_at_path` rebuild
  against `root_constraints()` too (`layout.rs:1385`). They must see the same
  widened width (cache it on the engine), or the first p-lock edit inside a row
  snaps it back to viewport width.
- Perf: the pre-pass doubles measurement for the gated buffer. Acceptable for
  *sequencer* only; optionally skip the second pass when the natural width is
  <= viewport (no behavior change in that case).
- Preserve working case: viewport wider than content must still stretch-to-fill
  (max() gives this for free).

## Rejected alternatives

- Per-row max(viewport, own content) inside box measure: rows with shorter
  patterns would be narrower than a 64-step row; borders would not align while
  scrolled. Shared ROOT width is required, not per-row widths.
- Changing `:width :fill` semantics globally: many layouts rely on
  fill-as-clamp (text wrapping, flex distribution); too risky.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in root content-width layout, sequencer gating, targeted relayout preservation, and regression coverage.

title: Expand-before-ship at capture sites
description: At every auto-quote capture site (def-process clauses, every/after/on/tap bodies, def-sequencer :tick/:init and graph mode) run macro expansion FIRST, then quote/serialize the residue. Shipped source becomes macro-free kernel forms; the scheduler VM never expands macros; jaki's dual-VM macro dependency (pat expanding scheduler-side) goes away. Spec: 'Rule 1'.
close_reason:
Reviewed against acceptance criteria; done.

Verified in 6c9435ef: compile_expanded_quoted_expression{,_preserving_quotes}
run expand_macros before quoting, and are wired into all four enumerated
capture sites -- def-process clauses (:in/:out/:state/:every/:phase/:listen/
:target/:targets/:seed/:doc/:run/:init/:on-*), every/after/on/tap bodies,
def-sequencer :tick/:init (preserving inner quotes), and graph mode. Probed
the residue directly: nested macros deep in a body expand; macros inside
quoted data do NOT (expand_macros skips QuoteList); non-macro bodies are
byte-identical to before.

Site enumeration checked for holes: def-accumulator and def-song are
correctly excluded -- def-accumulator builds a ProcessDef with
run_source: None and def-song is a host declaration, so neither crosses the
VM boundary as source. :material/:shader go through the runtime SDF path.

Found and fixed one gap (e58582e5): process sugar expanded only args 1..n,
quoting the leading trigger/source verbatim. That contradicted def-process,
whose structurally-parsed :every/:listen clauses this same slice expands, so
(every (my-interval) ...) shipped an unexpanded macro into
parse_process_time_expr. All four sugars now expand every argument; added
process_sugar_expands_the_trigger_argument_too.

Filed eseq-dvs.8 for a pre-existing defect this slice surfaces but does not
own: the dvs.1 read-time (__source-origin start end "revision" form) wrapper
survives into the quoted residue, so shipped run_source embeds buffer byte
offsets and a per-revision hash (breaking the Rule 2 source-identity
property), and declaration clauses see the wrapper rather than the form.
Reproduced identically at de0f707f, so not a regression from this commit.

Checks: cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp -> 1718 passed / 6 skipped.
cargo nextest run -p sequencer --no-fail-fast -> 2686 passed / 28 skipped.
cargo clippy -p eseqlisp --lib clean over the changed lines.

title: Expansion-safe native whitelist + diagnostics
description: Expander bodies and everything they call are restricted to pure natives (list/dict/string/math, source) plus in-whitelist module functions. No mutation surface, send/channels, widgets, host handles, rand, load. Enforced as compile diagnostics naming the native and macro, reusing the publish-time whitelist seam specced for shipped process bodies; VM backstop when the expander runs. Purity => same source, same expansion => hot-swap identity survives. Spec: 'Rule 2'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Template-macro compatibility audit + lint
description: Behavioral change: unquotes of non-parameters are today passed through unexpanded (expand_quasiquote_inner fallback) but will be EVALUATED at expansion time. Lint all checked-in defmacros (content/, content/packages/, content/defmacros/, defmacro_library.rs corpus) for reliance on the old fallback before flipping the switch. Pure-template macros migrate for free. Spec: 'Backwards compatibility'.
close_reason: Audit clean: all 433 checked-in defmacros linted (content/, crates/, docs/), 46 quasiquote-bodied; zero rely on the expand_quasiquote_inner non-parameter fallback. lint_template_macro_compatibility + regression test in defmacro_library.rs. Commits 86a12119, c98a2a5f.

title: Procedural expander core: compile defmacro bodies, expand by evaluation
description: Compile each defmacro body into a VM function at definition time; expansion calls it with parameter forms bound as data (&rest as list) and uses the returned form, re-expanded to fixpoint via the existing expand_macros loop/depth limit. Adds the compiler-to-VM callback seam (compiler currently owns no evaluator). Preserves in-unit definition order. Spec: docs/procedural-macro-spec.md 'Kernel change'.
close_reason:
Reviewed against acceptance criteria; done.

Verified in 82fed2e8: defmacro bodies compile to a VM function chunk at
definition time (compile_macro_function + compile_macro_quasiquote, new
ConcatLists opcode for ,@); expansion invokes it via the new compiler->VM
callback seam (Compiler::set_macro_evaluator / VM::evaluate_compiled_macro,
chunks+globals handed across in MacroCompilerState); params bind to argument
forms as data with &rest as a list; the result re-expands to fixpoint through
the existing expand_macros depth-100 loop; in-unit definition order preserved
(macro defined and callable later in the same compile unit). Expander errors
abort the compile with 'error expanding macro `NAME`'. Runtime SDF expansion
now routes through VM::expand_macros_expression instead of a macro-table-only
compiler.

Found and fixed one regression (f82a9a7e): expression_to_macro_value collapsed
QuoteSymbol/QuoteList and dropped Quasiquote/Unquote/UnquoteSplicing, so
(defmacro m (x) `(list ,x)) called as (m 'foo) expanded to (list foo) ->
UnknownVariable, and (m '(1 2)) -> ExpectedFunction. Both worked under the
template expander. Reader wrappers now round-trip as their canonical
two-element list spellings ((quote x), (quasiquote x), (unquote x),
(unquote-splicing x)) in both directions.

Semantic note for downstream beads: a quoted argument is now the form
(quote X), not X. macro_can_splice_a_quoted_list_parameter was renamed to
macro_can_splice_a_list_parameter and now splices a bare list — ,@ on a quoted
argument splices the quote form, which is standard Lisp.

Known limits, not blockers: nested quasiquote inside an expander body is still
spliced at level 1 (no checked-in Lisp uses it); a macro body cannot call a
helper defined in the same compile unit, since globals are not set until the
unit executes; arity-mismatched macro calls still fall through silently to an
unresolved function call (pre-existing).

Checks: cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast -> 4392 passed, 0 failed,
34 skipped. cargo clippy -p eseqlisp --lib clean over the changed lines. Added
4 regression tests (quoted arg preservation, quote-form visibility to first/nth,
quoted &rest args, macro-expanding-to-macro).

title: Procedural macros: evaluated defmacro bodies, expand-before-ship
description: Upgrade eseqlisp defmacro from quasiquote substitution to procedural expansion: macro bodies run at compile time on the authoring VM, receive call forms as data, and return the expansion. Three discipline rules make it sound in the two-VM world: expand-before-ship (shipped bodies are macro-free residue), pure expander sandbox (whitelist), deterministic gensym (site-keyed, re-eval stable). Kills the eval/source-string pattern in alez.sig and alez.jaki. Spec: docs/procedural-macro-spec.md

title: Process state set! inside nested let is not persisted
description: A def-process state binding is wrapped in an outer lambda and flushed with __process-state-set! after the authored :run body. If set! phase occurs inside a nested let, the nested assignment does not update the outer lambda binding, so the generated flush writes the original value every tick. Repro: :state ((phase 0)) with :run (let ((unused 1)) (do (send :wave phase) (set! phase (mod (+ phase 0.1) 1)))); the mirrored output remains 0. Directly placing the do/set! at :run top level advances correctly. Fix lexical assignment/capture semantics robustly and add process-runtime coverage.

title: Anonymous jaki channel sweep: retire "<seq>#<n>" channels on re-eval
description:
docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md (rev 2) section 10.2, promoted out of
open questions into a required slice. MUST ship with phase 3, not after.

Anonymous "<seq-name>#<n>" channels are created by the :chan expansion walk
(eseq-jo7.10) and renumbered whenever a widget is inserted or removed above
another one. Without a sweep they accumulate in the authoring registry across
every eval as bodies are edited.

Sweep keyed on the owning sequencer name: on re-declaring a jak body, retire
any anonymous channel carrying that sequencer's prefix that the new walk did
not re-declare.

SCOPE IS ALREADY REDUCED by two rev 2 decisions -- do not re-widen it:
  - Named :chan "name" channels are idempotent by name (spec 4.4 reuse), so
    they never churn and must NOT be swept; an explicit name is a public
    declaration that may outlive any one body.
  - Only :chan-marked widgets declare at all. Implicit promotion of every
    widget in a jak body was rejected (spec 4.1), which is what kept this
    bounded enough to stay a normal slice rather than a prerequisite redesign.
notes: eseq-jo7.18 (skip the release-time buffer eval for channel-bound inline widgets) removes most of the per-drag re-eval churn this sweep absorbs, but does not replace the sweep: editing/inserting widgets still renumbers anonymous channels on the author's own eval. Related, not blocking.

title: eseqlisp :chan widget property + source-identity target binding
description:
Phase 3b of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md (rev 2), sections 4.1 and 7.4.
ESEQLISP SIDE ONLY -- the jaki expansion walk is eseq-jo7.10.

Work:

1. register_inline_value_widget_natives (crates/eseqlisp/src/widgets.rs:103):
   accept :chan on ~slider / ~knob / ~toggle. Value form only -- :chan true or
   :chan "name" -- never a bare flag, because the arg convention is strictly
   pair-wise (keyword_string_arg uses args.windows(2), the property loop steps
   index += 2) and an unpaired keyword desynchronizes every following pair.
   Deliberately a property, not a new ~chan form: channel-ness and renderer
   choice are independent axes, and a form would need a parallel :as registry
   that drifts from is_inline_widget_constructor_name and cannot express ~lane.

2. Source-identity target binding. THE REV 1 MECHANISM DOES NOT WORK. Rev 1
   said the jak walk calls attach_inline_widget_runtime_target(callee, inlet,
   handle) with \"set\". Two independent blockers:
     (a) That function resolves through recent_runtime_inline_widgets, which
         register_inline_widget populates ONLY under
         !registering_static_inline_widget (vm.rs:4915). Statically drawn
         widgets -- which is what a quoted jak body produces, since it never
         executes on the editor VM -- are unreachable through it. The lookup
         always misses.
     (b) There is no (callee, inlet) pair anyway. register_static_inline_widget_expr
         computes a parent only when the widget's immediately preceding sibling
         is a Keyword. In (dashdecay (~slider 0.294 :chan true)) the parent is
         None -- jaki flags are head positions, not keyword args.

   FIX: key on inline_widget_source_identity (vm.rs:1151) =
   (source_revision, start_byte, end_byte), which IS recorded for static
   widgets. Either add a span-keyed variant of
   attach_inline_widget_runtime_target, or preferably let the widget native
   attach its own target at static-registration time -- with :chan the form
   itself knows it is a channel, which dissolves the parent-pair dependency.

NO NEW CODE IN THE WRITE PATH: apply_widget_output already fires
runtime.invoke(target, [:inlet, value]) per drag frame for any widget
resolving __inline-runtime-target, and separately rewrites the literal without
evaluating. Only the binding changes.

COROLLARY TO 2(b): min/max inference does not reach jaki bodies either, since
resolve_inline_widget_metadata needs the same absent (callee, inlet) pair.
Widgets there fall back to the default 0.0..1.0 unless :min/:max are explicit.
Worth a doc note; not a bug to fix here.
notes: Implemented generic source-identity binding in commit 56a89067. ESeqLisp exposes __bind-inline-widget-target; process channels expose channel-handle; Jaki composes both from one expansion walk with separate declaration and binding records. :chan is consumed as an inline-widget property, named and anonymous handles both write live, and static true/false widget args are supported. Validation: 10 targeted Jaki/channel tests passed in the working checkout; staged-only clean worktree validation passed the ESeqLisp source-binding test and both sequencer integration tests.
close_reason: Implemented and validated in 56a89067

title: jaki: (quant tb) route word — grid-quantize a route's surviving events
description: Shipped (quant :16 | :8t | ...) as a jaki route post op: apply-quant snaps each event offset to the nearest multiple of the grid (exact rationals, r-mod wrap into the cycle like shift), composing in authored word order (left (quant :16) quantizes the filtered hand) and every-wrappable via route-post-op. quant-units resolves (beats tb)/(jaki-unit) at ROUTE time over denominator 96 (exact for straight+triplet ratios incl :16t=2/3 unit) so the memoized evaluator never depends on generator resolution; memo tags embed the resolved rational (also fixed every-post tags to use resolved post source). Deliberately NOT reusing MIDI FX quantize / seq-emit :quantize: those are forward-push-only float-beat deferrals at the stream layer (ceil_to_grid deadline, midi_fx.rs:634) — cannot pull late tuplet hits earlier and cannot compose with jaki gate ops. Test jaki_route_quant_snaps_offsets_to_straight_and_triplet_grids covers tuplet→straight ((% 4) fit onto :16) and straight→triplet (:16t). Spec §11.2 updated. jaki suite 26/26.

title: jaki: every-wrapped post words + cyc route destinations/note/vel
description: Shipped two route-surface upgrades. (1) (every n w) dispatch: new route-post-op helper lowers post-op words (stac, shift, left/right/accent, nested every) to cycle-gated (:every n post) post ops applied in authored order; apply-post-one gained an :every recursion case. Fixes '(every 2 stac)' being clobbered by filters and '(every 2 (shift 1))' being a silent no-op (apply-one-xf has no :shift case). (2) Per-cycle emit args: emit* resolves track, :note, and :vel-scale through resolve-arg with the routed pattern's cycle index — '-> (cyc 1 3) left' bounces destinations per cycle, '(note (cyc 0 4 12))' cycles transpose; also fixes latent crash where (note (cyc ...))/(vel (cyc ...)) passed a raw list to seq-emit. Spec §11.2 updated. Full jaki suite 25/25.

title: jaki :chan expansion walk: naming, declaration, rewrite to (chan ...)
description:
Phase 3a of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md (rev 2), sections 4.1-4.4.
JAKI SIDE ONLY -- the eseqlisp widget half is eseq-xdw.

REV 2 CHANGED THE SURFACE. There is no ~chan form. Channel-ness is a :chan
keyword on the existing widget forms:

  (dashdecay (~slider 0.294 :chan "hit.dashdecay"))
  (dotdecay  (~slider 0.177 :chan true))
  (* (~knob 3 :min 1 :max 4 :step 1 :chan true))

:chan true = anonymous. :chan "name" = public, global, flat -- a def-process
can read or send to the same value. :chan takes a value because the widget arg
convention is strictly pair-wise (keyword_string_arg uses args.windows(2)); a
bare flag desynchronizes every following pair.

Work (content/packages/alez.jaki/src/surface.lisp:34):

1. jak walks its quoted body at macro-expansion time on the editor VM,
   recognizes :chan on value widget forms, and rewrites each into
   (chan <name> <default>). Anonymous ones get "<seq-name>#<n>", n a pre-order
   index. The rewrite is load-bearing: the scheduler VM has no widget layer, so
   an unrewritten form evaluates to its bare literal and no channel exists.
2. Declare each channel (spec 4.4): push an AuthoredChannel {handle_id, name,
   initial: <literal>, message_only: false} as defchan does, REUSING the
   existing handle_id when the name is already declared.

WHY 2 IS MANDATORY, NOT A CONVENIENCE:
  (a) process_channel_handle resolves its name via channel_name_for_handle,
      which reads registry.channels / channel_handles -- populated only by
      declaration. defchan is currently the sole producer of channel handles.
      Undeclared, eseq-xdw has no handle to bind and cannot be built.
  (b) sync_channels ends with self.channels = next, dropping anything absent
      from the authored list. A channel conjured by send_channel_at's
      or_insert would be destroyed by the first sync_authoring after any eval,
      taking the dragged value with it.

SEED RULE on re-declaration -- compare the new literal against the STORED
AuthoredChannel.initial, never against the runtime value. Differs => author
hand-edited the text: update initial and push the value through the eseq-jo7.8
pending-write queue. Matches => unchanged re-eval: leave the runtime value
alone. Comparing against the runtime value instead makes a hand edit a no-op
until app restart. Spec 4.4 has the full case table.

Reuse-by-name also makes declaration idempotent; defchan today does
registry.channels.push (not an upsert) so re-eval appends a duplicate every
time. Named channels must not inherit that.

MESSAGE-ONLY COLLISION IS A HARD ERROR: defchan with one arg is message-only
and holds no value (send_channel_at skips storing). Binding :chan "ping" to an
existing (defchan ping) must fail at expansion, or the symptom is a slider that
moves smoothly and does nothing.

Blocked on eseq-jo7.14 (anonymous channel sweep) shipping in the same phase --
anonymous "<seq>#<n>" channels churn as bodies are edited and renumbered.
notes: Follow-up regression fixed in 2b718807: the first implementation called __register-sequencer, which only populated the editor-local registry and never published to SequencerState. channel-register now calls the UI-overridden def-sequencer through a validated :tick-source path. Added a production-split regression that evaluates the user's plain no-slider script in a regular authoring Runtime, verifies publication, loads it on the scheduler VM, and observes triggers. All 8 jaki_surface tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed editor-to-scheduler publication regression in 2b718807

title: jaki Tier A: late channel resolution for payload args + payload-epoch memo key
description:
Phase 2 of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md sections 5 (Tier A) and 6.
Authorable via the bare (chan name default) primitive; the ~chan sugar is
phase 3 (separate bead). At the end of this phase a process or a UI channel
write can drive dashdecay live with no evaluation anywhere.

Tier A = payload arguments only: basevel, dotdecay, dashdecay, minvel, maxvel,
and the route-word vel/note arguments. These affect emitted event payload only
-- not the symbolic grid, not cycle length, not phase.

Work:
1. resolve-arg (content/packages/alez.jaki/src/core.lisp:208) gains a `chan`
   head alongside `cyc`, returning (chan-get name default). Value is read at
   tick time; :id is unchanged so no pattern is rebuilt.
2. Add a global payload-epoch counter, bumped whenever any channel value
   changes, and join it to the eval-cycle memo key (core.lisp:653).

WHY 2 IS REQUIRED: vel-overrides (core.lisp:342-355) runs inside eval-at and
therefore inside the eval-cycle memo. A late channel read behind an unchanged
key would serve a stale velocity forever.

DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY -- do not extend the epoch to the other two memos:
len-memo (core.lisp:664) and lens-memo (core.lisp:712) must stay untouched by
Tier A, because payload channels provably cannot change length. lens-memo
exists specifically to stop rich patterns pinning the scheduler
(core.lisp:706-709); losing it per drag frame would reintroduce that. Net
per-drag cost is one cycle re-evaluation per active route, versus a whole
buffer eval today -- that is the entire performance argument for the feature.

A single global payload-epoch is intentionally coarse (any slider invalidates
the per-cycle memo for every pattern). Per-pattern read sets are a later
optimization only if a measurement asks for one.
notes: Implemented Tier A late (chan name default) payload resolution and payload-epoch cycle-memo invalidation. len-memo and lens-memo retain structural keys. Targeted tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented Tier A late  payload resolution and payload-epoch cycle-memo invalidation, with targeted regression coverage.

title: UI to scheduler channel writes: callable channel handle + chunk-boundary drain
description:
Phase 1 of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md section 7. The one piece of
plumbing that does not exist today: nothing outside ProcessRuntime can write a
channel value. ProcessRuntime::send_channel_at (runtime/process.rs:2241) is the
correct entry point and every caller is internal.

Work:
1. process_channel_handle (lisp_host/eseq/process_dsl_parse.rs:1418) currently
   returns EValue::Bool(true) for any call -- a no-op stub. Give it a real
   callable so (handle :set value) enqueues a pending channel write.
2. Add pending_channel_writes to the shared authoring registry, mirroring
   pending_step_inlet_writes (runtime/process.rs:1747).
3. Drain the queue in the lookahead worker at the top of a chunk and call
   send_channel_at(name, value, beat, sample_time) BEFORE the channel snapshot
   is published at scheduler/lookahead.rs:1458-1461.

GOTCHA (the reason this is a queue and not the authoring path): sync_channels
(runtime/process.rs:1790) prefers an existing runtime value over `initial` and
falls back to initial only when unset. A value smuggled through the authoring
snapshot as an initial is therefore silently swallowed.

Independently testable with no jaki or widget changes: defchan a value channel,
call the handle, assert a chan-get in a generator tick observes it on the next
chunk. Writes land on a chunk boundary in order with a defined beat, same
discipline as every other control-thread -> scheduler command.
close_reason: Phase 1 shipped in 12ebc56e: callable defchan handle enqueues (handle :set value) onto a pending-write queue on SequencerState; the lookahead worker drains it at the top of each chunk via send_channel_at, ahead of the chan-get snapshot. Deliberately off the authoring snapshot (sync_channels prefers the runtime value over initial). __inline-read echoes the last write for widget binding. Queue capped at 512 since nothing drains while stopped. Tests: lisp_host::tests::channel_handle_set_queues_writes_for_the_scheduler_in_order, scheduler::tests::channel_handle_write_reaches_generator_chan_get_on_the_next_chunk.

title: jaki: route-word stac silently clobbered by hand/accent filter gate extension
description: route-step 'stac appends a figure xf, but left/right/accent are :post filters whose gate extension (extend-kept/extend-unfiltered, spec §7) always runs after xfs — so '-> 1 left stac' and '-> 1 stac left' both emit full legato gates (probe: [0.5,0.25,0.5] vs stac's [0.0625,...]). Fix: in the route surface make stac a post-op (cap gate at 1/4 unit) so posts apply in authored word order — 'left stac' caps after extension, 'stac left' lets the filter win. Figure-segment stac (inside pat/fig) keeps the scale-aware xf-flag path.
close_reason: Fixed: route-step 'stac now appends a (:stac) post op (add-post) instead of the figure xf; new apply-stac in apply-post-one caps every gate at 1/4 unit. Posts run in authored word order, so 'left stac' caps the filter's extended gates ([0.0625;3]) while 'stac left' lets the legato extension win ([0.5,0.25,0.5]). Unfiltered-route stac unchanged numerically (0.0625 at :16). Figure-segment (stac) keeps the scale-aware xf-flag path. Regression test jaki_route_stac_applies_in_word_order_with_filters covers all four orderings; full jaki neighborhood 23/23 green. Spec §11.2 updated with the ordering rule.

title: Default inline sliders to a 0..1 range
description: Inline ~slider and ~knob forms outside process-inlet metadata currently require explicit :min/:max. Give normalized controls sensible 0..1 defaults while preserving explicit and process-inferred ranges, with targeted regression coverage.
close_reason: Implemented normalized 0..1 defaults for inline sliders and knobs, preserving explicit and process-inferred ranges; added quoted-pattern regression coverage and updated the spec.

title: jaki (chan name default) surface form: pre-resolved channel args
description: Add a 'resolve-chans' tree-walk at the top of alez.jaki.core/run (and pat path) that substitutes each (chan name default) form in the quoted body with the channel's current value via chan-get, BEFORE pattern construction. Early resolution (not the resolve-arg eval fallback, core.lisp:208-217) so the literal lands in the pattern source and :id — every value variant is a distinct pattern, keeping eval-cycle memo, cycle-length memo, and the pat-lens super-cycle table automatically correct (they are keyed by :id; late eval would serve stale lengths since arg-period treats non-cyc forms as period 1). Works anywhere resolve-arg positions exist: fig (* n)/(/ n), fast/slow, rot, trunc, shift, every, vel, note. Semantics v1: per-tick latch, transport-locked phase on length change (same as per-route fast/slow). Depends on the chan-get native bead.
notes:
2026-08-21: this bead is now Phase 4 of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md
(Tier B, structural arguments). The spec keeps the early-resolution design here
unchanged and adds one requirement:

TIER ASSIGNMENT IS SYNTACTIC, NOT ANNOTATED. resolve-chans substitutes early
only for structural positions -- (* n)/(/ n)/(% n), fast/slow, shift, rot,
trunc, every, align -- and leaves every other (chan ...) for the Tier A late
path (eseq-jo7.9). Those positions are exactly the ones fig-period /
xf-period / arg-period consult, so the tier list and arg-period must be the
same list, with a test asserting they agree.

WHY THAT TEST MATTERS: if a structural position is later added to jaki without
arg-period learning about it, a (chan ...) there resolves late and the
super-cycle table goes quietly wrong -- musical drift, not a crash.

Latch semantics: Tier B values latch at a cycle boundary with phase staying
transport-locked across a length change (same as the per-route fast/slow
behavior from ca3342f5), so a structural slider never flips a length mid-cycle.

title: chan-get bridge native: generator ticks read process channels
description: Register a read-only 'chan-get' native alongside the sequencer natives on the scheduler runtime: (chan-get "name" default) samples a channel's current value from inside a def-sequencer tick. Rationale: processes and generator ticks already share the scheduler VM (lisp_host/shared_state.rs registers both native sets on one Runtime), but 'read' requires the process eval context (process_natives.rs ~1009) so generators cannot sample channels today. This is the single bridge that lets def-process modulate jaki patterns per process-channels-spec.md's channels-distribute-values philosophy. Value channels return last value (or default if unset/message-channel); no writes from generator scope. Decide snapshot ordering: generator tick at beat N should observe channel writes made by processes evaluated for the same lookahead beat.
close_reason: Shipped chan-get: SharedGeneratorChannels snapshot cell on ScratchControlRuntime (shared_state.rs) published via set_generator_channel_values; scheduler refreshes it from ProcessRuntime::channel_values() (new accessor, value channels only, initial-seeded) once per lookahead chunk right before generator_runtime.process_block (lookahead.rs). Native registered beside state-get in sequencer_natives.rs: (chan-get "name" [default]) requires a live generator tick ctx, returns snapshot value or default/nil. Snapshot ordering decision: generators tick before processes within a chunk, so a tick observes writes from earlier chunks — a process write lands on subsequent ticks (documented in the native docstring). Tests: chan_get_reads_channel_snapshot_inside_generator_tick, chan_get_outside_generator_tick_errors (native errors surface as false + status message, not eval Err), runtime::process::tests::channel_values_snapshot_holds_value_channels_only. Unblocks eseq-jo7.5 (jaki chan surface form) and eseq-jo7.6 (restart/anchor).

title: jaki (* n) fast diverges from JakiEvaluator.swift double-time transforms
description: Intended semantics (behavioral reference: patch-editor Sources/Jaki/JakiEvaluator.swift, transformSymbolDouble + related): with (. . -) (. -), applying (* 2) to the first figure keeps that figure's ORIGINAL time span and plays it 'twice at double time' — via the specific symbol-level double-time transforms (dot/dash rewrites) the Swift evaluator defines, which interact with hands/velocity like any other event stream. Current jaki.lisp expand-fast (content/scripts/sequencers/jaki.lisp, expand-fast/units) is suspected to be a naive 'repeat the same pattern at double speed' — ignoring the Swift transform table's specific rewrites. Compare against transformSymbolDouble in the Swift source and the Jaki*.swift tests, port the exact rewrite rules, and add Lisp-level tests locking the expected event streams for (* 2)/(* 3) on dot-only, dash-containing, and mixed figures. Spec §4.3 wording ('n cycles of the figure in the space of one') may also need correcting to the reference semantics.
close_reason: Not a bug: expand-fast already implements the Swift transformSymbolDouble rewrites (dot→m dots, dash→(2m-2) dots + dash over raw units); user confirmed correct behavior on listening again.

title: Buffer re-eval causes momentary timing wobble / off-grid trigs
description: Re-evaluating *scratch* (eval-buffer) makes playback timing shaky for a split second — trigs land slightly off before settling. Suspects on the re-eval path: the scheduler runtime is rebuilt wholesale (build_scheduler_scratch_runtime) on scratch_source version change, generator sync_definitions realigns/reuses clocks, and register_published_sequencer recompiles tick lambdas — any hitch there delays the lookahead chunk being scheduled, and jaki state cells (jaki-cycle/hand/vel) plus memos restart cold. Investigate whether the rebuild can be done off-line and swapped, or the old runtime kept ticking until the replacement is warm.

title: Dead scratch_runtime: rebuild_scratch_runtime_from_buffer has no callers; run_pending_hooks silently drops hooks
description: app/effects.rs:218 rebuild_scratch_runtime_from_buffer is never called (predates jaki work — also uncalled at 25561858), so editor.scratch_runtime is always None. app/hooks.rs:106 run_pending_hooks clears all pending hook invocations when scratch_runtime is None, meaning *scratch*-registered control hooks (register-hook, every :bar) are likely silently dead; params.rs:111/121 readers also never fire. Either delete the field+fn and the dependent paths, or restore a real (command-driven) rebuild.

title: Preserve unaffected audio across multi-track and group deletion
description: The seamless topology reconciliation handles one-track deletion, whose deleted index is published by the existing topology boundary request. Atomic multi-track and delete-group-with-members commands can remove several non-contiguous tracks but currently publish only one boundary track, so they retain the conservative full callback reset. Extend topology mutation metadata to carry the ordered deleted stable identities/indices and remap surviving voice pools, keyboard notes, custom routes, choke state, and delayed events for the whole deletion set. Add active-playback regressions for non-contiguous multi-delete and group-with-members deletion.

title: Restore sample waveform display in instrument racks after content tiers migration
description: Regression introduced after the content tiers epic completed: adding a sample to a sampler inside an instrument rack results in the rack UI displaying 'no sample' instead of the waveform. Playback from the track still produces the correct sample audio, so the sound engine resolves and loads the sample successfully; the failure appears isolated to the instrument-rack UI waveform/sample metadata path. Regular standalone sampler tracks continue to display their waveforms correctly. Compare rack and standalone sampler resolution paths and fix the shared model/UI boundary rather than adding a rack-specific path workaround.

The waveform remains correct after saving and reloading the project. 3. Sample playback from instrument racks remains correct. 4. Standalone sampler-track waveform display remains correct. 5. Focused regression coverage exercises instrument-rack sample resolution through the post-tiers content/path model and verifies that waveform data reaches the UI.
notes: Reported screenshot path: /var/folders/w0/m727twr50851tbqdlkbl_c1c0000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_x71NeP/Screenshot 2026-08-21 at 9.10.47 AM.png. The screenshot itself may be ephemeral; the visible symptom is waveform text reading 'no sample'.

Investigate the shared bus-backed effect serialization/restoration and UI construction paths, fix both at their underlying source, and add focused regression coverage for each supported owner type or the common abstraction that proves all three routes.

Saving and reloading a project preserves the selected Filter Table preset and restores it in the UI instead of reverting to Procedural shapes. 3. title: Perf: *fx* owner-switch rebuilds every effect panel (~30ms for a 5-effect group chain)
description: Found during eseq-4jv: switching the *fx* buffer owner (track <-> group bus) full-re-evaluates the fx root, constructing every builtin panel from scratch (~30ms for the 5-effect group chain, rack-track->group median ~45ms release). The keyed bus-fx-panel-*/audio-fx-panel-* subtrees are re-rendered because subtree registrations do not survive being absent from a flush; reuse across absence (deps-unchanged keyed subtree cache in process_dirty_reactive / flush) would make repeated owner toggles near-free. Probe: tests::project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_end_to_end_perf, rack-track-to-group scenario (input_ms phase).
close_reason: Fixed in f8df1011: top-level effect reruns now detach (not remove) keyed subtree owner nodes; a clean re-registration with the same body chunk + equal captured inputs reuses the memoized last render instead of re-invoking the panel body. rack-track->group probe median 45.4ms -> 11.5ms (input 42.5 -> ~8ms), other transitions unchanged, all ceilings hold. Cache invalidated on import pass, symbol redefinition, rollback, clear_* teardowns, and ancestor-stale on standalone subtree rerenders. New VM tests: keyed_subtree_reused_across_absence_when_dependencies_unchanged, keyed_subtree_rerenders_when_captured_inputs_change. eseqlisp 1657 + sequencer 2616 green.

title: Perf: *samples* sidebar re-renders (~35ms) on every track switch
description: Found during eseq-4jv probing (project-92 full-layout owner-switch probe): every current-track change republishes SEQ.sidebar-kind/sidebar-track-index/sidebar-selected-sample, and ui/browser.lisp's *samples* root calls %sync-track-search inside build-widgets, so the whole samples browser re-renders (~35ms release) on every track selection. This dominates the same-instrument track->track transition (48ms total). Suspects: hoist %sync-track-search into an inert named effect (the *plock-sync*/*sel-sync* precedent), wrap tabbed-content in a keyed subtree, and stop per-item selected-sample render reads (bind or project the highlight). Probe: tests::project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_end_to_end_perf reactive-cycle phase.
notes: eseq-pgru (2026-08-25) measured this on the checked-in drift-switch fixture under the production multi-pane layout on the Linux workstation: the *samples* buffer root rerun is 2.0-2.3 ms per track switch, not ~35 ms, because an instrument track shows the presets tab rather than a large sample list. It does NOT contribute materially to same-instrument track-switch latency there, so eseq-pgru did not fold it in. Still real for sampler tracks with a big library; staying open as an independent issue. Related: the presets tab does re-read and re-parse the instrument .presets bank from disk on every switch, filed as eseq-md1n.6.

title: Make ESeqLisp compiler traversal iterative
description: The eseq-4tl stack investigation captured a debug overflow in ui/effects.lisp. LLDB showed deep frames through Compiler::compile_expression -> compile_list -> compile_if_statement/compile_let_statement/compile_function, preceded by recursive Expression::clone. eseq-4tl makes Expression cloning iterative, but compiler recursion remains proportional to authored Lisp nesting and still exceeds the default ~2 MiB debug test stack. Release handles checked-in UI on the normal stack, but sufficiently nested user-authored source is a production crash risk. Convert compiler traversal/desugaring to an explicit stack (without changing evaluation semantics), then remove/reduce the suite stack budget.

title: DGen: delay-op time input in an adsr/adsrexp dependency cone corrupts the envelope state
description: Repro (harness, instruments/bass/morph1 pre-workaround): a (delay sig t) whose t depends on an adsrexp output (even through latch, even latched at note-on) makes that envelope's release snap to zero instantly while attack/decay/sustain stay correct — symptom matches release_start_hist being clobbered. t from params, LFOs (phasor cone), or constants is fine; feedback combs without delay are fine. Likely another state-buffer/cluster collision (cf. phasor state buffer collision, make-history @hop clobber). Bisect script: scratchpad verify flow in session 64782e4b (2026-08-20). Workaround in morph1: comb delay time derived from env-free cutoff.

title: Promote morph-svf defmacro from instruments/bass/morph1 into the shared defmacro library
description: morph1 ships a Vital-style morphing ZDF SVF as a local defmacro in crates/sequencer/instruments/bass/morph1/dsp.lisp (continuous LP->mid->HP tap-weight blend; character picks BP vs notch mid tap). Once the sound is signed off, move morph-svf into the shared instrument preamble / defmacro library so any instrument or patcher patch can use it. Consider a companion ladder pole-mixing morph macro as a second family.

title: Replacing a sound on an OCCUPIED drum-rack pad still steals the selected track
description:
FOLLOW-UP to eseq-07y (closed, 717df6a6), reported by user while click-testing 2026-08-20.

eseq-07y fixed the EMPTY-pad drop: filling a blank pad now leaves the selected track alone. Dropping onto an OCCUPIED pad — which swaps that pad's sound in place — still jumps the panel to the pad's member track, so the view keeps switching out from under you exactly as before, just on the replace gesture instead of the fill gesture.

WHY IT MISSED THE FIX: the two gestures do not share a code path. crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp:1888 %drop-on-pad-cell branches on whether the cell has a member track: empty -> %drop-on-empty-pad (add-track-sample / add-track-instrument, carrying :pad-note, now routed through host_commands::selection_after_added_track), occupied -> the shared drop-on-track (sequencer.lisp:384). The occupied branch is not an add-track path at all, so selection_after_added_track never sees it, and it carries no pad discriminant — %pad-cell-drop-meta (sequencer.lisp:1879) deliberately emits (dict :kind \"track\" :track track) for an occupied cell so it looks identical to a drop on the member's own grid row.

WHERE THE SELECTION IS SET (all unconditional, all shared with the legitimate grid-row/mixer drop):
- sample: browser.lisp drop-sample-on-track -> load-sample-into-track / convert-track-to-sampler -> load_or_convert_sampler_track, crates/sequencer/src/ui/reactive_sync.rs:2470 current_track.store(track) + app.ui.cursor_track = track + set_current_track_reactive at :2474.
- sound: browser.lisp drop-sound-on-track -> load-sound-onto-track, host_commands/tracks.rs:1029.
- saved/builtin instrument: browser.lisp %swap-track-instrument / %swap-track-builtin-instrument -> swap-track-instrument (tracks.rs:654) / swap-track-builtin-instrument (tracks.rs:454).

SCOPE — the drop-on-track paths must keep selecting when the drop really is on a track (mixer strip, grid row, track area). Only the pad-cell call site should suppress. Needs a pad discriminant threaded the way :pad-note already is for the empty case: either have %pad-cell-drop-meta mark the target (e.g. :from-pad true alongside :track) and have the three host commands route their selection through the same selection_after_added_track-style helper, or give %drop-on-pad-cell its own occupied branch that restores the prior selection after the swap. Prefer the discriminant — restoring afterwards will fight the reactive syncs (instrument-panel, sampler selection fields, sidebar browser) that all key off the new index.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Dropping a sample, a Sound, or a saved/builtin instrument on an OCCUPIED pad swaps the pad's sound and leaves the selected track unchanged; the pad shows the new sound immediately.
- Empty-pad drops still behave as eseq-07y left them.
- Dropping the same items on a mixer strip, a sequencer grid row, or the track area still selects that track.
- Pad identity, pattern data, mixer settings and chokes still stay put across the swap (the property the occupied branch exists to preserve).
close_reason: Implemented occupied-pad origin metadata and selection-preserving host synchronization for sample, Sound, saved-instrument, and builtin-instrument replacements; targeted regressions pass.

title: Dropping a sound on an empty drum-rack pad should not switch the selected track
description:
Dragging a sample/instrument onto an empty drum-rack pad correctly creates the member track, but also makes it the selected/current track. The panel then jumps to the new track, so filling several pads in a row means the view keeps switching out from under you.

Scope: ONLY the empty-pad drop. Every other add-track path (mixer drops, browser drops onto the track area, Add Track, loose sample drops) must keep selecting the new track.

The discriminant already exists end to end: crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp %drop-on-empty-pad sends :pad-note with add-track-sample / add-track-instrument, and the Rust side threads it as rack_pad_note (crates/sequencer/src/ui/host_commands/tracks.rs:505) and as SavedInstrumentLoadTarget::AddTrack { pad_note } / SavedInstrumentLoadApply::Added { pad_note } (crates/sequencer/src/ui/edit_sessions.rs:226). So 'the drop landed on a pad' is already known where the selection is set.

What sets the selection in the sample path (tracks.rs ~line 540 onward): current_track.store(idx, Ordering::Relaxed), set_current_track_reactive(rt, .., idx), and the sync_track_params_with_neural_selection / sync_fx_param_binding_fields_with_neural_selection / build_step_has_plocks calls that all key off idx. When pad_note is Some, those should target the currently-selected track instead of the new one (and the current track index must stay valid — new tracks are appended, but confirm group insertion does not shift indices below it). Mirror the same change in the add-track-instrument completion path.

Status text ('Added track N: name') is fine to keep; the rack pad itself should still show the new sound immediately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dropping a sample or saved instrument on an empty drum-rack pad creates the member track and leaves the selected/current track unchanged; the focused panel does not jump.
- Several samples can be dropped onto different pads in a row without the selection moving.
- The pad shows its new sound, and is playable by pad click / armed key, immediately after the drop.
- All other add-track paths (mixer drop, Add Track, loose sample drop, non-pad browser drops) still select the newly created track.
- Regression test covers both the pad-drop (selection preserved) and a non-pad add (selection moves).
close_reason: Fixed in 717df6a6: pad drops route selection through selection_after_added_track; non-pad adds unchanged. Unit tests in host_commands::tests cover both.

title: Context-menu styling still diverges from dropdown menus (font much larger)
description:
Follow-up to eseq-ag4 (closed), which shared panel chrome/row metrics via widget_render/menu_style.rs but did not converge typography. In the running app the mixer track/group context menu renders with a visibly much larger font, looser rows and squarer corners than a dropdown menu opened in the sequencer tile.

Root cause candidate: menu-item takes its font size from get_prop_num(node,'font-size') or ctx.inherited_font_size (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/context_menu.rs measure + build_metal_primitives, falling back to DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE at render). Dropdown call sites in the Lisp UI pass an explicit small :font-size, while crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp %track-context-menu passes none — so the context menu inherits whatever the surrounding tile font is. menu_style.rs owns ROW_HEIGHT/padding/corner radius but has no font-size constant, so the two menus cannot help drifting.

Fix direction: give menu_style a shared default font size (and matching row metrics derived from it) that both the dropdown popup rows and menu-item use as their fallback instead of the inherited tile font, keeping an explicit :font-size prop as the override.
acceptance_criteria:
- Context-menu item text renders at the same size/weight as dropdown menu item text with no per-call-site :font-size in mixer.lisp.
- Row height, padding, corner radius, hover fill and separators visually match a dropdown popup side by side.
- The shared default lives in widget_render/menu_style.rs, used by both renderers; an explicit :font-size still overrides.
- Screenshot comparison of the mixer track context menu vs a sequencer dropdown confirms the match.
close_reason: Shared menu_style::MENU_FONT_SIZE (10px) now backs both menu-item and dropdown popup rows; explicit :font-size still overrides. Committed f96fe1ee. Not screenshot-verified in the running app.

title: Mixer shift-click range selection follows visual track order
description: Shift-clicking mixer track badges currently selects raw contiguous track indices rather than the tracks in rendered mixer order. Derive range selection from the same Lisp ordering used to draw grouped, nested, and collapsed mixer tracks, with focused regression tests.
close_reason: Mixer shift-click now builds ranges from shared visual track order and atomically selects the explicit track set; covered grouped, nested, collapsed and non-contiguous cases.

title: Step sequencer arrow up/down navigates visual row order, not track index
description:
Now that regular groups and drum racks contain their member tracks in the step
sequencer (eseq-b4m / eseq-4b5), the rendered row order no longer matches track
index order. Up/Down arrow still walks the raw track index, so the selection
jumps off-screen.

Repro (screenshot case): "Group 2" contains tracks 1, 7, 10, 11 rendered in that
visual order. Track 7 is selected; pressing Down selects track 8, which is far
below the group block. It should select track 10 — the next row as drawn.

Current behavior lives in crates/sequencer/src/ui/input.rs:1274:

    (KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Down, KeyModifiers::NONE) => {
        let track_count = state.active_track_count();
        let current = current_track.load(...).min(track_count - 1);
        let next = if Up { current.saturating_dec / wrap } else { (current + 1) % track_count };
        select_track_for_edit(editor, next);

It is pure index arithmetic over active_track_count with wraparound, and knows
nothing about groups or collapse state.

The visual order is already computed in Lisp and is the single source of truth:
- eseq.drum-rack-v2/grid-render-items (crates/sequencer/ui/drum-rack-v2.lisp:158)
  emits the top-level row list: loose tracks in index order, plus one "group"
  item per top-level group anchored at its lowest member (group-anchor), with
  unanchored groups appended last.
- eseq.drum-rack-v2/visible-members (drum-rack-v2.lisp:66) gives a group's drawn
  member tracks (collapsed members already filtered).
- eseq.drum-rack-v2/child-racks (drum-rack-v2.lisp:86) gives nested racks, which
  the parent block renders after its own members (see %group-block in
  ui/sequencer.lisp).
- A collapsed group (eseq.drum-rack-v2/collapsed?) draws no member rows at all.
- Loose collapsed tracks (eseq.track-collapse/collapsed?) are already excluded
  from grid-render-items.

Rust has no equivalent group model, so do NOT reimplement the ordering there.

Suggested shape:
1. Add a Lisp helper next to grid-render-items — e.g.
   (eseq.drum-rack-v2/visible-track-order) — that flattens the rendered rows
   into the ordered list of selectable TRACK indices, applying exactly the same
   traversal %group-block uses: for each render item, a "track" item yields its
   track; a "group" item yields nothing if collapsed, else its visible-members
   in order followed by each child rack expanded recursively.
2. Add a small navigation entry point, e.g.
   (eseq.sequencer/select-track-relative delta) or
   (eseq.drum-rack-v2/track-after track) / track-before, that finds the current
   track's position in that list and moves +/-1 with the same wraparound the
   current code has (Up from the first row wraps to the last, Down from the last
   wraps to the first).
3. In input.rs, replace the index arithmetic with a call to that Lisp function
   (use the existing runtime global_value/invoke pattern from
   select_track_for_edit, input.rs:185, with a fallback to today's arithmetic if
   the global is missing so headless/older-UI paths keep working).

Edge cases to handle:
- Current track not present in the visual list (it is inside a collapsed group,
  or is a collapsed loose track): pick the nearest row that IS visible rather
  than doing nothing — e.g. move to the first visible row at or after the
  collapsed group's position for Down, at or before for Up.
- Empty visual list (all tracks collapsed): no-op, no panic.
- Group headers/buses are NOT selectable by arrow keys; this navigation stays
  track-only. Selecting the group bus keeps its existing click-only path
  (%select-group).
- Nested racks inside a regular group must be walked in the same order they are
  drawn (parent members first, then each child rack's members).

Out of scope: horizontal navigation, mixer-buffer arrow behavior, and
making group headers a selectable stop.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a group/drum rack containing non-contiguous tracks (e.g. 1, 7, 10, 11), Down from track 7 selects track 10 and Up from track 10 selects track 7 — i.e. arrow navigation follows the rendered row order exactly.
- Down from the last member of a group moves to the next rendered row below the group block (the next loose track or the first member of the next group), not to track index+1.
- Members of a collapsed group are skipped entirely; collapsed loose tracks are skipped (matching grid-render-items).
- Nested racks inside a regular group are traversed in draw order: parent members first, then each child rack's members.
- Wraparound is preserved: Up from the first visible row goes to the last visible row and vice versa.
- If the currently selected track is not visible (inside a collapsed group), Up/Down moves to the nearest visible row in that direction instead of no-op'ing or panicking; with zero visible rows the keypress is a safe no-op.
- The row order used for navigation is derived from the same Lisp source as rendering (eseq.drum-rack-v2/grid-render-items + visible-members + child-racks); the ordering is not duplicated in Rust.
- Focused tests: a Lisp-order unit test over a fixture with a group of non-contiguous members, a nested rack, a collapsed group, and a collapsed loose track; plus an input-path test that Up/Down selects the expected track for that fixture.
- cargo check -p sequencer passes; scoped tests only.
close_reason: Implemented visual-row-order step sequencer navigation in Lisp with collapsed/nested group handling, Rust input integration and focused tests.

title: Composite group tint over theme buffer background
description: Restore the appearance of the former alpha-0.22 sequencer group fill without allowing the selected border behind the fill to show through. Compute the opaque RGB equivalent by compositing the group color over THEME.buffer_bg in Lisp.
close_reason: Group container fill now computes the opaque equivalent of the old 22% track-color alpha by compositing against THEME.buffer_bg; targeted group layout test passes.

title: Match context-menu styling to dropdown menus
description: Context menus currently look noticeably less polished than dropdown menus. Update context menus to use the same visual styling as dropdown menus, including typography, font sizing and weight, item padding, spacing, colors, borders, corner radius, shadows, hover/selected states, and separators where applicable. Prefer a shared menu style or shared primitives so the two menu types remain visually consistent rather than duplicating constants.
acceptance_criteria:
- Context-menu typography matches dropdown-menu typography.
- Menu item padding, spacing, alignment, and overall density match dropdown menus.
- Backgrounds, borders, corner radius, shadows, separators, and interactive states are consistent between both menu types.
- Disabled and selected items remain clear and accessible.
- Shared styling/primitives are used where practical to prevent future drift.
- Existing context-menu behavior and dropdown-menu behavior remain unchanged.
- A representative visual capture confirms the menus are consistently styled.
close_reason: Implemented shared popup-menu styling primitives and aligned context-menu chrome, row metrics, padding, hover states, and separators with dropdown menus; targeted tests and visual captures pass.

title: Render regular groups like drum racks in the step sequencer
description: Regular track groups should use the same visual and interaction model that makes drum racks effective in the step sequencer. A group should visually contain its member tracks, and users should be able to hide/collapse the group there, matching the existing drum-rack behavior. The intentional difference is that regular groups must not show an Arm button, because groups cannot be armed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Regular groups visually contain their member tracks in the step sequencer, consistent with drum-rack grouping.
- Regular groups can be hidden/collapsed from the step sequencer using the same interaction model as drum racks.
- Expanding the group restores its contained tracks.
- Regular group headers do not display an Arm control.
- Existing drum-rack appearance and behavior remain unchanged.
notes:
Implemented shared step-sequencer group render ordering and collapsible containers for regular groups and drum racks. Regular group headers expose collapse/mute/solo/name/bus volume without Arm; nested drum racks remain contained. Visual-review follow-up generalized drum-rack-indicator to group-track-indicator and applies the same indented prefix to every regular-group member. Added finite-layout, prefix, collapse/expand, no-Arm, nesting, and drum-rack regression coverage; targeted nextest checks pass.
Second visual follow-up: clicking group/rack container chrome should select its backing bus for the FX panel and selected containers need the same visible selected-border treatment as tracks.
Container selection follow-up implemented: exposed group/rack chrome selects the backing bus, selected state changes only the border color (no selected background), and nested track click targets remain deeper than the container. Added regular-group selected-state and both group/rack style regressions.
Visual correction: Box selected rendering applies a default selected background when selected-background-color is omitted. Explicitly pin selected-background-color to the normal group color so selection changes only the border.
Final color correction per visual direction: reverted the proposed shared box-renderer change completely. Group/rack container fills now premultiply each group RGB channel by 0.22 and render at alpha 1.0; selected-background-color is explicitly identical, so the existing border-under-fill renderer cannot tint the interior. Verified with targeted tests and /tmp/eseqlisp-opaque-selected-border.png.
close_reason: Selected group/rack containers now use opaque premultiplied dark fills so only the border changes

title: Context-menu hover highlight lags ~1s (dropdown is instant)
description:
Hovering over context-menu items (context-menu/menu-item widget from 1b04088d, used for the mixer track/group menus) takes on the order of a second to show the hover highlight, while the dropdown widget's hover tracking is instant. Fix the context menu so hover feedback lands on the next frame like the dropdown's.

How the two differ (the likely root cause lives in this asymmetry):
- Dropdown: owns its own hover state (hovered_idx in dropdown.rs) and updates it via dropdown::hover_overlay(widget_id, local_row) — a cheap row calculation — and the caller explicitly calls mark_needs_redraw() when it changed (editor/mod.rs:2597-2601, update_inactive_overlay_hover).
- Context menu: menu-item render reads the GLOBAL pointer-hover slot via pointer_hovered(node.widget_id) (context_menu.rs:417). That slot is set on MouseEventKind::Moved in widget_interaction.rs:896-905 via set_pointer_hover_widget(hover_node_at_local(...)), which bumps WIDGET_STATE_GENERATION on change — but AUDIT whether that path requests a repaint: set_pointer_hover_widget itself does not call mark_needs_redraw, and if the Moved branch in widget_interaction.rs returns without marking, the highlight only appears when the NEXT scheduled frame happens for some other reason (meters, epoch ticks) — which would read as exactly this ~1s lag. The scene caches do key on widget_state_generation (widget scene key at widget_render/mod.rs:1370, miss accounting at metal_backend.rs:7147), so once a frame IS drawn the new hover renders; the missing piece is triggering the frame.

Debug order:
1. Confirm the repaint-trigger theory: instrument set_pointer_hover_widget (or the Moved branch) and see whether mark_needs_redraw runs on hover change over a menu-item. If not, add it (mirror the dropdown caller's changed→redraw contract) — likely a one-liner fix.
2. If repaint IS requested, check the other suspects: (a) Moved-event coalescing/throttling before widget_interaction; (b) hit-test coordinate mismatch — the context menu draws as an overlay at anchor-col/row while hover_node_at_local hit-tests LAYOUT rects; if the overlay's drawn position diverges from the layout rect the hover would misregister (this would also make the highlight land on the wrong item — verify which item highlights after the delay); (c) hover_node_at_local cost over the full layout on every Moved event.
3. Whatever the fix, consider aligning the context menu with the dropdown's owned-hover-state pattern if the global-pointer-slot path can't be made frame-accurate — but prefer the minimal fix first.

Perf-verification convention: this repo has established real-handler perf test patterns (see plock-knob-curve-editor-perf / step-buffer-edit-perf memories) — a regression test should assert the hover change marks a redraw (or the equivalent observable), not wall-clock timing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hovering across context-menu items updates the highlight within one frame (subjectively instant, matching the dropdown), in both the mixer track menu and group menu, for active and inactive tiles.
- The fix identifies and documents the actual root cause (repaint trigger, event throttling, or hit-test mismatch) in the close notes.
- Dropdown hover behavior and general pointer-hover consumers (e.g. other pointer_hovered users) are unchanged.
- A focused test covers the regression mechanism (e.g. hover change over a menu-item triggers a redraw request / state-generation-visible frame), not wall-clock sleeps.
- cargo check -p eseqlisp passes; scoped tests only.
notes: Root cause confirmed: active-tile pointer movement updated the global pointer-hover slot and widget-state generation, but captured gen_before only afterward and never requested a redraw. The cached scene therefore reflected hover only on an unrelated later frame. set_pointer_hover_widget now reports whether visual state changed, and all editor hover-update/clear paths request redraw on that transition; dropdown-owned hover remains unchanged. Added focused context-menu handler regression coverage asserting a menu-item hover transition sets pointer state and schedules redraw. Validation: cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp -E 'test(/editor::tests::context_menu_/)'; cargo check -p eseqlisp.
close_reason: Fixed missing repaint trigger for global pointer-hover transitions; scoped context-menu tests and cargo check pass.

title: Multi-selected tracks arm all their badges for delete (mass delete)
description:
When 2+ tracks are multi-selected (cmd-click toggle or shift-click range, the latter landed in 5bf0cbc2), arm the whole selection for delete: every selected track's badge shows the delete-armed (selected) color, and Backspace/Delete deletes all of them at once. Besides enabling mass delete, this makes multi-selection visually obvious — today the badges don't change color at all because the multi-select click paths deliberately clear the delete target.

Current machinery:
- Delete target is a SINGLE Option<ActiveDeleteTarget> slot (crates/sequencer/src/ui/edit_sessions.rs:11), armed from Lisp via seq-set-delete-target :mixer-track (natives.rs:3008/parse_delete_target:1764), consumed by the seq-delete-active-target native (natives.rs:3105) which enqueues the "delete-track" host command for MixerTrack — one track only.
- Badge visual: box :selected (%track-delete-target-binding i) in mixer.lisp (~line 60) reads the per-track reactive field mixer-track-delete-target-<i>, computed in state_values/steps_and_pattern.rs:400 by matching MixerTrack{track}, invalidated via bump_delete_target_version.
- Multi-select paths clear the target: %toggle-track-select and %range-track-select in mixer.lisp both call %clear-delete-target.

Work:
1. Add a multi-track target variant — recommended: ActiveDeleteTarget::MixerTracks { tracks: Vec<usize> } (or generalize MixerTrack to hold a set). Update parse_delete_target, active_delete_target_kind, buffer_name (edit_sessions.rs:1159 — still "*mixer*"), and the badge-binding computation in steps_and_pattern.rs:400 so mixer-track-delete-target-<i> is true for every member.
2. Arm on multi-select: in mixer.lisp, %toggle-track-select and %range-track-select should, after updating the selection, set the delete target to the current SEQ.selected-tracks set (when 2+; a selection collapsing back to 0-1 members falls back to today's behavior: cleared target, or single-track target if that matches existing gestures). Plain click keeps its current single-select/delete-target semantics (select-track clears, label click arms single).
3. Mass delete execution: seq-delete-active-target's MixerTracks arm enqueues a new "delete-tracks" host command (host_commands/tracks.rs, next to "delete-track" at line 781) that deletes all listed tracks as ONE recorded/undoable edit. Do not loop "delete-track": indices shift after each removal and undo would be N steps. Delete by descending index or resolve to stable identities first. Reuse delete-track's per-track teardown logic (factor, don't duplicate).
4. Guards, mirroring the single-track arm (natives.rs:3113-3129): refuse to delete ALL tracks ("Cannot delete the last remaining track" — if the selection covers every track, either refuse or delete all but one, implementer's pick with a clear status); drop stale indices when the track count changed, invalidating via bump_delete_target_version; only fire when current buffer is *mixer*.
5. Invalidation: any selection change re-arms (or clears) the target and bumps the version so badge visuals track the selection exactly. Also confirm tracks-in-groups members mass-delete cleanly (delete-track already handles group dissolution below two members — verify the batched edit keeps that behavior).
6. Interaction with grouping (eseq-412.3, eseq-412.2): grouping a selection consumes it — after group-selected-tracks the armed set must clear (host side already bumps on structural changes; verify).

Related: %group-delete-target? / MixerGroup covers group badges — out of scope here except that mixed selections don't exist (selection is tracks only).
acceptance_criteria:
- Cmd-click or shift-click selecting 2+ tracks turns every selected track's badge to the delete-armed/selected color immediately; deselecting updates the badges in step.
- Backspace/Delete in the mixer with a multi-selection armed deletes all selected tracks in ONE undo step; a single undo restores all of them with names, instruments, patterns, and group membership.
- Selecting every track and deleting is refused or leaves one track, with a clear status message; no panic on stale indices after track-count changes.
- Single-track flows unchanged: plain label click still arms exactly one badge and Backspace deletes just it; group-badge delete arming unchanged.
- Grouping an armed selection (Ctrl+G/Cmd+G/menu) clears the armed state; no ghost-armed badges afterwards.
- Focused tests: MixerTracks parse/kind/binding, delete-tracks host command (descending-index correctness, single undo, group-dissolve interaction, last-track guard), and badge-binding updates on selection change — pattern after delete_target_tests (natives.rs:1889) and the steps_and_pattern binding tests.
- cargo check -p sequencer passes; scoped tests only.
close_reason: Implemented multi-track delete arming, atomic mass deletion, grouping cleanup, stale/last-track guards, and focused tests.

title: Fix pre-existing mixer click test drum-rack icon expectation
description: The focused metal_seq test state_values::tests::metal_seq_mixer_clicks_dispatch_to_matching_track_and_bus_controls fails at clean HEAD 4d495931 because the drum-rack mixer badge icon is None rather than :sampler. Reproduced in an isolated git worktree on 2026-08-20 with: cargo nextest run -p sequencer -E 'binary(metal_seq) and test(=state_values::tests::metal_seq_mixer_clicks_dispatch_to_matching_track_and_bus_controls)'. Investigate whether the fixture or icon propagation is stale and restore this regression test without weakening its functional assertion.
close_reason: Current HEAD test passes exactly and in repeated full debug/release suites; stale pre-existing report.

title: Context menu: Group Tracks on multi-selection; Ungroup on group/drum-rack headers
description:
Two context-menu additions to the mixer track/group menu (context-menu widget wired in mixer.lisp; see also eseq-0wb which adds group rename to the same menus — coordinate but don't block).

PART A — "Group Tracks" on track badges when 2+ tracks are selected:
- %track-menu-actions (crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp:28) is a static list by design ("Data ... is the extension seam"); make it (or %track-context-menu-actions, line ~891) selection-aware: when (len SEQ.selected-tracks) >= 2 AND the right-clicked track is part of the selection, append (dict :id :group :label "Group Tracks").
- Action routes to the existing %group-selected (mixer.lisp:1617, host-command "group-selected-tracks"). Close the menu first (see %select-track-menu-action, ~line 899).
- Right-clicking a track OUTSIDE the current multi-selection should show the normal single-track menu (and per existing click conventions may leave the selection alone — right-click currently doesn't change selection; keep it that way).

PART B — "Ungroup" on group and drum-rack headers:
- Menu side: %track-context-menu-actions returns %group-menu-actions for plain groups and an EMPTY list for rack groups (mixer.lisp:891-897; eseq-0wb changes this for Rename). Add (dict :id :ungroup :label "Ungroup") to both plain-group and rack-group menus. The header right-click already exists (%open-group-menu, ~line 1365).
- Rust side: there is NO whole-group ungroup host command today — only per-track "remove-track-from-group" (host_commands/tracks.rs:1123) and the internal dissolve_group_if_undersized (app/edit.rs:2464). Add an "ungroup-tracks" host command (group-id) as ONE recorded/undoable edit that releases all member units back to the parent scope (master mix, or the enclosing parent group if nested — follow the routing semantics documented at edit.rs:2395-2447) and removes the group + its backing bus. Do not implement it as N remove-track-from-group calls (N undo steps, and the group would dissolve midway).
- Drum racks: a rack group carries extra identity (rack flag, pads, Patch.rack_track wiring, pad-note transposes — see racks/rack-glyph specs). Ungrouping a drum rack should be the inverse of convert-group-to-drum-rack (host_commands/tracks.rs:168): member tracks survive as plain tracks with their instruments/patterns intact, rack-specific state (pad assignments, rack panel focus, forced_group) is cleanly torn down. If a true inverse turns out to have blockers (e.g. rack-only state with no plain-track home), scope PART B's rack case down to a follow-up bead and land plain-group ungroup — note the decision in the close notes.
- Guard rails: mid-play ungroup must not leave dangling bus routing (the remove-track-from-group path at tracks.rs:1123-1140 shows the master-mix rewiring to mirror); the sidebar rack panel, group collapse state, and SEQ.groups consumers must all handle the group disappearing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Right-click on a badge of a multi-selected track (2+) shows "Group Tracks"; selecting it creates the group exactly like Ctrl+G. Single-selection menus are unchanged.
- Right-click on a plain group header and on a drum-rack header shows "Ungroup"; selecting it releases all member tracks (instruments, patterns, names, p-locks intact) back to the parent scope and removes the group and its bus.
- Ungroup is a single undo step; undo restores the group with its membership, name, and routing (and rack identity for drum racks, if the rack case ships in this bead).
- Ungrouping while playing does not glitch audio routing of the released tracks (they route to master/parent immediately).
- Nested case: ungrouping an inner group re-parents members to the enclosing group, not master.
- Focused tests: ungroup-tracks host command (membership, bus teardown, undo, nested), and menu-action visibility for multi-select vs single, plain group vs rack.
- cargo check -p sequencer passes; scoped tests only.
close_reason: Implemented selection-aware Group Tracks context action and undoable plain/drum-rack Ungroup with nested reparenting, routing teardown, host command sync, and focused tests.

title: Cmd+G groups selected tracks (retire agent-mode binding)
description:
