title: Shift+click range-selects tracks in the mixer
description:
Support shift+click on mixer track strips/badges to select a contiguous run of tracks, complementing the existing cmd+click toggle multi-select.

Current selection plumbing (crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp):
- %multi-select-click? (~line 148) checks event :cmd/:super/:meta; %track-body-click (~line 160) and %track-label-click (~line 165) route to %toggle-track-select (per-track toggle via seq-toggle-track-selected native, natives.rs:4047) or plain select-track.
- Click events already carry a :shift modifier (click_info in crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/button.rs:162 populates "shift"/"alt"/"super" alongside cmd), so detection is (get event :shift).
- Selection state is SEQ.selected-tracks (a list of indices).

Work:
1. Anchor semantics: shift+click selects the contiguous range between an anchor and the clicked track. Recommended anchor: the most recent plainly-selected or toggled track (fall back to SEQ.current-track when there's no explicit anchor). Match the familiar file-browser convention: plain click sets the anchor; shift+click extends from it; a following shift+click re-extends from the same anchor (replacing the previous range extension), and cmd+click still toggles individual membership without moving the anchor.
2. Add a native or host path to set the selection to an explicit range/set in one operation (e.g. seq-select-track-range anchor..target, or a set-selection native), rather than looping seq-toggle-track-selected from Lisp — toggling would flip already-selected members and emit N reveal commands. Pattern after seq-toggle-track-selected in crates/sequencer/src/ui/natives.rs:4040.
3. Range is over VISIBLE mixer order: decide behavior across group boundaries (tracks inside collapsed/expanded groups between anchor and target). Recommended v1: include all tracks in the index range regardless of group membership — group-selected-tracks (host_commands/tracks.rs:987) already handles pulling tracks out of source groups on regroup (see edit.rs:2403 comments); note in the bead if testing reveals a constraint.
4. Wire :shift into %track-body-click and %track-label-click before the %multi-select-click? branch. Keep the label's plain-click delete-target gesture unchanged.
5. After a shift range-select of 2+, ctrl+G grouping must work exactly as it does after cmd-click selection (seq-ctrl-g reads (len SEQ.selected-tracks), mixer.lisp:1624).
acceptance_criteria:
- Click track 2, shift+click track 6 → tracks 2-6 selected (both strip body and label clicks); shift+click track 4 afterwards → 2-4 selected (re-extend from anchor).
- Cmd+click still toggles single membership; plain click still single-selects and resets the anchor; label plain-click delete-target gesture unchanged.
- Reverse ranges work (anchor 6, shift+click 2).
- Ctrl+G after a shift range-select groups the selection.
- Focused tests cover anchor/extend/re-extend and the new range-selection native (state_values/tests.rs has existing selection tests to pattern after).
- cargo check -p sequencer passes; scoped tests only.
notes: Implemented anchored Shift+click selection for mixer strip bodies and labels. Plain selection resets the anchor; Cmd+click keeps toggling without moving it; repeated Shift+click replaces the prior extension. Added atomic seq-select-track-range native using inclusive track-index order, including all group members regardless of collapsed/expanded state. Validation: native exact test passed; mixer Lisp parse test passed; cargo check -p sequencer passed. The existing mixer click integration test reaches/passes the new range assertions, then fails at an unrelated drum-rack icon assertion; reproduced at clean HEAD 4d495931 and tracked as eseq-owd.
close_reason: Implemented and committed as 5bf0cbc2; targeted native and parser tests plus cargo check pass. New mixer range assertions pass before the integration test reaches pre-existing eseq-owd.

title: Mixer: drum rack (and group) headers get context-menu rename
description:
Right-clicking a drum rack's header in the mixer shows no context menu, and there is no way to rename a drum rack (or any track group) from the mixer. Tracks got the right-click → Rename flow in 5a0f3dad; extend the same flow to group headers, drum racks included.

Why it's missing today (all in crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp unless noted):

- %group-menu-actions (~line 31) contains only :convert-drum-rack — no Rename even for plain groups.
- The group header renders the name as a plain label (group-name-label-, ~line 1377) with no rename input variant; there is no %group-renaming state.
- Rust side: app/edit.rs:2928 rename_group_recorded(group_id, name) already exists as a recorded/undoable edit, but NOTHING calls it — there is no "rename-group" host command (grep host_commands/ confirms). rename-track (host_commands/tracks.rs:107) is the pattern to follow.

Work:
1. Host command: add "rename-group" (group-id + name) → rename_group_recorded, mirroring rename-track's trim/empty-reject behavior (see the recorded_track_rename test at app/edit.rs:9682 for the semantics).
2. Menu actions: add (dict :id :rename :label "Rename") for group menus. Rack groups get a real action list instead of (list) — at minimum Rename; keep :convert-drum-rack out of rack groups as today (already converted). %select-track-menu-action routes :rename by %track-menu-group-id >= 0 to a new %begin-group-rename.

Inline rename input: add %group-renaming/%group-rename-draft state and swap the group name label for the shared %track-rename-input pattern (~line 919: text-input with :auto-focus, :select-all-on-focus, on-submit/on-cancel/on-blur), committing via the new rename-group host command. description:
The track context menu (context-menu widget from 1b04088d / eseq-dkn, wired into the mixer in the recent rename work) currently opens only when right-clicking the track name badge/label. Extend it so right-clicking ANYWHERE on a track's strip row (the whole horizontal track component: number badge, S button, icon+name, meter, knobs area — see screenshot context: user right-clicked the body of a "Layer R.." row and expected the menu) opens the same menu, with Rename working from there. Current wiring (all in crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp):
- %open-track-menu (line ~859) sets %track-menu-track/-col/-row/-open; %track-context-menu (line ~909) renders the context-menu with %track-context-menu-actions; %select-track-menu-action routes :rename → %begin-track-rename.
- on-right-click handlers exist only on the label box: expanded strip ~line 949 and collapsed strip ~line 1013 (plus group header ~line 1365 for %open-group-menu).

1. Attach :on-right-click (lambda (event) (%open-track-menu event i)) to the outermost container of the full strip row for BOTH the expanded and collapsed strip variants. Find the row root (the widget that spans the whole strip incl. controls) rather than adding handlers to each child.
2. Event precedence: verify how right-click propagates through the widget tree (right-click plumbing landed in 1b04088d). Inner widgets that already have their own right-click behavior must keep it; the row-level handler should only fire when no inner handler consumed the event. If the current plumbing dispatches to the deepest handler only, this is free; if it bubbles, guard accordingly. Keep the existing label-level handler or remove it if the row-level one subsumes it — don't double-open.

title: Instruments sidebar: make Modulator / Drum Rack / Instrument Rack draggable
description:
In the Instruments sidebar tree, only custom (saved) instruments and the builtin Sampler are draggable; Modulator, Drum Rack ("rack"), and Instrument Rack ("layer-rack") are not. Make all builtin instruments draggable like the rest.

Root cause of the current restriction: crates/sequencer/src/ui/browser.rs:606 builtin_instrument_leaf() sets ("draggable", Value::Bool(item.name == "sampler")). The tree widget honors the per-item flag (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/tree.rs:182,918). Flipping it to true for all builtins enables dragging, but the DROP handlers must also route builtin payloads correctly:

1. Drop onto an EXISTING track: eseq.browser/drop-instrument-on-track (crates/sequencer/ui/browser.lisp:237) already branches on payload :kind == "builtin-instrument" → %swap-track-builtin-instrument (browser.lisp:229), but that fn only supports "sampler" and statuses "Only sampler conversion is supported" otherwise. Decide the UX per type: modulator likely should NOT convert an existing track in place (or should, via a new swap host-command — implementer judgment); drum rack / instrument rack are group/slot entities where in-place conversion doesn't apply — for those, falling back to adding a new track (%add-builtin-instrument-track, browser.lisp:837) with a clear status is acceptable v1 behavior. Mirror the guard rationale in %activate-builtin-instrument (browser.lisp:848) which already routes click-activation: sampler may swap in place, everything else adds a new track.

2. Drop onto the NEW-TRACK / empty zone: these handlers ignore :kind and unconditionally call host-command "add-track-instrument" with the payload :name, which only resolves SAVED instruments — dropping a builtin there today would try to load a saved instrument literally named "modulator". Fix both:
   - crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp drop-sample-new-track (~line 180, instrument branch ~192)
   - crates/sequencer/ui/sequencer.lisp drop-new-track (~line 391)
   Route payload :kind == "builtin-instrument" to %add-builtin-instrument-track (browser.lisp:837), which dispatches to add-track-sampler / add-track-modulator / add-track-rack / add-layer-rack-track host commands. Also skip the sbrowser-loading-instrument-name spinner for builtins (it is keyed to saved-instrument load).

3. Check remaining "instrument" drop sites for the same :kind blindness: mixer.lisp:1396 and sequencer.lisp:1829/2196 accept drag-type "instrument" — audit each and either route builtins sensibly or reject with a clear status message (no silent misroute into add-track-instrument).

Note: drag onto a folder in the tree itself (drop-instrument-on-folder → "move-saved-instrument") must reject builtin-instrument payloads gracefully — builtins are not files that can be moved.
acceptance_criteria:
- Modulator, Drum Rack, and Instrument Rack rows in the Instruments sidebar are draggable (Sampler and saved instruments unchanged).
- Dropping each builtin onto the new-track/empty zone in both the mixer and the sequencer creates the correct track type (modulator track, drum rack, instrument rack) — never a saved-instrument lookup by builtin name.
- Dropping onto an existing track behaves deliberately per type: sampler keeps its in-place swap; the others either swap via a supported path or add a new track with a status message — no "Only sampler conversion is supported" dead-end for a drop that visually landed.
- Dragging a builtin onto a sidebar folder does not emit move-saved-instrument.
- Focused tests cover the new drop routing (state_values/tests.rs has existing host-command drop tests to pattern after, e.g. the add-track-instrument assertion ~line 4945).
- cargo check -p sequencer passes; scoped tests only.
close_reason: Shipped in 5d95945f: all builtin instrument rows draggable; shared eseq.browser/drop-instrument-new-track routes :kind builtin-instrument to add-track-sampler/-modulator/-rack/-layer-rack; existing-track drop falls back to adding a track; group-header, empty pad and folder drops refused with clear status.

title: Mixer track/rack rename: caret draws mid-string while typing
description:
Repro: open the mixer, start an inline track/rack rename (feature from 5a0f3dad), type a name like "lush sound". The text renders correctly but the caret is drawn in the middle of the string (roughly 60-70% in) even though the logical cursor is at the end (typing keeps appending at the end, so cursor_pos is correct — only the drawn x-position is wrong).

Where the caret x comes from: crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/text_input.rs
- Render pass: metal render computes cursor x via cursor_x_from_char_cache(text, font_size, cursor_pos, cell_w) (~line 1085-1101). Selection rects use text_range_width_from_char_cache the same way.
- The cache (CHAR_WIDTH_CACHE, keyed on (font_size.to_bits(), text)) is only populated during the MEASURE pass: TextInputWidget::measure calls cache_char_widths(value, font_size, ctx) (~line 751-759).
- On cache miss the render falls back to an approximation: cursor_pos * font_size * 0.55 / cell_w (~line 568). 0.55*font_size is narrower than the real average glyph width, which visually places the caret mid-string — exactly the observed symptom.

Primary hypothesis: after each keystroke the input's new value string never goes through measure, so the render pass misses the cache and uses the fallback. Plausible causes to check:
1. Subtree/in-place layout reuse: the rename input lives in the per-track label subtree (%strip-label / %track-rename-input in crates/sequencer/ui/mixer.lisp ~line 918) that is deliberately rerun in isolation ("rename/mute changes rerun just the label"), and the layout-reuse optimizations (in-place subtree layout reuse from the full-layout-selection perf work) may skip re-measuring a widget whose SIZE is unchanged — text-input has a fixed :width, so the size never changes even though the value did. cache_char_widths is a side effect of measure, so skipping measure starves the cache.
2. font_size key mismatch between the measure pass (explicit :font-size prop vs ctx.inherited_font_size) and whatever font_size the render pass resolves — f32::to_bits keying means any tiny difference misses.

Fix direction (implementer's choice): don't rely on measure-pass side effects for render-pass metrics — e.g. have the render path populate CHAR_WIDTH_CACHE itself on miss (it can measure via the same measurer), or ensure a value change always re-measures the text-input even under subtree layout reuse. Verify the selection-rect path (select-all-on-focus highlight) with the same fix, since it uses the same cache and fallback.

Diagnostic first step: log/breakpoint the fallback branch in cursor_x_from_char_cache while typing in the mixer rename — if it fires, hypothesis 1 or 2 is confirmed and the key values (font_size bits, text) on both sides tell you which.
acceptance_criteria:
- While typing in the mixer inline rename, the caret is drawn at the true end-of-text glyph position for proportional text (no mid-string caret), including after every keystroke, backspace, and cursor-key movement.
- The select-all-on-focus selection highlight covers exactly the rendered text width (same metrics source as the caret).
- Other text-input usages (e.g. sound palette rename, search fields) still position the caret correctly.
- A focused test covers the regression mechanism found (e.g. cache populated for the current value at render time, or measure re-runs on value change under subtree reuse) — pattern it after the existing select_all_on_focus test in text_input.rs.
- cargo check -p eseqlisp and the scoped text_input/widget_focus tests pass (scoped tests only, per repo convention).
close_reason: Closed

title: Group context menu: convert group → drum rack
description:
Add a "Convert to Drum Rack" option to the track/group context menu (the rename menu from eseq-g7r) shown when right-clicking a GROUP strip.

A drum rack is already a track group carrying a pad map (creation path: ui/host_commands/tracks.rs ~:194 — "Creating a drum rack builds a track group carrying a pad map"; rack groups answer `group.is_rack()`). Conversion should upgrade an existing plain group in place rather than making users rebuild:

- New host command (e.g. convert-group-to-drum-rack, group idx) that marks the group as a rack and assigns pad notes to the existing member tracks (sequential pads starting at the drum rack home octave — pad_note is a transpose, 0 = C4, domain -36..51 per drum-rack-v2).
- Reuse the drum-rack creation plumbing from tracks.rs rather than duplicating it; the difference is adopting existing member tracks instead of creating new ones.
- Menu entry only appears on group strips that are NOT already racks.
- Undo restores the plain group (members, name, routing untouched).
- Save/load round-trips the converted rack like a born-drum-rack group.

Acceptance:
- Right-click a plain group strip → "Convert to Drum Rack" → group becomes a functioning drum rack: pads trigger member tracks, pad lights work, rack UI (pads/slots) shows the members.
- Existing member track sounds, patterns, and mixer state are preserved.
- Option absent on non-group tracks and on groups that are already racks.
- Undo/redo works; project save/load round-trips.
close_reason: Corrected conversion pad ordering to start at transpose 0 (C4) and wrap from the maximum pad note to C1; targeted conversion and wrap tests pass.

title: Track header icons for instrument racks and drum racks
description:
Instrument rack and drum rack tracks show no type icon in track headers, while sampler (:waveform) and custom (:piano) tracks do — rack tracks (e.g. "Layer R..") look bare next to them. Add distinct icons for both rack flavors, in BOTH the mixer strips and the sequencer track headers.

Where (from grep, 2026-08-19):
- The single mapping lives in crates/sequencer/ui/track-collapse.lisp:43 `type-icon`: returns :waveform for "sampler", :piano for "custom", nil otherwise — so "rack" tracks get nothing. The comment above it says icon names intentionally match the sound browser tab icons; pick rack icons consistent with that set.
- Consumers (all already call the shared helper, so fixing the mapping covers both surfaces): mixer.lisp:864 and :925 (mixer strips), sequencer.lisp:869 (sequencer track headers) via `(eseq.track-collapse/type-icon i)`.

Flavor discrimination:
- SEQ.track-instrument-types only publishes "rack" (InstrumentType::Rack, src/ui/state_values/track_and_mixer.rs:76) — that is the Instrument Rack (slot-based) track type.
- Drum racks are track GROUPS (`group.is_rack()`, see src/ui/state_values/drum_rack.rs read_rack_pad_trigger_flags); their header strip is the group strip. If the drum-rack group header doesn't currently flow through type-icon, add the drum-rack icon at whatever renders that group header, or publish a per-track/per-group rack-flavor state value so lisp can distinguish.

Acceptance:
- Instrument rack tracks show a rack icon in mixer strips and sequencer headers.
- Drum rack headers show a distinct drum-rack icon in both surfaces.
- Icons visually match the existing sound-browser icon language.
notes: Implemented shared instrument-rack (:sliders) and drum-rack (:sampler/Kits) icon mappings in mixer and sequencer headers. Added finite-layout/icon assertions for both surfaces and expanded the production Metal capture fixture. Targeted nextest: 3 passed. Visual captures inspected at /tmp/metal-seq-track-type-icons-{mixer,sequencer}.png. Commit: 42ece34a.
close_reason: Implemented and validated rack identity icons in mixer and sequencer headers

title: Track rename via mixer badge context menu (inline edit)
description:
Ableton-style track rename, first consumer of the context-menu widget.

**Interaction (per Ableton reference):**
- Right-click a track badge in the mixer (mixer.lisp:862 renders `(nth SEQ.track-names i)` as the badge) opens the context menu with at least **Rename**. Room to grow later: Duplicate, Delete, Group, color swatches — keep the menu definition data-driven so those slot in.
- Selecting Rename swaps the badge into an inline text-input pre-filled with the current name, focused, text selected. Enter commits, Esc cancels, blur commits (match text-input rename behavior from sound palette S3 — see its rename gotchas).

**Plumbing:**
- New host command `rename-track` (track_idx, name) in ui/host_commands/tracks.rs: trims, rejects empty (revert to previous), writes app.tracks[idx], marks the name user-authored.
- Undo: run through the history host-command path (undo-drag-invalidation pattern — targeted invalidation, no ui_epoch bump).
- Renaming must survive save/load (depends on the ProjectTrack name persistence bead) and must NOT be clobbered by instrument/preset swaps: once user-authored, instrument loads keep the custom name. Decide + document the rule (suggest: explicit user rename pins the name; loading a .sound preset onto an unpinned track still adopts the preset name).
- Should work for all track kinds (rack, sampler, custom, modulator) and ideally group strips too (group rename may already exist — check).

**Acceptance:**
- Rename a rack track, name shows everywhere (badge, collapsed label at mixer.lisp:880, seq header), survives save/load and undo/redo.
- Loading an instrument into a renamed track keeps the custom name.
- Empty-string commit reverts.
close_reason: Implemented mixer badge context-menu rename with focused inline editing, recorded undo/redo, persisted user-authored name pinning, and instrument-swap preservation.

title: Contextual menu widget (anchored right-click popup) for the Lisp UI
description:
A real context menu widget — pointer-anchored popup opened by right-click — distinct from the dropdown widget. This is missing infrastructure that blocks a whole class of interactions (rename, duplicate, delete, color, group actions on tracks/clips/slots). First consumer: track badge menu (see dependent bead).

**Two layers of work:**

1. **Right-click event plumbing.** The event loop only routes left-button mouse events today (src/ui/event_loop.rs — crossterm MouseButton::Left only). Route MouseEventKind::Down(MouseButton::Right) through hit-testing and expose an `:on-right-click` handler on widgets (event carries pointer position). Consider ctrl+click as a synonym (macOS convention) since some terminals swallow right-click.

2. **`context-menu` widget.** Model on the modal widget (docs/modal-widget-spec.md, already merged — see choose-model.lisp / sound-palette.lisp usage) but anchored at the pointer instead of centered:
   - Opens at the event's x/y; flips/clamps to stay on screen.
   - Items: label, optional shortcut hint (right-aligned), separators, disabled state, :on-select handler. Ableton's track menu is the reference layout.
   - Dismiss on outside click, Esc, or item selection. Reuse the modal overlay/focus-capture mechanics (watch the overlay gotchas from modal-widget-phase01).
   - Declarative Lisp API, e.g. `(context-menu :is-open ... :anchor-x/:anchor-y ... (menu-item "Rename" :shortcut "⌘R" :on-select ...) (menu-separator) ...)`.

**Acceptance:**
- Right-click on a widget with :on-right-click opens the menu at the pointer; opening near screen edges stays fully visible.
- Esc / outside-click closes without firing items; clicking an item fires exactly its handler and closes.
- Headless UI test driving a right-click event end to end.

Not a dropdown: dropdowns are value pickers attached to a control; this is an action menu anchored to a pointer event.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 1b04088d: right-click plumbing (:on-right-click on box, ctrl+click synonym, ancestor bubbling, event carries :col/:row layout coords) + context-menu/menu-item/menu-separator widgets as an anchored modal-family overlay with flip/clamp placement, Esc/outside-click/select-to-close, and headless end-to-end tests.

title: Drum rack meter in *sequencer* buffer stays static when the mixer buffer is closed
description:
Repro: close/hide the mixer buffer. The level meter shown inside the drum rack view in the *sequencer* buffer freezes — it stops receiving updates. Reopen the mixer and it updates again.

Suspected cause: somewhere in the codebase there is a gate that checks which buffers are open and uses that to throttle/skip high-frequency UI updates (meter values etc.) — it presumably only pushes meter updates when the mixer buffer is visible. The drum rack meter in *sequencer* is a second consumer of that data and needs to count as one: fix the visibility check to account for any open view that displays meters (or key it off the widgets/subscriptions actually present rather than a hardcoded buffer name).

Search leads: meter update / high-frequency UI throttle keyed on open buffers; node-state→widget meter pattern (see builtin OTT/compressor meter plumbing) for how meter data flows to widgets.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mixer: mute/solo/arm buttons on drum rack strips; mute/solo on regular group strips
description:
The mixer strip for a drum rack currently shows no mute/solo/arm buttons (see the collapsed group strip: fader + sends + badge only). Add them:

1) Drum rack strips get the full mute + solo + record-arm button row, like regular track strips. Arm on a rack is meaningful (arming the rack turns the keyboard into pads for live play/record).

2) Regular (non-rack) group strips should also gain mute + solo — but NOT record-arm, which doesn't make sense for a plain group. So the rack strip and the group strip diverge: rack = mute/solo/arm, group = mute/solo.

3) Layout: the group/rack strip is narrower than a track strip; widen it enough to fit the button row.

Semantics: group/rack mute mutes all member tracks' output at the group bus (or equivalent); solo solos the group against the rest of the mixer, consistent with track solo behavior. Related: track-groups feature (docs/track-groups-spec.md, mixer grouping phases 1+2), drum-rack-v2 spec.
close_reason: Closed

title: Delete a drum rack/group via badge-select + backspace in the mixer, undoable
description:
There is currently no quick way to delete a drum rack from the project. Mirror the existing track-delete flow in the mixer: clicking a rack/group's badge (the labeled pill at the bottom of the group strip, e.g. 'test drum') selects/arms it for delete, and Backspace then deletes the rack/group — exactly like clicking a track's badge arms that track for delete via backspace.

Deleting a rack removes the group and all its member tracks (pads) from the project.

Must be UNDOABLE — undo restores the rack, its member tracks, pad map, patterns, p-locks, mixer routing, etc.

Related code: existing mixer track badge-select + backspace delete path; track group model (docs/track-groups-spec.md, docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md).
close_reason: Closed

title: Kit + sound auditioning on a selected drum rack: feel like a single-track instrument, undoable
description:
Auditioning must make the rack feel like a single-track instrument even though underneath it is a group of tracks.

1) Double-clicking a kit in the browser Kits tab currently always APPENDS it to the project as a new track/rack. Instead, when a drum rack is selected, double-clicking a kit should audition/load that kit INTO the selected rack (replacing its pad/sound assignments), exactly like double-clicking an instrument auditions it onto the selected track.

2) Auditioning something else instead of a rack: clicking a sound in the browser while a rack is selected should audition that sound over the rack (i.e. the selection behaves like a single track whose instrument gets swapped for the auditioned sound).

Both operations must be UNDOABLE — undo restores the previous rack contents (or restores the rack after it was swapped for a sound).

Related code: browser Kits tab %kits-panel in ui/browser.lisp, kit load plumbing in src/project.rs / src/app/projects.rs, existing single-track instrument audition path for reference. See also eseq-4b5.17 (save-kit flow).
close_reason: Closed

title: Cmd+= / Cmd+- on a selected drum rack doubles/halves pattern length for ALL rack member tracks
description:
Currently Cmd+= doubles the pattern length of the selected track (and Cmd+- halves it). When the selected track is a drum rack, these shortcuts should instead apply to every member track in the rack: Cmd+= doubles each rack member's pattern length, Cmd+- halves each one.

Notes:
- Members can have different pattern lengths (that's a core drum-rack-v2 feature), so double/halve each track's own length rather than setting a uniform value.
- Respect existing clamping rules (min length on halve, max on double) per track; a track already at a limit stays put while the others still change.
- Should be a single undo step covering all member tracks.
- Relevant code: pattern-length double/halve handlers in src/ui/input.rs -> host_commands/tracks.rs / history_commands.rs; rack membership via the track group model (docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md).
notes: Implemented rack-aware Cmd+=/Cmd+- routing, atomic composite pattern-geometry history across all rack member tracks, per-member clamping/duplication semantics, and regression coverage for shortcuts plus undo/redo.
close_reason: Implemented and validated targeted rack pattern-resize and shortcut regression tests.

title: Soothe v2: builtin spectral resonance suppressor (peak-excluded detector + bounded-IR application)
description:
# Soothe v2: spectral resonance suppressor rebuilt from first principles

Replace the failed `crates/sequencer/effects/spectral-cumsum-soothe/` attempt with a design that reuses the Filter Table's proven bounded-IR spectral application machinery.

**Ship as a BUILTIN effect**, following the Filter Table graduation path: DSP authored in DGenLisp but hosted as a builtin (`src/effects/filter_table.rs` + `filter_table_dsp*.lisp` is the template — .lisp files live in src/effects/, host integration in a soothe.rs registered in effects/mod.rs, params exposed through the standard builtin param/mod-lane plumbing). Not a user-space effects/ directory package.

## Why the current attempt fails (diagnosis)

The existing dsp.lisp is not rudimentary — log-mag analysis, constant-Q cumsum smoothing, hop-gated attack/release, mirror-symmetric CQ index tables (verified). It fails structurally:

1. **Self-masking detector.** `contrast = log-mag − boxcar(log-mag)` where the boxcar INCLUDES the peak being detected. At low freq the CQ windows are 3–5 bins, so a 1–2 bin resonance IS most of its own reference → contrast ≈ 0. At high freq windows are 100+ bins, so broadband harshness lifts the reference with the signal → contrast ≈ 0 again. Only fires on isolated spikes against silence, which real material never presents.
2. **Raw per-bin gain application.** `exp(-amount·excess)` applied directly, no frequency smoothing, no IR bounding → circular-convolution time aliasing (IR wraps the 1024 frame) + musical noise, aggravated by only 2x overlap. filter-table-effect-spec.md documents this exact failure mode: "The wrapped IR window is required."
3. **1024 FFT = 43 Hz bins.** Too coarse below ~800 Hz where boxiness/honk lives (resonance spans 1–2 bins).
4. **Units in nats, not dB.** threshold 0.35 ≈ 3 dB but amount 4 → 1 nat excess = −34 dB cut. Acts as an all-or-nothing spectral gate, not a compressor.

The old file's header says 256-hop broke live-wrapper stereo state, forcing 1024/512 at 2x overlap. The Filter Table has since proven 2048 FFT / 512 hop (4x overlap) works live — that constraint is obsolete.

## Architecture

Two separable problems: a resonance DETECTOR (where is the spectrum locally proud of its own envelope?) and a clean dynamic-filter APPLICATOR (apply a smooth time-varying gain curve without artifacts). Filter Table already solved the applicator (`src/effects/filter_table_dsp_spectral.lisp`): response-mag → zero-phase IFFT → wrapped-cosine IR bound (~768 taps, IRHALF idiom) → FFT → complex multiply → IFFT/OLA, at 2048/512 with √Hann·0.7071 pair and latency-aligned dry path. Lift it verbatim.

### Stage A — Analysis
2048 FFT, hop 512, 4x overlap. Detect on mid (0.5·(L+R)); real M/S processing is a v2 follow-up. Work in dB: `mag-db = 8.6859 · log(mag + 1e-6)`.

### Stage B — Peak-excluded envelope (clip-and-resmooth) — THE key detector fix
Cheap with existing cumsum+gather CQ machinery, reused 2–3x:
1. `env0 = CQ-smooth-wide(mag-db)` (~1 octave windows)
2. `clipped = min(mag-db, env0 + margin)` — shave peaks off
3. `env = CQ-smooth-wide(clipped)` — reference now hugs valleys instead of being dragged up by peaks (SNIP-style baseline estimate; 2 iterations suffice)
4. `contrast = CQ-smooth-narrow(mag-db) − env` with ~1/6-octave narrow smoother so single-bin FFT noise doesn't trigger

Needs a second (wide) set of cq_lo/cq_hi/cq_inv_count tables for 2048 bins alongside narrow ones — same generator, different Q. All tables must stay mirror-symmetric about Nyquist (the old tables were; keep that property at 2048).

### Stage C — Compression law in dB
`reduction-db = depth · softknee(contrast − threshold)` with a relu-based quadratic soft knee. depth 1.0 = 1:∞ above threshold; ~0.3–0.5 ≈ ratio-like. Attack/release: keep the old max-of-two-one-poles at hop rate (that part was correct) but parameterize in ms → per-hop coefficients (hop = 11.6 ms @ 44.1k). Hop-gated via make-history @hop 512 + hop-hold, as before.

### Stage D — Frequency-smooth the gain curve BEFORE applying
Run the reduction curve itself through a CQ boxcar whose width is the **selectivity** param (narrow = surgical notches, wide = gentle). This is what separates soothe from a bin gate: the applied filter is always a smooth proportional-Q shape even when detection is sharp. Also keeps the equivalent IR short so Stage E truncation is near-lossless.

### Stage E — Bounded-IR application (Filter Table idiom, verbatim)
`gain = 10^(−reduction-db/20)`, mirror-symmetric about Nyquist (automatic if computed from symmetric mag + symmetric tables). Zero-phase IFFT of gain curve → wrapped-cosine window to ~768 taps (IRHALF) → FFT → complex-multiply input STFT (both channels, one shared curve) → IFFT/OLA with √Hann pair. No musical noise, no time aliasing, by construction. Every response control hop-holded before tensor math (Filter Table rule).

### Stage F — UX essentials
- Latency-aligned STFT dry path (Filter Table already does this) for `mix`.
- **Delta monitoring** param (dry − wet) — soothe is tuned entirely by listening to what it removes.
- Threshold **tilt/focus**: per-bin dB offset tensor scaled by low/high focus params using bin_norm — replaces the old hard band mask.
- `output` trim. No makeup needed.

## Params (sketch)
depth, threshold (dB), selectivity, attack-ms, release-ms, focus-low, focus-high, delta (listen), mix, output. Standard 4 host mod lanes on depth/threshold/selectivity/mix.

## Validation (C harness method — compile .lisp to C, drive the dylib)
1. Sine + pink noise: measure notch depth at the sine, flatness elsewhere.
2. Pure pink noise: gain stays ~unity (old design fails this — broadband self-triggering).
3. Swept resonant peak: notch tracks the sweep; check attack/release timing.
These three tests directly probe the three failure modes of the old version. Also verify generated C keeps tensor work hop-gated (no per-frame FFT fusion regression — see dgenlisp-stft-cpu-temporality memory).

## Known gotchas to respect
- Spectral masks must be conjugate-symmetric about Nyquist (dgenlisp-spectral-mask-symmetry).
- hop-hold param scalars before tensor math (dgenlisp-stft-cpu-temporality).
- make-history @hop buffer-reuse clobber was fixed but pattern per dgen-tensor-history-feedback-fix.
- noise-node dedup gotcha if any dither/noise is added (spectral-shatter).

One-sentence summary: keep the cumsum/gather CQ machinery but fix the detector with a peak-excluded (clip-and-resmooth) envelope in dB, and replace raw per-bin gain with the Filter Table's frequency-smoothed, bounded-IR application at 2048/512. Recomposition of proven parts, no new infrastructure.

title: Retire '444 Compressor' and 'Delay' from the browsable builtin effect list
description:
INTENT (user, 2026-08-19): clean up the builtin effect picker. Remove "444 Compressor" (superseded by the newer "Compressor" and "Glue Compressor" builtins) and the plain "Delay" (superseded by "Str8 Delay", the main delay in use alongside "Space Echo"). NOT to be confused: "Str8 Delay" and "Space Echo" stay; the other compressors ("Compressor", "Glue Compressor", "OTT", "Limiter") stay.

SCOPE — hide from the picker, do not break existing projects:
- The authoritative name lists live in crates/sequencer/src/effects/mod.rs: EffectDescriptor::builtin_insert_names() and builtin_effect_names() (see the canonical-names test at mod.rs:1502 which pins both lists — it must be updated). These lists feed whatever the browser/add-effect surfaces enumerate; verify where they're consumed (browser-builtin-flattening-spec.md surfaces, ui/effects/builtin/audio-fx.lisp references "444 Compressor" at line 46, DJ-mixer/topology lists, etc.) and make the two retired names stop appearing anywhere a user picks a new effect.
- LOAD COMPAT IS REQUIRED: saved projects containing "444 Compressor" or "Delay" instances must keep loading and sounding as before. Keep builtin_444_compressor() / builtin_delay() descriptors and the by-name lookup (mod.rs:2506/2515) working for deserialization — retired means un-listable, not un-loadable. Note existing legacy aliasing precedent: canonical_builtin_insert_name maps "Dynamics"/"404 Compressor" -> "444 Compressor" and "Utility Compressor" -> "Compressor"; keep those aliases resolving (they now resolve to a hidden-but-loadable effect). project.rs:4563 constructs effect: "delay" in some path — check whether that path is a default that should now point at Str8 Delay instead.
- Special-case plumbing keyed on the retired names stays until the descriptors themselves are ever deleted (out of scope): e.g. effects_panel.rs "Delay" BPM-sync branches, app/effects.rs:1278/1315 param maps. Do not delete runtime DSP.
- Suggested mechanism: a "listed" / "retired" flag or a separate retired-names set consulted by the listing fns, rather than string-filtering at each call site — whatever fits how builtin_insert_names() is consumed.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. "444 Compressor" and "Delay" no longer appear in any add-effect/browser picker surface; "Str8 Delay", "Space Echo", "Compressor", "Glue Compressor" still do.
2. A project saved with a "444 Compressor" and a "Delay" instance loads cleanly, audio path intact, params/p-locks preserved, and the loaded instances still render their panels.
3. Legacy alias names ("Dynamics", "404 Compressor", "Utility Compressor") still canonicalize without panic.
4. The pinned name-list test(s) in effects/mod.rs updated to the new listing behavior (asserting both that retired names are absent from listings AND still loadable by name).
5. Scoped test run for the touched modules passes (per repo policy: scoped tests only, -p sequencer).

title: Light up the currently-triggered drum rack pad (grid + mini-map)
description:
INTENT (from user's Ableton screenshot, 2026-08-19): when a pad sounds, its cell lights up — in the enlarged 4x4 grid AND in the octave-overview mini-map (eseq-4b5.15, if built; degrade gracefully to grid-only if that bead isn't in yet). This is the play-feedback half of the Ableton drum rack look: you always see which pad just fired, even when it's on a non-visible page (the mini-map flash shows it).

TRIGGER SOURCES that must all light the pad:
1. Pad click in the grid (eseq.sequencer %pad-cell on-click -> eseq.drum-rack-v2/trigger-pad) — trivial, UI-side.
2. Armed-rack live keyboard: incoming note -> pad map -> member track (audio.rs rack_slot_matches_routing / the armed-rack routing path, docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md "Playability").
3. Sequenced playback: a member track's steps firing while its rack panel is visible.

MECHANISM: sources 2 and 3 fire on the audio/engine side, so this needs a host->UI reactive signal: per rack (or per member track), the recently-triggered pad note plus a trigger timestamp/epoch, exposed as a state value the lisp UI can read reactively. Look for existing precedent before inventing one — the OTT/compressor builtins push live meter data node-state->widget (builtin-ott-effect memory: "node-state→widget meter pattern"), and mixer strips already show per-track level meters; whichever engine->UI channel those use is the seam to reuse. State-value plumbing lives around crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/drum_rack.rs. Keep the signal cheap and coalesced (latest trigger per rack is enough — this is a light, not an event log) and make sure idle racks publish nothing (no per-frame ui_epoch churn; see glyph-tick-perf memory — drags/meters must not bump ui_epoch).

title: Jaki: package-ification + params/UI + seeded pitch
description: Spec §11 phases 4-6 (docs/jaki-sequencer-spec.md): package-ify the working Jaki module (module header, load path, import jaki — Jaki is the FIRST package, pilot content for eseq-mods.6); params + UI panel after the def-sequencer param contract lands (pattern String param, level, root/scale/direction, event-dot viz); seeded pitch v2 once generator seeding exists. Evaluator/macro/generator work is eseq-5k5 (unblocked).
notes:
## Macro naming under packaging -- RESOLVED, no blocker (2026-08-21)

DESIGN INTENT: requiring an explicit import to use Jaki is the intended UX,
not a regression to work around. Do not preserve the current zero-import
behavior.

Target surface:

    (import alec.jaki.surface :refer (jak))

    (jak "kit" :16
      . . - . (every 2 swap)
      -> 0)

This WORKS. `Compiler::lookup_macro` (crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/compiler.rs:416)
resolves bare macro names through the refers table, per its own doc comment
("bare names prefer the current module, then `:refer`s, then the flat table"):

    self.macros
        .get(&qualify(&self.current_module, name))
        .or_else(|| self.refers.get(name).and_then(|q| self.macros.get(q)))
        .or_else(|| self.macros.get(name))

Recording this because it is easy to talk yourself into a false blocker here.
The chain that LOOKS like one, and is not:

1. `content/scripts/sequencers/jaki-surface.lisp` is deliberately headerless
   so `jak` keeps a flat key -- its header comment says so.
2. That is because inside a declared module, `(defmacro jak ...)` interns
   QUALIFIED: compiler.rs:2328 rewrites the key to `<module>/jak`.
3. And package validation forbids headerless files: `validate_modules`
   (crates/eseqlisp/src/package.rs:244) rejects a package with "package Lisp
   files must declare a module".

Steps 1-3 are all true, and the conclusion "therefore bare `jak` cannot
survive package-ification" is FALSE -- `:refer` is exactly the mechanism that
closes it. Macros go through the same refers path as functions.

Two conditions that DO bind:

- `jak` must appear in an `(export ...)` list in the surface file.
  `Compiler::validate_refers` (compiler.rs:377) rejects `:refer` of a
  non-exported symbol with "cannot :refer non-exported symbol".
- A plain `(import alec.jaki.surface)` with NO `:refer` does not bring `jak`
  in bare (bare lookup tries `<current-module>/jak`, then an empty refers
  table, then the flat table, and misses). Callers write either
  `:refer (jak)` or the qualified `alec.jaki.surface/jak`. Pick one spelling
  for the docs and use it consistently.

So jaki-surface.lisp GAINS a module header under the package prefix and an
export list. No language change, no new bead.

## The actual risk in this bead: import on the SCHEDULER VM

`def-sequencer` auto-quotes the tick body and RE-SERIALIZES IT AS SOURCE to be
compiled in the scheduler VM (see the header comment in jaki.lisp). The open
question is whether the import -- and the refers table it populates -- reaches
that VM, or only the UI runtime where the user typed the form.

Today this is sidestepped: `crates/sequencer/src/scheduler/lookahead.rs:118`
textually sniffs the source for "jak" and injects the entire library. When
that stopgap is removed, `import` has to work there instead. PROVE THIS FIRST,
before moving any files -- it is the only thing left that could send the
design back.

Nothing has exercised it. The alec/hello smoke package proved the loader scans
and validates a package; it never imported a package module into a running VM.

## Rust stopgaps to remove (all self-labelled "pre-package")

- crates/sequencer/src/ui/natives.rs:2454 -- evals the library into the UI runtime
- crates/sequencer/src/app/effects.rs:235 -- prepends it to user scratch source
- crates/sequencer/src/scheduler/lookahead.rs:118 -- injects it into the
  scheduler VM, gated on the textual "jak" sniff
- crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/eseq/scratch_runtime.rs:248 --
  `include_str!`s both content/ files as a packaged-build fallback; stops
  making sense once Jaki lives in ~/.eseq.d/packages/

## Scope note

This bead bundles spec section 11 phases 4-6: package-ification, params + UI,
and seeded pitch. Phase 5 depends on the def-sequencer String-param contract
(spec section 9.1), which is a separate prerequisite -- confirm it exists
before assuming phases 4-6 are one unit of work. Consider splitting.
2026-08-21: Phase 4 package-ification completed in commit 499e0009. Jaki is now the validated alec/jaki factory package; authoring and scheduler VMs use explicit imports; all pre-package sniff/prepend/embed paths are removed. Phases 5 and 6 were split into child issues eseq-jo7.1 and eseq-jo7.2 because their shared def-sequencer params/telemetry/UI and generator-seeding prerequisites do not exist. Parent remains open as their rollup.

Also load_jaki_library_source now ships TWO files: jaki.lisp (module jaki) + jaki-surface.lisp (headerless, defines the bare `jaki` macro — headerless only because a module would qualify it as jaki/jaki). The package story needs an answer for unqualified macro export or the surface file needs to ride along. Replace all of it with import jaki resolution in both VMs.

title: Mono legato (single-trigger) track option per docs/legato-mono-spec.md
description:
Implement docs/legato-mono-spec.md in full (Phases 1-5; Phase 6 — rack per-slot legato and legato+glide — is explicitly deferred, do not build it). Classic mono-synth single-trigger behavior as a 'trig' track option (retrig default | legato): on mono tracks, overlapping notes change pitch/velocity without retriggering envelopes; releasing the newest key falls back to the previous held note (last-note priority) without retriggering; releasing the last key gates off.

The spec is the authoritative implementation guide and is written to be followed phase-by-phase with exact seams:
- Phase 1: GatePitch legato event — widen the timeline stride with TIMELINE_LEGATO, aux[2]=legato on GBE_NOTE_ON, gate-low fallback to a full trigger (effects/gatepitch.rs).
- Phase 2: truthful per-voice gate_open bit in the custom pool (distinguish gated from ringing-in-release).
- Phase 3: sequenced mono path — at the chord and single note-on sites, skip the gate-off and send legato NOTE_ON when mode==Legato && gate_open; new note owns the gate-off schedule.
- Phase 4: live-input held-note stack (mono_held, press order) with re-keying of the sounding ActiveKeyboardNote; NOTE this also fixes the latent bug where releasing an OLDER held key can gate off the voice a newer key is using — in Retrig mode the stack still gates which note-off may release.
- Phase 5: the setting end-to-end cloning the fts-scale groove (TrackParams atomic, ProjectTrackParams serde default 0, snapshot/undo witness, AppCommand::SetTrackMonoTrigger, TUI TP_MONO_TRIG row, Metal track-panel 'trig' dropdown + SEQ.tp-mono-trigger reactive; hidden/disabled for sampler and rack tracks).

Honor the locked decisions verbatim (aux[2] extension not a new event kind; legato-if-possible fallback semantics; legato only while gate open; same-pitch overlap is legato; v1 scope Custom/dgenlisp tracks only). Spec line numbers may have drifted slightly — verify each seam. Edge cases (§Edge cases): clear mono_held on stop/panic/poly-toggle; block-local gate-off race resolves to retrigger, never silence. Scoped tests only per repo convention.
acceptance_criteria: All four spec test categories pass: GatePitch unit test (legato mid-gate = one trigger pulse, pitch steps, gate never dips; legato after GATE_OFF = full trigger); sequenced allocator test (overlapping mono-legato steps = one trigger, no intervening GBE_GATE_OFF; gapped steps retrigger); held-stack test (on A, on B, off B returns to A with no trigger; off A gates off; buried note-off sends nothing); track-param roundtrip serialize/load + undo/redo of mono_trigger. 'trig' dropdown works in both TUI and Metal UI and is hidden/disabled on sampler and rack tracks; default behavior on existing projects is unchanged (retrig); audible audition-harness check with a slow-attack pad swells once across an overlapping phrase; Phase 6 not implemented.

title: *step* buffer transpose edits a dead slot when chord notes carry the sounding note
description:
Editing Transpose in the *step* buffer sometimes changes nothing audibly or in the piano roll — only moving the note vertically in the piano roll works. Hits recorded patterns with varied pitches, but the affected step has NO polyphony at the time.

Deterministic repro (no recording needed):
1. Toggle step 1 on. Piano roll shows the note at C4 (default transpose).
2. Set transpose +12 in the *step* buffer → piano roll correctly shows C5. (So the edit path works on a fresh step.)
3. In the piano roll, add a second note to that step (making it a chord), then DELETE the original note.
4. Select the step and set transpose to anything in the *step* buffer → piano roll unchanged; the surviving note ignores it.

Data-model context + hypothesis: a step stores its own params (transpose, velocity, duration, ...) plus 'chord notes' — lesser sub-steps that carry a subset (duration, transpose) for polyphony. After step 3 the ORIGINAL note (the step's own transpose slot) is deleted and the sounding note lives only in a chord-note slot — so the step's base transpose is a dead value. The *step* buffer, however, appears to read/write the step's base transpose (or 'the first note in the chord') rather than 'the first note that is actually ON', so edits land in the dead slot while the chord note keeps playing its own value. The recorded-pattern case is probably the same shape reached via the record path (main slot dead or displaced, chord notes the real attraction).

IMPORTANT — assess before fixing (explicit instruction): do NOT just patch the *step* buffer to chase the first live note. First map the step/chord-note data model (step base params vs chord-note params: where each is stored, which one playback voices actually read, what piano-roll delete of the 'original' note does to the base slot — does it clear a flag, zero it, or promote a chord note?) and write the assessment into this bead's notes. Then decide the right invariant. Candidate fixes to weigh: (a) normalize on delete — deleting the base note promotes a chord note into the base slot so the step's own params always describe a sounding note; (b) make the *step* buffer read/write the first SOUNDING note wherever it lives; (c) restructure so all notes are uniform and 'step params' are a view of the first note. Option (a) likely fixes every downstream consumer at once (p-locks, live step-param printing eseq-jc9, roll recording) and should be evaluated first, but the assessment decides. Whatever is chosen, check the same aliasing for velocity/duration, the '0 selected' multi-select edit path, and serialization of old projects already containing dead-base-slot steps.

Seams: *step* buffer panel + step-edit host commands (crates/sequencer/src/sequencer/state/sequencer_state/step_edit.rs, ui/host_commands/step_history.rs), piano-roll note add/delete path, step/chord-note storage (sequencer/state/ step snapshot + track pattern data).
acceptance_criteria: Assessment of the step vs chord-note model recorded in bead notes before the fix, naming which invariant was chosen and why; after the fix, the 4-step repro passes (transpose edits in the *step* buffer move the surviving note) and the *step* buffer always displays the params of a note that is actually sounding; velocity and duration verified for the same scenario; old projects containing steps in the broken state load and behave correctly; regression test covering delete-original-note-then-edit-transpose at minimum.
notes:
Assessment before fix (2026-08-18, corrected after tracing the canonical state mutation): StepPattern's active bit says the step triggers. When chord_data is empty, that trigger sounds one note from step_data Transpose/Duration/Delay. When chord_data is nonempty, it is the complete sounding-note list; playback reads chord transpose/duration/delay (duration <= 0 falls back to base Duration). Velocity and other params remain shared in step_data. The piano-roll writer rewrites this full list and mirrors chord[0].transpose plus the maximum sounding duration into base Transpose/Duration. The canonical SequencerState step-param mutation already defines the intended transpose invariant: base Transpose is the step-level chord anchor/control, and changing it shifts every stored chord pitch by the same delta. The bug is that set-step-param-history bypasses this canonical mutation and writes step_data directly, so after delete-original leaves a one-entry chord, the edit changes only the anchor while the chord note remains unchanged. Live step printing has the same bypass. Velocity does not alias because all voices read its shared base value. Duration does alias for explicit chord durations and needs the same anchor/delta treatment. The selected-count-zero path resolves to the cursor step and uses the same host command. Serialized old projects may contain the one-entry chord shape; no migration is needed if all step-param mutation uses the canonical state operation.

Invariant chosen: the existing uniform chord representation plus coherent step-level controls. A nonempty chord contains every sounding note. Base Transpose is mirrored to the first chord pitch and edits transpose the chord as a unit by delta; base Duration is mirrored to the maximum sounding duration and edits shift explicit chord durations by delta while zero duration entries continue to inherit the base fallback; Velocity remains shared. Option (a) was evaluated first and rejected: promoting only one-entry chords fixes this repro but requires normalization at every piano-roll, recording, restore, and load seam, and does not address dead aliases in polyphonic chords. A panel-only first-live-note chase was rejected because it would duplicate mutation policy. The fix routes history and live-print writes through SequencerState::set_step_param_no_publish and extends that operation to Duration, preserving one authoritative invariant. Old broken-state projects then behave on their first edit without destructive or ambiguous load migration.

Implementation: routed set-step-param-history and live step printing through the canonical no-publish SequencerState setter; renamed that API to make its publication contract explicit; extended it so Duration changes move explicit chord durations by the step-control delta while inherited zero durations keep using the base fallback. Regression drives the exact piano-roll add-second/delete-original sequence, then verifies step-panel Transpose moves the surviving piano-roll note and verifies Duration/Velocity and picker readouts. A separate print regression verifies chord-backed Transpose/Duration. Validation passed: cargo nextest run exact host regression + print regression (2/2); canonical transpose/adjust and duration-surface regressions (3/3).
close_reason: Fixed step-panel and live-print edits to preserve chord-backed sounding-note invariants; exact repro and related parameter regressions pass.

title: Live step-param printing: *step* buffer params write onto the playing step while recording
description:
Make the *step* buffer's param box (the Transpose / Velocity / Duration readout, shown per current step) a live performance recorder. Today it edits the selected step(s) while stopped. New behavior when the transport is PLAYING and RECORD is ON: the pattern plays back as already input, but the moment the user starts adjusting one of those params in the *step* buffer, the panel switches to PRINT mode — the adjusted value is written onto whatever step the playhead is currently on, and keeps printing onto each step as the playhead passes it, so sweeping a value while the pattern loops lays the gesture into the steps. Printing stops when the transport is paused/stopped or recording is toggled off (either one ends print mode); it re-arms on the next param touch during the next record+play session.

Semantics to implement (user-specified): (1) arm-on-touch — playback+record alone changes nothing; only touching a param in the *step* buffer starts printing, and only the touched param(s) print (untouched params on passing steps are left alone); (2) latch — once touched, the current value continues printing onto passing steps until pause or record-off, not just while the value is moving; (3) print target is the step under the playhead on the record-armed track (the track whose *step* buffer is focused); steps without triggers are skipped, existing trigger values are overwritten for the printed param only — p-locks vs base value should follow however live-recorded step values are stored today.

ROLL INTEGRATION (key motivator, epic eseq-767): this must compose with track roll + recording (eseq-767.3, eseq-767.10) so a performer can hold a roll while sweeping Duration/Velocity/Transpose in the *step* buffer and lay down exactly the hits they want, with the right durations, in one motion. Rolled hits recorded while print mode is armed take the currently-set printed values at record time. Duration is the star: roll records the trigger, live print gives it length.

Implementation seams: the *step* buffer panel and its param editing path (see the *step* panel edit-perf work — the panel already has focused-step reactive state and its editing goes through step-edit host commands, crates/sequencer/src/sequencer/state/sequencer_state/step_edit.rs); playhead step position is already published per track; writes should go through the normal step-edit mutation path so they are undoable (ideally coalesced per record pass, mirroring how live note recording batches) and reactive-sync cheap (don't epoch-bump per printed step — see step-buffer-edit-perf gotchas). Recording/transport state gates already exist for note recording; reuse them.

Open question for the worker (resolve, note the decision on the bead): what one printed 'pass' means for undo — one undo entry per record session per param is suggested; per-step undo entries would be unusable.
acceptance_criteria: With transport playing and record on: pattern plays untouched until a *step*-buffer param is adjusted; from that touch until pause or record-off, the touched param's current value is printed onto each trigger step as the playhead passes on the focused track, audible on the SAME pass's subsequent steps; untouched params and trigger-less steps are unaffected; pause or record-off cleanly ends printing (no stray writes); printed values persist, survive save/load, and undo restores pre-print values in a small number of steps (not one per printed step); combined with track roll + recording, rolled hits capture the live-set Duration/Velocity/Transpose so a roll+sweep lays down triggers with correct durations in one motion; regression tests cover arm-on-touch gating, latch printing across a loop wrap, stop conditions, and the roll interaction.
notes:
Undo decision (was the open question): printed writes ride the existing per-pass RecordingHistoryTransaction via mark_recording_take_changed, exactly like live note/roll recording — one 'Record take' undo entry per record pass (play+record edge to edge), shared with any notes recorded in the same pass. No per-step or per-param entries.

Implementation: ui/step_print.rs (StepPrintState latch, wrap-aware print_pass, tick_step_print in the reactive tick next to tick_roll_record). Arm path: %step-set-param branches on SEQ.playing && SEQ.recording -> seq-print-step-param native -> print-step-param host command (cursor-edit fallback if the gate raced off; skips cool-off-follow so auto-follow stays alive). Writes hit live step_data with targeted UiInvalidation::Step pushes (no ui_epoch bump). Snapshot republish per printed boundary, deferred while a roll hold has unpublished writes (double-trigger rule); rolled hits take the latched values via override_roll_hit before write-back — transpose only overrides when touched, so rolled key pitch survives a velocity/duration-only print.

Committed 1f2433f2 on main. Tests: 8 step_print unit tests, dispatch gate test in step_history, lisp routing test driving the real picker on-change. Full metal_seq suite 628 pass; 3 failures (browser/sound-palette layout) confirmed pre-existing at clean HEAD via worktree.

Follow-up 11924dd6 after user hands-on test: picker readouts were bound to the cursor step and lagged during a sweep. tick_step_print now re-asserts the latched values into fx-step-value-* every armed frame (+ reactive cycle & *step* refresh) and restores cursor-step values on disarm.
Two follow-ups from hands-on testing (commit f4c795c8):

1. AUDIBILITY ORDERING BUG (user-diagnosed): playhead atomic advances at schedule time, so write-behind stamped each step after it was scheduled — prints were only heard next loop. Fix: StepPrintOverride on SequencerState (lock-free atomics), mirrored from the latch; scheduler substitutes latched values into ResolvedStep at resolution (lookahead.rs) and at emit_roll_hit (velocity/duration only there — transpose keeps the rolled key's pitch; duration converted pattern-steps -> roll grid via step_dur/grid). Substitution mirrors what the stamped pattern plays later.

2. SEMANTICS CHANGE (user direction): hold-to-print replaces latch-until-stop. A param prints only while its picker is mouse-held; release unlatches that param (last release disarms, clears engine override, restores readouts). New on-release callback added to the number-picker widget; drum-sound dropdown routes back to the plain cursor edit (discrete pick, no release). Stop/record-off/focus-move still clean up. Known edge: typed commits (Enter) have no release, so they latch until a stop condition.
Chord-backed regression after fe138305 (commit d641fcbb): chord notes own their sounding durations (chord.durations[idx]>0 beats resolved.duration at fire time), so the engine-side substitution missed duration on recorded/chord-backed steps — heard one loop late again. Fix: lookahead computes the latch's delta over the snapshot base duration and shifts the scheduled chord's explicit per-note durations (clamped), mirroring set_step_param_no_publish's stamp. Transpose was already covered by resolved_chord_transpose's delta form; velocity has no per-note lane. RULE: any param that grows a per-note chord lane needs BOTH the stamp move (step_edit) and the audible substitution (lookahead) updated together.
close_reason: Closed

title: Filter Table: visualizer follows modulation (effective spectrum from host-sampled mod values)
description:
When frame/cutoff/resonance are modulated from the mods tab (e.g. an LFO on frame + cutoff), the Filter Table spectrum visualizer stays frozen at the knobs' base values, so the sickest use of the effect gives no visual feedback. Make the visualizer render the EFFECTIVE spectrum — the currently-modulated frame/cutoff/resonance — animating with the modulation.

Approach constraint (deliberate, from the user): do NOT touch dgen or the compiled DGenLisp engine. Implement entirely at the Rust wrapper level around the effect node: the host-side mod matrix already computes the modulation signals and writes the effective parameter values into the engine, so intercept there. Sample the effective values at a visualizer rate — e.g. ~20-30Hz, tied to the UI tick, NOT every audio block and never in the audio callback's hot path beyond a cheap atomic store — and publish them to the panel so the existing spectrum-curve rendering re-evaluates with the live values. Precedent to follow: the node-state→widget live-meter pattern used by the OTT builtin and the Compressor meter ring (engine writes a small state snapshot, widget polls/reacts per UI tick); the phaser-flanger notch viz widget is the closest visual analog. The visualizer already knows how to draw a spectrum for a given (table, frame, cutoff, resonance, phase mode) — this bead only feeds it live effective values, no DSP-side spectrum probing.

Details to handle: (a) publish effective values only when they differ from base (unmodulated = zero overhead, no redraw churn); (b) when modulation stops or the panel reopens, the display settles back to the base-value spectrum; (c) knob rings ideally also show the modulated value (like Ableton's mod indicators) but that is optional polish — the spectrum curve is the deliverable; (d) multiple simultaneous mods (frame+cutoff as in the repro) must both be reflected; (e) redraws go through the normal dirty-widget path so an idle modulated panel doesn't force full-UI repaints (see scroll-render dirty-widget-id precedent).
acceptance_criteria: With an LFO modulating frame and/or cutoff, the spectrum visualizer visibly animates in time with the audible modulation (both curve shape from frame and cutoff position), sampled at a UI-tick rate with no audio-thread work beyond a bounded lock-free state write; no dgen/DGenLisp changes; unmodulated panels have zero new per-frame cost and render exactly as today; modulation stopping returns the display to the base spectrum; a test (or capture fixture) covers the effective-value plumbing from mod-matrix output to the widget state.

title: Track roll: apply track swing to rolled hits (play swung, record straight)
description:
Found while testing the shipped track-roll core (eseq-767.1): rolled hits ignore the track's swing — roll-grid boundary emission fires on the rigid grid, so holding a pad on a swung track sounds straight and machine-gun-like, out of feel with the rest of the pattern.

Required behavior, two halves:
(1) PLAY SWUNG: while a track roll is held, each emitted hit must be offset by the track's current swing setting exactly as a real sequenced step at that grid position would be (off-beats delayed per the swing amount, same swing resolution rules the normal step scheduler uses). The roll emission path (roll-grid boundary emission via enqueue_step_event in the phase-1 code) currently bypasses whatever the sequencer clock/step pipeline does for swing — route the emitted event time through the same swing computation, keyed to the step position the hit lands on. Changing the swing knob mid-hold should affect subsequent hits.

(2) RECORD STRAIGHT — do NOT print the swing: when rolled hits are recorded into the pattern (phase 3, eseq-767.3 write-on-release), the recorded steps must be quantized to the straight roll grid with NO micro-timing offset baked in from the swing delay. The swing then applies at playback through the track's normal swing setting, so playback feels the same as the live roll did — and stays correct if the user later changes the swing amount. Recording the swung timestamps would double-apply swing on playback and freeze the current swing value into the notes.

This bead blocks eseq-767.3 so the recording slice implements the record-straight rule from the start (record the grid step index the hit was emitted for, not its swung wall-clock time).
acceptance_criteria: On a track with nonzero swing, held track-roll hits are audibly swung, matching the timing of equivalent sequenced steps on the same grid positions (verified by comparing emitted event times against the step scheduler's swing offsets in a test); with swing at 0 behavior is unchanged; recorded rolled steps land on straight grid positions with no swing-derived micro-timing, and playing the recorded pattern back through the track swing reproduces the live roll feel; changing swing after recording re-swings the recorded hits correctly (nothing printed); regression tests cover swung emission timing and straight recording.
close_reason: Roll emission now applies track swing via SnapshotSequencerClock::roll_swung_sample_time (track-local swing bucket, same delay math as the step scheduler; snapshot re-read per chunk so mid-hold swing changes take effect). Record feedback unchanged — straight boundary geometry, nothing printed. 3 regression tests (swung emission vs scheduler offsets, straight recording under swing, mid-hold knob change). Committed 2dcb7137.

title: Roll play-start reliability: arm-while-stopped + 50ms play-start hold
description: Fixes coin-flip play+press: presses while stopped arm the roll (worker clears held only on the playing->stopped transition), and with roll mode on the worker pins the scheduling frontier for 50ms after Play so racing NoteOns land before beat zero. Shipped commit 40c8967b.
notes: Follow-up e3ddf273: removed the stopped-transport live trigger entirely — roll mode owns the keys (silent while parked, rolls from line 0 on Play). The 'live note leaks ahead of the roll' caveat from this bead is gone.
close_reason: Shipped commit 40c8967b. input.rs: roll_mode presses always push NoteOn (immediate live trigger still sent while stopped, suppressed while playing per F1). worker.rs: roll.clear_all() moved to the playing->stopped transition only; ROLL_PLAY_START_HOLD=50ms pins scheduled_until_sample=rendered after Play while roll_mode on (commands/song-handover/launch deadlines keep draining each held iteration). Press before Play or within 50ms after -> line 0 sample-exact; 50-90ms -> catch-up grace (slightly late, records on the line); later -> next line. Caveat: 50ms transport start delay whenever roll mode is on; a live note held from before Play sustains under the roll (voice policy chokes it on mono kits).

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text: Follow-up 1bf5694c: the 40ms catch-up grace caused late hits mid-playback (a press just after a grid line emitted it up to 40ms behind the render head -> one-off swung first hit, 'temporary 1-step swing'). Catch-up now only claims scheduled-past-but-UNRENDERED lines (always sample-exact); rendered-past lines are missed and wait for the next boundary per F1. User rule: 'if you miss it we just go to the next'.

title: Roll play-start first-hit catch-up grace
description: Boundary catch-up grace (40ms, capped at grid/2) emits the just-missed grid line for freshly pressed roll keys — fixes play+press never recording step 1, and late presses mid-roll.
close_reason: Shipped commit c7b9205f. schedule_roll_hits gains a catch-up pass: RollState.newly_pressed (set on fresh NoteOn, pruned on NoteOff/ClearAll) is consumed each scheduling pass; the most recent grid line at/before the frontier is emitted retroactively for those notes when it is <=40ms (capped at grid/2 to avoid flams) behind the render head — usually sample-exact on time thanks to lookahead, records on the line (step 1 at play start). Emission factored into emit_roll_hit shared by catch-up + boundary scan. Tests: play-start catch (unaligned frontier 1300-block harness) + grace refusal.

title: Roll record live step-grid feedback: write hits immediately, defer snapshot publish to release

Bail path (roll off/stop/record off) publishes owed writes instead of discarding. title: Scene banks: divide the scene list into switchable banks
description:
Organize scenes into banks (Elektron-style: banks A/B/C/... each holding a fixed or flexible group of scenes), so large sets — the hundreds-of-scenes live rig described in the live-set vision — stay navigable: the session grid shows one bank at a time and the performer switches banks to reach other scenes.

NO SPEC EXISTS YET (verified 2026-08-18: nothing in docs/ or crates/sequencer/docs/; 'bank' hits there are wavetable banks and voice-pool A/B banks in rack-scene-swap-spec.md, unrelated). First deliverable is a short spec at docs/scene-banks-spec.md resolving at least: (1) bank model — fixed-size banks (e.g. 16 scenes each) vs named variable-size groups, and whether a scene belongs to exactly one bank; (2) data model + serialization — where bank membership/ordering lives in the project format and version bump strategy; (3) interaction — bank selector UI in the session view, keyboard/pad access, what happens to the playing scene when you view a different bank (viewing must not stop playback); (4) launch semantics — scene launch/quantized-launch is per-scene and must be unaffected by banking (see QUANTIZED_SCENE_LAUNCH_FOUNDATION_SPEC.md); (5) interaction with song/arrangement mode — arrangement rows reference scenes; banks should be a session-view organization layer that does not change scene identity or arrangement references; (6) editing ops — create/rename/reorder/delete banks, move scenes between banks, undo coverage.

Then implement per that spec. Key seams: scene list/grid UI in the session view, project serialization (scene collection), scene-switch paths (must remain identity-based — banking is presentation/organization, scene ids do not change). Perf note: scene-switch cost work (subtree-scene-switch, scene/clip launch perf) assumed a flat scene list; bank switching should be a pure view change with no engine work.
acceptance_criteria: docs/scene-banks-spec.md exists and answers the six design questions; scenes can be grouped into banks, with a bank selector in the session view showing one bank at a time; switching the viewed bank never interrupts playback and launching a scene from any bank behaves identically to today (including quantized launch); bank membership/order persists through save/load with existing projects loading into a sensible default (e.g. all scenes in bank A); bank edit operations (create/rename/move scene/delete) are undoable; arrangement references to scenes are unaffected by any bank operation.

title: Dropdown widgets: first click only focuses, second click opens (conditionally-shown dropdowns)
description:
UI-wide dropdown widget bug: dropdowns frequently need two clicks to open — the first click visibly focuses the dropdown (focus ring appears) but does not open the option menu; a second click opens it. Most reproducible in the 'mods' tab of a synth or effect panel (e.g. Filter Table): click the mods tab so the mod-selector view appears, then click a mod-source dropdown ('off') — it focuses but does not open. It happens in other places too, and the common thread appears to be dropdowns that are CONDITIONALLY SHOWN (rendered after a tab switch or state change), suggesting the first click is being consumed by focus acquisition / widget-identity churn instead of reaching the open-menu handler.

Diagnose in the shared dropdown widget implementation (eseqlisp UI widget layer), not per-panel: likely candidates are (a) the click handler requiring the widget to already hold focus before treating a click as open, so click #1 becomes focus-only; (b) the conditional subtree remounting the widget (new widget id after tab switch) so the first click's hit-test or interaction state targets a stale/fresh widget; (c) a focus-change event swallowing the mouse-down. Prior related work worth checking: stale focus-ring frame cache (TileFrameCacheKey must include focused_widget_id) and modal/overlay hit-testing gotchas. Fix should make a single click on an unfocused dropdown both focus AND open it, matching standard platform behavior, across all panels — not a mods-tab-specific patch.
acceptance_criteria: A single click on any dropdown — including one just revealed by a tab switch or conditional render (mods tab repro) — opens its menu on the first click while also taking focus; behavior verified in at least the mods-tab repro and one other previously-affected conditional location; a regression test at the dropdown-widget level (real-handler/capture style) covers click-on-unfocused-dropdown opening the menu; no double-open or immediate-close regression for already-focused dropdowns.
notes:
User verified commit 63f90b02 does not fix the exact effect Mods-tab flow. Reopened for production-path reproduction and corrected diagnosis.
Corrected diagnosis after reproducing the user's exact production flow with metal_seq capture: click effect 'mods' button, then first Mod 1 dropdown. Mouse Down/Up did open state under provisional widget_id 900145, but the post-click relayout settled the same stable dropdown at widget_id 900108, so the render looked up an empty state and showed only focus; click #2 used the settled ID and opened. Fixed by keying state to buffer-scoped stable_widget_id and mapping transient event/overlay IDs to that key. Exact production capture now shows the Mod 1 menu open after one click (/tmp/filter-table-mods-click-flow-fixed.png). Added ID-churn regression; dropdown suite 17/17 passes.
close_reason: Reproduced and fixed exact Mods-tab flow by preserving dropdown state across provisional-to-settled widget ID churn.

title: Drum rack v2 slice 5: rack inside a track group — BusOutput::Bus + GroupMember::Rack
description: Phase 3 of docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md (section 'Racks inside track groups'). A rack must be groupable exactly like a single track (multi-select rack + loose tracks, cmd+g). Two primitives: (1) Bus->bus output: add '#[serde(default)] pub output: BusOutput' to ProjectBusChannel — enum BusOutput { Mix, Bus(u64) }, Mix default so old projects deserialize unchanged. Today bus creation hard-wires volume_id -> bus_l_id/bus_r_id unconditionally (tui/graph.rs:1157 per spec). When a rack joins a parent group, set rack bus output = Bus(parent.bus_id) and reconnect its volume_id into the parent bus's left_id/right_id inputs (same connect/disconnect pattern as track sends at graph.rs:1500). Validate acyclicity on load even though the nesting rule guarantees max depth 2 (rack bus -> plain-group bus -> mix). (2) GroupMember enum { Track(usize), Rack(u64 GroupId) } for plain-group membership. Nesting rule: plain groups may contain tracks and racks; racks contain only member tracks; plain groups never contain plain groups; a rack belongs to at most one parent group. Fallout to implement: parent render-order block treats the rack as one entry (collapsed = single header strip; expanded = nested header+members); parent-group fx/volume apply via the bus chain with no special casing; parent-bus mute silences the rack; SOLO must walk BusOutput::Bus edges in both directions when computing the audible set (soloing parent keeps upstream rack bus audible; soloing rack keeps downstream parent bus open). Parent groups reference racks by stable GroupId so they are immune to track reindexing.
acceptance_criteria: ProjectBusChannel.output serializes with Mix default; existing projects load and route unchanged. Grouping a rack with loose tracks puts the rack in the parent group as one unit, rack bus feeding the parent bus; ungrouping restores output=Mix wiring. Parent-group volume/fx/mute affect rack audio through the chained bus. Solo on the parent keeps the rack audible and solo on the rack keeps the parent bus open (chained-bus solo test). Nesting rule enforced: no group-in-group, no rack-in-rack, rack in at most one parent. Load-time acyclicity validation rejects/repairs a cyclic bus graph. Nested render order: collapsed parent shows rack as one strip; expanded shows nested rack header+members.
close_reason: Closed

title: Drum rack v2 slice 4: choke groups as cross-track voice release
description: Phase 2 of docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md (section 'Trigger routing', choke bullet). Choke groups become a cross-track voice-release pass: when a pad in choke group g triggers (live OR sequenced), release the sounding voices of OTHER member tracks in g.
