title: Roll phase 3: record rolled hits (RollHitRecorded feedback, write-on-release)
description:
Spec: docs/rolling-core-spec.md §6, §9 phase 3. Track-roll recording only (sequence-roll gesture capture is phase 5).

Gate: recording && is_playing() && track armed — same as live-key recording.

Build:
- Scheduler side: per emitted roll hit at beat b, derive track-local (step, phase) from SnapshotTrackClockState.boundaries (no wall-clock latency comp — we are upstream of render, unlike record_beats_at_instant) and send RollHitRecorded { track, step, delay, transpose, velocity } on a feedback channel to the control thread. delay = phase within step, so grids finer than the track timebase (and triplet offsets) land as sub-step delays.
- UI thread (drain in reactive tick alongside other scheduler feedback): toggle_step if inactive + ChordData::add_note_with_timing(step, transpose, duration, delay) (data.rs:1223) + mirror Transpose/Velocity into step_data — same write-back as ui/input.rs:1600-1621 — then publish_scheduler_snapshot(). When song/take recording active, route through take_record_note (fork as ui/input.rs:1575).
- Double-trigger hazard rule (v1): batch RollHitRecorded events and perform write-back + publish on NoteOff (write-on-release). The written steps sit on the same grid the roll emitted on, so the pattern takes over seamlessly.
- F5: NO additional quantize — record_quantize is ignored for rolled hits; the roll grid already quantized them. Mixed-grid recordings from rate switches are steps with differing delays; never write timebase changes.
acceptance_criteria: With recording+playing on an armed track, each audible rolled hit is written to the pattern at the exact roll-grid line that produced it (F5, record-as-heard): step + sub-step delay from boundary geometry, no record_quantize applied, no timebase changes written; mid-roll rate switches yield mixed-grid recordings via differing delays; pattern writes happen on the control/UI thread, batched and applied on NoteOff (write-on-release) so held roll stays authoritative with no double-trigger; song/take recording routes through take_record_note. Test: recorded (step, delay) equals emitted beat; replay through the chord-delay split is sample-accurate.
close_reason: Shipped in commit 228be95e. Scheduler stamps each emitted roll hit with exact (step, sub-step delay) via new SnapshotSequencerClock::roll_record_position (same boundary geometry that scheduled it) + absolute beat + duration in track-step units, pushed on SequencerState::push_roll_recorded_hit. Control side (ui/roll_record.rs): reactive tick drains into per-key batches, note release schedules a 40ms-grace flush; write-back mirrors live-key path (toggle_step + add_note_with_timing + step_data mirrors) with record_quantize IGNORED (F5, roll grid is the quantize; finer-than-timebase hits land as chord sub-step delays). Take fork: take_record_note refactored into beats-domain take_record_note_at_beats; rolled hits route through it with quantize Off; overdub/song-authority rules match live keys. Lifecycle: roll off / stop / record off discards batches. Tests: boundary-exact feedback straight+triplet incl. 1/32-on-1/16 delays; pattern write stacking delays. Known edge: hits emitted in the ~1 worker iteration after release land before the flush grace so they are captured; recording toggled off within the 40ms grace discards that key's batch.

title: Drum rack v2 slice 3: rack arming — pad-to-key live play and per-track recording
description: Phase 2 of docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md (sections 'Arming & live play', 'Trigger routing'). Two independent arm targets: (a) Arm the rack header — live keyboard becomes pads: incoming note n -> look up pad with pad_note == n -> trigger that member track at its base pitch (transpose 0 + track base-note offset); while transport records, the hit is written into THAT member track's pattern via the existing per-track record path (record_position_at_beat quantizes against the target track's own timebase, so a 1/64-timebase hat pad and a normal kick pad each land on their own grid in one performance). (b) Arm a member track directly — identical to arming any normal track: chromatic keyboard, transpose is pitch, recording writes transposes. Arm exclusivity follows the existing single-armed-track rule; the rack header is one more armable target; arming the rack does not arm members and vice versa (spec open question: default is exclusive). Live pad routing happens where v1's ByPitch dispatch ran, but targets a member TRACK trigger — reuse the existing cross-track retarget path (rebind_midi_fx_event_to_track machinery), not the slot fan. Notes with no matching pad are ignored. Sequenced playback needs no rack routing at all.
acceptance_criteria: With the rack armed, playing note n triggers the pad_note==n member track at base pitch; unmapped notes do nothing. Recording while rack-armed writes hits into the correct member track's pattern, quantized to that member's own timebase (verify with two members at different timebases in one recording pass). Arming a member track gives normal chromatic play/record on that track alone. Rack-arm and member-arm are mutually exclusive per the single-armed rule. Live routing goes through the cross-track retarget path; no ByPitch slot matching is exercised for v2 racks.

title: Roll phase 2: sequencer rolling (window capture + clock read-remap in process_chunk)
description:
Spec: docs/rolling-core-spec.md §5, §2 F6-F10, §9 phase 2. Depends on phase 1's RollCommand plumbing (SequenceRoll commands already arrive).

Build:
- RollState.window_start: [Option<f64>; MAX_TRACKS] (beats within the track's cycle; f64 for triplet windows).
- Capture (§5.1) on SequenceRoll{on:true}, per track (v1: every track; opt-out is phase 4): grid = roll_rate.step_beats(); pos = anchored_local_beats % cycle_beats (SnapshotTrackClockState); start = pos - pos%grid, wrap % cycle_beats, then if off the 1/16 grid bump UP: ceil(start/0.25)*0.25 (F6 — never start on an off-1/32). Per-track wrap matters: independent cycle_beats (clock.rs:199).
- Remap (§5.2), THE core line: read_pos = (window_start + (live_pos_in_cycle % grid)) % cycle_beats. Seam: SnapshotSequencerClock::process_chunk (clock.rs:224) — after computing pos_in_cycle, substitute read_pos before derive_local_step (clock.rs:207). Everything downstream (boundaries, step_ends, timebase overrides, Sync steps, swing, p-lock resolution, ResolvedStep build) runs untouched on the substituted step — this is why full fidelity is free. last_local_step machinery already handles the remapped jumps.
- Release: clear all window_start; next sample reads true position. Seamless by construction — no queue clear, epoch bump, or resync. If sub-chunk exactness matters, reuse the quantized-launch chunk-split pattern (lookahead.rs:240-274, next_session_chunk).
- Rate switch (§5.3, F9): SetRate while sequence_rolling → recompute capture per track at the CURRENT live position. Same-rate re-press re-anchors iff rate.step_beats() <= 0.125 || rate.is_triplet() (stutter gesture); slower straight rates no-op. Plus per-chunk idempotent correction: re-snap window_start down to a multiple of the current grid.
- Interaction (§5.4): sequence roll is independent of held note keys; track rolls layer on top; releasing backquote ends sequence roll only.
- Lifecycle (§7): window_start survives scene/pattern switch and quantized-launch install (re-wraps % cycle_beats each chunk); ClearAll on stop/toggle-off. Resync branches (worker.rs:469-530) need no special handling.
- Playhead publication (track_playheads / track_playhead_phases, clock.rs:319): publish the READ position while rolling; add SEQ.roll-window reactive state (per-track start_beats,len_beats) for the phase-4 bracket.
acceptance_criteria: Holding backquote with roll_mode on loops each track's own pattern window (length = one roll-rate note) with full fidelity — chords, p-locks, swing, timebase overrides all replay (F10); window phase is live transport position mod grid (F7); transport free-runs and release resumes at the true position seamlessly, no queue clear/resync (F8); rate switch mid-roll re-anchors at the current position (F9), with same-key re-press re-anchoring only for 1/32 or triplet rates; window start obeys F6 snapping (down to window multiple, wrap per-track cycle, bump up onto 1/16 grid). Playheads publish the read position. Tests: window remap step sequences across cycle wrap and odd pattern lengths; re-anchor on rate switch; release-resume position.
notes: TRIGGER KEY DECISION (from the user, 2026-08-18): sequence roll is engaged by HOLDING backquote (`) — same gesture as the prior implementation in the user's other app (zequencer lineage); releasing backquote ends the sequence roll (consistent with §5.4 already in this bead). Backquote is the DEFAULT, not hard-coded: the binding must be customizable through the lisp keybinding layer. Concretely: do not bury the key match in Rust event interception only — route the sequence-roll engage/release through the lisp mode-keymap system (define-mode :on-key handlers + (mode-bind-key ...) as in crates/sequencer/ui/seq-grid-mode.lisp:80-89 and the *sequencer* keymap in ui/sequencer.lisp) or an equivalent named-command seam, so a user lisp file can rebind it to another key without touching Rust. Note the gesture is HOLD (press engages, release disengages), so the seam must deliver both key-down and key-up — if the current lisp on-key path is press-only, expose a hold-capable binding (e.g. named engage/release commands the Rust key handler resolves through the keymap) rather than degrading to a toggle. Acceptance addition: default backquote hold engages/releases sequence roll; rebinding via lisp keybinding code moves the gesture to the new key with no Rust change; this also resolves the epic's open question #1 (toggle key TBD) for the sequence-roll gesture.
close_reason: Replaced the bespoke comma interception with a true global Lisp bind-key. This follows the editor's normal priority (focused widgets first, then global binding), works regardless of active tile, and is covered end-to-end by pressing comma on the transport-focused production editor and asserting toggle-roll-mode dispatch.

title: Drum rack v2 slice 2: grid/mixer UI — header row + full member track rows
description: Phase 1 UI of docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md (section 'UI'). Grid view renders the rack as a header row plus full member rows. Header row: arm (pad-play mode target — the control only; behavior lands in the pad-play slice), mute/solo (drive the backing bus), name, volume (bus fader), collapse folding members like the mixer group collapse. Member rows are EXACTLY the normal track UI — same widget path, not a miniature: timebase p-locks, pattern length, accumulator, expand-to-step-editor all work because members are real tracks. Follow the each-based widget generation convention (never map) per project lisp-UI rules. Relevant areas: crates/sequencer/ui/ lisp layouts, crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/rack_panel.rs and track_and_mixer.rs, reactive_sync.rs.

Each member row is the standard track row widget: step editor expansion, pattern length, timebase p-locks, and accumulator all function on a pad's member track. title: Drum rack v2 slice 1: rack data model on track groups + lazy pads + audio routing
description: Phase 1 of docs/drum-rack-v2-spec.md (sections 'Core model', 'Data model', 'Audio / fx routing', 'Track budget'). Extend the track-group record instead of a parallel container: add rack: Option<ProjectRackConfig> to ProjectTrackGroup; ProjectRackConfig { pads: Vec<ProjectRackPad>, choke_groups: Vec<Option<u8>> }; ProjectRackPad { pad_note: i32, member: usize } (member = index into group.members). Enforce invariants: pad.member points at a live member of the same group; a member backs at most one pad (pad-less members legal); pad_note unique within a rack; deleting a member track removes its pad; deleting the group deletes the rack config; pads survive track reindex-on-delete because they reference positions in members. Lazy pads: creating a drum rack creates group + bus and ZERO member tracks; a pad claims a track only when a sound is dropped on it. Retarget creation entry points: add_sampler_drum_rack_track becomes 'create rack group'; pad-fill helpers become 'create member track + assign pad'. Every member's output = Bus(group.bus_id); the backing bus's effect chain is the rack fx chain; header volume fader = bus fader. No new per-track state — TrackParams/PatternState unchanged. Members sequence like ordinary tracks with no rack routing in the audio hot path. Key files: crates/sequencer/src/project.rs (serialization), crates/sequencer/src/app/graph/bus_routing.rs, track-group code per crates/sequencer/docs/track-groups-spec.md.
acceptance_criteria: ProjectTrackGroup carries Option<ProjectRackConfig> with serde default; projects round-trip through save/load with pads + choke_groups intact and old projects load unchanged. Creating a drum rack yields a group + backing bus and zero member tracks. Dropping a sound on an empty pad creates a member track wired output->group bus and records the pad_note->member mapping. Invariants (unique pad_note, member-backs-one-pad, pad removal on member delete, group delete removes rack config) enforced and covered by tests, including track reindex-on-delete keeping pads pointing at the right members. Sequenced playback of member patterns works with no transpose->slot matching involved.
close_reason: Rack config on ProjectTrackGroup (serde default), lazy pads, invariants enforced on load/delete/attach, member output->group bus. Commit 4119ded1. Note: v1 add_sampler_drum_rack_track intentionally left in place (UI is slice 2, v1 deletion is slice 7); creation/pad-assign go through new create_drum_rack_recorded / attach_track_to_group APIs.

title: Roll phase 1: track rolling core (RollCommand channel, grid emission, key interception)
description:
Spec: docs/rolling-core-spec.md §3, §4, §7, §9 phase 1. Audible track rolling, no recording yet.

Build:
- TransportState atomics (sequencer/state/core.rs:59, next to record_quantize/metronome_enabled): roll_mode: AtomicBool, roll_rate: AtomicU32 (Timebase discriminant), sequence_rolling: AtomicBool.
- RollCommand channel (NoteOn/NoteOff{track,transpose}, SetRate{Timebase}, SequenceRoll{on}, ClearAll) drained at top of every scheduler worker iteration, next to drain_live_keyboard_inputs (worker.rs:~285). Atomics = current state; channel = ordering.
- Scheduler-side RollState on SchedulerLookaheadState (lookahead.rs:8): held: [SmallSet<i32>; MAX_TRACKS] (set semantics — dup presses collapse), generation: u64. Do NOT store rate or start-time (F2/F7).
- Emission: each schedule_playing_lookahead chunk, for every roll boundary k*grid_beats (grid = roll_rate.step_beats(), reuse Timebase from sequencer/data.rs:168) inside [chunk_start, chunk_end), for every track with non-empty held: build ResolvedStep from track defaults (one note per held transpose = chord), push via enqueue_step_event (enqueue.rs:179) as normal ResolvedTrigger — no new event kinds. Boundary math per launch_deadline convention (quantized_launch.rs:603) or GridBoundaryClock (runtime/grid_clock.rs).
- Cancel: commands drained before lookahead extension; horizon (scheduler_block_size*4 samples) is the cancel window; at most one trailing enqueued hit may sound (exact generation-stamp cancel is phase 4).
- Input interception at ui/event_loop.rs:700 BEFORE editor.handle_key (editor drops Release events): when roll_mode on and key routes to live keyboard — Press → RollCommand::NoteOn per armed track (no immediate KeyboardTrigger, F1); Release → NoteOff + normal audio note-off (envelope release); number keys 1-8 unmodified → SetRate + atomic, do not reach editor; backquote → SequenceRoll{on} key-repeat-deduped (consumed here even though sequence roll logic is phase 2); z/x octave shift unchanged; held_notes bookkeeping unchanged. roll_mode off = zero behavior change.
- Lifecycle (§7): ClearAll on roll-mode toggle-off and transport stop (clear held, bump generation). Roll only runs with transport playing (§4.3).
- Minimal UI: transport-bar Roll toggle + rate display reactive on the atomics (transport.lisp:~709); toggle key TBD (original used ' — pick chord or UI-only given editor key pressure, note the choice).
acceptance_criteria: Holding a note key on an armed track with roll_mode on retriggers on the roll grid, transport-locked; first hit waits for the next boundary (F1, no hit on keydown); rate keys 1-8 switch rate mid-hold instantly (F2); release cancels all hits not yet in the lookahead horizon (F3); rolled hits use track default velocity + held transpose (F4); pattern playback layers underneath (no suppression); roll mode off / transport stop clears everything. Tests drive schedule_playing_lookahead directly (scheduler/tests.rs) asserting boundary-exact emission per rate incl. triplets.
notes: Coordination note (2026-08-18): the sequence-roll trigger is now decided — hold backquote (`), customizable via the lisp keybinding layer (see eseq-767.2 notes). This bead's key-interception work at event_loop.rs:700 should therefore treat raw-key matches as defaults resolved through a rebindable seam (named commands / mode keymap), not hard-coded literals, so phase 2 can reuse the same mechanism. The epic-level 'roll-mode toggle key TBD' ambiguity is resolved for the sequence-roll gesture; the track-roll rate keys remain default choices with the same rebindability expectation.
close_reason: Shipped in commit ae598cc0. TransportState roll atomics + RollCommand channel (drained in worker next to drain_live_keyboard_inputs), scheduler RollState (held sets + generation, no rate/start-time per F2/F7), boundary-exact emission via enqueue_step_event in [chunk_start,chunk_end) on the absolute grid, event_loop/input interception (F1 no-hit-on-keydown, rate keys 1-8, backquote consumed+deduped, z/x unchanged), ClearAll on toggle-off + transport stop, transport-bar ROLL toggle + rate display. Toggle key decision: UI-only host command 'toggle-roll-mode' (no editor key claimed — key pressure; revisit if a chord frees up). 8 new scheduler tests incl. triplets, mid-hold rate switch, note-off cancel, chord collapse. Note: the uncommitted in-flight track-send test scheduler_events_apply_track_send_plock_then_restore_zero_baseline needed the run_with_scheduler_stack wrapper (stack overflow); fixed in the working tree but left uncommitted with that feature's diff.

title: Drum Rack v2: rack as play surface over real tracks

title: Rolling: track roll + sequencer roll (rolling-core-spec)
description:
Implement the Roll performance feature per docs/rolling-core-spec.md (rev 1, authoritative — supersedes docs/sequencer-roll-spec.md). Two coupled gestures gated by one Roll mode toggle:

1) TRACK ROLLING — while Roll mode is on, holding a note key on an armed track retriggers the sound at the current roll rate (1/4..1/32, straight or triplet, keys 1-8), locked to the global transport grid; every audible hit is recordable exactly where it sounded (MPC note-repeat/roll feel).

2) SEQUENCER ROLLING — holding the sequence-roll key (backquote) makes each track loop a window of its own pattern (window = one roll-rate note), anchored where triggered, while the transport free-runs underneath; release resumes exactly at the true position (beat-repeat at sequence level).

Design is reverse-engineered from the zequencer/visual-sampler browser DAW; all needed behavior is captured in the spec's feel invariants F1-F10 (§2) — workers do NOT need the zequencer repo. Key insight: sequencer rolling is a CLOCK READ-REMAP (read_pos = (window_start + live_pos % grid) % cycle_beats) at the SnapshotSequencerClock::process_chunk seam — replaying real steps through the real pipeline gives full fidelity (chords, p-locks, swing) for free (F10, §5.2, §10).

Child beads follow the spec's §9 phases: 1 track-rolling core, 2 sequencer rolling, 3 recording, 4 polish, 5 song/take capture. No serialization; rolling is pure performance state (§7).

title: Conv reverb: arbitrary IR length (per-instance K, no fixed cap)
description:
Today the IR is hard-capped at K=128 partitions of HOP=512 → 65536 samples ≈ 1.49s @ 44.1k (constants in crates/sequencer/src/effects/conv_reverb.rs, tensor shapes [128 1024] in conv_reverb_dsp.lisp). Requirement: the user can set the IR length to anything — most convolution reverbs let you go hard; CPU cost is the user's problem, not a reason to cap. Practical shape: a generous soft ceiling (e.g. 30s ≈ K=2584 @ 44.1k) purely to bound memory/typo damage, clamped to the source region length.

Approach — per-instance K: the builtin already compiles its dgenlisp source fresh per instance (app/effects.rs builtin add path), so make K a template value instead of a constant. Compute K = ceil(region_samples / HOP) at IR-apply time (round up to a small granularity, e.g. multiples of 32, to avoid recompiling on tiny length nudges), substitute the [K 1024] tensor shapes into conv_reverb_dsp.lisp (string template or a @K binding if dgenlisp supports it), and recompile+swap the node when K changes. The recompile is the same machinery as instance creation but must preserve mix/gain values, p-locks, routing, PDC, and node identity (or handle rebinding cleanly — see the instrument-swap rebind-not-reload precedent). Debounce: only recompile on committed length changes (knob release), and only when the rounded K actually differs.

Mechanical footprint: N/HOP unchanged; K, IR_LEN, PART_LEN become per-instance values (functions of K) rather than consts; StereoIrSlots/apply_ir_to_node are already length-agnostic (whole-tensor writes) but prep must produce K-matched block lengths; the ESEQIR01 cache header already stores K and rejects mismatches — include K in the cache key so shaped/sized variants cache independently. Memory is ~16KB per partition across the four tensors (K=2584 ≈ 41MB/instance) — acceptable, but surface the number in the panel if cheap. Measure and record CPU at K=256/512/1024/2584 with the C-harness or cost_probes approach so the UI can honestly hint at cost; do NOT use the measurements to justify a lower cap.

Update the LENGTH control's host-exposed max (eseq-hsk.2 reads it) to the soft ceiling, and its effective max to min(ceiling, source region length).
acceptance_criteria: Setting length to e.g. 8s on a long sample yields a genuinely 8s tail (delta-input render, measured RT tail); K only changes on committed length edits crossing a granularity boundary, and the recompile preserves mix/gain values, p-locks, and routing; default instances (bundled 1.49s IR) compile with K=128 and show no CPU/behavior regression; project save/reload restores length and recompiles to the right K; CPU numbers at several K recorded in bead notes; conv_reverb tests updated for non-const K pass

title: Restore Filter Table dropdowns in instrument-rack slot effect chains
description:
## Problem
When the Filter Table effect is added to the effect chain of an instrument-rack slot, its UI omits the Filterable and Spectral vs Min-Phase dropdown controls. These controls are present when the effect is hosted in the normal effect-chain context, so the rack-slot host path is rendering an incomplete effect UI.

## Scope
Trace the effect UI construction, state/prop binding, and layout path used for instrument-rack slot effect chains. Make the Filter Table UI expose the same functional dropdown controls in that host context without duplicating or special-casing the effect UI. Verify that reactive props required by the dropdowns are accepted through every wrapper and that the controls receive finite, visible layout geometry.

## Acceptance criteria
- A Filter Table effect hosted in an instrument-rack slot effect chain displays both the Filterable dropdown and the Spectral vs Min-Phase dropdown.
- Both dropdowns show current effect state and update the correct rack-slot effect instance.
- The normal track/effect-chain Filter Table UI continues to work.
- A regression test constructs the rack-slot host context and verifies the functional dropdown widgets/bindings and finite, nonzero visible geometry; it must not depend on cosmetic headings or captions.
- If practical on the development platform, inspect a headless `metal_seq capture` of the rack-slot effect panel to verify clipping, spacing, and visibility.
acceptance_criteria:
- Instrument-rack slot Filter Table UIs visibly render the Filterable and Spectral vs Min-Phase dropdowns.
- Dropdown state and edits target the correct effect instance.
- Regression coverage verifies widget bindings and finite, nonzero layout in the rack-slot context.
- Existing non-rack Filter Table UI behavior remains intact.
notes: Restored rack-slot Filter Table preset and engine dropdowns using the shared effect UI. Added rack-slot table metadata, rack-aware source/engine command routing with recorded undoable mutations, preservation of per-pattern rack values during engine recompilation, layout/targeting regression coverage, and a production capture fixture. Validation: RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo nextest run -p sequencer -E 'test(/metal_seq_filter_table_(rack_slot_dropdowns_are_visible_and_target_the_slot_effect|panel_has_visible_nonzero_content)$/)' (2 passed); production metal_seq capture inspected at /tmp/metal-seq-rack-filter-table-panel.png.
close_reason: Implemented and validated rack-slot Filter Table dropdown rendering, bindings, routing, and visible layout.

title: D: lookahead dynamics should declare a constant latency
description:
The limiter and compressor delay the audio path on purpose while the detector
runs undelayed -- that is what lookahead IS -- and both report zero.

  limiter.rs:84-87,113-118: lookahead 0-20ms, DEFAULT 3ms, read_pos =
    write_pos - lookahead_samples. So the default instance delays audio and
    claims not to.
  compressor.rs:203-212: lookahead_samples(mode) -> 0 / 1 / 10 ms;
    :393-405 documents that dry and wet alike are delayed.
  Params exposed to the user at effects/mod.rs:6345-6348 and :6670-6678.

The awkward part: this latency depends on a PARAM, so a knob drag would
re-plan every frame and move every pad in the graph continuously.

Mechanically it is easy to support -- latency_samples would take a param-
reader closure, and all three call sites already build exactly that closure
for the bypass check (app/graph/latency.rs:220-222, 240-243, 267-276) -- plus
a sample rate to convert ms to samples, which the plan does not thread today.

But the RECOMMENDED shape is to avoid param-dependent latency entirely:
have both effects declare a CONSTANT latency and always delay internally by
that amount, using the lookahead param only to position the detector within
the buffer. Latency stops depending on a knob, nothing re-plans, nothing
clicks.

Cost is always paying the declared latency. 20ms is a lot to always pay for
the limiter, so quantize its lookahead to a few discrete modes like the
compressor already has and declare the max. Set-and-forget in practice, and
with the crossfade from eseq-lat.5 a mode change is inaudible anyway.

Decide between the two shapes before implementing.

title: C: crossfade pdc_delay across delay changes
description:
pdc_delay reads its delay fresh each block and jumps the read pointer with no
ramp (effects/pdc_delay.rs:77-110). The ring is kept warm so a change replays
real history rather than a burst of zeros (:86-97, test at :230), which
softens it -- but it is still a hard splice, and because a re-plan moves every
pad at once, the splice hits every branch in the graph simultaneously.

This already fires today:
- toggling the Filter Table engine (spectral 2048 <-> causal 0)
- toggling bypass on a latent slot, since latency is now enabled-aware
  (fixed in 3e95c1c7; correct -- a 46ms misalignment is far worse than one
  click -- but it added a second trigger)

and it is a hard prerequisite for any effect whose latency varies at runtime
(eseq-lat.5).

Work: ramp across delay changes -- crossfade old and new read positions over
a short window (a few ms) rather than switching instantly. Must stay
allocation-free on the audio thread; the ring is already preallocated at
PDC_MAX_DELAY_SAMPLES (:19,:24).

Keep the existing guarantees: zero delay stays a bit-exact memcpy passthrough
(test :177) and steady-state delay stays sample-exact (tests :187,:208).
notes: Prerequisite for eseq-lat.6 (runtime-variable latency on the lookahead dynamics).

title: B2: conv reverb blends an undelayed dry against a late wet
description:
Audible today, independent of PDC and of everything else in this epic.

conv_reverb_dsp.lisp:42-43 does

    (out (mix inL wetL wet-amt) 1 @name left)

where inL is the RAW input and wetL came through (buffer inL 512 512) +
overlap-add (:25,:30). So the dry and wet arms of the crossfade are 512
samples apart and comb-filter each other on every instance -- worst at 50%
mix, which is where a reverb usually sits.

Filter Table solves the same problem by routing its dry path through the
identical STFT so both arms share the latency (filter_table_dsp_spectral.lisp:
2-3,28-33 -- "the dry path traverses the same STFT so mix stays aligned").
Conv reverb does not need the full round trip; delaying dry by 512 directly
is enough and cheaper.

Verify with the C harness method rather than by ear: a flat/impulse IR at
50% mix should reconstruct the input, not a comb.
close_reason: Fixed: dry arm now delayed by the wet path's measured 511-sample (hop-1) latency in conv_reverb_dsp.lisp; C-harness regression test bundled_dsp_dry_arm_matches_wet_hop_latency verifies delta-IR reconstruction at 0/50/100% mix. Committed 40368502.

title: Make track bus sends pattern-scoped and p-lockable
description:
## Problem
Track bus send values currently remain at the most recently edited value when switching scenes/patterns. For example, raising a track send in scene 2 and returning to scene 1 leaves the scene-2 send active until the user touches the send knob. This leaks state across patterns and can cause unexpected audio.

## Scope
Integrate track bus send parameters with the same pattern-state and parameter-lock mechanisms used by other track parameters. Each pattern must own its track send baseline values, scene/pattern changes must apply them immediately, and individual steps must be able to p-lock sends without permanently overwriting the pattern baseline. Ensure the behavior is preserved through the relevant project save/load and editing flows.

## Acceptance criteria
- A track send value edited in one pattern/scene is stored for that pattern and does not alter another pattern's send value.
- Switching from a scene with a high send back to a scene with a lower send restores/applies the destination pattern's value without requiring knob interaction.
- Track send parameters are available as step parameter-lock targets.
- A send p-lock applies at the intended step and returns to the pattern baseline according to normal p-lock semantics.
- Save/load preserves pattern-scoped send values and send p-locks.
- Regression tests cover scene/pattern switching and send p-lock application.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pattern/scene switching immediately restores each destination pattern's track send values.
- Track sends can be parameter-locked per step and return to the pattern baseline afterward.
- Save/load preserves both pattern send baselines and send p-locks.
- Automated regression coverage protects these behaviors.
notes: Implemented pattern-owned dynamic bus-send baselines and per-step BusId-keyed p-lock storage across live state, pattern pools, step copy/history, scheduler snapshots, and project serialization. Scene/project restore reapplies bus-send graph edges immediately; zero-baseline edges remain addressable for realtime p-lock dispatch. UI selected-step send edits create p-locks and projected rows can be edited/cleared. Follow-ups eseq-x3q and eseq-ccy fixed selection-aware knob bindings, including transport/full-refresh overwrite. Validation includes cargo check -p sequencer --tests plus exact scene recall, serialization, scheduler event, and Metal UI binding regressions.
close_reason: Implemented and validated pattern-scoped, p-lockable track bus sends with save/load and regression coverage.

title: Make Filter Table engine selector a dropdown

title: Filter Table STFT goes silent when a render block is split off the 512-sample hop grid
description: Found while fixing the preset probe harness: rendering the compiled Filter Table DSP with a block split at a non-hop-aligned boundary (the offline harness splits blocks at param-event frames) makes the STFT path stop emitting entirely from that point on. The old preset audio probes were silent after ~0.3s partly because of this. Workaround in generate_filter_tables: sweep events snapped to the 512-sample block grid. The engine uses fixed block sizes so live playback is likely unaffected, but any harness/offline path with arbitrary block splits hits it — and it may indicate hop-phase state that desynchronizes on partial blocks. Worth a root-cause look in the generated OLA/hop logic.

title: Wire rack-slot chain PDC pads at the track voice sum
description: The latency planner (app/graph/latency.rs) computes per-rack-slot chain latencies and the required alignment pads at the track voice sum, but the pad nodes are not yet wired there — rack rebuilds are owned by the rack-rebuild signature machinery and need pdc nodes threaded through it. Marker RACK_SLOT_JOIN_UNCOMPENSATED in code; spec Known-limits section documents it. Until wired, parallel rack slots with differing chain latencies sum out of phase. Also consider raising/streaming the 16383-sample pad clamp.
notes: Part of the eseq-lat latency epic (Phase E): the last structurally uncompensated join point. The other gaps are eseq-lat.7 (sidechain/meter taps read pre-PDC).

title: Compiled DGen effect dylib renders are not reentrant for same-source concurrent use
description: Concurrent renders of the same DSP source share one cached dylib image (same cache key -> same dlopen handle) and the compiled code is not reentrant, so two parallel renders corrupt each other. Found via mutually racy bundled-DSP render tests in effects/filter_table.rs (pre-existing mix test failed when a new render test ran beside it; each passes alone). Stopgap: the three render tests in that module now serialize through a shared render_lock(). Underlying non-reentrancy affects any future same-source concurrent render in tests or host.
notes: Second manifestation: the app::effects live-graph e2e tests (filter_table_asset_loads..., filter_table_editor_session...) execute the same cached effect dylib via the real engine and raced the offline render tests — bundled_dsp_low_cutoff_resample_keeps_narrow_features failed intermittently (gain 4.73 vs bound). Stopgap extended: both live-graph tests now hold filter_table::tests::render_lock() for the whole session; suite stable across 4 consecutive parallel runs.

title: Add a nondestructive Filter Table response editor
description: Add an editor centered on the representation the effect actually consumes: frame-indexed frequency-response magnitudes. Provide log-frequency/dB editing, keyframes, table overview, cutoff-reference marker, live audition, and nondestructive operations. A source-waveform view may support import diagnostics but should remain secondary.
design: Use a document/command model independent of widgets so undo, serialization, validation, and headless tests are first-class. Edit in dB with a defined floor while preserving a validated linear runtime representation. Do not clone a general wavetable editor when the product semantics are filter-response editing.
acceptance_criteria: Users can create, load, edit, audition, save, and restore a table; editing supports draw and parametric nodes, frame insert/duplicate/delete/reorder, keyframe interpolation, spectral and temporal smoothing, shift/stretch/tilt/normalize, and undo/redo; displayed response matches the runtime response within defined tolerance; visible editor content has finite nonzero layout and receives a production Metal capture review.

Document/command model in effects/filter_table_editor.rs: EditorDoc = dB base grid (floor -80/ceil +24, 1-256 frames) + ordered EditOp history + undo cursor; bake() resamples to 64x1025 via the same deterministic mapping as import then validates linear — displayed == runtime by construction. Ops: draw, parametric peak/notch/LP/HP/tilt on octave axis about harmonic 24 (transpose with cutoff), frame ins/dup/del/move, keyframe interpolation, spectral/temporal smoothing, shift/stretch/tilt/normalize; drag coalescing. Document serializes into .fltab recipe field w/ tamper-safe replay — saved edits reopen with full history. Host: single EditorSession on track/bus nodes; previews write node tensor + published bank without touching prepared-table registries; save writes user filter-tables/*.fltab through recorded-mutation (app-undoable); dirty-close rolls back. UI: EDIT button swaps panel for toolbar + response-curve-editor surface (cutoff-reference pin) + NODE/FRAME/TABLE toolbars; viewer doubles as overview with selected-frame highlight. title: Build original Filter Table preset generator and factory library
description: Build a deterministic offline authoring/generation tool and an original factory preset library designed directly in spectral-magnitude space. Create coherent morph families rather than one table that jumps between unrelated responses. Candidate families include pass/notch motion, formants, harmonic and inharmonic combs, phaser banks, tilt/color, harmonic masks, and controlled textures.
design: Author response curves in dB on a musically meaningful frequency/harmonic coordinate, convert to linear magnitudes only for runtime, and make interpolation/floor/normalization policies explicit. Keep each preset a coherent spectral trajectory. Use conventional DSP equations and independently chosen parameters, with external products only as qualitative benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: The generator deterministically produces validated assets plus response visualizations and audio probes; factory presets are original and carry project-compatible licensing/metadata; each table has smooth intentional frame motion and sensible cutoff-reference behavior; listening validation covers noise, impulse, saw, drums, and broadband material; no third-party factory data is shipped or transformed into distributable assets.

Presets in assets/filter-tables/: glide-low, glide-high, band-flight, notch-drift, vowel-drift, comb-bloom, glass-comb, phase-flower, tilt-horizon, odd-even, dust-veil. Probes (PPM heatmap + 2 WAVs each through real DSP) in session scratchpad ft-presets/ — LISTENING SIGN-OFF OPEN. Verified: filter_table 40/40 incl. determinism, smoothness bounds, on-disk-matches-recipe, cutoff transposition through compiled DSP; cargo check --lib --bins clean. title: Define a versioned Filter Table asset and preset format
description: Create a durable, original asset model for authored/imported Filter Tables instead of treating every table as an ephemeral decoded sample. Store validated dimensions, reference harmonic/frequency semantics, magnitude domain/floor, metadata, default controls, and compact baked magnitude data with explicit format versioning.
design: Use human-readable versioned metadata plus compact lossless binary magnitude storage. Runtime consumes baked linear magnitudes; authoring may use dB and optional recipe metadata. Treat reference harmonic as asset metadata rather than an undocumented global constant where practical.
acceptance_criteria: Assets round-trip without numerical or metadata loss; malformed dimensions/non-finite values/version mismatches are rejected with actionable errors; projects reference assets deterministically and remain replayable through undo/redo and reload; the format supports generated presets, imported tables, and future editor documents without embedding proprietary content.
close_reason: Versioned .fltab asset format shipped (uncommitted, feature/filter-table). Container v1: FLTABLE magic + u32 header len + JSON metadata header + 64x1025 LE f32 linear magnitudes, bit-exact round-trip. Metadata: format_version, name, frames/bins, per-asset reference_harmonic (default 24; non-24 rejected with actionable error until DSP reads it as a param — documented), magnitude_floor, provenance (analysis_mode, source_name), default_controls, opaque dB recipe field reserved for .7/.8. Actionable rejects: bad magic, truncation, newer/zero version, dim mismatch, non-finite/negative values, unsupported harmonic; write_asset refuses inconsistent metadata. Refs persist as fltab:<stem>, resolved via user filter-tables/ then bundled assets/filter-tables/; apply path loads baked bank with no analysis; undo/redo rides existing memento. Verified: filter_table 31, app::effects 22, project 36, app::edit 51 pass; cargo check clean. Deferred: DSP-param reference harmonic, export-current-table UI, .fltab browser drag-drop (host command path works).

title: Smooth and anti-alias Filter Table response automation
description: Filter Table V1 rebuilds its response once per 512-sample hop and directly resamples the magnitude curve when cutoff closes. Add response-to-response interpolation/crossfading for zipper-free automation and a principled anti-alias strategy for downward cutoff shifts; preserve hop-gated tensor execution.
notes: Listening feedback describes current direct magnitude-mask sound as AI stem-separation-like. Beyond response zippering/aliasing, investigate perceptually smoother table preprocessing/interpolation (frequency smoothing or envelope extraction) so imported broadband material does not reproduce noisy frame-local spectral masks.
close_reason: Shipped on feature/filter-table (uncommitted). (1) Response smoothing: frame/cutoff/resonance pass a per-sample scalar one-pole (SMOOTH-MS=30ms, self-seeding) before hop-hold; with 4x OLA crossfade, hop responses now change near-continuously — zipper test shows 0.55x jerk vs disabled (fail-before via SMOOTH-MS 0); mix stays sample-rate. (2) Cutoff anti-aliasing: rows pre-band-limited by a 4-level a-trous dilated 3-tap cascade, blending the two levels bracketing log2(resample stride); stride<=1 exactly neutral; narrow one-bin feature survives stride-8 cutoff (naive path drops it — fail-before via AA-MAX-LEVEL 0). (3) Audio-mode perceptual smoothing: 1/6-octave constant-Q box average, re-peak-normalized, DC untouched; other modes exact. CPU verified in generated C: all 1025-wide loops stay inside hop gate; only 3 scalar one-poles added per-sample. Harness: EffectRenderOptions gained param_events + input_tones, report exposes samples. Verified: filter_table 35/35, app::effects 22, effects 251, graph 69; cargo check clean; 2 lisp_host failures are pre-existing/environment-dependent per project memory. Deferred: EQ8 overlay does not mirror the stride band-limit below ~517Hz (visual only — align in eseq-dtx.8); 30ms/1-6-octave defaults pending listening.

title: Expose configurable Patch Learn CMA-ES pipelines
description: Upgrade the *patch-learn* configure and progress interface to support the three agreed training presets: legacy Adam with basin check, CMA-ES search only, and CMA-ES search with batched shortlist refinement plus winner training. Represent optimizer configuration as validated typed host data, expose controls for epochs and every supported CMA setting (generations, population/auto, sigma, RNG seed, forward batch/auto, local fallback epochs, shortlist count, refinement epochs/mode, and final winner epochs), persist the semantic request, generate explicit CLI flags, and render multistage progress honestly when stages do not emit incremental events.

CMA presets initialize to: search-only = 12 generations/automatic population/no Adam; search+training = 12 generations/automatic population/8 candidates/5 batched refine epochs/300 winner epochs/no local fallback. Users may tune every value. Do not fabricate CMA generation or batched-refinement progress before the trainer emits corresponding protocol events.
acceptance_criteria: Patch Learn can launch each of the three presets; all optimizer values are editable and validated; request.json records the typed configuration and argv contains explicit CMA enable/disable flags; legacy behavior remains the default; training UI identifies CMA, local, refinement, and final stages without labeling generations as epochs; targeted host and layout tests pass.

title: Productize tensor-batched CMA-ES synth fitting in dgenlisp train
description: Implement a product-facing gradient-free global-search mode for dgenlisp train using canonical full-covariance CMA-ES over normalized transformed parameter coordinates. Evaluate populations through the generic tensor-lane Lisp forward path, preserve the user's local seed outcome, and optionally run scalar Adam on the best diverse global candidates as final polish. Motivation: the real 65,536-frame Korg1 patch evaluated and independently scored 64 candidates in 1.44 s, while five B=16 Adam steps took 45.55 s; forward search supports the complete phasor+SVF topology. Follow the linked DGen spec.
design: Canonical Hansen CMA-ES in Float64 on CPU; reflected [0,1] bounds; deterministic anchors/RNG; generic fixed-shape tensor population renders; independent vDSP MR-STFT fitness; generation checkpoints and resumable state; top-K scalar Adam continuation; explicit local-seed versus global result reporting. Compare against seeded+midpoint, one-shot multistart, and short batched Adam at equal wall-clock budgets.
acceptance_criteria: CMA math passes deterministic sphere and rotated-ellipsoid tests; Korg1 completes >=10 generations from unmodified lowered Lisp; fitness is invariant to lane position/chunking and recurrent state is lane-isolated; cma_es_report.json records generation trace/timings/state/local-vs-global outcomes; optional Adam never replaces a better pre-Adam independently scored candidate; equal-wall-clock known-config benchmarks across multiple patches/seeds document median score, failure rate, and product-default recommendation.

Proposed product is CMA-ES for global basin discovery with optional scalar Adam cherry-on-top, preserving local seed versus global outcomes.

title: Explore tensor-batched multistart training for dgenlisp train
description: Replace or augment dgenlisp train's single deterministic midpoint basin-check with tensor-lane batched multistart search/refinement, especially for short direction-training jobs. Eseq's recent tensor-enablement work may make arbitrary complicated patches much easier to lift into a candidate batch than earlier estimates suggested. Revisit the SynthID results: the 23,552-candidate B=256 forward basin search achieved ~13.6 ms/candidate but raw initial score weakly predicted the result after Adam; later B=64-72 independent batched Adam trajectories were genuinely useful (~7-9x cheaper per lane-step and escaped basins). The experiment should therefore rank starts after a short optimization horizon, not merely by initial forward loss. Candidate policy: always retain the supplied seed and midpoint; add bounded stratified/random starts and seed jitters; evaluate cheaply; keep a diverse 32-64 lane set; run 20-50 independent batched Adam steps; then continue the seed plus the best few lanes and report local-seed versus global-candidate outcomes. Preserve the semantic distinction between direction finding around the user's seed and finding the globally best fit. Investigate lane-isolated state/history, per-lane spectral losses, memory scaling, and which remaining Lisp ops are not tensor-enabled. Coordinate with the DGen temporal-gradient composability fix: trainable stateful-phasor frequency currently composes incorrectly with coupled-history SVF BPTT, now pinned by TemporalGradientCompositionTests.
design: Treat forward-only population ranking and batched gradient refinement as separate stages. Use post-short-horizon loss as the primary predictor. Benchmark against the existing seeded+midpoint two-run policy at equal wall-clock budget, with particular emphasis on short jobs. Prefer one generic lane-batching mechanism over patch-specific rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: Document a feasibility inventory of tensor-enabled versus blocking Lisp/DSP operations; implement or prototype a representative complicated patch as B independent lanes; compare seeded+midpoint against batched multistart at equal wall-clock budget across known-config round trips; report initial-score versus post-horizon/final-loss correlation; recommend whether and how to integrate the policy into dgenlisp train.
notes: Related existing bead: eseq-bwb covers basin-check/reporting honesty and cold-phase params; this spike concerns replacing the weak two-start search policy with batched exploration/refinement.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text: 2026-08-14 dgen Korg1 prototype landed in ~/code/swift/dgen working tree. Generic LispEvaluator lane lifting now batches params, scalar phasors, make-history SVF state, broadcasting, and tensor outputs from unmodified lowered Lisp. Opt-in dgenlisp train policy: --multistart-candidates N (+ --multistart-batch/--multistart-lanes/--multistart-steps/--multistart-seed), forward rank with independent vDSP MR-STFT, diversity retain, short batched Adam, then full local-seed + global-candidate continuations; artifact multistart_report.json. Real Korg1 65,536-frame run: 64 candidates, B=16 forward, retain/refine 16 for 5 steps, 53.0 s total including two one-epoch continuations/renders; seed CPU score .5654, initial population best .4855, post best .4812, initial/post Pearson .992. Important blocker confirmed: tensor phasor-frequency and shared accum temporalGradRead blocks schedule after tensor-history BPTT consumers; short-horizon path currently detaches those adjoints, while forward search varies them and scalar continuations train normally. Full details docs/TRAIN_SUBCOMMAND_NOTES.md.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text: Committed dgen implementation as bb44b82 (feat(train): add tensor-batched multistart search). Bead remains open: equal-wall-clock/multi-target acceptance work and full tensor temporal-gradient composition are not complete. Exact blocker handoff: with B=2 Korg1 and detach flags off, backward creates phasor temporalGradRead nodes (e.g. #1964, shape [2], scaleBySampleRate true). consolidateTensorBPTTBackwardBlocks puts the tensor-history SVF reverse recurrence/its consumer add #1966 in an earlier sequential [2] block (#202), while temporalGradRead #1964 is emitted later in a parallel [2] block (#207). At add emission, ctx.values[1964] is absent: add#1966 inputs=[1947,1964], missing=[1964], yielding insufficientInputs(operator:add, expected:2, actual:1). Three oscillator phasors reproduce analogous late reads (#2235/#2540); shared analytic-envelope accum clocks create the scale=false variant. Scalar TemporalGradientCompositionTests pass after consolidateScalarBPTTBackwardBlocks, but tensor-history composition is not covered. Suggested new test: B=2 Tensor params -> Signal.statefulPhasor(freq SignalTensor) -> Lisp-style two-TensorHistory coupled SVF -> batched loss; compare SVF cutoff lane grads against B independent scalar runs/FD and assert backward compiles. Inspect bpttRecurrenceClosure boundaries (.temporalGradRead), consolidateTensorBPTTBackwardBlocks beforeDeps/insertion/descendant movement, and any later splitReduceBlocks/BackendBlockSafetySplitPass reorder. Correct ordering must remain temporalGradStore -> temporalGradScan -> temporalGradRead -> tensor-BPTT consumer while retaining reverse-frame and per-lane tensorIndex semantics. Current workaround in BatchMultistart.refine sets detachPhasorFrequency + detachAccumInputs only for the short batched horizon; remove once test passes.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
2026-08-14 blocker CLOSED (dgen commit cd3aa3b, branch dgenlisp-train): tensor phasor/accum suffix adjoints now compose with tensor-history SVF BPTT; the detachPhasorFrequency/detachAccumInputs workaround is removed from BatchMultistart.refine, so the batched short horizon trains frequency and accum-clock dimensions.

Root causes (three block-formation bugs + one emission bug):
1. consolidateTensorBPTTBackwardBlocks computed beforeDeps one dep deep, but isolated-pass adjoints are 3-phase chains (temporalGradStore->Scan->Read; spectral gradSpec->gradIFFT->gradRead) and the closure consumes only the final read. Deferred intermediate phases made the read a descendant of the deferred set, so it was moved after its consumer (the insufficientInputs failure). beforeDeps is now transitively closed over backward ancestors, guarded by a value-edge closureConsumers set.
2. Tail (deferred/moved) fragments ran directly after the consolidated block even when producers sat in later blocks; the MSE path only passed because ordering edges on tensorAccumulate accidentally inflated insertAt. Producers of tail nodes are now hoisted into the node-ID-sorted tail.
3. Sandwich shape (the actual Korg1 add-#1966 failure, 3 phasors hit it): the store input is the per-frame grad computed inside the reverse recurrence, yet the read's consumer add (temporal + per-frame grad merge) is a carry-read descendant swept into the closure. Fixed-point eviction removes such nodes; they read the closure's per-frame outputs from frame-aware cells in later blocks. Eviction must follow value edges only (carry memoryRead deps are ordering-only) or the cascade falsely reaches carry writes.
4. Bonus: shape-[1] tensor phasor freq grads were silently 0 — temporalGradStore's elementCount==1 scalar fast path read an unwritten scalar slot for tensor grad inputs; now branches on grad-input shape.

Verification: new Tests/DGenLazyTests/TensorTemporalGradientCompositionTests.swift (9 tests) — B=2 phasor + coupled TensorHistory SVF under MSE and batched spectral loss with per-lane FD checks, sandwich shape (freq feeding phasor AND cutoff), shared accum clock, B=1 lane, B=2-vs-B=1 parity, controls. Korg1 end-to-end smoke (benchmarks/train_monologue, 8 candidates -> 2 lanes -> 3 batched Adam steps -> both continuations) completes with all grads live. Full-suite A/B vs baseline: no new failures (remaining ones reproduce on clean HEAD: C-backend sincosf_stret audit env issue, shrink tests, golden transcript).

Test-conditioning note for future FD work: spectral-loss FD checks need L2/linear magnitude and a low sample rate (2 kHz, so a 128-window resolves the freqs); L1/log FD is kink-noisy and produces false mismatches.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text: Tensor temporal-gradient blocker resolved in DGen cd3aa3b. Verified locally: all 9 TensorTemporalGradientCompositionTests pass, covering B=2-vs-B=1 lane parity, finite differences, trainable tensor phasor -> coupled TensorHistory SVF under MSE and batched spectral loss, shared freq feeding phasor+cutoff, and shared accum clock composition. BatchMultistart no longer detaches phasor frequency or accum inputs, so the proposed 20-50-step horizon can optimize the complete parameter set. Prior Korg1 5-step numbers were measured with the workaround and should be rerun before drawing post-horizon conclusions.

title: dgenlisp train reporting: level-normalize loss, emit cold-phase params, honest abs_distance

Today there are no ~/.eseq.d or content-tier user roots: saved instrument/effect/MIDI-FX/defmacro roots resolve relative to cwd/repository candidates, while arbitrary out-of-checkout ESeqLisp can enter through explicit load/import paths, editor buffers, scratch script loads, and capture --script. Therefore real out-of-checkout input exists at the generic VM seam; generated-source bypasses need explicit calls to the same scanner before transformation/concatenation.
Scope correction after domain-owner review: crates/eseqlisp/defmacro_library.rs loads DGenLisp macro packages, not ESeqLisp UI/runtime content. Like instrument/effect DGenLisp dsp.lisp, it is outside the 720 module-alias vocabulary and is intentionally NOT scanned. The ESeqLisp seams remain VM::eval_module_source plus authored custom UI files and the sequencer MIDI-FX control-Lisp library.
Completed 2026-08-13. Detection: crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/vm.rs::VM::eval_module_source is the generic path-backed chokepoint (SourceManager load/import, editor eval/hot reload, arbitrary external paths, scratch/project/capture scripts). Process-global canonical-path warn-once state lives in module_alias_migration.rs; warned files short-circuit before rescanning, while clean files are rescanned so a later edit introducing debt is detected. title: Give import a compile-time half so module order stops mattering
description:
Slice 4 (eseq-mods.9) dissolved the ui/main.lisp manifest but could NOT make the surviving root entries reorderable. Root cause is spec §10 hazard (p): import is a RUNTIME form. A file is compiled in full before it executes, so an (import eseq.x) inside F guarantees only that eseq.x is EVALUATED before F's body runs — it cannot supply anything F needs at COMPILE time: another module's defstate keyspace (Compiler::state_binding_for reads a state_bindings table seeded from the VM when F's compiler is built), its macros, or its compat-alias spellings. :refer does not help; it is consulted BY state_binding_for and misses for the same reason.

Proposal: evaluate the import target when the compiler COMPILES the import form, not when the chunk runs. The compiler already walks top-level forms in order (compiler.rs:1950), so this is a callback into the VM at that point rather than a redesign; the runtime __import-module call stays for the load-once/hot-reload-pass ledger.

Measured evidence that this is the blocker: reversing main.lisp's root block fails 157 metal_seq tests, and so does merely hoisting the three library anchors above the render roots (seq-script-picker reads eseq.seq-step-tabs defstates).

The SECOND blocker is separate and not solved by this: the 4 UI roots reference each other bare and a module must never import a UI root (broke 60 tests in S3b wave 2), so their relative order has no declared expression at all. Full order independence needs both.
acceptance_criteria: ui/main.lisp's root entries can be shuffled and metal_seq still passes 586/2 (or the remaining ordering is reduced to the UI-root cycle alone, documented).
notes:
PROGRESS (session 2026-08-13): infra COMMITTED c99c7569 — design (b) realized as segmented unit compilation: VM::eval_str splits at top-level imports, compiles+executes segment-by-segment, re-seeds continuation compilers from the VM; Compiler::take_module_context threads (module …)/:as/:refer across segments. Literal mid-compile VM callback impossible (eval_str MOVES chunks/global_names into the compiler). 6 new vm tests. Unpinning UNCOMMITTED: browser/mixer/sequencer/transport/seq-panels/seq-layout/seq-macro-mapping-hooks import seq-core-state; seq-script-picker+seq-layout import seq-step-tabs; piano-roll-default-pane-height moved home piano-roll→seq-step-tabs (load-time read of a render root inverted; piano-roll imports the hub); browser harness stubs (flat selected-bus defstate + seq-has-selected-bus?) deleted, SEQ.bus-names added to fake. Reproducer test PASSES with import present. NEW TEST metal_seq_main_import_block_boots_in_reverse_order PASSES (full reversal incl render roots). Full gates in flight.
=== OUTCOME (eseq-mods.12 DONE, branch eseq-mods, commits c99c7569/4819a45f/feb4ea5f) ===
DESIGN: (b), realized as SEGMENTED UNIT COMPILATION, not a mid-compile VM callback — impossible because eval_str MOVES chunks/global_names into the compiler. VM::eval_str splits at literal top-level (import …) forms; each segment compiles then EXECUTES before the next compiles; continuation compilers re-seed state_bindings/macros/compat_aliases from the VM via the existing new_repl path; Compiler::take_module_context threads (module …)/:as/:refer/known_namespaces across segments; continuation entry chunks stamped with the declared module. No-import units = 1 segment = old path exactly.
EDGE VERDICTS: load-once per pass holds (compile-time import consults the same ledger; hot_reload_reevaluates_imported_children… still green). Mid-unit failure: transactional entry points roll back via snapshot; bare eval_str keeps earlier segments (load-once precedent) — tested. Cycles terminate (module-declare executes in segment 1 before its imports; back-import = ledger hit) — tested; declare-before-import remains the convention or a cycle can double-eval. REPL import works, no per-keystroke re-eval — tested. Standalone harnesses resolve via source-manager cwd per (n2) — browser + piano-roll harnesses prove it. No new VM state → nothing new to snapshot (ledger already snapshot-aware).
ORDER INDEPENDENCE: FULL for the import block, proven by new test metal_seq_main_import_block_boots_in_reverse_order (buffers + rendered trees + probe values identical under full reversal INCLUDING render roots). Scoped rule that remains: never import a UI root; freedom comes from no module needing a root edge — the one load-time edge into a root (piano-roll-default-pane-height) was inverted by moving the constant home to seq-step-tabs. load lines stay ordered with their callers (themes).
HARNESS LESSON: standalone-harness stubs that fake another module's surface now CONFLICT with the real module the import pulls in — browser harness's flat selected-bus defstate + seq-has-selected-bus? stub deleted; fake SEQ needed bus-names. Expect the same pattern when adding imports to other standalone-evaled files.
FOR .10: alias retirement unblocked — cross-module defstate reads no longer need loader ordering, so the state_values/tests.rs-held aliases are now the payable subset; vocabulary-hub identity aliases serving headerless content remain API. FOR .6 (S5): packages can export macros/defstates via plain import, no loader coordination (spec §8 note).
GATES: eseqlisp 1588/0 (threads=1), sequencer --lib 1720/2 pre-existing, metal_seq 587/2 pre-existing (587 = 586 baseline + reversal test), build clean.
close_reason: Import gained its compile-time half (segmented unit compilation, commit c99c7569); kernel unpinned + reproducer inverted (4819a45f); spec hazard (p) RESOLVED (feb4ea5f). Full import-block order independence proven by metal_seq_main_import_block_boots_in_reverse_order; never-import-a-UI-root scoped in spec. All gates at/above baseline.

title: Dissolve the ui/main.lisp load manifest via import
description: Each module declares its deps with import (load-once + declared ModuleGraph edges per spec §4); main.lisp shrinks from ordered load list to distro assembly stub. Delete ordering comments (overlaps eseq-mods.5's first line — coordinate). Load stays for themes and side-effect files. Precondition: S3b tail converted.
notes:
INPUT FROM eseq-mods.8 (slice 3 complete, 2026-08-13). Read spec section 10 hazard (o) BEFORE starting — it is the standing hazard for this bead.

*** HAZARD (o): DISSOLVING THE MANIFEST CHANGES LOAD ORDER BY CONSTRUCTION ***
A cross-file call that runs at RENDER time (inside a widget/subtree body, NOT inside an on-click lambda) against a file that loads LATER caches EMPTY FOREVER once the caller is a module.
Worked example: transport.lisp loads at main.lisp:25 and its view-button subtrees call seq-arrangement-view?, owned by seq-step-tabs.lisp at :41. Headerless it survives by accident (the bare reference interns the flat slot the later def fills). As a module the late-binding heal has nothing to land on, AND — the part that makes it permanent — no reactive dependency is recorded, because the failing LoadGlobal errors before record_symbol_read. The subtree caches empty and never re-runs.
NEITHER PINNING NOR AN ALIAS FIXES IT (both reach the same still-empty flat slot). Only an import fixes it, because import EVALUATES its target first.
=> SAFE DISSOLUTION ORDER: for each (load ...) line, FIRST add the import that encodes its ordering constraint, verify, THEN delete the (load ...). Never delete first.
=> AUDIT RULE: list every cross-file call that executes at render time or load time and check it against main.lisp order. Event-time calls (on-click, key handlers) are always safe.

MUST STAY LOAD-ORDERED (main.lisp's comments are load-bearing):
1. themes.lisp -> (seq-theme-mac-osx-dark) -> materials.lisp. Themes stay headerless by design (flat theme-slot bags), and materials' macros are referenced FLAT from shader/material bodies, which expand OUTSIDE the importing module. Do NOT convert themes and do NOT requalify material macro refs.
2. track-collapse.lisp MUST precede browser/mixer/sequencer (they call its helpers bare).
3. choose-model.lisp MUST precede transport.lisp (patcher buffers mount choose-model-panel).
4. seq-core-state.lisp early — it is the shared-state hub (~20 consumers).
5. seq-step-tabs.lisp (:41) is called at RENDER time by transport (:25). Already fixed with an import; this is the worked example of (o).
6. step-grid.lisp is deliberately NOT loaded (perf: its whole-list SEQ reads forced hidden-buffer reruns on every step/scene edit). Keep it unloaded.

NEVER IMPORT THE 4 UI ROOTS: eseq.mixer, eseq.browser, eseq.sequencer, eseq.arrangement. import evaluates its target; this broke 60 tests in wave 2. Additional render roots that register buffers/modes/keymaps at top level (their headers carry the warning): eseq.transport, eseq.agent, eseq.patch-macros, eseq.piano-roll, eseq.effects.buffers.

STAY HEADERLESS BY DESIGN: main.lisp + effects.lisp + builtin-effects.lisp (the manifests you dissolve), effects/step-buffer.lisp, themes.lisp + 10 themes/*, the 58 capture-fixtures, and the ~305 content lisp files outside ui/ (instruments, effects, scripts, midi-fx, defmacros).

TWO IMPORT CONSTRAINTS FROM RUST HARNESSES (spec hazards n and n2):
- a file whose source a Rust test SLICES cannot use :as aliases (an undotted namespace is a hard compile error; a dotted full module name only warns and heals) — use full dotted spellings. Affected: seq-panels, step-grid-interactions.
- a file that any harness evals STANDALONE into a bare Runtime cannot import AT ALL (no @/ source root, so the import resolves to a nonexistent path). Affected: piano-roll, macros, agent.
Check both with: grep -rn '<file>.lisp' crates/sequencer/src

ALIAS FLOOR: 720 aliases across 65 modules. Those serving content files and capture fixtures can NEVER retire — treat vocabulary-hub identity aliases as API surface, not migration debt. The payable debt is the subset held open only by state_values/tests.rs.

GATE BASELINES: metal_seq 586 passed / 2 pre-existing (RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 is REQUIRED — it silently aborts on the default stack); sequencer --lib 1720/2; eseqlisp 1581/0 at --test-threads=1 (the patcher writeback tests flake in parallel, user-confirmed). Keep metal_seq_core_lisp_files_parse's file list current: add each newly-converted file in the same commit.

=== OUTCOME 2026-08-13 (eseq-mods.9 DONE, branch eseq-mods, uncommitted) ===
main.lisp: 26 loads -> 3 loads + 15 imports (64 -> 63 lines). All four gates at
baseline: metal_seq 586/2, sequencer --lib 1720/2, eseqlisp 1582/0 (1581 + one
new test), build clean.

DISSOLVED (8, now reached only by declared import edges):
  track-collapse   <- browser, mixer, sequencer, arrangement
  seq-step-tabs    <- transport (already had the edge)
  seq-layout       <- seq-macro-mapping-hooks
  seq-panels       <- sequencer
  step-grid-interactions + seqv-track-params + seq-grid-mode <- bus-grid
  sound-palette    <- arrangement
LOAD -> IMPORT, still listed (15): the render roots + eseq.materials and
  eseq.seq-core-state (pinned to the top by the new hazard (p), below).
STILL LOAD (3): themes.lisp, effects.lisp (nested manifest, out of scope),
  effects/step-buffer.lisp.
COMMENTS: track-collapse ordering comment deleted (four real edges replace it);
  choose-model comment deleted as STALE — the patcher buffers that mount
  choose-model-panel are Rust-generated lisp (edit_sessions.rs) evaluated when a
  patch editor opens, so any boot position satisfies it. The step-grid.lisp
  comment stays: it documents an absence + perf regression, not order.

*** NEW HAZARD (p) — import is a RUNTIME form (spec §10, full writeup) ***
A file is compiled IN FULL before it executes, so an import inside F only
guarantees the target is EVALUATED before F's BODY runs. It cannot supply
compile-time surface: defstate keyspace, macros, compat-alias spellings.
:refer does NOT rescue it (state_binding_for consults refers, so it misses for
the same seeded-table reason). Reproducer: adding (import eseq.seq-core-state)
to browser.lisp broke metal_seq_browser_audio_effect_activation_uses_selected_bus
even though main.lisp had already evaluated that module.
=> RULE: compile-time deps are ordered by the LOADER, runtime deps by import.
A module publishing defstates/macros consumed elsewhere is a ROOT ENTRY.

(n2) CORRECTED: "standalone-evaled files cannot import at all" is too strong.
module_file_candidates resolves against the source-manager cwd, which for the
metal_seq/state_values harnesses IS crates/sequencer, so ui/<name>.lisp resolves
and the import evaluates. The real hazard is semantic — it pulls a REAL module
into a world the harness faked — and it arrives a phase too late to be useful.

ORDER INDEPENDENCE: NOT achieved, and measured. Reversing the root block fails
157 metal_seq tests; so does merely hoisting the three library anchors above the
render roots (seq-script-picker reads eseq.seq-step-tabs defstates). Two
blockers: (1) hazard (p); (2) the 4 UI roots reference each other bare and a
module must never import a UI root. No shuffled-order test was added — it would
codify a red bar. Filed eseq-mods.12 for the infra fix (give import a
compile-time half: evaluate the target when the COMPILER compiles the import
form; the compiler already walks top-level forms in order).

HOT RELOAD (§11 q4) — ANSWERED, AND IT NEEDED A FIX. reload_paths_transactional
re-evaluates a changed file's OWNER ROOT, which now reaches children by import.
Permanent load-once made that re-eval skip every child => edits silently dropped,
i.e. the whole ui/ tree would stop hot-reloading. import is now load-once PER
IMPORT PASS: VM::imported_at_epoch + import_pass_epoch, bumped by
begin_import_pass() from both transactional eval entry points; (module …) records
the epoch too so a `load`ed module is not double-evaluated by a later import in
the same pass. New test (fails on the old ledger):
hot_reload_reevaluates_imported_children_from_the_owner_root.
NB import edges were ALREADY recorded in ModuleGraph exactly like load edges
(__import-module goes through SourceManager::load_source) — only now declared.

FOR .10/.11: the alias table cannot shrink by conversion alone while hazard (p)
stands — every cross-module defstate read still needs loader ordering, and every
headerless content file still needs the flat alias. .11's rewriter should treat
defstate spellings as the risky class.
close_reason: main.lisp 26 loads -> 3 loads + 15 imports; 8 files dissolved into declared import edges. All gates at baseline (metal_seq 586/2, lib 1720/2, eseqlisp 1582/0). title: dgen: tensor-aware delay (per-lane delay lines)
description:
delay currently hard-rejects tensor inputs in the dgen compiler (separate repo: /Users/alecresende/code/swift/dgen). Sources/DGenLisp/LispEvaluator.swift:1305-1316 evalDelay calls requireSignal (:2685-2691) which throws a generic typeError on .tensor/.signalTensor. Underlying Graph.delay (Sources/DGen/HigherOps.swift:664-710) is a single scalar circular buffer (MAX_DELAY = 88000, one alloc + one write head) — there is nothing per-lane to hang a tensor off, so this is real compiler work, not plumbing.

Scope:
- Per-lane circular buffers + per-lane interpolated reads for tensor signal input; delay time may be scalar (broadcast) or tensor (per-lane times — the classic mc move).
- Memory design decision: N lanes x 88000 samples adds up fast. Consider a @max-delay attribute and/or a shorter default max for tensor delays.
- Update the manifest entry (eseq repo: crates/sequencer/tools/dgenlisp-operators.json:2210-2226 declares both inputs signal|float) so the patcher's port metadata accepts tensors.
- Ride-alongs in the same scalar-only bucket, same fix pattern (requireSignal sites in LispEvaluator.swift): accum (:1200-1209, scalar-only increment); noise (:1181-1195, tensor only via 1-D @size, cannot match an arbitrary shape). Optional stretch: biquad per-lane coefficients (:1274-1292 — signal is tensor-aware but cutoff/q/gain/mode are requireSignal, blocking per-voice cutoffs).
- Remember tensor-history buffer-clobber lessons: history cells are pinned via persistentCells (Sources/DGen/Tensor.swift:1258-1264); delay state buffers need the same protection from tensor-temp reuse (see prior phasor state buffer collision bug).

Note: changes span the dgen repo and the vendored toolchain in eseq — commit/revendor together (same workflow as tensor-api-cleanup).
acceptance_criteria: tensor -> phasor -> delay compiles and runs with independent per-lane delay lines; scalar delay unchanged (regression: existing instruments/audition output stable); tensor delay time gives per-lane delay amounts; error message for unsupported shapes is actionable, not 'Expected signal, got other type'.
notes: dgen side DONE: PR https://github.com/universalsequences/dgen-audio/pull/11 (branch tensor-delay, commit 883d375). New .delayLine op: lane-major ring (lanes x maxDelay), shared write head, frame-aware output cell (spectrumDelay/tensorNoise pattern), persistentCells-pinned. Scalar delay unchanged (88000); tensor default SignalTensor.defaultMaxDelay=48000/lane; @max-delay attr overrides. Tensor delay times shape-checked; actionable errors. 14 new tests pass; DGenLispTests 105/105; verified vs clean-main baseline: 12 DGenLazyTests failures (Sample*/SVFBPTT/MSE/Harmonic) + order-dependent CTensorOpsTests full-suite crash are pre-existing and identical on main (each test passes isolated). accum-with-tensor already passes; shaped noise untouched. REMAINING TAIL (this bead): after PR merge, re-vendor toolchain into eseq + loosen delay entry in dgenlisp-operators.json (both inputs currently signal|float) so patcher accepts tensor cables; commit dgen+eseq together per tensor-api-cleanup workflow.

title: Patcher history node: explicit @shape lowers to tensor history
description:
Make the patch editor's history operator support an explicit shape (typed as e.g. 'history @shape [2 2]') so it lowers to dgenlisp tensor history and tensor feedback loops work from the patcher. Keep the polymorphic (make-history name @shape [..]) / read-history / write-history spellings — do NOT emit make-tensor-history/write-tensor-history, because feedback-edge classification keys on the literal string "write-history" (lisp.rs:528-534) and the polymorphic forms already dispatch on the history's shape in the evaluator.

All paths are in crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/ (generate.rs is the real emitter; writeback.rs is the legacy incremental path; emit.rs is debug-only):
- lisp.rs:541 node_label special-cases history and skips attributes_suffix, so @shape cannot round-trip; project.rs:184-231 project_make_history discards args. Fix both so @shape survives source<->patch round-trips.
- writeback.rs:1372-1374 created_history_edit matches only the literal text 'history'; accept 'history @shape [..]'.
- generate.rs:561/681 emit (make-history name) — append @shape when the node carries one. Read (generate.rs:810) and write (generate.rs:858-903) sites stay as-is thanks to polymorphism; multiple writes summed via (+ ..) are fine since dgen broadcasts, but shapes must agree.
- lisp.rs:297 NodeKind projection doesn't recognize make-tensor-history/read-tensor-history/write-tensor-history, so hand-written tensor instruments (e.g. crates/sequencer/instruments/drums/membrane-snare-rim/dsp.lisp) project as plain builtins with no history/feedback semantics. Recognize them (and classify write-tensor-history as Feedback in connection_kind_for_op) even though we don't emit them.
- Document the @shape overload of make-history in crates/sequencer/tools/dgenlisp-operators.json:7552 (mirrored in docs/dgenlisp-api.json) so manifest-driven completion/port metadata see it.

Payoff beyond feedback loops: stdlib filters (onepole, dcblock, svf, slew) are defmacros built on make-history + arithmetic, so they become tensor/multichannel-capable for free once history is shape-aware.
acceptance_criteria: A patcher graph: tensor const -> phasor -> history with @shape [2 2] and a feedback write loop compiles and runs, produces per-lane state; @shape round-trips through source projection and writeback; onepole/svf over a tensor signal works from the patcher; write-tensor-history in hand-written instruments projects as a Feedback edge.
notes: BUILT on worktree /Users/alecresende/code/learning/anthropic/eseq-tensor-history (branch tensor-history off main), uncommitted. All planned seams done: label attribute round-trip (lisp.rs node_label + project.rs project_make_history), generate.rs emission of @shape on make-history (both sites + emit.rs debug), writeback created-node path ('history @shape [2 2]' typed text -> (make-history historyN @shape [2 2])), tensor spellings (make/read/write-tensor-history) recognized in projection with write-tensor-history classified Feedback, manifest + api.json @shape overload documented, autocomplete docs updated. Bonus fixes: format_writeback_list bracket-run mangling (@shape [2 2] re-emitted as '[2 2.0 ]' - scoped to bracket runs only so @default 5.0 stays), tools/audition/audition.py stale LISP_HOST path after lisp_host split. Verified: 4 new tests + full eseqlisp suite green (3 writeback fuzz tests are flaky under parallel load - fail on clean main too, pass isolated); polymorphic (make-history grid @shape [2 2]) + tensor feedback write compiles to dylib through real DGenLisp via audition harness. CAVEAT: the 'onepole/svf tensor for free' acceptance bullet was wrong for this slice - stdlib macros declare shapeless (make-history s) internally, so they only go tensor once shape inference (eseq-0td.3) lands.

title: Tensor multichannel: patcher history + delay over tensors
description: Tensors-as-multichannel is our version of Max mc: define a DSP graph once, feed it a tensor (e.g. per-voice frequencies), and the shape broadcasts through the whole computation. The compiler side (dgen, /Users/alecresende/code/swift/dgen) already propagates shapes through arithmetic, phasor, latch, hop-hold, biquad, and dgenlisp already has shape-polymorphic history: (make-history name @shape [..]) creates a tensor history and read-history/write-history are polymorphic on it (LispEvaluator.swift:293-338). The gaps are (1) the patch editor's history node is scalar-only and actively erases @shape attributes, and (2) delay hard-rejects tensors in the compiler. Closing these two gets tensor feedback loops and per-lane delays working end to end from the patch editor. Design decision: explicit @shape on the history node (matches the old patch editor); shape inference is deferred — patcher-side inference would duplicate compiler shape rules (reshape/gather/matmul) in Rust, and evaluator-side inference needs a restart pass. See conversation notes in child issues.
