title: T4+S5: packages — lisp module packaging, packages dir, copy-on-write forking
description:
Merged bead: was eseq-tiers.6 (T4) + eseq-mods.6 (S5: packages), combined 2026-08-21. Same feature described in two specs -- module spec section 8 owns symbols and loading, content-tiers 4.0/4.1 owns the directory, install and fork mechanics. Neither ships anything usable alone.

CODE HALF (was mods.6, module spec slice 5 + section 8):
- Manifest format: name, version, deps, entry module, external assets declared by name + hash so a package reports what is missing instead of silently loading broken. The asset-declaration seam is filled by eseq-lc0's design.
- Load path: the ~/.eseq.d/packages/<pkg>/src/ rung (rung 2, between user modules and factory).
- Author-scoped names: alec/acid-tools owns alec.acid-tools.*; collision-proof by construction, provenance visible in every qualified symbol and in the inspector. eseq.* and ALL single-segment module names are reserved for core, forever.
- defcustom: declared knobs (type, default, docstring, auto-qualified); the settings UI is generated from the declarations since the UI is lisp. Genuinely new -- no defcustom/setopt exists in the Rust source today.
- Generalize crates/eseqlisp/src/defmacro_library.rs (1024 lines). It ALREADY implements dir-per-package, manifest.json with a version field, use-defmacro imports with cycle detection and local shadowing, and atomic manifest rebuild -- and 12 packages already ship on it in content/defmacros/. The blocker is a deliberate constraint: exactly one public defmacro per package whose name must match the package name (defmacro_library.rs:374, :384). Relax that to a general multi-symbol package while keeping the loading machinery that works.
- Version lives in the MANIFEST, never in a module name (mixer-v2- is the cautionary tale, 113 defs deep). Breaking change = new name; otherwise only accrete.
- Package exports need no loader coordination (unlocked by import's compile-time half): a consumer's (import alec.acid-tools.ui) supplies macros and defstates at the consumer's own compile time. This is what makes third-party packages composable.

MECHANICS HALF (was T4): in-app fork-to-user-tier / revert-to-factory per docs/instrument-fork-spec.md (incl. the param_index p-lock positional-remap gotcha); ~/.eseq.d/packages/ scan; package = git repo mirroring factory layout; install v1 = git clone.

Specs: docs/module-system-spec.md section 8 + slice 5; docs/content-tiers-spec.md 4.0-4.1 + slice T4; docs/sample-store-spec.md (the samples half, eseq-lc0, which BLOCKS this).
notes:
S4 inheritance (2026-08-13): VM::overrides is a snapshot-aware HashMap keyed
  by qualified symbol; each OverrideSet holds registrations keyed/replaced by 
  overriding module, with the most recently evaluated entry active and remove-
  override clearing the set. Factory global cells remain untouched. Cached    
  LoadGlobal and host by-name reads use an empty-registry fast branch then an 
  effective dispatcher; :around original late-resolves the raw factory cell.  
  S5 defcustom/setopt should build alongside this registry shape rather than  
  storing customization in global function cells.

title: Post-Linux-port cleanup
description:
Deferred work split out of the eseq-linux epic when that branch went up for
PR. Nothing here blocks the merge: the Linux port works, its tests pass, and
each item below is either hygiene, a margin-case correctness question, or a
debt that only becomes real once Linux packaging is in scope.

The split exists so the eseq-linux epic can close on "the port works" rather
than staying open on a tail of P3/P4 polish.

title: rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh does not preflight the Linux stage's linker or builtins
description:
rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh checks a per-target REQUIRED_FILES list before swapping
a staged toolchain into place. The arm64-apple-macos list covers bin/ld64.lld
and lib/clang/20/lib/darwin/libclang_rt.builtins.a; the
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu list covers neither bin/ld.lld nor
lib/clang/20/lib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libclang_rt.builtins.a.

So an incomplete Linux archive stages "successfully" and only fails later, at
DGenToolchainPolicy's own preflight, at first compile. The point of the local
check is to fail at stage time with the archive named.

FIX: add both paths to the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu branch of REQUIRED_FILES.
They are exactly the two the policy's linux-x86_64 HostProfile declares
(stageLinkerRelativePath, stageBuiltinsRelativePath).

Found while working eseq-linux.49; kept out of that commit to keep it scoped.

title: Portable dgen FFT kernel has no end-to-end coverage through generated code
description:
Off Apple the shipped host-services table is the rustfft one (dgen_fft.rs,
eseq-linux.78). The portable C kernel it replaced (audiograph/dgen_fft.c) is
still linked and still runs in production: it is the fallback whenever a
setup's workspace pool is contended, and what ESEQ_DGEN_PORTABLE_FFT=1 forces.

Today it is covered only by the direct-callback tests in
lisp_host/dgen/dgen_host_services_tests.rs, which pin each of the four hooks
against an f64 reference DFT. Nothing drives it through a real generated .so,
so a composition-level divergence (lazily created per-call-site setup, hop
scheduling, partitioned complex MAC, baked-in gain compensation) would only
appear in production, on the contended path, as wrong gain or a wrong
spectrum.

eseq-linux.40 added lisp_host::tests::spectral_partitioned_convolution_matches_closed_form,
which pins that composition numerically (worst error 5.2e-8 vs a 2e-5
tolerance) — but only for the shipped table.

BLOCKER for reusing that test against the portable kernel: dgen_manifest.rs
load_dylib_prewarmed() warms every spectral dylib with dgen_host_services_v1()
before the caller sees it, so the generated code's function-local
'static DGenFFTSetupV1' is already populated by the shipped table. Handing that
same image a second table then reinterprets a RustFftSetup* as a portable
setup — confirmed as a SIGSEGV while implementing .40. Two CompileResults of
one source do not help; the cache clones to a distinct dyld image, but each
clone is prewarmed the same way.

WORK: give the load/prewarm path a table parameter (or a test-only
non-prewarmed load), then render the same source through both tables and
assert both land inside the same closed-form tolerance.
close_reason: Added explicit host-services selection to dylib load/prewarm and effect rendering, exposed the portable C table on every platform, and validated shipped and portable generated spectral convolution against the same closed form.

title: [Linux host] Regenerate wgsl-linux-x86_64 shader capture at schema 3
description:
eseq-linux.25 bumped the shader-capture scene set to schema 3:

* added the `widget-dropdown-checkmark` scene — that fragment had no capture
  in either language, so eseq-linux.8's port of it was never diff-reviewed;
* moved `widget-roar-shaper` and `widget-roar-filter` off the exact 0.5
  round() tie (see eseq-linux.76) and onto four real mode indices each, with
  usable cutoff/resonance and drive uniforms.

The committed `msl-macos-arm64` and `wgsl-macos-arm64` captures are at
schema 3. `wgsl-linux-x86_64` is still schema 2, so compare_captures.py
prints a schema-mismatch warning and skips the scene the old capture lacks,
and the two roar rows in the cross-GPU column are meaningless.

WORK: on the Linux host, run

  cargo run -p eseqlisp --features wgpu --bin eseqlisp_shader_capture -- \\
      --name wgsl-linux-x86_64 \\
      --output-dir crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/shader-capture/goldens

and commit the regenerated directory, then drop the schema-2 caveats from
goldens/README.md and goldens/JUDGEMENT.md.

This does not reopen the shader-port sign-off: that was decided on the
same-GPU msl-vs-wgsl comparison, which is unaffected.
close_reason: Regenerated wgsl-linux-x86_64 at schema 3 on the Linux host (Intel UHD 620 / Vulkan). Adds widget-dropdown-checkmark and redraws the two widget-roar-* scenes from schema-3 uniforms; compare_captures.py now runs clean over all 38 scenes in both comparisons, with the roar rows at maxd 1 (0.15% / 0.02% of pixels) and checkmark at maxd 12 (0.21%). Schema-2 caveats dropped from goldens/README.md and goldens/JUDGEMENT.md. Committed as b852e366.

title: MSL round() breaks ties away from zero, WGSL rounds half-to-even: audit round() mode selectors in the ported shaders
description:
Found while diff-reviewing the MSL and WGSL captures for eseq-linux.25.

The roar-shaper and roar-filter fragments select their mode with
`clamp(int(round(value_t)), ...)`. When value_t sits exactly on .5 the two
languages disagree: MSL's round() breaks a tie away from zero (0.5 -> 1) and
WGSL's rounds to even (0.5 -> 0). The capture scenes fed exactly 0.5, so the
two backends drew different modes; with value_t moved to real mode indices the
two captures are byte-identical, which is how the cause was confirmed.

The capture side is fixed (crates/eseqlisp/src/capture_scenes.rs sets real mode
indices). What is NOT settled is production: any shader that rounds a value
which can legitimately land on .5 will select a different branch on Linux than
on macOS.

WORK: grep the ported fragments for round() (roar_shaper.rs, roar_filter.rs,
sound_glyph.rs at minimum), decide per site whether a .5 input is reachable
from the widget's props, and where it is, replace round() with an explicit
tie rule (e.g. floor(x + 0.5)) in BOTH languages so the two agree by
construction rather than by luck.

Not urgent: every known caller passes an integer-valued index today, so no
shipped widget is currently affected.

title: Packages tab (v0.2): browse everything importable; attach inserts the (import …) line into *scratch*
description: Spec: docs/attachable-packages-spec.md rev 2 §5; the fuller worked design (use-package, entry evaluation, on-attach/on-detach, single-file synthesized-manifest packages, git-install UI) is rev 1 in git history. Deliberately deferred past v0.1. Browser tab listing everything importable on the load path — user modules, installed packages with manifests, factory modules — where attach appends the (import …) line to *scratch* and detach removes it. Pure sugar over the textual record; never a parallel attachment mechanism.

title: sync_sidebar_browser re-reads and re-parses the instrument preset bank on every track switch
description:
## Problem

state_values::project_state::sync_sidebar_browser runs on every track switch and
calls ui::browser::visible_preset_items_for_track, which calls
lisp_host::load_instrument_presets(name) — a std::fs::read_to_string plus a
serde_json parse of the instrument's .presets bank, synchronously, inside the
switch. content/instruments/core/drift.presets is 132 KB; several factory banks
are 40-130 KB.

Filesystem I/O and JSON parsing have no business being on the click-to-frame
path. Found while measuring eseq-pgru; it is inside that bead's ~14 ms
track_switch_ms phase (see eseq-md1n.2, which owns the phase as a whole).

## Goal

Cache the parsed preset bank per instrument, invalidated when the bank is
written (save_instrument_presets) or the instrument source changes. Nothing on a
track switch should touch the disk.

## Acceptance

- no preset-bank read or parse happens on a track switch with an unchanged
  instrument
- saving a preset still shows up in the sidebar without restarting
- track_switch_ms on the drift probe drops by the measured share

title: Invisible buffer roots (*patch-mixer*, *piano-roll*) rerun on every track switch
description:
## Problem

tests::drift_same_instrument_track_switch_end_to_end_perf reports 5 full buffer
reruns per track switch. Two of them are for buffers that are NOT in the
production layout the probe installs: *patch-mixer* (~1.5 ms) and *piano-roll*
(~1.1 ms). *step* and *track* also rerun their roots.

~2.6 ms per switch is small next to the fx rerun, but it is pure waste and it
scales with however many effect-buffers a project has defined, so it will matter
more as the UI grows.

## Goal

An effect-buffer whose buffer is not visible in any tile should not re-run its
root on a state change; it should re-run when it becomes visible. Check whether
the existing invisible-buffer gating (the fx_visible / mixer_visible /
sequencer_visible flags in apply_ui_invalidations) can be extended, or whether
the reactive dag should skip effects whose target buffer has no tile.

## Acceptance

- the drift probe's full_reruns count drops by the invisible buffers
- making one of those buffers visible still produces a correct, up-to-date tree
  in the frame it appears (no stale panel, no one-frame-late content)

title: Un-strand the project-92 perf probe family on Linux (fixture samples + ceiling calibration)
description:
eseq-eeng made its two cold-drag probes machine-independent by loading a patched copy of the 92.json fixture that redirects sample references which do not resolve against the local store to a checked-in WAV (crates/sequencer/src/ui/tests.rs, probe prologue). The rest of the project-92 probe family still loads the pristine fixture and therefore cannot run on the Linux workstation (the WAVs live only in the author's Mac library).

On 2026-08-25 the plock knob probe was run once on the Linux workstation against the patched fixture (release): every machine-independent gate passed (plock1_vs_live=3.87x, plock64_vs_live=5.74x vs the 8x gate; live knob median 3.206ms; zero ui/fx epoch updates), but the Mac-calibrated absolute ceiling failed: plock1 median 12.414ms / plock64 18.412ms vs the 12ms ceiling, dominated by apply_coalesced_device_plock_batch (host apply_ms 8.070/12.323; display_sync only 1.750/2.908). So un-stranding the family needs (1) extending the fallback-only fixture patch to all variants (a no-op on machines that have the samples) and (2) a per-machine story for the absolute ceilings — plus possibly a look at why the plock batch apply costs 8-12ms on this machine.
notes: The generalized patch was written and reverted in eseq-eeng (see the comment above the fixture-patch block in tests.rs); re-applying it is a two-line change.

title: Linux audiograph efficiency follow-ups: voice-driven worker hint, worker wait strategy
description:
# Linux: audiograph workers burn CPU when graph is loaded but mostly silent

## Symptom

On Linux, pausing a busy track and live-playing a single synth makes CPU% shoot UP
compared to busy playback. Not observed on macOS.

## Root cause (confirmed by code inspection, pending workers=0 A/B)

The worker pool degrades into a polling/spinning regime whenever the graph is
large but the audible work is small/serial:

1. `choose_active_worker_count` (audiograph/graph_engine.c:2037) sizes the active
   worker set from `cached_total_jobs` — TOTAL node count in the graph, not
   audible work. Pausing does not remove nodes, so the paused busy track keeps
   `jobs` above the 24-job threshold and workers stay engaged, while the only
   real work is one synth's mostly serial chain.

2. Active workers that find the ready queue empty do 8 pause-spins then
   `rq_wait_nonempty` with a 50us timeout (`AUDIOGRAPH_WORKER_WAIT_TIMEOUT_US`,
   graph_engine.c:72; hot loop graph_engine.c:915-937). On Linux that is
   `sem_timedwait` (ready_queue.c:133) — ~20k futex round-trips/sec per worker
   while jobsInFlight > 0 and the queue is dry (i.e. the entire block drain for
   a serial chain).

3. Over-limit workers poll with `usleep(50)` — 50 MICROseconds — until the block
   completes (graph_engine.c:901-911). The per-block `pthread_cond_broadcast`
   (graph_engine.c:2178) wakes ALL 4 workers (~375x/sec at 128 frames)
   regardless of the active limit.

4. The RT audio callback's help-loop never sleeps: `cpu_relax()` busy-spin while
   the queue is empty but jobs are in flight (graph_engine.c:2202-2210). When
   the block is hundreds of near-no-op silent nodes ping-ponged between threads
   via sem_post/futex handoffs, drain time is wake-latency-bound and the
   callback burns a full core spinning through all of it.

Playing the busy track HIDES this: nodes are expensive, the queue has width,
waits succeed immediately, CPU is real DSP. Pause it and overhead/work inverts.

## Why Linux only

- Workers run SCHED_FIFO/SCHED_RR (direct promotion or rtkit). Linux gives RT
  threads ZERO timer slack, so 50us timeouts/usleeps fire at exactly 50us =
  ~20k kernel entries/sec/worker, each an hrtimer + futex wake + RT preemption.
  macOS applies leeway/coalescing to short `dispatch_semaphore_wait`/`usleep`.
- macOS workers join CoreAudio's os_workgroup (graph_engine.c:829-889, Rust
  `engine_set_os_workgroup`): kernel schedules callback+workers as one audio
  deadline group. No Linux equivalent exists in the engine.
- RT accounting: SCHED_FIFO spinning steals cycles system-wide and is fully
  visible in CPU%; Linux-only `checkpoint_rtkit_cpu_budget` nanosleep churn
  (graph_engine.c:952-957) adds to it.
- Also check negotiated period size: if ALSA/PipeWire runs 128-frame periods vs
  CoreAudio 512, all per-block overhead is 4x.

## Diagnostics

- A/B: `TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_WORKERS=0` (env override src/audio/engine.rs:389).
  If CPU% collapses in the paused+1-synth case, worker thrash confirmed.
- `pidstat -t -p <pid> 1` to see which threads burn.
- `perf stat -e syscalls:sys_enter_futex,syscalls:sys_enter_clock_nanosleep -t <worker-tid> -- sleep 5`
  to see the ~20k/sec wait rate.

## Fix plan: Rust voice-activity-driven worker hint

Rust already computes "what is audible" per block in the audio callback:
`publish_active_voice_counts` (src/audio/voices/runtime.rs:904, called from
callback.rs:752) counts active voices across sampler pools, custom-engine
pools, and rack slots; `shrink_released_voices` tracks release tails.

- C side: add `_Atomic int workerLimitHint` to Engine + exported
  `engine_set_worker_limit_hint(int)` (graph_api.h + extern block in
  src/audio/audiograph.rs). In `choose_active_worker_count`, clamp the existing
  jobs-based result to the hint (hint < 0 = no hint / current behavior).
  Hint is a clamp under the jobs ceiling, so a stale hint can only
  over-provision, never starve a busy graph.
- Rust side: where `publish_active_voice_counts` tallies, derive the hint:
  0 audible (active + release-tail + free-patch engines + live keyboard notes)
  => hint 0 (callback drains silent graph serially, zero worker wakes);
  otherwise scale with audible estimate. Single atomic store, RT-safe.
- Asymmetric hysteresis: raise immediately on note-on; hold last nonzero
  ~100-250ms of silence before dropping to 0 (release tails give most of this).
- Caveat: voices are not the whole graph — count free-patch engines
  (`custom_engine_requires_idle_voice`, runtime.rs:345), modulators, and active
  bus/send effects coarsely, or a paused project with a heavy master chain gets
  under-provisioned.

## Complementary C-only fixes (Linux polling cost when workers ARE active)

- Over-limit workers should re-park on `sess_cv` instead of usleep(50)-polling.
- Empty-wait timeout should back off exponentially after repeated dry rounds.
- Both ~20-line changes in graph_engine.c.
notes:
UPDATE 2026-08-25: workers=0 A/B DISPROVES worker thrash as the primary cause.

Verified live on PID 1215128 (metal_seq): with TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_WORKERS=0 the
process has NO audiograph worker threads (thread listing confirms), yet the
paused+1-synth CPU spike persists. 3s per-thread sampling: cpal_alsa_out burns
~87% of a core alone (261/300 ticks); sequencer-sched ~3%; everything else idle.
So the cost is inside serial block processing on the callback thread itself.

NEW PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS: x86 denormals. After pause, filter/delay/envelope
feedback states decay into subnormal float range; x86 pays ~50-150 cycles/op
microcode assist, Apple Silicon handles subnormals at full speed => explains
Linux-only AND paused-is-worse-than-playing (loud signals never go subnormal).

Evidence:
- No FTZ/DAZ (MXCSR) setup anywhere: no _mm_setcsr / _MM_SET_FLUSH_ZERO_MODE /
  fpcr in crates/sequencer/src, audiograph C, or eseqlisp.
- multiverb.rs:1159 manually flushes denormals in its recursive paths and has
  test tail_survives_long_silence_without_denormal_blowup — the project already
  hit this bug once at single-effect level; every other IIR/delay/smoother and
  all dgen-generated effect C (checked cache: no protection) is exposed.
- Callback thread is also SCHED_OTHER (rtkit promotion did not take effect —
  separate issue worth its own bead once confirmed).

Proposed fix: set FTZ+DAZ on every audio-processing thread at startup
(x86_64: MXCSR bits 15+6 via _MM_SET_FLUSH_ZERO_MODE/_MM_SET_DENORMALS_ZERO_MODE
in the cpal callback init and audiograph worker entry; aarch64: FPCR FZ bit,
optional). Cheap, standard practice in audio engines. The original
worker-scaling findings in this bead remain valid as a secondary efficiency
issue once workers are re-enabled.

Profiling gap: perf not installed, ptrace_scope=1 blocks gdb/eu-stack attach as
non-root, so no stack profile yet. FTZ rebuild A/B is the decisive test.
FTZ/DAZ wired in (working tree, uncommitted):
- audiograph/graph_engine.c: flush_denormals_to_zero() helper (x86 only, pmmintrin FTZ+DAZ) called at worker_main entry, so workers are covered when re-enabled.
- src/audio/callback.rs: enable_flush_denormals_to_zero() sets MXCSR FTZ|DAZ bits via _mm_getcsr/_mm_setcsr (the _MM_SET_DENORMALS_ZERO_MODE intrinsic is not exposed in this toolchain) on first callback entry; the rt_promotion_attempted first-entry block now runs on all platforms with RT promotion still Linux-only inside it.
- aarch64 deliberately untouched (full-speed subnormals; macOS behavior unchanged).
- cargo check -p sequencer green; gcc -fsyntax-only green.
- Not covered yet: any offline/preview render threads (bin/multiverb_render etc.) — only matters if their perf is measured.
A/B pending: rebuild, pause busy track + play 1 synth, watch cpal_alsa_out thread CPU.
CLOSE-OUT 2026-08-25: Root cause of the original symptom was x86 subnormal floats, NOT worker thrash. FTZ/DAZ fix validated live on Linux in both workers=0 and default-worker configs (paused CPU spike gone) and committed on branch eseq-linux. RT scheduling verified healthy in default config: callback SCHED_FIFO 21, four workers SCHED_FIFO 20 (direct promotion; rtkit fallback not needed — earlier SCHED_OTHER observation was the workers=0 artifact, since TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_WORKERS=0 also disables rt_default, engine.rs:392). Busy-playback worker CPU (~30%/worker) confirmed to be legitimate parallel DSP.

Remaining scope of this bead (all secondary efficiency work, P3):
- Rust voice-activity-driven worker limit hint (plan in description).
- Park over-limit workers on sess_cv instead of usleep(50) poll; exponential backoff on the 50us empty-queue sem_timedwait.
- pthread_setname_np for audiograph workers (they show as 'metal_seq', hurts debugging).
- FTZ/DAZ for offline/preview render threads (only the realtime path is covered).
- Consider decoupling rt_default from worker count so workers=0 experiments don't silently disable RT.

title: content_shader_corpus_emits_valid_wgsl turns the suite red on every authored shader edit
description:
lang::sdf_codegen::tests::content_shader_corpus_emits_valid_wgsl hashes the concatenated MSL and WGSL output of all 63 authored content shaders and asserts two absolute digests. Any deliberate edit to any content/*.lisp shader body moves both digests, so the test fails and someone has to hand-copy two hashes out of a panic message before the workspace is green again.

That fired twice in one session on 2026-08-25: commit 7396708d ('styling tweaks') restyled ui/transport.lisp and both goldens had to be re-captured under eseq-linux.12. Alec is actively restyling the UI, so this will keep recurring, and the failure mode is indistinguishable at a glance from a real emitter regression.

The coverage the test actually exists for is already carried by its other assertions, which are edit-insensitive: every shader compiles under BOTH emitters, metal.region_count == wgsl.region_count per shader, assert_valid_wgsl parses the WGSL with naga, and shader_count >= 60. The two digests add 'no unintended emitter change' on top of that, which is worth something during the port but is being paid for on every content edit.

Options worth weighing: keep the digests but make re-capture a one-command operation (an env var or an --ignored companion test that prints both) rather than a copy-paste from a panic; or drop the absolute digests and replace them with a structural invariant that is insensitive to authored content.
acceptance_criteria: Editing an authored content shader no longer requires hand-copying hashes to get the workspace green, and unintended emitter changes are still caught.
notes:
Confirmed live on macOS on 2026-08-25 while running eseq-linux.26 (host: Apple M1 Max, branch eseq-linux at 78ad4c8c). The MSL digest assertion at sdf_codegen.rs:2097 fails:

  emitted  17426e68b350275389ec3223354cb3e7a27b81aa520a1bf96d0fdc48dbdeb8c1
  recorded f84ae308e450ed2a5af0ad03b40fd5d3948ba2536509fb6f29e383fbf6b8c7f4

Reproduced at CLEAN HEAD in a detached worktree (same digests), so it is not
working-tree drift: authored content shaders changed after 7396708d -- where
both goldens were last captured under eseq-linux.12 -- and nobody re-captured
them. This is the recurrence the bead predicted, one day later. It is not
platform-specific; it will be red on Linux at this commit too.

Anyone re-capturing by hand needs the WGSL digest as well, which this run did
not reach because the MSL assert panics first.

title: Scale remaining raw-px UI constants by ui_px_scale (patcher metrics family)
description: Follow-up to eseq-linux.63, which scaled tile corner radii, autocomplete panel/row radii + anchor gap, and the ADSR shader's handle/bracket px by ui_px_scale(). Remaining raw-px constants are still framebuffer pixels authored at the 2x macOS reference and read ~1.25x proportionally large at Hyprland scale 1.6: the widget_render/patcher/metrics.rs family (NODE_BORDER_WIDTH_PX, NODE_CORNER_RADIUS_PX, PORT_*_DIAMETER_PX, AGENTIC_* radii/diameters), patcher alignment thresholds, and patch cable thickness/paddings. Live verification on the 1.6 workstation (2026-08-24) did not flag these as visually wrong, so this is polish, not a bug. Hairline widths (AGENTIC_CARD/INNER_BORDER_WIDTH_PX, panel border 1px strokes) were intentionally left raw so they stay crisp — re-evaluate per-site rather than blanket-scaling. metal_backend never calls set_ui_scale_factor by design: the default factor equals the 2.0 reference, so scaling is identity there and capture goldens stay byte-stable.
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable: patcher node/port/agentic geometry at Hyprland 1.6 proportionally matches the macOS design; capture/shader golden tests unchanged; cargo check -p eseqlisp --features wgpu clean.
notes: Scaled patcher node/port/agentic geometry, alignment thresholds/guides, cable radii, and backend cable raster padding through ui_design_px; retained deliberate device-pixel hairline borders. Validation: cargo check -p eseqlisp --features wgpu; 3 targeted patcher nextest tests; ignored Metal Lexilush capture generated and visually inspected at the 2.0 reference scale.
close_reason: Implemented patcher design-pixel scaling and validated compile, targeted behavior, and Metal capture.

title: project_92 owner-switch smoke test depends on a sample WAV absent from fresh checkouts
description:
First Linux run of the sequencer suite (2026-08-24, during eseq-linux.59): 2731/2732 passed; the one failure is tests::project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_owner_switch_smoke. It loads tests/fixtures/projects/92.json, whose sampler tracks reference samples/9151328c....wav by content hash - that file lives in the local sample library, not in git, so the load fails with 'No such file or directory' on any machine without that library (Alec confirmed: depends on samples that are not here). Not Linux-specific and not a port regression, but it blocks a green Linux suite (eseq-linux.12) and CI (eseq-linux.32).

Fix options: commit a small fixture sample under tests/fixtures and point 92.json at it; or make the test skip (with a visible skip reason) when the referenced sample is unresolvable.
close_reason: Skipped the project 92 owner-switch smoke test with a visible reason because its sample WAV is absent from fresh checkouts.

title: UI load reports 'Error: substring expects a string' at startup (cross-platform)
description:
During app startup the Lisp UI load logs: 'metal_seq: Lisp UI status during startup: Error: substring expects a string'. Non-fatal; the UI loads and renders normally afterwards.

Per Alec (2026-08-24): this predates the Linux port epic and also happens on macOS, so it is a plain content/runtime bug, not a port issue. Some (substring ...) call site in content/ui/*.lisp receives nil (or a number) instead of a string, plausibly from an empty/default data source (sample db entries, sound-palette sources, track/group names). Candidate call sites: content/ui/sound-palette.lisp:127/185/206, mixer.lisp:804/1071/1507, browser.lisp:684/1306, sequencer.lisp:100/1390/1999. Reproduces at least with a fresh/empty user tier.

description:

title: Evaluate enabling cpal's jack feature for low-latency Linux audio
description: Carried over from eseq-linux.11 and eseq-linux.53 (both deferred it as out of scope). cpal 0.15's ALSA backend is the current Linux host; the jack feature would let eseq attach to a JACK/PipeWire-JACK server for lower-latency scheduling. Needs evaluation, not just a feature flag flip: adds a system JACK dependency, host-selection logic, and interaction with the SCHED_FIFO promotion added in eseq-linux.53. Decide whether PipeWire's ALSA emulation already makes this moot on modern desktops.
close_reason: Not needed on current evidence: modern Linux targets run PipeWire, so cpal's ALSA backend already routes through pipewire-alsa and gets PipeWire's low-latency scheduling — JACK's historical advantage is absorbed (PipeWire is also the JACK server on these systems). With RT promotion handled by eseq-linux.53/.54/.58, the remaining latency lever is buffer/period size on the existing ALSA path (e.g. PIPEWIRE_LATENCY), not a host switch, and cpal's jack feature would add a system dependency plus host-selection complexity for a second-class backend. REOPEN TRIGGER: if eseq-linux.12's latency/perf validation measures the ALSA-via-PipeWire path failing the frame/latency budget at reasonable buffer sizes, recreate or reopen this.

title: Document the container DGenLisp release recipe in-repo, with the missing HOME override
description:
The only record of how to build and publish a Linux DGenLisp release is the description of
eseq-linux.33, which is closed. It is also incomplete: the docker invocation it gives fails.

  docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v /home/alec/code/dgen-audio:/src -w /src \
    swift:6.3.3-jammy swift build -c release --static-swift-stdlib \
    --product DGenLisp --scratch-path /src/.build-container

With --user and no HOME override the container's HOME is /, which the mapped user cannot
write, so SwiftPM cannot create its caches and the build dies with a diagnostic that names
neither cause:

  warning: /.swiftpm/configuration is not accessible or not writable ...
  error: unable to open output file '/.cache/clang/ModuleCache/.../SwiftShims-*.pcm':
         'Permission denied'
  error: could not build C module 'SwiftShims'

Adding -e HOME=/tmp fixes it (verified 2026-08-24 building the v0.1.2 release). Note the
error is about SwiftShims and module caches, so it reads as a toolchain problem rather than
a permissions one -- which is exactly why it belongs in a written recipe.

Move the recipe into the repo (docs/, or a scripts/publish_dgenlisp.sh that encodes it) so
it is versioned, reviewable, and findable without archaeology on a closed bead. It should
cover: the container invocation with -e HOME=/tmp, the pre-publish verification gates from
eseq-linux.33 (max GLIBC symbol <= 2.35, ldd showing only libc/libm/libstdc++/libgcc_s/
loader and no swift/Foundation/ICU, functional smoke emitting .c/.json/.so with processAbi
dgen-host-abi-v1), the target-qualified asset naming, and the lock re-pin that follows.

ALSO WORTH ENCODING: gh release create times out uploading the 64 MB bare binary over a
slow link and leaves the release as a DRAFT with only some assets attached. That is a safe
failure -- nothing is public -- but the recovery step (gh release upload --clobber, then
gh release edit --draft=false) is not obvious mid-incident.
acceptance_criteria: The container build+publish recipe lives in the eseq repo, includes -e HOME=/tmp, and a fresh run of it on this Linux box produces a binary passing every eseq-linux.33 verification gate without consulting a bead.
close_reason: Added a complete in-repo Linux DGenLisp build, verification, draft publication/recovery, and eseq lock re-pin recipe, including the required container HOME=/tmp override. Linked it from README. Validated all shell blocks with bash -n, resolved local links, and ran the documented GLIBC 2.35, exact ldd allowlist, standalone .c/.json/.so, and dgen-host-abi-v1 gates against the published v0.1.2 distribution. Committed as 7dcbcdf4.

title: Split live_spectrogram_frag into per-mode WGSL entry points
description:
The WGSL port of LIVE_SPECTROGRAM_SHADER_SRC (eseq-linux.7) evaluates the 13-tap EQ spectrum curve unconditionally, including in waterfall mode. MSL only evaluated it inside 'if (mode == 1u)', but WGSL requires derivative builtins (fwidth) to be reached from uniform control flow, and the eq branch takes fwidth(uv.y - y) where y is the curve value -- so the curve must exist before the branch.

Fix: give the mode-1 (EQ) and mode-0 (waterfall) paths their own @fragment entry points in LIVE_SPECTROGRAM_SHADER_WGSL and two pipelines, selected on the CPU from LiveSpectrogramInstance.mode. That removes the wasted work AND lets each fragment keep its derivatives at top level. Requires grouping spectrogram instances by mode at draw time, so it belongs with the wgpu backend draw-walk integration rather than the shader port itself.

Cost today: ~13 cubic bin samples per waterfall-mode pixel that are computed and discarded.
acceptance_criteria: live_spectrogram waterfall mode no longer evaluates sample_eq_spectrum_curve; the live-spectrogram capture scene still renders both modes and its self-consistency test still passes on Linux.
close_reason: Split live spectrogram WGSL into waterfall and EQ fragment entry points, added mode-specific pipelines and grouped capture draws by mode; targeted Linux validation and capture tests pass.

title: Post-CoreText cleanup: dead objc2 deps, stale comments, warn spam
description:
Loose ends left by 57b76e2a. All verified by grep over crates/:

1. objc2-core-graphics (Cargo.toml:50-55, features CGBitmapContext/CGColorSpace/CGContext/CGImage) is now entirely unused - zero references to objc2_core_graphics::, CGBitmapContext, CGColorSpace, CGContext, CGGlyph or CGImage remain. Drop the dependency.
2. objc2-core-foundation still enables features CFAttributedString and CFDictionary (Cargo.toml:48); the only remaining use is objc2_core_foundation::CGSize at metal_backend.rs:21. Trim the feature list.
3. widget_render/patcher/display.rs:310 still explains a constant in terms of CoreText measurements. Reword for the portable path.
4. glyph_atlas.rs:239 eprintln fires whenever the resolved PostScript name differs from the requested string. Resolution via the family-name branch always trips that, so a correct resolution warns - and it warns again on every atlas rebuild. Warn only when the fallback is genuine.
5. glyph_atlas.rs:246 calls font.rasterize('m', size) purely to read advance_width and discards the bitmap; font.metrics('m', size) gives the same number without rasterizing.
6. load_font and load_named_font duplicate the same with_face_data / Font::from_bytes / FontSettings block; factor it out (folds naturally into the caching in eseq-linux.21).
acceptance_criteria: unused dependency and features removed; cargo check clean on Linux; stale CoreText comment reworded; warn fires only on genuine fallback. The x86_64-apple-darwin cross-check moved to eseq-linux.26 (needs the macOS SDK).
close_reason: Removed dead CoreGraphics declarations, trimmed CoreFoundation features, clarified portable text comments, and made font warnings fallback-aware; Linux checks and targeted tests pass.

title: Atlas rebuild re-copies and re-parses the whole font file on every text-zoom step
description:
glyph_atlas::load_named_font / load_font call db.with_face_data(...) and then Font::from_bytes(data.to_vec(), ...) - a full heap copy of the font file plus a full fontdue parse, every time.

metal_backend.rs:3767 rebuilds text_atlas whenever |text_atlas_zoom - zoom| > 0.001, i.e. on every zoom step, and :6119-:6135 builds three atlases (atlas, text_atlas, prop_atlas) on scale change. JetBrains Mono Nerd Font is roughly 4 MB, so that is ~12 MB of copying and three parses per rebuild.

The old CoreText path was effectively free here - CTFont::with_name hits the system font cache.

Cache the parsed fontdue::Font (or at least the face bytes) keyed by face id; fontdue::Font is size-independent, so one parse can serve every size and zoom level.
acceptance_criteria: rebuilding the text atlas at a new zoom does not re-read or re-parse font file bytes
close_reason: Cached immutable parsed fontdue fonts by fontdb face ID and verified atlas rebuilds at different sizes share the parsed font.

title: Share the scissor/clip math with metal_backend.rs instead of two copies
description:
eseq-linux.5 introduced ui::gpu_geometry::{ScissorRect, ClipStack} for the wgpu backend, but metal_backend.rs still carries its own intersect_scissor_rects (:9562) and scissor_segments walk over MTLScissorRect. The two now compute the same clip-stack intersection independently and can drift.

Convert the Metal path to build ScissorRect via the shared helpers and convert to MTLScissorRect only at the encoder boundary. This is a Metal-side change, so it needs a macOS machine to test - it was deliberately left out of eseq-linux.5, which could only be verified on Linux.
acceptance_criteria: metal_backend.rs no longer defines its own scissor intersection; both backends derive clip rects from ui::gpu_geometry; Linux-runnable clipping tests pass and the macOS-only clipping tests are left untouched and compile-checked as far as Linux allows. Running the macOS clipping tests moved to eseq-linux.26.
close_reason: Metal clipping now uses ui::gpu_geometry::ScissorRect and ClipStack; Darwin checks and shared clip-stack test pass.

title: ui::theme tests race on the process-global ACTIVE_THEME
description:
`ui::theme::tests::theme_slot_overrides_apply_to_named_colors` (theme.rs:~1180) calls `sync_from_value` to swap every theme slot, then restores it with `set_current`. `ACTIVE_THEME` is a process-global RwLock, so while that body runs every concurrently-scheduled test that reads `theme::current()` sees the override colours.

Observed: `ui::theme::tests::agentic_bubble_slots_round_trip_through_a_theme_override` fails intermittently in a full `cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib` run (2 of 4 runs at 7f580a54, i.e. pre-existing, not caused by eseq-linux.3). eseq-linux.3's shader golden test hit the same race and was fixed by threading an explicit theme instead (commit 6a5fb546) - the theme tests themselves still race.

Fix options: serialise the theme-mutating tests behind a shared mutex, or make them operate on an explicit `Theme` value rather than the global.
acceptance_criteria: A full cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib run passes the ui::theme tests repeatedly (>=5 consecutive runs) with no theme-related intermittent failures

title: Linux validation: iGPU perf budget, full test suite green, CI target
description:
Confirm the renderer is actually usable on non-Apple hardware, and that the
whole workspace builds and tests green on Linux.

Perf reality check. The dev box is an Intel UHD 620 (Kaby Lake-R). eseq's
renderer is tuned for Apple GPUs - see UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md. SDF-heavy
fragment shaders with per-widget instancing is a different regime on a weak
iGPU with shared memory bandwidth.
  - The retained primitive-run cache has to be genuinely effective, not just
    present: WIDGET_PRIMITIVE_CACHE (widget_render/mod.rs:245),
    MetalPrimitiveRunIndex (:806), RetainedMetalPrimitiveRunStats (:814).
    Instrument reuse rate on Linux.
  - `vulkaninfo` is not installed on the dev box; confirm mesa's vulkan-intel
    is present or wgpu silently falls back to GL with different perf and
    feature characteristics. Log and assert the chosen wgpu backend at
    startup.
  - Establish a frame-time budget on the reference project and treat
    regressions against it as bugs.

Build and test. Get the full workspace green:
  cargo nextest run  (see CLAUDE.md for the test stack budget - 16 MiB
  RUST_MIN_STACK from .cargo/config.toml, and the disposable worktree
  recipe for clean-HEAD checks)
Baseline as of 2026-08-20 on macOS: 4,272 passed / 32 skipped debug,
4,270 / 32 release, per docs/test-suite-performance.md.
  - crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/tests.rs has ~12 cfg(target_os="macos")
    gated tests, and widget_render/patcher/tests.rs (49) and editor/tests.rs
    (48) have many more. Decide per test: genuinely macOS-specific, or just
    gated because the primitive IR was gated (eseq-linux.1 should free most
    of these).
  - Add Linux to CI so the port does not rot.
acceptance_criteria: Full workspace test suite passes on Linux; every test skipped or gated for Linux is enumerated with a stated reason (not silently gated); wgpu backend selection asserted at startup; frame-time budget recorded for the reference project on UHD 620; Linux job added to CI. Confirming the gated tests still pass on a Mac moved to eseq-linux.26.
notes:
COMPLETE. Commits 733af2a0, 872a6912 and 2db06647 on branch eseq-linux.

WORKSPACE IS GREEN ON LINUX. cargo nextest run --workspace --features eseqlisp/wgpu on the Intel UHD 620 reference machine: 4508 run, 4508 passed, 33 skipped, 534s debug. cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features eseqlisp/wgpu is clean too (the CI check step).

Getting there took three real fixes:

1. BUILD BREAK AT HEAD. state_values/tests.rs referenced crate::ui::editor_setup, but that module tree only exists under the metal_seq bin root (ui/main.rs includes metal_main.rs) where the path is crate::editor_setup. Introduced by 1625f999. The bin test target failing to compile meant its ENTIRE test module had never run on Linux and the whole workspace build failed. The previous attempt's blocker (missing DGen toolchain) was already gone thanks to eseq-linux.47.

2. MACOS GATES. All 36 cfg(target_os = macos)-gated test functions (editor/tests.rs, lib.rs, ui/layout.rs, widget_render/patcher/tests.rs, state_values/tests.rs) were gated only because the primitive IR they assert against was gated before eseq-linux.1; none test Metal. All now run on both platforms. Only crates/eseqlisp/tests/capture.rs stays gated - it drives eseqlisp_capture, a MetalBackend PNG tool, and its 3 tests are ignored on macOS too. Every one of the 33 remaining skips is an ignore equally true on macOS: no test is skipped for being on Linux. Enumerated with reasons in docs/linux-validation.md. eseq-linux.26 covers re-confirming the ungated tests on a Mac.

3. TESTS THAT PINNED STYLING, per Alec's rule that tests must not assert colors or placement. metal_seq_fx_space_echo_layout_contains_mode_grid_and_knobs (written blind, never compiled) asserted the panel sat inside the viewport at col 0 and each control's rect sat inside the panel's - now asserts the panel's own extent, which is the real Linux-scale regression. metal_seq_transport_view_buttons_switch_to_wide_arrangement_layout was DELETED at Alec's instruction. metal_seq_transport_scene_pills_are_drag_drop_reorder_targets asserted the transport-scene-strip-bg widget name that 7396708d replaced with a themed box - assertion dropped, push-interpolation state assertions kept.

Also re-captured both digests in content_shader_corpus_emits_valid_wgsl after 7396708d changed authored shader bodies. That test goes red on every authored shader edit and needs two hashes hand-copied out of a panic to recover; filed as eseq-5ed.

BACKEND ASSERTED AT STARTUP. crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/gpu_adapter.rs logs the selected adapter and refuses to start on wgpu's silent degradations (OpenGL fallback, Cpu rasterizer, Empty backend), naming the fix. ESEQ_GPU_BACKEND pins a backend; ESEQ_ALLOW_GPU_FALLBACK=1 permits fallbacks but cannot override a pin. Pure policy function over wgpu::AdapterInfo, 9 unit tests, no GPU needed. This machine reports vulkan / Intel UHD 620 / Mesa 26.1.7.

FRAME BUDGET, MEASURED. crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/wgpu_frame_stats.rs adds [ui-profile][wgpu] under the existing ESEQLISP_PROFILE_UI switch, with a dedicated scroll-frame section and tail percentiles, separating scene rebuild from the rest of planning from swapchain backpressure. 7 unit tests. Alec captured a real scroll on the reference project on 2026-08-25; the full table is in docs/linux-validation.md.

Headline: scrolling a multi-track sequencer buffer runs at 6-8 fps. Per second, ~758ms goes to full relayouts (~76% of wall clock) and ~116ms to the entire wgpu render path (~12%). acquire_avg is 0.06ms, so swapchain backpressure and frame pacing are ruled out entirely. GPU side is not the constraint either: the SDF probe measures p95 3.672ms full lighting / 3.021ms flat, consistent with Alec's report that SDF panels feel fast.

That measurement REFUTED two of the three static hypotheses I had filed, and eseq-pzp was rewritten and retitled around the real cause: about 2.1 full relayouts per frame at ~45ms each, with reused=0 full=17 subtree=0 and reactive/s=0 - the widget tree is not being rebuilt, yet layout is recomputed from scratch twice a frame. The porting-the-retained-scene-cache work is still worth doing but is worth ~5.6ms out of ~94ms.

CI. .github/workflows/linux.yml runs the check and the suite on ubuntu-24.04, fetching both pinned DGen archives first. Load-bearing apt deps: libasound2-dev (cpal), mesa-vulkan-drivers (so headless wgpu captures find an adapter instead of skipping), fonts-jetbrains-mono (glyph metrics come from the system font db and several layout tests measure that exact family). Sets ESEQ_ALLOW_GPU_FALLBACK=1 because a runner has no GPU. NOT YET EXERCISED: the workflow has never run, because GitHub only picks it up once it is pushed and the push trigger is limited to main. Expect the first real run to need a fix or two. The repo is public, so standard GitHub-hosted runners are free; adding working branches to the push trigger costs only wall-clock.
close_reason: All five acceptance criteria met: workspace green on Linux (4508/4508, 33 skipped), every skip enumerated with a reason in docs/linux-validation.md, wgpu backend asserted at startup via ui/gpu_adapter.rs, frame-time budget measured on the UHD 620 reference project, and .github/workflows/linux.yml added. Scroll perf follow-up is eseq-pzp; shader-corpus golden friction is eseq-5ed; macOS re-confirmation of the ungated tests is eseq-linux.26.

title: Inline-widget release evals report misleading "no changed symbols" noise
description:
Even where a re-eval is legitimately needed, the minibuffer flashes
"Lisp reload ok (no changed symbols; no roots rerendered)" on every inline-widget
mouse release. The string comes from `ReloadReport::success_message()`
(`crates/eseqlisp/src/hot_reload.rs:558-581`), shown unconditionally by
`process_lisp_reload_report` (`crates/eseqlisp/src/editor/mod.rs:7009`).

Two independent problems, either or both worth fixing:

1. NOISE. A drag-initiated eval is not an author-initiated eval; it should not
   report like one. Options: stay silent when the report carries no changed
   symbols, no rerendered roots and no diagnostics AND the eval came from
   `finish_inline_widget_writeback`; or thread an "originating gesture" flag
   through `evaluate_buffer_transactional` so only keystroke evals announce.

2. THE MESSAGE IS ALSO WRONG. `jak` (and `def-sequencer` generally) registers a
   STRING-named sequencer, not a global symbol, so a real change to a jak body
   still reports "no changed symbols; no roots rerendered". Authors evaluating a
   jak buffer by hand get told nothing happened when something did. Consider
   having sequencer/process registration contribute to
   `ReloadReport.changed_symbols` (or a sibling list) so the message is truthful.

Fix (1) becomes much less pressing if eseq-jo7.18 lands, since the common case
stops evaluating at all — but (2) stands on its own regardless.

description: Sweep the open questions: (1) takes snapshot pattern state — verify slots ride the take lifecycle (release-time stamping) correctly; (2) a (scenes) introspection native listing declared slots and which patterns override them; (3) soft size cap with diagnostic for pathological slot values (serialized per pattern, so a huge list bloats every overriding scene). Spec: 'Open questions'.

title: Jaki builder panel: defscene proving ground
description: UI frontend for jaki patterns: (defscene jb-figures ...), figures rendered gvr-style (each + dropdowns for modifiers like 'fast 2' / 'every 4 swap' / 'stac'), edit handlers are plain set!, channel-register published ONCE at load with (run jb-figures) — body resolved per pattern at tick time, so scenes carry different patterns with no republish. Validates all three seams + undo end to end. Spec: 'Worked example'.

description: set! on a scene slot routes through the history host-command pattern: one command per committed edit carrying (pattern id, slot name, old, new); drag-style continuous edits coalesce to one command on release. Undo/redo re-dirty via the reactive seam's targeted invalidation, no ui_epoch bump. Spec: 'Undo'; playbook: undo-drag invalidation pattern.

Do NOT add :run-source to def-process — superseded by expand-before-ship. Spec: 'Migration'.

Add a macroexpand native for the scratch buffer as the debugging story. Spec: 'Source mapping'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deterministic site-keyed gensym
description: (gensym base) in expanders derives its suffix from expansion-site identity (buffer, ordinal, optional :key — same convention as widget keys/process IDs) plus an in-expansion counter. Same site+source => same symbols (re-eval stable for source-identity diffing); distinct sites never collide. Full hygiene explicitly out of scope. Spec: 'Rule 3'.

title: Inline channel widgets show a live numeric readout
description: When a scheduler/process drives a :chan inline slider or knob, show the current mirrored value next to/in the control. Do not rewrite the source literal: it remains the persistence fallback and divergence reference; the readout is display-only and must update from the widget's live value prop.

title: Scheduler to UI channel mirror: a process visibly drives a slider
description:
Phase 6 of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md (rev 2), section 8.1.
Optional and separable -- phases 1-4 already give a slider that drives a
process; this is the reverse.

WHAT WORKS ALREADY (as of eseq-jo7.8, commit 12ebc56e): slider -> process.
send_channel_at calls propagate_source_at, which writes patched
ProcessTargetRef::Inlet targets directly and then walks every running
instance's listens via listener_invocations_for_source; the section 7 drain
feeds the resulting invocations into the lookahead cascade.

WHAT DOES NOT: process -> slider. Phase 1's __inline-read returns an echo of
the author's last write, falling back to the declared initial, and
deliberately does not read the scheduler-side value.

Work: publish a channel-value snapshot on SequencerState going scheduler -> UI
(the mirror of the eseq-jo7.8 pending-write queue), and have __inline-read
prefer it over the echo. The polling half already exists --
refresh_inline_widget_runtime_values invokes __inline-read per binding and
pushes results through set_inline_widget_live_value.

NO DRAG SUPPRESSION. Do not add a guard that pauses the mirror while a widget
is being dragged. It is the UI special-casing that section 8 rules out, moved
into the display layer; it defers the conflict rather than resolving it (the
value snaps away on release instead of during the drag); "actively dragging"
is mode state that sticks on lost pointer capture, focus change, or a modal
opening mid-drag, leaving a slider permanently deaf; and it staleness-traps the
divergence flag, which set_inline_widget_live_value only recomputes on update.

Unconditional mirroring is safe and invisible in the common case:
set_inline_widget_live_value never fires on-change (the write path is
apply_widget_output, interaction only) so there is no feedback loop; it returns
false early when value and flag are both unchanged, so echoing your own value
costs no revision bump and no re-render; and it computes diverged as
__inline-text-value != value, comparing against the literal in source rather
than the last write, which self-clears on reconvergence. The slider therefore
moves under your hand only when a process genuinely contends for the value --
which is the case you want surfaced.
close_reason: Fixed autonomous updates for visible inactive source tiles; added exact standalone started :every process coverage and active/inactive frame polling regressions.

title: Customize Tab to toggle sequencer and scratch buffer
description: Update the user's ~/.eseq.d/init.lisp so Tab toggles between the sequencer view and *scratch*, replacing the default arrangement/sequencer toggle only for this user. Validate the init script with the available Lisp/config loading path.
close_reason: Implemented user Tab override targeting only the sequencer tile; updated Vim routing so Tab runs the app command in normal-mode text buffers while Tab and literal character bindings remain editor input in insert mode. Targeted tests pass.

title: jaki memo cap tuning under live channel drag
description:
Phase 5 of docs/jaki-live-channel-widgets-spec.md sections 6 and 11.

With live channel writes, a drag generates many distinct values per second.
Tier A invalidates the 15-entry eval-cycle memo (core.lisp:653) on every
payload-epoch bump; Tier B (eseq-jo7.5) rebuilds a pattern per distinct
structural value, which rekeys all three memos including the 23-entry
lens-memo (core.lisp:712).

Risk being mitigated: if caps are too low, a fast drag on a (* n) slider could
pin the scheduler the way rich patterns did before lens-memo was introduced
(core.lisp:706-709).

Raise memo-store from 15 and lens-memo from 23. The exact numbers are a
measurement, not a design decision -- use the ignored scheduler-tick timing
probe added in b4411cdf as the instrument, with a slider drag as the load.

title: jaki restart/anchor: re-anchor pattern position from a channel epoch
description: Anchor mechanics: store an anchor tick in generator state and evaluate patterns at (- (gen-tick) anchor) in emit* (core.lisp:806). Restart = set anchor to current tick; ensure-state's jump path (core.lisp:765) already restarts threading state from defaults on backward cycle jumps. Channel wiring: a process bumps an epoch counter on a value channel (e.g. coin flip via rand every beat); the jaki tick compares (chan-get epoch) with a stored state cell and re-anchors when it changed. Optional surface sugar later: restart word or :restart flag on (chan ...) to re-anchor on any value change instead of transport-locked phase. Depends on the chan-get native bead.

title: Cache Source-callback compiles for accumulators + midi-fx invokes
description: shared_state.rs:599 (invoke accumulator) and :746 (invoke midi-fx) still eval_str the Source variant per step — same pattern fixed for sequencer ticks in 16cbc6f5 (sequencer_tick_callback lambda cache). Closure-registered callbacks are unaffected; Source arm hits string/data-registered callbacks. Port the (lambda () source) compile cache keyed by identity+source.

title: eseqlisp: variadic + splicing defmacro (jaki/pat sugar)
description: eseqlisp defmacro is a fixed-arity template engine: exactly one quasiquote body, params are bare symbols, no &rest, no unquote-splicing, no expansion-time evaluation (compiler.rs expand_quasiquote). This forced jaki/pat (eseq-5k5) to take quoted data — (jaki/pat '(. . -)) — instead of the spec's variadic (jaki/pat . . -) spelling, and it is the same wall any package author hits when wrapping list-shaped DSLs. Adding &rest params plus ,@ splicing (and ideally gensym) would let jaki/pat become sugar over the existing function with no library changes. See docs/jaki-sequencer-spec.md §11.1.
close_reason: Implemented variadic &rest defmacro parameters, ,@ quasiquote splicing, and variadic jaki/pat sugar; targeted eseqlisp and Jaki tests pass.

title: project_92 owner-switch smoke test panics when the gitignored projects/ fixture is absent
description: sequencer::bin/metal_seq tests::project_92_full_layout_group_track_selection_owner_switch_smoke (added 6844d2dd for eseq-4jv) asserts 'project 92 must be available at crates/sequencer/projects/92.json' (crates/sequencer/src/ui/tests.rs:2499). crates/sequencer/projects/ is gitignored (crates/sequencer/.gitignore:17), so the test fails 100% of the time in any fresh worktree or clone that has not had projects/ populated. The always-run smoke variant should skip (or use a checked-in fixture) when the project file is missing, instead of failing the package suite. Found while reviewing eseq-xpt.1; it fails identically at that bead's parent commit, so it is not a regression from the export work.

title: defhook natives stay flat: decide whether module-owned hooks should qualify
description: Reviewing eseq-xpt.1 surfaced a latent ergonomic gap that the export work touched and then reverted. (defhook "x") inside a named module registers its caller-facing native under the FLAT name x at runtime, while the module's own bare call site (x) compiles first and interns a dead eseq.M/x slot (module-system-spec.md §11 e documents this; ui/macro-state.lisp:24-28 repeats the warning and tells authors to use (run-hook "x") instead). The eseq-xpt.1 worker qualified the native to eseq.M/x, which happens to close that gap and makes (export x) meaningful for hooks; it was reverted in 90ece7fe as out of scope and contradicting the parent spec. Decide deliberately: either (a) keep flat forever and delete the temptation by making a bare in-module hook call a compile error with a 'use run-hook' message, or (b) qualify the native, update module-system-spec.md §11 e + macro-state.lisp's comment, and check every add-hook/run-hook site (all current call sites pass hook names as strings, so the keyspace itself is unaffected). No in-tree lisp or Rust calls a hook native by bare name today, so either direction is safe now.

The current mixer group name uses a label and does not set an icon. Reconcile the UI behavior and regression expectation.

title: Auditioning an instrument onto a selected drum rack targets the stale current track
description:
eseq-4b5.19 made the browser's Kits and Sounds tabs address the selected drum rack (load-kit :group-id / audition-sound-on-rack). The Instruments tab did not change: with a rack selected, double-clicking an instrument still emits the plain load-onto-track command against SEQ.current-track, which is whatever track was selected before the rack. title: Drum rack v2 follow-up: delete vestigial RackRouting runtime enum and dead :routing UI plumbing
description:
From the eseq-4b5.7 review (commit 3f3f488a), two CONFIRMED cleanup findings left behind by the ByPitch deletion:

1. RackRouting (sequencer/data.rs:177) is now a single-variant enum threaded through the rack stack as if routing still varied: the routing field on RackTrackSnapshot, the routing params on RackTrackSnapshot::new / append_rack_slot_* — and guards like rack.routing != RackRouting::Broadcast are statically unreachable (app/graph/rack_slots.rs:359-361 — dead code whose error message still references the deleted v1 pad model — rack_slots.rs:422, app/effects.rs:405). Delete the runtime enum and its field/params; KEEP the serialized ProjectRackRouting enum (legacy by_pitch load) and map it at the deserialization boundary as today.

2. The published :routing reactive prop (ui/state_values/rack_panel.rs ~1238) can only ever be 'broadcast' now; browser.lisp ~291-300 (%current-rack-routing, the (= ... "broadcast") test) uses it purely as a rack-panel-presence flag steering add-layer vs create-new-rack — rename to an honest presence predicate. The drop-meta :routing keys at instrument-panel.lisp 474 and 579 are never read by any drop handler (nor are the :kind keys in the same dicts) — delete them.

Behavior-preserving; all sites verified by the review's adversarial verifiers.
acceptance_criteria: RackRouting runtime enum, its snapshot field, and the unreachable != Broadcast guards are gone; ProjectRackRouting still deserializes legacy by_pitch projects (existing tests pass). The browser rack-presence check no longer masquerades as a routing comparison; unread drop-meta :routing/:kind keys are removed. Workspace builds, scoped sequencer tests pass, Instrument Rack still builds/loads/plays.

title: Drum rack v2 follow-up: harden add-track-rack error path and rack-structure sync focus
description:
From the eseq-4b5.7 review (commit 3f3f488a), two CONFIRMED findings in the retargeted browser creation path:

1. Phantom rack group on error (ui/host_commands/tracks.rs ~183, 'add-track-rack' Err arm): create_drum_rack_recorded commits and records the group+bus FIRST via apply_recorded_bus_group_structure_mutation; if the sample half then fails (add_track on a bad path, pad attach, or commit_created_track), the handler reports 'Error adding drum rack', skips sync_after_rack_structure_change, and rolls nothing back. Result: a recorded rack group exists that the UI does not show and the status message denies. The sibling add-track handler (tracks.rs ~333-344) clones groups and restores them on commit failure — mirror that, or defer the group commit until the member track succeeds. Also: attach errors are collapsed to bool in add_new_track_to_group (host_commands/mod.rs:500), losing the real message.

2. Empty-rack focus hijack (ui/host_commands/drum_rack_v2.rs:229): sync_after_rack_structure_change kept sync_after_kit_load's assumption that the last track is the new one — it unconditionally focuses app.tracks.len()-1. Creating an EMPTY drum rack adds no track, so it focus-hijacks whatever unrelated track happens to be last. Pass the focus target explicitly (Option<usize>) instead.

Minor, same area: the group-name-by-id lookup is duplicated 3x (tracks.rs:173, drum_rack_v2.rs:121, 154) — extract a helper; and 'Add drum rack' with a sample lands as two undo entries (Create drum rack + Add drum rack pad) — defensible, fold only if easy.
acceptance_criteria: Failing sample half of 'Add drum rack' leaves no recorded phantom group (rolled back or committed only on full success), the status message matches reality, and the UI is synced. Creating an empty drum rack does not move track focus to an unrelated track. Scoped sequencer tests cover both paths.
close_reason: Closed

title: Drum rack v2: remove PADS/KIT buttons from the sequencer track header
description:
The PADS and KIT buttons crowding the rack's sequencer header row (user feedback 2026-08-19: 'i dont like the pads vs kits buttons here') should go once their functions have better homes. Current behavior: PADS (ui/sequencer.lisp:1910-1918) toggles the inline %rack-pad-grid via local %pad-grid-open state (:1750-1760, one grid open at a time, bank reset); KIT (:1919-1925) fires 'save-rack-as-kit' (ui/drum-rack-v2.lisp save-kit → host_commands/drum_rack_v2.rs:103-137) — save only; kit LOADING lives in the browser Kits tab (ui/browser.lisp:957-972) and always creates a new rack.

While in there, consider making browser kit-load target the SELECTED rack (fill it) rather than always spawning a new rack — if that's real scope, file it as its own bead rather than expanding this one.

title: TrackCreation undo arm skips macro_engine.remap_after_track_delete
description: The EditPatch::TrackCreation Undo arm in app/edit.rs deletes the created track but never calls macro_engine.remap_after_track_delete(track), unlike the TrackDeletion Redo arm right below it. If the created track was not the highest index at undo time (creation moves the appended track to patch.index), macro mappings for higher tracks keep stale track indices. Pre-existing, noticed during eseq-4b5.4 review when the group-remap half of the same gap was fixed (commit 39eb9b6c).

title: Print mode: clamp *step* buffer Duration picker range to 0.125-2 while recording
description:
Follow-up to live step-param printing (eseq-jc9). While recording (i.e. whenever the *step* buffer's params are in the print-mode context — transport playing + record on), the Duration numberpicker in the *step* buffer should use a restricted range of 0.125 to 2, instead of its normal full range. Rationale: this makes printing far more expressive as a performance gesture — the full range wastes most of the drag/scroll travel on values that are useless while jamming: printing a duration of 0 must be impossible (it kills the hit), and durations above 2 don't matter for this use case (it's mostly a drum workflow). With the range clamped to 0.125-2, the whole travel of the picker maps to musically useful lengths.

Scope: only the Duration picker, and only while the recording print context is active — outside recording the picker keeps its normal full range and behavior. When record/play ends, the control returns to the full range without snapping the underlying value (a value legitimately outside 0.125-2 that was set before recording should not be clobbered by merely entering/leaving record mode; entering print mode clamps only what the user actually dials from then on). If eseq-jc9 lands a distinct armed/print state, gate on that state's availability (record+playing) rather than inventing a second condition.
acceptance_criteria: While transport is playing with record on, the *step* buffer Duration numberpicker's dialable range is exactly 0.125 to 2 (cannot dial or type outside it, so 0 can never be printed); Transpose and Velocity pickers are unaffected; outside recording the Duration picker has its normal full range; toggling record/play does not itself alter an existing duration value, including values outside the clamped range; printed durations from a full drag sweep span 0.125 to 2.
close_reason: Duration picker now uses a 0.125-2 range only during playing+recording print context, with regression coverage for unaffected controls and value preservation.

title: Modulated-value display for all modulatable params (knobs, curve visualizers)
description:
Generalize the Filter Table effective-spectrum work (eseq-dtx.13) into a UI-wide capability: any parameter that can be modulated (mods-tab LFOs/envelopes on builtin effects and synths) shows its live MODULATED value in the UI, not just its base knob value — like Ableton's modulation indicators. Two display surfaces: (1) knobs — render the effective value as a secondary indicator on the ring (base value stays where the user set it; a lighter/animated marker or arc shows the live modulated position); (2) curve/spectrum visualizers — any panel that draws a curve derived from params (filter curves, EQ8, phaser-flanger notches, filterbank, compressor knee, etc.) re-evaluates with effective values, reusing whatever seam eseq-dtx.13 lands.

Build on eseq-dtx.13's plumbing and generalize it rather than inventing a second path: the host mod matrix is the single interception point — publish a per-node sparse snapshot of (param index -> effective value) for params whose effective value differs from base, sampled at UI-tick rate, via the node-state→widget pattern (OTT/Compressor meters precedent). The knob widget then needs one generic extension (an optional 'modulated value' input rendering the secondary indicator), so every panel gets knob display for free; curve visualizers opt in per-widget by reading effective values where they currently read base params.

Scoping guidance for the worker: do knobs generically first (one widget change + plumbing = coverage everywhere), then convert curve visualizers incrementally starting with the panels where modulation is most audible (filter, phaser-flanger, filterbank). Perf rules carry over from eseq-dtx.13: zero cost when nothing is modulated, dirty-widget redraw path only, no audio-thread work beyond bounded lock-free writes. Watch the drag interaction: while the user drags a knob, base-value editing must stay authoritative and the mod indicator must not fight the drag (see p-lock knob drag perf work for the epoch/echo gotchas).
acceptance_criteria: Knob widgets across builtin effect/synth panels show a secondary live indicator at the modulated value whenever their param is modulated, with the base value still shown and editable; at least two curve visualizers beyond Filter Table (e.g. filter and phaser-flanger) animate with effective values; unmodulated UI has zero new per-frame cost; dragging a knob whose param is modulated remains smooth and edits the base value; implementation reuses/extends the eseq-dtx.13 seam (single mod-matrix interception, node-state→widget publication) rather than adding a parallel mechanism.

title: Order builtin effects alphabetically in effect lists
description:
The builtin insert effects currently appear in an ad-hoc historical order (Filter, EQ8, Delay, Str8 Delay, Space Echo, Dimension, Phaser-Flanger, Roar, DJ Mixer, Reverb, Multiverb, 444 Compressor, Glue Compressor, Compressor, OTT, Limiter, Tape, Filterbank, ...). Make every user-facing list of builtin effects alphabetical.

The canonical source is EffectDescriptor::builtin_insert_names() in crates/sequencer/src/effects/mod.rs (~line 2413). Before reordering, check what consumes this order: (a) the effect browser / add-effect picker (see docs/browser-builtin-flattening-spec.md and the browser tab rail work) and any other dropdowns/menus that enumerate builtins; (b) whether anything depends on positional indices into this slice (serialization uses names via canonical_builtin_insert_name / BUILTIN_INSERT_PREFIX, so reordering the array itself should be safe, but verify no test or UI code indexes it positionally). Either sort the array in place or sort at display time — prefer sorting the canonical array so every consumer inherits the order, and fix up any order-sensitive tests (effects/mod.rs tests around lines 1499/2419 assert list contents). Also confirm newer builtins registered elsewhere (e.g. Filter Table, UZU, spectral effects, conv reverb) appear in whatever list the browser shows and end up in the same alphabetical ordering — if they come from a second registry, apply the same sort there or at the merge point.
acceptance_criteria: Every UI surface that lists builtin effects (effect browser/picker, any add-effect dropdown) shows them in case-insensitive alphabetical order, including builtins registered outside builtin_insert_names(); existing projects still load every builtin by name (no positional-index breakage); affected list-content tests updated and passing.
close_reason: Alphabetized native builtin effect names and centralized case-insensitive sorting across merged native/DGenLisp UI effect lists; targeted tests pass.

title: Roll phase 5: capture roll gestures into song/takes
description:
Spec: docs/rolling-core-spec.md §7 (Song/arrangement capture note), §9 phase 5. The original (zequencer/visual-sampler) recorded SequenceRollEvents with nested rate changes into the mix; eseq should ride the existing takes capture path.

Scope: design + implement event capture of roll gestures during song/take recording so they replay in the arrangement. Track-roll HITS are already recorded as pattern/take notes by phase 3; this bead is about the sequence-roll gesture itself (window looping over time, rate switches) and any gesture-level representation the takes model needs. Out of scope for v1 per the spec — this is the follow-on; expect design work: decide event representation, replay seam (likely driving the same RollCommand channel from arrangement playback), and interaction with quantized launch/scene rows. Regular rolling remains unserialized.
acceptance_criteria: While song/take recording, roll gestures (sequence-roll press/release with nested rate changes, and track-roll performances) are captured as events on the takes capture path so arrangement playback reproduces the performance; live rolling is otherwise unserialized (pure performance state per spec §7).

title: Roll phase 4: polish (per-track participation, exact cancel, UI bracket, MIDI pads)
description:
Spec: docs/rolling-core-spec.md §8, §9 phase 4. Polish on top of phases 1-3.

Items (each independently shippable):
- Per-track participation: the original's Roll Effect setting per track — always-on / always-off / synced — plus a 0.125-8x per-track rate factor (original: getFactoredResolution). Applies to which tracks capture window_start in §5.1 and which tracks emit track-roll hits.
- Exact cancel: stamp RollState.generation onto enqueued roll events; audio-callback pop drops events whose generation predates the last NoteOff/ClearAll — removes the one trailing hit the lookahead-horizon cancel (phase 1) can leak. Only needed if the horizon proves audibly too long; verify first.
- UI: roll-window bracket on track lanes / step rows driven by the SEQ.roll-window reactive (per-track start_beats,len_beats — published in phase 2); UI playhead already loops the window. Momentary UI roll buttons (the original's RollButtons) for touch/mouse parity.
- MIDI pad mapping with hold-refcount (original: rollingCount) so multiple pads mapping to the same roll voice don't drop the roll on first release.
acceptance_criteria: Per-track roll participation (always-on / always-off / synced) with a 0.125x-8x per-track rate factor works for both track and sequence rolling; audio-side generation-stamp check drops stale trailing roll hits so NoteOff cancel is exact; roll-window bracket renders on track lanes/step rows from SEQ.roll-window while sequence-rolling; MIDI pad mapping drives rolls with a hold-refcount so overlapping pads behave; momentary UI roll buttons give touch/mouse parity.

title: E: surface total output latency in the UI
description:
Nothing tells the user their project is running 46ms late.

LatencyPlan::mix_latency (app/graph/latency.rs:65) is the honest total and is
currently read by nobody outside that file. The only user-facing mention of
latency anywhere is a Filter Table engine tooltip
(ui/effects/builtin/filter-table.lisp:263-264), which says "PDC-compensated
latency" vs "zero latency" -- accurate, but it undersells that choosing
Spectral delays the ENTIRE project, not just that track.

Worth showing the number somewhere persistent (transport or mixer), and worth
rewording that tooltip once the number is visible.

Depends on eseq-lat.3 only in the sense that both want mix_latency published
out of the planner; do that once and serve both.
notes: Implemented graph-wide output latency publication to SEQ.output-latency-ms and a persistent OUT …ms transport readout. The reactive is initialized from SequencerState, diff-published after each PDC refresh, and backed by a public pdc_latency_seconds accessor. Added a finite/nonzero render-bound layout regression. Updated the Filter Table engine documentation to state Spectral delays the entire project output (the referenced 'tooltip' is currently a source comment; no generic tooltip prop exists). Validation: targeted transport layout test, latency-plan test, and recording latency composition test pass under nextest; inspected /tmp/metal-seq-output-latency.png from metal_seq capture.
close_reason: Implemented and validated persistent total output latency display in transport

title: E: sidechain taps and bus meters read pre-PDC
description:
Two places read the signal upstream of its compensation pad, so they see
audio that is misaligned against the compensated mix.

Sidechain: app/effects.rs:2827-2836 connects
track_node_ids[src].delay_id -- the track fx output, BEFORE the primary-edge
PDC node -- straight into the destination effect's sidechain input. The key is
therefore skewed against the program material by whatever pad the source
track carries. Bus sidechains have the same shape at effects.rs:2902-2937.

Metering: watchlist meters attach to merge_id/gate_id/volume_id
(app/graph/bus_routing.rs:105-107, audio/engine.rs:307-309), all upstream of
the bus PDC node inserted at bus_routing.rs:117. audio_tap.rs reads its ring
with no pad offset either. So bus meters show pre-compensation audio.

Neither corrupts the mix; both make the tools lie about it. Fix by tapping
post-pad, or by offsetting the reader by the known pad.
