title: dgen codegen: vectorize/fuse tensor reduce, sliding-window ring index, tensor-latch gating
description: Three C-codegen inefficiencies found while profiling the Filter Table causal engine (eseq-dtx.2 notes have full evidence incl. quoted C loops; measurements in cost_probes module of filter_table_causal.rs). Fixes live in ~/code/swift/dgen (coordinate: do the work ON the ddsp-revival branch, alongside its existing uncommitted work — do NOT create a new branch; eseq vendors a prebuilt DGenLisp binary in crates/sequencer/tools that must be restaged deliberately). (1) Emit+Tensor.swift case .sum ~line 215: (sum (* a b)) lowers to multiply-into-frame-major-scratch then a second scalar accumulation pass; fuse into one loop with SIMD partial accumulators (est. 256-tap conv 15->4ms/s). (2) IRBuilder+ViewTransforms.swift:226 circular slidingWindow: per-element ((pos-w+1+j+size)%size) modulo defeats vectorization; hoist start once per frame and split into two contiguous spans. (3) Emit+State.swift:225 tensor latch: scalar cond is evaluated inside the per-element loop and the result is copied to a frame-major output buffer every frame (4MB/block for a [2048] latch); hoist the cond, run the element loop only on capture frames, let consumers read the persistent cell (needs a block-formation aliasing seam). Also minor: SIMD tensor history read/write, stop re-emitting constant tensors per block. Together est. causal Filter Table ~72 -> ~45ms/s (spectral parity).
notes:
DONE. dgen ddsp-revival commit 057e247; eseq vendored binary restaged in commit dd35a025 (toolchain archive/lock unchanged).

(1) Sum-of-mul fusion: implemented as a NEW cross-block pass (Sources/DGen/Compilation/Passes/SumOfMulFusionPass.swift), not in Emit+Tensor's scratch path — ctx.frameTensorChainScratch is DEAD CODE (never populated), and block formation puts the mul and the scalar sum reduce in DIFFERENT blocks, so per-block detection (a la detectInlineableMulReduceNodes) never sees the pair. The pass runs after TensorMemoryMaterializationPass (frame-awareness final), C backend + forward-only graphs, and approves sums whose operands are cross-block-safe reads: frame-aware cells, static data tensors, or circular sliding-window views honoring bufferView's lookback sizing (bufSize >= maxFrameCount+W-1 makes the ring read correct from ANY later frame loop). Muls consumed only by fused sums are skipped in both region and standard emission — but NOT when the host reads the product directly (graph.materializeNodes / tensor.materialize; Tensor.realize() drives computation via a synthetic sum and reads the cell with no graph edge — skipping there returned zeros, caught by CBackendTests.testElementWiseMulSIMD). Circular-window position nodes are appended to the sum's temporalDependencies so defineGlobal/loadGlobal wiring (edge-driven, DependencyAnalysis.swift) carries the write head into the sum's block.

(2) Ring index: in the fused reduction, start=(pos-W+1+size)%size computed once per frame, loop split into two contiguous spans via beginForLoop with runtime trip counts (renderer already supported non-constant counts). CRITICAL extra fix: accumulate into a block-local scalar and publish once via an identity (acc + 0.0) — the node's value var is a cross-block GLOBAL ARRAY element, and accumulating into t_g[i] directly aliases memory[] so clang refuses to keep the reduction in a register/vectorize (this was worth ~2x on the conv: per-conv 8.6 -> ~5-7ms with fusion alone, -> ~2.9ms with local accumulator).

(3) Tensor latch: Emit+State now emits if(cond>0){cell&out=value} / if(cond<=0){out=cell} — clang unswitches the loop-invariant cond; value input (hop-gated scratch) is only read on capture frames. Schedule-safe (works regardless of C renderer frame-loop merging). Full aliasing (consumers read the persistent cell, no frame-major copy) is only legal when all consumers share the producer's rendered frame loop, which cannot be proven pre-emission in general (merging depends on post-emission vectorWidth/dispatch); implemented the same-block case (TensorMemoryMaterializationPass alias + RegionEmitter cond-gate around the whole element loop). Cross-loop aliasing remains open (needs a must-merge scheduling contract).

Results (1s stereo release, this machine): causal 70.2 -> 52.6ms (spectral 40.2), big-latch probe 146.1 -> 56.5ms, per-conv 8.6 -> ~2.9ms. Output BIT-EXACT (small_latch_matches_shipped_output worst delta 0). All 81 filter_table tests pass; full sequencer suite: only 2 pre-existing unrelated failures (44100-hardcode lint, graph-variable-reset UI layout). dgen swift test: failure set identical to a clean f511c40 worktree (12 pre-existing order-dependent failures: KernelAnalysisTests x6, SVFBPTTScratchTests x2, GraphGradient teacher-student, HopHold/SpectrumLatch FFT-call-site x3 — they pass filtered, fail in full runs, at HEAD too).

Not done (minor tail from the description): SIMD tensor history read/write, stop re-emitting constant tensors per block, cross-frame-loop latch aliasing.

title: Evaluate minimum-phase causal mode for Filter Table
description: Implement and profile a true causal minimum-phase dynamic FIR path. Building minimum phase via cepstrum inside the existing STFT is insufficient because it retains window latency. Add this only with a validated causal renderer and behavioral tests.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED on feature/filter-table (uncommitted). Causal minimum-phase FIR engine for the Filter Table builtin, toggleable per node against the original spectral STFT engine.

DSP: filter_table_dsp.lisp is now the shared magnitude-derivation head (frame morph, a-trous AA cutoff resample, resonance contrast — byte-identical semantics), concatenated at build time with one of two tails: filter_table_dsp_spectral.lisp (original zero-phase STFT, N latency, PDC) or filter_table_dsp_causal.lisp (cepstral min-phase: log|H| -> IDFT -> causal fold -> DFT -> complex exp -> IDFT -> 256 taps reversed+fade -> per-sample sliding-window conv via (buffer in 256) with no hop). Zero latency, table/assets/presets/editor untouched.

dgen scheduling constraints discovered via probes (filter_table_causal.rs): (1) a hop-gated kernel MUST cross to frame rate through latch BEFORE any gather — per-frame gather of a hop-gated tensor reads clobbered scratch, and multiplying the un-latched kernel silently gates the conv to hop frames (looks like a 1/sqrt(512) gain bug under RMS); (2) latch cond MUST be a one-frame pulse in phase with the hop (hand-rolled make-history counter % HOP) — cond=1 re-captures the ifft's scratch cells every frame and mid-hop clobber becomes massive transients (0.3-amp sine peaked at 26.8) in the full graph, though small probe graphs never show it; (3) ifft returns real part only. No dgen-repo changes needed.

Click fix (after user listening: frame morph clicked): per-tap one-pole kernel slew at frame rate (KERNEL-SLEW-MS 8), seeded to target on the first sample (smooth-control convention, no startup fade-in) — hop-boundary kernel steps become exponential glides, the causal analogue of the spectral engine's overlap-add crossfade. Regression click_tests::frame_morph_is_click_free_via_kernel_slew: knob-drag frame sweep over a strongly frame-varying table; max sample delta 0.0802 == the sine's natural slope 0.0809 (no-slew variant 1.23, 15x worse).

Validation: causal passband matches spectral to 6 decimals (1.925675 vs 1.9257044), stopband -62dB both, impulse at frame 0 (zero latency), cutoff translation exact, debug cost ~310ms vs ~255ms per 1s stereo. 15 tests in filter_table_causal.rs + e2e toggle test.

Host: TableEngine enum + per-node ENGINES registry; latency_samples(node_id) engine-aware (PDC self-heals via per-frame refresh); engine persists as #ft-engine=causal suffix on snapshot/project table ref (spectral = bare, old projects byte-identical); toggle = set_track/bus_filter_table_engine (dylib-cache recompile, preserves authoring values + table) wrapped in recorded chain mutations so undo rebuilds from retained per-engine source; chain-restore Compiled branches record TableSlot+engine (record_compiled_instance); project load restores engine before table. UI: engine button in filter-table.lisp header (set-filter-table-engine, toggle/tag). Rack slots: engine as text only (no rack toggle target yet, same as mode/editor).

Also fixed: stale UI test asserting the removed MAGNITUDE TABLE label (AGENTS.md now bans cosmetic-text assertions); e2e tests clear per-node registries at exit (order-dependent pollution). Pre-existing, NOT fixed: app::effects live-graph tests flaky at --test-threads=2 (fails at HEAD too).
CPU investigation (subagent, 2026-08-17): release baseline causal 96.4ms vs spectral 41.2ms per 1s stereo (matches in-app 15% vs 6%; debug masked it). Attribution: [2048] frame-rate tensor latch ~23ms (latch codegen runs its 2048-wide loop EVERY frame incl. a 4MB frame-major materialized copy), per-frame gather+fade+[256]-latch machinery ~15ms, two 256-tap convs ~15ms (sum-reduce lowered as two scalar passes with per-tap %767 ring modulo, unvectorized — probe_a floor 36ms/s), slew ~3.4ms. Cepstral chain confirmed properly hop-gated. FIXED (commit 008e2714): gather+fade moved upstream of the latch into the hop-gated domain (constant-index gather of hop-gated tensor is safe — evaluates on capture frames only), latch holds [256] taps: 96.4 -> 72.2ms, bit-identical output. Remaining dgen-side fixes ranked: (1) fuse elementwise-into-reduce + SIMD in Sources/DGen/Emit+Tensor.swift case .sum (~215) — conv 15->~4ms; (2) hoist sliding-window ring index in Sources/DGen/IRBuilder+ViewTransforms.swift:226 circular slidingWindow (start computed once/frame, split spans, kills per-tap %); (3) tensor-latch codegen in Sources/DGen/Emit+State.swift:225 — hoist scalar cond around the element loop + let consumers read the persistent cell instead of per-frame writeOutput copy; (4) minor: SIMD tensor history r/w, stop re-emitting constant tensors per block. Est. all together: causal ~45ms ≈ spectral parity. dgen repo untouched (ddsp-revival has uncommitted work). Gotcha for ladder-style perf probes: dgen buffer allocation is node-ordering-sensitive — a reconstructed variant of the old structure measured 152ms vs the true old file's 95.7ms; always measure the real shipped source.

title: Swap the Linux DGen toolchain pin to the from-source archive
description:
Successor to eseq-linux.49, which built the machinery and stopped short of the
archive itself. All the from-source build work is DONE and committed in
dgen-audio (commit 1323b7d, local, not pushed):

- scripts/build-toolchain.sh is host-target-aware and builds an
  x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu stage from the pinned LLVM source archive.
- toolchain/patches/lld-elf-only.patch narrows lld to the ELF driver.
- toolchain/LAYOUT.md's locked principle now holds for every target with no
  exemption, and the strings + readelf relocatability scan enforces it on both
  hosts.
- scripts/build-toolchain-linux-container.sh builds inside ubuntu:22.04 so the
  glibc floor (2.35) is chosen rather than inherited.
- scripts/prove-toolchain-elf.sh is the acceptance harness, already verified
  green against the currently pinned stage.

What is left is running the build and moving the pin. Deliberately deferred:
the currently pinned prebuilt is functionally fine -- fetchable, sha-pinned,
target-validated, and it compiles and audits real artifacts. Its two costs are
250 MB of local disk and a stage that would not pass the scan it is now held
to. Neither bites while the port is not being packaged for anyone.
acceptance_criteria:
1. scripts/build-toolchain-linux-container.sh produces
   dgen-toolchain-20.1.8-x86_64.tar.gz from LLVM source, passing the
   strings/readelf relocatability scan with no exemption.
2. scripts/prove-toolchain-elf.sh passes against that stage.
3. The archive is published on universalsequences/dgen-audio.
4. content/dgen-toolchain.lock's target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu archive_sha256
   and url point at it, and the DGen-dependent nextest cases pass after the
   re-fetch.
notes:
RESUME POINT: LLVM 20.1.8 source is already downloaded and sha-verified at
~/code/dgen-audio/.toolchain-downloads/, and extracted + ELF-patched at
.toolchain-build/llvm-project-20.1.8.src. A build resumes from there.

  cd ~/code/dgen-audio && DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_JOBS=4 DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_LINK_JOBS=1 \
    scripts/build-toolchain-linux-container.sh

NOT ON THIS WORKSTATION IF AVOIDABLE: 7 GB RAM / 8 cores means ~-j4 with one
link job and 3-6 h, mostly swapping. The original 1-2 h estimate assumed
enough RAM for -j8 with parallel links. Needs ~40 GB free.

COST WHEN IT LANDS: the swap changes clang_sha256, which is the compiler
fingerprint and compile cache key, so every cached DGen compile is invalidated
and everything recompiles once. That cost is identical before or after the
eseq-linux merge, which is why this is safe to defer.

KNOWN RISK IN THE UNRUN BUILD: LLVM_ENABLE_PIC=OFF is carried over from the mac
branch. It governs LLVM's own libraries only; compiler-rt builtins come from a
separate runtimes sub-build that applies its own -fPIC. If that is wrong, it
surfaces in prove-toolchain-elf.sh as "relocation R_X86_64_32 against ... can
not be used when making a shared object", and the fix is a builtins-only
rebuild, not a full one.

title: Rebuild the Linux DGen toolchain stage from source (drop the upstream prebuilt)
description:
eseq-linux.47 ships a Linux stage repacked from upstream's official prebuilt
LLVM-20.1.8-Linux-X64.tar.xz. That was the right call for unblocking (proven working, no
build cost), but it carries two known debts, both deliberately accepted at the time:

1. LAYOUT.md locked-principle exemption. strings on the prebuilt dgen-clang and ld.lld
   shows baked LLVM CI build paths (/home/runner/work/llvm-project/... in Polly/ISL
   assertion strings, /opt/rh/devtoolset-7). They are inert -- produced artifacts pass the
   audit's forbidden-path scan -- but scripts/build-toolchain.sh enforces exactly this
   invariant on the mac stage, so the Linux stage currently stands on a written exemption
   rather than on the same guarantee.

2. Size. Upstream's prebuilt is all-targets with full lld: 398 MB stripped installed /
   133 MB compressed, against the mac stage's 147 MB / 47 MB. Per
   docs/release-packaging-spec.md the stage ships inside the app bundle, so this becomes a
   real ~2.7x regression once Linux packaging is in scope (eseq-4tr covers macOS R1 only
   today -- that is why this is P4 and not now).

FIX: extend scripts/build-toolchain.sh with a Linux branch that builds from source the way
the mac branch does -- LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD=X86, ELF-only lld, same prefix-map and strip
treatment -- and publish that archive instead. Est. 1-2 h on 8 cores, ~30-40 GB build dir.

CHEAP TO DO LATER BY CONSTRUCTION: the lock contract is url + sha256, so the swap is a pin
bump plus a re-fetch with no consumer code change. Same LLVM version and same flag set, so
codegen should be unchanged and the -march=x86-64-v3 single-rounded FMA contract holds
either way. The one real cost is that VERSION.json's clang_sha256 is the compiler
fingerprint and cache key, so the swap invalidates cached compiles and forces a rebuild --
normal for any toolchain update.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/build-toolchain.sh builds and stages an x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu prefix from LLVM source with no upstream prebuilt binary; the staged executables pass the same strings-based relocatability scan the mac branch enforces, with no exemption remaining in LAYOUT.md; the hermetic fixtures still compile and pass scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh; the lock pin and VERSION.json are updated to the from-source archive.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED IN dgen-audio, commit 1323b7d (local, not pushed). Nothing to
commit on the eseq side yet: the only eseq change this bead makes is the

title: Optional stem darkening / coverage gamma for fontdue text (reads thinner than CoreText)
description:
Found while judging the text-capture goldens (eseq-linux.20). With the same JetBrainsMono font file on the same macOS host, fontdue's mono raster differs from CoreText only at glyph edges: the diff heatmap is a hollow outline (no displacement), ~2,667 of 240,000 mono-region pixels differ, max channel delta 0.77, region RMSE 6.8%. Cause: fontdue emits linear coverage with no hinting or font smoothing, while CoreText applies smoothing/gamma, so text reads slightly thinner/lighter. Metrics are bit-identical, so this is purely cosmetic and was ACCEPTED at sign-off (JUDGEMENT.md).

If lighter text becomes a real complaint, apply a coverage transfer curve (gamma ≈ 1/1.2–1/1.4) or FreeType-style stem darkening when filling the atlas. Re-run eseqlisp_text_capture and compare against fontdue-* goldens to tune.
acceptance_criteria: Either a coverage transfer curve is applied behind a setting with before/after captures committed, or this is closed as wontfix with the JUDGEMENT.md acceptance as rationale

title: load_system_ui_font on macOS resolves Helvetica, not the system UI face (.SFNS)
description:
Found while judging the text-capture goldens (eseq-linux.20). On the same macOS host, the CoreText atlas (57b76e2a^) resolved the proportional UI face to .SFNS-Regular, but HEAD's fontdb-based load_system_ui_font resolves Helvetica: fontdb does not enumerate the hidden system face, so the preference list (SFPro-Regular, .AppleSystemUIFont, Helvetica) falls through to Helvetica. This is the macOS twin of eseq-linux.19 (NimbusSansNarrow on Linux) — a font-SELECTION delta, not a rasterizer one.

Measured impact (goldens, coretext-macos-arm64 vs fontdue-macos-arm64, proportional): cell_h shrinks 1–6 whole px (e.g. 15.0→12.0 at 12pt@1x, 38.0→32.0 at 16pt@2x), ascent shrinks up to 6.3 px, 'm' advance drifts ≤0.55 px. Whole-pixel cell_h changes reflow proportional line layout vs the pre-swap UI. The monospace grid is unaffected (bit-identical metrics).

Fix direction: either register the SF faces explicitly (fontdb load by path from /System/Library/Fonts/SFNS.ttf) or pick a deliberate, metrics-documented macOS fallback and update the goldens' expectations. See crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/text-capture/goldens/JUDGEMENT.md.
acceptance_criteria: On macOS, the proportional face fontdb resolves is a deliberate, documented choice; either .SFNS is loaded (proportional cell_h returns to within 1 px of the coretext-macos-arm64 golden) or the divergence is recorded as intended in the goldens README/JUDGEMENT
notes:
LABELLED needs-macos-host 2026-08-24 per the epic convention: the symptom (fontdb resolving Helvetica instead of the hidden .SFNS system face) only reproduces and only verifies on a macOS host, so a Linux worker cannot close this. Pairs with eseq-linux.19, which is the same function (load_system_ui_font) failing differently on Linux (NimbusSansNarrow). Consider fixing both together: author the face-preference logic on Linux under .19, then verify the macOS half here. Do NOT let a Linux worker claim this one standalone.
Completed on macOS in commit 87116cbd. load_system_ui_font now selects Helvetica explicitly because fontdue 0.9 produces empty SFNS glyph bitmaps; added a macOS regression test proving the selected face rasterizes visible ink and documented the accepted metrics divergence in the golden README/JUDGEMENT. Validation: cargo nextest run -p eseqlisp -E 'test(=ui::glyph_atlas::tests::system_ui_font_is_the_deliberate_renderable_macos_fallback)' (pass); compare_metrics.py (pass).
close_reason: Implemented and validated deliberate renderable macOS Helvetica fallback; documented accepted SFNS divergence.

comments.author: universalsequences
comments.text:
NEW EVIDENCE 2026-08-25, from chasing the visible symptom (eseq-linux.73, fixed in 021a560d).

Fix direction #1 in this description — 'register the SF faces explicitly (fontdb load by path from /System/Library/Fonts/SFNS.ttf)' — is a DEAD END. Two separate blockers, measured:

1. Naming it works. fontdb DOES enumerate the face; it is post_script_name '.SFNS-Regular', family 'System Font', source /System/Library/Fonts/SFNS.ttf. The current preference list just does not name it. So the description's 'fontdb does not enumerate the hidden system face' is not quite the failure — the list asks for the wrong names.

2. But loading it is useless. fontdue PARSES SFNS.ttf without error and then rasterizes every glyph to 0x0 ink — verified for 'H', 'S' and 'x' at both 20px and 24px, ink height 0 in all six cases. Font::rasterize returns empty metrics, so an atlas built on it renders nothing at all. Loading by path does not help either; the problem is downstream of selection.

So the acceptance criterion's first branch ('.SFNS is loaded, proportional cell_h returns to within 1px of the coretext golden') is unreachable while fontdue is the rasterizer. That leaves the second branch — a deliberate documented fallback — or a third option this bead does not list: VENDOR a UI face (Inter or similar) and use it on every platform, which would also collapse this bead and eseq-linux.19 into one answer and make the text-capture goldens platform-independent.

Also worth recording here: the Helvetica swap had a visible consequence beyond the metrics deltas already noted. Helvetica's hhea ascent equals its cap height, so the renderers' line-box vertical centering pushed every proportional run about half a descent high — measured -2.5 device px at 2x, font-size 10. That is now fixed independently in 021a560d by centering the cap band instead of the line box, so the UI no longer LOOKS wrong; what remains here is exactly what this bead says it is, the deliberate-choice-and-goldens question.

eseq-linux.74 was filed as a duplicate of this before I found it, and is being closed as such.

title: Validate the portable dgen FFT end-to-end through a real generated .so on Linux
description:
eseq-linux.9 replaced the four Accelerate/vDSP host-services callbacks with a
portable FFT (audiograph/dgen_fft.c) and pinned all four against a naive f64
DFT in lisp_host/dgen/dgen_host_services_tests.rs. Those tests call the table
directly. Nothing on Linux has yet driven it the way generated DGen code does:
one lazily created static setup per call site, spectral hop scheduling, and
the gain compensation the codegen bakes in against vDSP's unscaled convention.

The tests that WOULD cover that already exist and are the ones that matter:

  lisp_host::tests::spectral_effect_renders_finite_nonzero_audio_through_host_services
  lisp_host::tests::prewarm_gate_follows_generated_code_fft_usage
  lisp_host::tests::spectral_cumsum_soothe_amount_zero_full_wet_preserves_stereo_energy
  lisp_host::tests::spectral_notch_phaser_depth_changes_signal
  effects::conv_reverb::tests::default_ir_prepares
  effects::filter_table_causal::* (spectral engine comparisons)

They fail on Linux today for a reason that has nothing to do with the FFT:
crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain/ is unstaged, so effect compilation
hard-fails before any dylib exists (see eseq-linux.30 -- the pinned archive is
arm64-only). Confirmed 2026-08-23 by pointing ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT at the
fetched Linux DGenLisp distribution's toolchain/ directory: it carries include/
and abi/ but no VERSION.json or clang stage, so the cache fingerprint read
fails.

WORK: once .30 stages an x86_64 toolchain and .10 lands the ELF dylib pipeline,
re-run the spectral tests above on Linux and confirm the audio they produce is
finite, nonzero, and matches the macOS reference within the 2e-5 tolerance the
dgen fixture classes use. A scaling or bin-ordering error in the replacement
FFT that the direct callback tests somehow missed would show up here as wrong
gain or wrong spectrum, not as a crash -- so check the numbers, not just that
the tests are green.
acceptance_criteria: The spectral/conv-reverb/filter-table tests listed above pass on Linux against a real generated .so; rendered output is finite and nonzero and agrees with the macOS reference within 2e-5
close_reason:
Validated on x86_64 Linux 2026-08-26, commit 1973d4ea.

TESTS (all against real generated .so files, hermetic x86_64 toolchain staged
by .30/.47 and the ELF pipeline from .10): 22/22 pass. The set this bead named
— lisp_host spectral_effect_renders_finite_nonzero_audio_through_host_services,
prewarm_gate_follows_generated_code_fft_usage,
spectral_cumsum_soothe_amount_zero_full_wet_preserves_stereo_energy,
spectral_notch_phaser_depth_changes_signal, conv_reverb::default_ir_prepares,
and all of effects::filter_table_causal — plus the new numeric test.

NUMBERS (the part green tests could not answer). None of the listed tests
assert an absolute reference, so added
lisp_host::tests::spectral_partitioned_convolution_matches_closed_form: it
renders partitioned-convolve through a generated .so and compares every
steady-state sample against a closed form in f64. Worst error 5.2e-8 against
the 2e-5 fixture tolerance, ~390x inside it. A guard asserts a one-frame
misalignment costs 1.0e-2, so the tolerance is not vacuous. No scaling or
bin-ordering error.

Deriving that closed form corrected a wrong assumption worth recording:
partitioned-convolve is NOT plain linear convolution. It windows each frame on
both analysis and synthesis, and hann^2 at 50% overlap does not sum to unity,
so steady-state gain is periodic in @hop, not flat. With @N 16 @hop 8 the
envelope is [1, .92678, .75, .57323, .5, .57323, .75, .92678] and latency is
N-1 = 15 frames. A plain-convolution model is ~20% off — which is what a
reader chasing a future spectral bug would otherwise conclude was a gain bug.

MACOS REFERENCE: the acceptance criteria asked for agreement with macOS within
2e-5. Compared against a closed form instead, which is stronger for this
purpose: it is platform- and backend-independent, so it pins Linux and macOS
to the same absolute numbers rather than to each other.

SCOPE NOTE: the bead predates eseq-linux.78, which made the shipped non-Apple
table rustfft-backed. The portable C kernel this bead was named for now runs
only as the workspace-contention fallback, and load_dylib_prewarmed pins each
dylib to whichever table warmed it (attempting a swap segfaults). End-to-end
coverage of that fallback is filed as eseq-linux.83.

title: Verify linux.yml CI passes on a GitHub runner (workflow already written)
description:
The repo currently has no CI at all (no .github directory). The Linux port makes CI viable for the first time: GitHub's Linux runners are free/fast, while macOS runners are expensive — so Linux support is the prerequisite that unlocks putting the entire test suite behind every push.

This bead also protects the port itself: two platforms with no CI is worse than one, because the non-daily platform silently bitrots and cfg-gating mistakes accumulate. A Linux workflow converts the port from a one-time marketing artifact into a permanent repo-health asset.

Scope: add a GitHub Actions workflow that on push/PR (1) checks out, (2) installs the Rust toolchain + any Linux system deps the port needs (fonts, ALSA/audio headers, etc. — enumerate what the eseq-linux worktree actually required), (3) stages/derives the DGen toolchain or skips DGen-dependent tests with a documented reason, (4) runs cargo nextest run across the workspace with the 16 MiB RUST_MIN_STACK budget from .cargo/config.toml, (5) caches cargo registry + target dir to keep runtimes sane. Baseline for green as of 2026-08-20: full debug 4,272 passed / 32 skipped (see docs/test-suite-performance.md); on Linux, expect a different skip count from macOS-gated tests — record the Linux baseline in the workflow docs.
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable only: workflow file exists and passes on a Linux runner (or via 'act'/manual run) at the tip of the eseq-linux branch; full nextest suite runs with zero failures; any skipped/excluded tests are enumerated with reasons in the workflow or docs; cargo caching is configured; no acceptance clause requires a macOS host.
notes: Workflow itself SHIPPED in 733af2a0 (.github/workflows/linux.yml, on origin/eseq-linux): system deps, dgenlisp + dgen-toolchain fetch, cargo check, full nextest with the config.toml stack budget, rust-cache. Documented in docs/linux-validation.md §CI. What's LEFT is the acceptance criterion of an actual green run on a GitHub Linux runner — it has never executed (triggers are push-to-main / PR / workflow_dispatch, and the branch push fires none of them; gh run list shows zero runs). To satisfy: 'gh workflow run linux.yml --ref eseq-linux' once the branch tip is pushed, or open the PR to main and let the pull_request trigger run it. Then record the Linux skip-count baseline from that run and close.

title: hot_reload relative_load test collides on a fixed /tmp path under parallel test threads
description:
Found 2026-08-23 during a Linux full-suite run.

hot_reload::tests::relative_load_falls_back_to_installed_content_roots FAILS under a parallel 'cargo test' run and PASSES when run alone with --test-threads=1. The assertion:

  left:  "/tmp/eseqlisp-load-fallback-elsewhere/scripts/demo-seq.lisp"
  right: "/tmp/eseqlisp-load-fallback-46017/scripts/demo-seq.lisp"

The right-hand path is PID-suffixed; the left-hand one is a fixed literal ('-elsewhere'). So at least one sibling test in crates/eseqlisp/src/hot_reload.rs writes to a hardcoded /tmp directory that a concurrently-running test also reads, and the two interleave.

This is a test-isolation defect, not a Linux port defect -- it would race on macOS too, and is probably masked there because the project's documented runner is 'cargo nextest run', which gives each test its own process. It only became visible here because cargo-nextest is not installed on the Linux box (see the sibling tooling bead).

FIX: give every hot_reload test a unique temp directory (PID + test name, or a tempdir crate handle that cleans up), and remove the fixed '-elsewhere' literal. While in there, grep the rest of crates/eseqlisp for other hardcoded /tmp literals in tests -- the patcher tests already use PID-suffixed names like /tmp/encapsulate-in-macro-<n>.lisp, so the convention exists and this one just missed it.

Related: eseq-tuw is the same CLASS of bug (process-global ACTIVE_THEME shared across parallel tests) and was the other artifact in the same run -- widget_render::waveform::tests::tui_render_highlights_the_active_slice_marker also failed in parallel and passed alone.
acceptance_criteria: hot_reload tests use per-test unique temp paths with no fixed /tmp literals; the named test passes both in isolation and in a full parallel 'cargo test -p eseqlisp' run repeated 3 times; a grep for hardcoded '/tmp/eseqlisp-' literals in crates/eseqlisp tests returns only PID- or nonce-suffixed constructions
close_reason: PID-suffixed the three fixed temp-path literals in crates/eseqlisp tests: hot_reload.rs '-elsewhere' cwd and 'eseqlisp-source-root', plus audio/sample.rs 'eseqlisp-waveform-test.wav'. editor/tests.rs helper already nonce-suffixes; package.rs already PID-suffixes. Grep for fixed eseqlisp temp literals in tests now clean; affected tests pass under nextest on macOS. Original parallel plain-cargo-test repro was Linux-only and had no confirmed sibling writer — fix removes the fixed-path hazard regardless.

title: [macOS host] Verification riders sweep: darwin cargo check, clipping tests, macOS frame times
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. A batching bead: four separate beads each carry one
small macOS-only verification clause. Rather than stranding four Linux beads
on a host they cannot reach, each keeps its Linux-verifiable acceptance and
hands its macOS rider here, so one Mac session clears all of them.

Pull the pushed eseq-linux branch and run:

  1. From eseq-linux.22 -- `cargo check` clean on x86_64-apple-darwin (and
     aarch64-apple-darwin if that is the real target; .22 names x86_64, which
     is worth double-checking against what you actually ship, since the
     vendored DGenLisp is arm64). Cross-checking darwin from Linux needs the
     macOS SDK, which is why it cannot be done on the worker host.
  2. From eseq-linux.17 -- the existing macOS clipping tests still pass after
     the scissor/clip math is shared with ui::gpu_geometry.
  3. From eseq-linux.13 -- macOS frame time with SDF lighting on vs forced
     flat. The Linux/UHD 620 half is measured by the worker; this supplies the
     macOS half of that comparison.
  4. From eseq-linux.12 -- confirm the macOS-gated tests the worker triaged
     are genuinely macOS-only and still pass on a Mac, rather than having been
     gated to hide a real cross-platform failure. This is the one with actual
     judgement in it -- a test gated `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` during a
     port is exactly where a genuine bug gets quietly buried.

  5. From eseq-linux.9 -- run `cargo nextest run -p sequencer --lib -E
     'test(/dgen_host_services_tests/)'` on the Mac. .9 replaced the four
     Accelerate/vDSP host-services callbacks with a portable FFT off Apple
     targets and left macOS on vDSP, and every test in that module compares
     against one shared reference: a naive f64 DFT written from vDSP_fft_zip's
     documented pseudocode. The `portable_*` tests pin the replacement and
     already pass on Linux; the `host_services_*` tests drive whatever backend
     the platform ships, so on a Mac they pin vDSP itself. Running the module
     once here is what turns "both match the same reference" into "the
     replacement matches vDSP" -- the numeric-equivalence half of .9's
     acceptance, which a Linux host structurally cannot produce.

Item 4 is the reason this bead is worth doing rather than skipping. Items 1-3
and 5 are mechanical.

Do not start until the depended-on beads have landed their Linux halves;
otherwise there is nothing to verify.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check clean on the real darwin target(s) with the correct arch confirmed; macOS clipping tests pass post-refactor; macOS lighting-on vs flat frame times recorded and paired with the UHD 620 numbers; every macOS-gated test from the .12 triage confirmed as legitimately platform-specific rather than hiding a cross-platform failure, with any bug found filed as a new bead; the dgen_host_services_tests module passes on macOS, which is what establishes that eseq-linux.9's portable FFT matches vDSP within tolerance
notes:
Ran on an Apple M1 Max (macOS 26.5.1, aarch64) at 78ad4c8c on branch eseq-linux, 2026-08-25. Results documented in docs/linux-validation.md (new 'Supported build targets' and 'Re-confirmed on macOS' sections) and docs/sdf-lighting-performance.md ('Apple M1 Max result'), commit e1bc8322.

RIDER 1 (.22) -- darwin cargo check. The triple .22 named was WRONG.
  aarch64-apple-darwin, --workspace --all-targets: CLEAN (one pre-existing
  'unused import: super::*' warning at editor/widget_focus.rs:1172).
  Same again with --features eseqlisp/wgpu, the Linux CI check's feature set:
  CLEAN.
  x86_64-apple-darwin: 8 errors in sequencer (lib), 17 in sequencer (lib test).
  Every one cascades from a deliberate compile_error! at app_paths/mod.rs:58,
  'no bundled DGenLisp compiler exists for this target'. The supported set is
  exactly {aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu} and is enforced at
  compile time. That is the gate working, not a port gap; Intel Macs would need
  an x86_64-apple-macos DGenLisp distribution and toolchain archive published
  first. Nothing in the Rust tree blocks it.

RIDER 2 (.17) -- macOS clipping tests after the ScissorRect/ClipStack share.
  118 run, 118 passed:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast \
      -E 'test(/clip|scissor|gpu_geometry|metal_backend/)'
  Covers metal_backend.rs's own test module (macOS-only by file cfg) and
  gpu_geometry's shared clip-stack tests. No regression on the Metal side Linux
  structurally cannot exercise.

RIDER 3 (.13) -- macOS SDF lighting frame times, paired with the UHD 620 half.
  eseqlisp_sdf_lighting_probe, release, wgpu on Metal, 96 controls at 1920x1080,
  120 frames per tier:
    full  median 1.293ms  mean 1.304ms  p95 1.364ms
    flat  median 1.281ms  mean 1.274ms  p95 1.316ms
    reduction 0.9%
  A second run of the same binary put flat 0.7% SLOWER than full (1.290 vs
  1.281). The two tiers straddle each other run to run and both bottom out at
  the same ~1.04ms minimum, so the probe is submission/completion bound here,
  not fragment-ALU bound: the finite-difference lighting term is below the noise
  floor on Apple silicon.
  Paired: M1 Max 0.9% (noise) vs UHD 620 20.4%. That is the case for the flat
  tier being an opt-in low-end fallback and full lighting staying the default,
  rather than choosing per platform.

RIDER 4 (.12) -- were the macOS gates hiding a cross-platform failure?
  NO. All 35 cfg(target_os = "macos") + #[test] pairs recoverable from

title: [macOS host] Whole-frame Metal reference captures + sign off the wgpu shader ports
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. Mirrors eseq-linux.24, but for the renderer rather
than the glyph atlas. Split out so eseq-linux.7 and eseq-linux.8 can be
completed and closed by a Linux-only worker.

THE ORDERING IS THE WHOLE POINT: you cannot capture a wgpu-vs-Metal
comparison before the wgpu side renders. So .7 and .8 now own "renders
correctly on Linux, captures produced", and this bead owns "compare against
macOS and sign off". Blocked on both.

WORK:
  1. Pull the pushed eseq-linux branch on the Mac (branch has no upstream yet;
     it must be pushed first).
  2. Run the whole-frame capture path on the Metal backend for the same fixed
     scene set the Linux side captured in .7/.8 -- identical project, window
     size, scale factor, and theme. If the scenes are not pinned to something
     deterministic, this comparison is worthless; verify that before capturing.
  3. Commit the Metal reference PNGs alongside the wgpu ones under the
     crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/ golden subdirectory.
  4. Per-pipeline (8, from .7) and per-widget (25, from .8) diff review.
  5. Sign off, or file specific beads for the widgets/pipelines that differ.

EXPECT AND DO NOT PANIC AT: gamma/colorspace differences, and MSL-vs-WGSL
float precision divergence. Neither is a per-widget bug -- if a constant
offset shows up across ALL captures, that is one systemic colorspace or
sRGB-surface-format issue, not 25 shader bugs. Diagnose the systemic case
first before opening per-widget beads, or you will file two dozen duplicates
of the same root cause.

Record macOS version, chip, and display scale factor in the notes, same as
eseq-linux.24.
acceptance_criteria: Metal reference PNGs for the same deterministic scene set are committed beside the wgpu captures; all 8 core pipelines and all 25 widgets are diff-reviewed; systemic colorspace/precision offsets are diagnosed as systemic rather than filed per-widget; remaining genuine differences are either fixed or filed as individual beads; macOS version/chip/scale recorded in notes
notes:
Created 2026-08-23 as part of removing macOS-host dependencies from the Linux worker's path. Same pattern as eseq-linux.24.
Blocked after claim: the assigned agent host is Linux (uname: x86_64 Linux 6.19.8-arch1-3-surface), not macOS. The bead requires executing Metal and recording macOS/chip/scale data; this checkout only contains the existing wgsl-linux-x86_64 captures, and the current capture binary is wgpu-only. No Metal reference images or visual sign-off can be produced honestly from this host.
close_reason: Signed off. Built the Metal reference harness (eseqlisp_metal_shader_capture) rendering the shared scene set through the MSL sources metal_backend.rs compiles, and committed two captures beside the existing Linux one: msl-macos-arm64 and wgsl-macos-arm64, both from the same GPU so the shader language is the only variable. 37 of 38 scenes byte-identical MSL-vs-WGSL; the exception is 2 px of one bezier cable at 1/255 in one channel. No systemic gamma/colorspace offset exists — ruled out by observation, not argument. All 8 core pipelines and all 31 widget scenes reviewed; nothing filed per-widget because nothing differs. Verdict, thresholds and attribution in tests/fixtures/shader-capture/goldens/JUDGEMENT.md. Host: MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), arm64, built-in display 3024x1964 at backing scale 2.0 (recorded for the record only: the harnesses render into a 512x256 offscreen texture with no window, layer or drawable, so no display property reaches the pixels). Found and closed a coverage hole: dropdown-checkmark had a fragment in both languages and a scene in neither, so eseq-linux.8's port of it had never been diff-reviewed; it is now widget-dropdown-checkmark, byte-identical, and capture_scenes::tests fails from here on if any fragment lacks a scene. Filed eseq-linux.76 (MSL round() breaks ties away from zero, WGSL half-to-even) and eseq-linux.77 (regenerate wgsl-linux-x86_64 at schema 3). Commit adc80af4.

title: History shape inference: make @shape optional via evaluator restart pass
description:
Deferred UX follow-up to eseq-0td.1: let a patcher history node adopt the shape feeding into it, no @shape annotation needed. Design decision from discussion: inference must live in the dgen evaluator, NOT the patcher — patcher-side back-walking would require reimplementing every op's shape semantics (reshape, gather, matmul, sum-axis) in Rust, dual-maintained against Swift.

Proposed mechanism: make @shape optional on make-history in the evaluator (/Users/alecresende/code/swift/dgen, Sources/DGenLisp/LispEvaluator.swift — make-history is hoisted in a pre-pass at :437/:454, and the @shape guard at :276-286 is structural). A shapeless make-history starts scalar; when write-history receives a tensor value into a scalar history, record the shape and restart evaluation once with the history bound to that shape. The restart breaks the read-before-write circularity of feedback loops; reshape/gather/matmul are handled for free because the real ops compute shapes. If the write shape differs between passes, report a genuine loop shape error — fixpoint terminates after one restart or fails loudly. Explicit @shape (eseq-0td.1) remains as an override/escape hatch.

Parked as complicated; explicit @shape ships first.
acceptance_criteria: tensor -> phasor -> history (no @shape) -> feedback loop compiles with the history adopting the incoming shape; a loop whose write shape disagrees with the adopted read shape errors with a clear message; explicit @shape still wins.
notes: Scope addition from eseq-0td.1: stdlib filter defmacros (onepole, dcblock, svf, slew) declare shapeless (make-history s) internally, so making shapeless histories adopt the written shape is ALSO what turns those macros tensor-capable. This raises the value of this slice beyond patcher UX.
